On Friday, Sumire thinks about families.
Makoto and Haru both expressed disillusionment from their most important family members,
desperately reaching for a connection that would not, or could not, be returned.
Makoto spoke of her sister’s desire for her success. Sumire thinks she understands why- she
knows that Sae is legally Makoto’s guardian after the sisters were orphaned, and she thinks
that would probably put stress on anyone. And knowing how Sae sees her workplace as a
twisted centre for gambling and black and white morality, she thinks it’s hardly any wonder
that she struggles to be there for Makoto, as what was a sisterly connection was turned into
that of essentially a single mother and child overnight.
But when Sumire joined the phantom thieves in January, Makoto spoke so highly of her
sister, as though all of their troubles had been resolved. Had Sae’s change of heart really been
so effective? Was that really all that was necessary to rid the prosecutor of the pressure and
corruption of her work?
Sumire remembers the reason why she initially disagreed with the phantom thieves. In her
eyes, changing problems reactionarily wasn’t much help in the bigger picture, even if she
could definitely see that each change of heart was helpful and likely necessary in context.
But then, there’s the similarities between the Phantom Thieves’ change of hearts and
Maruki’s actualisation.
Sumire knows that they’re different, deep down. But the idea of changing someone’s heart
for reasons other than the absolutely necessary doesn’t quite sit right with her, not after
experiencing a change of cognition firsthand. Was Makoto and Sae’s relationship only saved

because the thieves had forcibly altered Sae’s mind to their benefit? Or maybe that wasn’t
true, and Makoto really just got through to Sae, and the change of heart was just for how she
acted as a prosecutor. Even so, Sumire isn’t sure how to feel.
Haru’s situation with her father is different. Both in how it starts and how it’s destined to end.
Haru’s distance with her father is more of a yawning gap, that splits further and further the
more she tries to hold on to the sentiment of family.
From what little Sumire can gather, Haru’s father is not distant due to just the pressure of his
work. Or, at least, Haru didn’t see it as such. It seems more like Haru simply has a fading
relevance in her father’s mind, that she is unable to reinstate as the man succumbs further in
his obsession with his business.
Sumire never saw Okumura’s palace, but she does remember the rumours of horrible
business practices and insatiable greed that surrounded the CEO around the time the thieves
were targeting him.
She still doesn’t have any idea why he was murdered.
Sumire thinks about the fractured families of the two girls, and she thinks about the distance
between her and Kasumi.
Would the sisters have grown apart as Sumire wallowed further in self-pity and depression?
Would Kasumi have snapped her out of it? Would they have argued, unable to understand the
other as resentment festered?
Would Sumire have eventually grown a palace as she continued to force Kasumi away?
Sumire will never know, now.
After school, she pushes all those thoughts out of her mind and makes her way to the Shibuya
subway station. She hides around a corner in the station square, and whispers “Mementos”
into her newly acquired Nav app.
The world shifts, and Sumire jogs down the station steps, preparing to search the depths for
answers.
Her thief outfit materialises over her school uniform, and she feels Ella stir in her heart.
Quickly looking both ways, Sumire jumps onto the tracks, brandishing her rapier in a
flourish.
The first floor of Mementos is sprawling and nonsensical, and she already feels as though
she’s lost despite barely having taken ten steps in. She spots a shadow around the corner, and
squats in wait for it to move a little closer. As the shadow ambles within jumping distance,
Sumire jumps, and stabs down into the creature’s mask, flipping off it’s back at it screams
and bursts into black ooze, forming a squad of pixies surrounding a horse-riding shadow.
“Hear the word of the Lord!” The mounted shadow calls one of the many rotating phrases
that its kind tend to spout, brandishing its sword in preparation to attack.

But Sumire is faster, and she gets to act first.
“Ella!” she shouts, ripping off her mask, “Makougon!”
Light sears across the battlefield, the pixies screeching as they get fried by the blinding light.
The larger shadow shouts in pain as it tries to resist against the attack, but ultimately falls,
ending the battle before it had the chance to begin.
The creatures on this level of the collective unconscious may be a bit below you, Violet.
It certainly seems that way.
Sumire huffs gratefully at the lack of a challenge. She had been a bit concerned about coming
to Mementos without any teammates, but it’s nice to see that here worries are so far
unfounded.
She is a little concerned about going completely overkill on the weaker shadows, though,
since the only way she can technically hold back and save energy would be to forgo using her
persona all together, and Sumire doesn’t want to take unnecessary risks.
In considering that, Sumire opts to sneak around the bends and turns of Mementos, choosing
to avoid any battles for the time being. The shadows here would hardly even give her
experience if she fought them, anyway, so it’s not much of a loss.
When she hears the distant rattling of chains, however, she starts running past any potential
enemies, remembering the time when Joker decided it would be a good idea to fight the
reaper as a motivator for her sudden speed.
Hopping down the escalators to the next floor, Sumire is greeted with a sealed wall with
various nonsensical engravings carved in. Train tracks run on either side of the platform, with
these ones actually performing their intended purpose- the trains screeching past at random
intervals.
Sumire makes her way to the engraved wall, expecting it to open as it did for the thieves in
the past.
The door remains pointedly shut, and Sumire pouts.
“Please?” she tries, and she swears the wall is giving her side-eye.
Perhaps there is a requirement that we do not meet.
“Probably…” Sumire breathes. Oh well. Nothing to it but to make her way back.
She didn’t even run into José either. He probably could have told her something.
Sighing at the waste of time, Sumire heads back to the real world.

Ren pushes open the door to the final room in the palace, and is greeted with a sight of a
treasure trove of glittering gold and gems, all piled in heaps across the floor like a particularly
disorganised treasury.
“Is this it? Is this the last room we need?” Ryuji asks excitedly, placing a hand on Ren’s
shoulder.
Ren sure hopes it’s the last room. His legs are killing him, and he thinks a pixie could
probably push him over at this point. He knows his teammates aren’t faring much better.
“This is it!” Morgana calls, pointing at a shimmering mass hovering in the centre of the
room, “That’s the treasure!”
“The floating thing?” Ann cocks her head, trying to poke at it but phasing through.
“Sure is!” Morgana grins, “It’s just not materialised, yet. We need to send the calling card
first.”

“Oh, right, yeah you told us about that,” Ryuji says, scratching his head. “Should we get to it
then? Time’s a wastin’, right?”
Ren shakes his head, “Soon, but tomorrow’s Sunday. We need to wait till school’s open
again.” Though, he thinks, the school being closed for the day might be a very convenient

Morgana nods and gives a thumbs up, “You’ve got it, Joker!”
Ren nods, grinning at the codename, and signals for the team to move out.

Skull barks a laugh, “You got that right!” He sighs, “Man, s’real lucky you didn’t pass out on
us again, Joker.” Ren winces a bit at the reminder, but nods anyway.

“Yep,” he says, popping the ‘p’, “I’m all good now. I was just tired that day.”
Ryuji scoffs, “Musta been real’ tired…” as Morgana gives Ren a disapproving look for his
lie. Ren notes to buy yet another batch of quality sushi as thanks for the cat’s silence.
“Well, the important thing is that it won’t happen again, now.” Ann says brightly.
Ren nods, and activates the Nav.
When Ren arrives back at Leblanc, Morgana in tow, the cat immediately turns to glare at him.
“I can tell you’re lying; you know!” He yowls as soon as he hops out of the bag.
Ren keeps his face very still, “I don’t know what you’re talking about,”
“Don’t play dumb!” Morgana whines, hopping up on the bed, pacing in a circle, “You asked

You hear that, birdman?
I have nothing to say to you that you do not already know.

I’m fine,” he tacks on at the cat’s disbelieving look.

It’s fine. He’s fine. He doesn’t need help, or anyone worrying about him.

The other’s face twitches in what must be a violent internal debate. He eventually huffs,

Ren blinks, and quickly pumps his fist in success, jogging to fall into step alongside him.
When Ren wakes up the next morning, he doesn’t remember the dream.

When Akechi finally falls asleep that night, he spins the wheel of nightmares and lands on
something new.
That could mean anything, of course -there’s no way to tell if it will be better or worse than
any of his other recurring dreams- but it does mean that it’s unexpected, and that is both very
interesting and horrifically terrifying.

He can’t quite tell he’s dreaming, at first, and he probably won’t notice until he wakes up
later in a cold sweat.
So, Akechi reads the script and plays his role.
He’s walking down a long corridor, his footsteps echoing against the oppressive silence. He
passes by a faceless guard, at some point, not even stopping to look at the man before Akechi
pulls out a gun and shoots him in the back.
He turns, ignoring the blood as it pools around his feet, and looks at the boy sitting at the
table. His most striking feature is the bullet hole adorning his forehead behind his curly hair,
followed by the bruises that litter his face in alarming numeracy.
“Hey,” the boy says, like his brains aren’t scattered somewhere across the opposing wall.
“Hey,” Akechi returns, like he didn’t just kill a man and is about to kill this boy too.
The boy doesn’t say anything else, just stares at Akechi like he expected this, and is waiting
for him to get on with it.
Akechi obliges, lifting the gun in line with the bullet hole already present. He clicks off the
safety, and, he must have taken his gloves off at some point, because his hands are dripping
with blood.
“Case closed,” he murmurs, because that sounds like something he should probably say, and
the boy smiles, and Akechi pulls the trigger“The watertight bulkhead door has closed, please evacuate immediately-”
Akechi slams his full weight against the newly erected wall, staring himself in the face as
someone screams.
His doppelgänger spits up blood and re-aims his gun, “Do you really think death will be
enough for someone like you? Do you think saving them will make them love you? You’ve
failed, so you move the goalposts, is that it?”
“No,” Akechi whispers, because he doesn’t know, just that he’s done with this, and he might
as well do one fucking good thing in his miserable excuse for a life, and its not like the law
would have let him live anyway, should he choose to face it“Akechi!” the screaming voice on the other side of the door cries, “Don’t you dare- don’t you
dare listen to that thing! You promised! We can still get out of this together-!”
Akechi’s doppelgänger dissolves into cackles at that, and Akechi himself rasps a laugh as he
aims his gun.
“Do you really answer to him?” The doppelgänger croons, “Would you trade one master for
another, just because he said some pretty words and made you feel special?” he spits the last
word like a curse.

“No,” Akechi whispers again, “I won’t let anyone control me ever again.” He fires at the
same time as his double, the voice on the other side of the wall giving one final scream before
everything goes dark.
And as it all fades, he can hear the tinkling of a bell as a door slams closed for the final time.
When Akechi wakes up, shaking and nauseous, he can’t remember what he dreamed about.

Absolutely not, Akechi thinks, “What might that be?” He says instead.

Akechi wracks his brain for the last time he met the younger Yoshizawa twin. Or, more

Akechi investigates, Sumire interrogates, and the first change of heart kicks in.

When Sumire gets home and collapses onto her bed -something that appears to be becoming
a habit of hers- she’s still a bit miffed that no one thought to mention how palaces collapse
when you deal with them.
Would Maruki’s palace have collapsed when they stole the treasure? Or was he unique in
even more ways than the thieves implied?
It doesn’t particularly matter either way, since Maruki is no longer the most current issue.
Part of Sumire has wondered if she could perhaps speed up the timeline, and call on the
thieves before Maruki had the chance to attain godhood in order to steal his treasure. She had
partially thrown out this plan when she decided to not join the thieves right now, and has now
fully thrown it out after witnessing the thieves’ current strength.
Kamoshida’s shadow had looked fearsome, sure, but Sumire’s pretty sure that she fought
stronger normal enemies in Maruki’s palace in January- and if the thieves are really
struggling now, then it would definitely be some time before they could challenge Maruki.
This whole mess leads to her core problem with the thieves. Sumire doesn’t want to join
them. Not yet. She assumed she would join them as soon as possible, originally, but she
changed her mind in a split-second decision after everything that happened when she ran into
Maruki again.
Because she still doesn’t forgive Ren. And she doesn’t know if she can, while he isn’t even
the person he was when he wronged her- not yet, at least.
Anger is admittedly new for her. She would usually turn any form of animosity against others
back on herself, believing that she must be the problem, of course, because the people around
her would surely only have the best of intentions.
This rule comes with four notable exceptions. The first being her original awakening to
Cendrillion; she was finally feeling the weight of attention from the pressure of her dream,
and she was sick, and tired, of people telling her what they thought was best for her.

The second exception was during her reawakening after she remembered she was Sumire.
This anger was directed at herself, technically, but she also felt a deep frustration towards
everything that had happened. It wasn’t fair, that her sister had died so young, and she was
angry at the world for the way the wheel turned.
The third exception, (and the final of the original timeline) was directed at Ren, and finally,
finally, after having previously been so forgiving, Sumire got angry at Doctor Maruki. Who
was he to tell her that Sumire Yoshizawa doesn’t deserve to exist? If one twin had to die, why
did he believe the world would be better off with Kasumi being the one still alive? And
towards Ren, she felt the sting of betrayal, and angry at the fact that it wasn’t even about her.
All that effort and grief and for what?
The fourth exception is more of a permanent change. Because she’s still angry. For the first
time in her life, Sumire feels like she can’t just let this go. She can’t step aside and assume
better intentions until she gets some proof.
So, she wants to wait. And… figure things out first. It wouldn’t be helpful to rush into things
just yet- she can spend some time gathering information, and then she can act.
And who knows? Maybe, maybe someday, Ren will remember what he did, and Sumire can
face him, and ask why.
Or maybe he won’t.
But Sumire has plenty of time; while waiting for Kamoshida’s heart to change, at least. She’ll
never have enough information, she thinks, but she won’t gain any more by thinking until her
brain hurts.
So she turns off the light and goes to sleep.

“Right,” Makoto smooths out her skirt, “I assure you that I’m alright, I’m just,” she rolls her
lips, “Overwhelmed, I guess, by everything that happened today.”
Sumire nods and takes a seat across form her. “Do you want to talk about it?”
Makoto sighs, fidgeting as an internal debate casts a shadow across her face, “I suppose that
I’m just… frustrated, with everything that has now come to light.”
Sumire shifts in her seat, “How come?”
“Because what is the point,” she throws her hands up as the dam breaks, “In being the

“Did you even know about it, though?” Sumire asks.
Makoto flops her head back in her hands, “Yes and no. I should have. I mean,” she runs a
hand through her hair, “You told me in your first week here that you were concerned about
how Mister Kamoshida was treating certain students, and I just brushed it off!”

“Well, I didn’t have any evidence or anything. It’s not fair to beat yourself up for not
believing rumours-”
“But I didn’t even try,” Makoto’s voice cracks, “You don’t have to make excuses for my sake,
Sumire-chan. In the end, I should have investigated, brought it up with the principal, done

Sumire stays silent as Makoto sinks into her chair.
“I need to try harder,” Makoto mumbles, mostly to herself, “The next time something comes

Sumire nods encouragingly, “That’s the spirit, senpai. Even if you couldn’t help here, I’m

Makoto nods, seemingly having calmed down, “I- thank you, Sumire-chan. I’m sorry for
breaking down like this.” She hastily wipes her eyes again, “Thank you for letting me vent.
You didn’t have to do that.”
Sumire smiles, “It’s not a problem at all, Makoto-senpai. I’m sure that you’ll figure it out.”
Makoto offers a small smile in return, “I hope so.” She says, not for the first time. And, not
for the first time either, Sumire hopes that it will turn out okay.

If those two are heading to the Wilton to ‘celebrate properly’ on Thursday, then could it be

Cinder, the answer will not change every time you ponder it.
Yeah, that’s fair.

Her parents agree- far quicker than Sumire thought they would.
Plans for Thursday set, Sumire sets out to her Wednesday booking.
Sumire sits across from Akechi, lightly amazed that he didn’t cancel last minute. Or block her
number. Or, frankly, give her his number at all- she still hasn’t figured out a possible reason
for that one.
“It certainly is fascinating.” Akechi muses, placing a hand on his chin, “That calling card
turned out to be telling the truth. It could just be a coincidence, of course, but it seems
awfully suspicious, don’t you think?”
He turns his TV smile at Sumire, and she quickly nods, unsure what she’s doing.
The two are sitting in one of the more popular Kichijoji café’s, picking at their cakes as the
conversation continues in fits and starts, Sumire scrambling for topics as Akechi -for oncedoesn’t seem to be in the mood to carry the conversation on his back. Or maybe he’s just
waiting to see where Sumire will take it?
In that case, she knows what she needs to find out.

It is highly unlikely, she thinks, that Akechi has knowledge or access to the Metaverse at this
point. He probably would have found out who the thieves are on the spot, in that case, and
Sumire can’t think of a reason he would just keep that to himself.
But, if he is in the Metaverse, then Sumire would love to know.
So, she steers the conversation towards trying to discover just that.
She nods, “It does seem kind of crazy. I mean, ‘Phantom Thieves of Hearts’?”
“I must say, I had thought that the accusations on the cards would be the more pressing
matter, but I didn’t expect them to be resolved through a confession- seemingly enacted
through sudden, crushing guilt.” Akechi sighs and takes another sip of his coffee, “Perhaps
Kamoshida was so paranoid from the threat that he caved and confessed? But then, why
would a man who clearly felt no remorse for his disgusting actions,” Sumire sees a flash of
anger dart across his face, “Suddenly panic like that?”
Sumire hums, “Maybe someone really did ‘change his heart’, like the calling cards said.” She
pushes, innocently as possible.
Akechi chuckles a dainty laugh, “Are you suggesting supernatural influence, Yoshizawasan?”
Sumire shrugs weakly, “Hypothetically…?”
Akechi laughs, like he isn’t taking her seriously, and Sumire frowns.
“Um, genuinely though,” Sumire tries again, “Do you think that supernatural methods are
completely impossible?”
Akechi regards her a little more seriously, seemingly considering her question, “My stance is
generally that, as supernatural methods in all forms have not yet been documented anywhere
in particular, then it would be a bit foolish for me as a detective to automatically leap to such
assumptions when there are other explanations available.”
Sumire nods. That’s a fair stance, she thinks.
But, wasn’t Akechi one of the first people in the last timeline to say outright that the thieves
had unknown methods? What changed, in that case?
“What kind of other explanations are there, do you think?” Sumire asks.
“Blackmail.” Akechi states flatly, “Paranoia on Kamoshida’s part, as I said earlier.” He hums,
“Though, that remains to be seen as we question him in the coming days. I’m not on this
investigation at the moment, so I don’t know what’s come up.”
Sumire tilts her head, confused, “I thought you were at Shujin to investigate?”
“The calling cards, yes.” Akechi sighs, “But at present, the calling cards and Kamoshida’s
confession are being treated as separate cases, until the cards can be proven as more than just

a prank.”
Sumire nods, considering. Maybe Akechi’s stance will change when the cases are connected,
or more examples of a change of heart come up?
“When Kamoshida confessed,” Sumire says, as surreptitiously as possible, “It seemed almost
like he was a completely different person, like his personality really did change.”
Akechi smiles, “Trying to convert me into being a believer of the Phantom Thieves?” He
chuckles as Sumire looks embarrassed, “I suppose being a witness to the event itself gives
you better information than I.”
Sumire smiles, “Are you willing to give the supernatural explanation a shot, then?”
Akechi’s smile turns a bit wry, “Not if I want to keep my job, I don’t.” He tilts his head,
“Though, I suppose if the case were to develop in such a way where it seems likely, then who
knows? Maybe there really are some people who can steal hearts.”
Sumire laughs awkwardly, “It does sound kind of crazy when you put it like that…” She
straightens up, “Well, I guess we’ll just have to wait and see!” She says brightly.
“Expecting more than a one-hit-wonder, then?” Akechi chuckles, “Perhaps so. Though I still
hesitate to say that the calling card was anything more than a prank or warning done by
students who knew what Kamoshida’s crimes were.”
Sumire hums, “I guess that’s fair.” She laughs, “I wonder how it would even be possible,
stealing someone’s heart?” She tries not to sound too eager for his response.
Akechi just takes another sip of coffee, “I wonder,” he murmurs over the rim.
Sumire nods, taking a bite of her cake, and finds herself once again deeply confused about
the enigma that is the detective before her.
He probably doesn’t know about the Metaverse yet, she decides.

The other -definitely a person, definitely a man, Ren notes- cocks his head. “Are you going to
sit there and gawk? Or are you going to do something about this?”
Ren swallows, “About what?” He finally says.
The man rasps a laugh, “God forbid you ever say more than two words at a time.”
Ren scowls at the other’s amusement, “You didn’t answer my question,” he folds his arms,
“Who are you?” He adds.
The other whips his head around to look at him, “You don’t remember?” He places a hand
dramatically on his chest, but Ren can still hear the edge in his voice, “I’m hurt, Joker.”
Ren shakes his head, “Am I supposed to know you?” he tries.
The other scoffs, “Clearly not.” He leans back into the bench in a huff, “This conversation is
pointless if you can’t even remember what it’s supposed to be about.”
Ren rolls his lips together, frustrated, “You could start by telling me, then.” When the other
ignores him, he shifts a little closer, “I can’t help with anything if you don’t explain what’s
happening.”
The other clicks his tongue, “Help?” He hisses, “Even as an amnesiac in your dreams,
you’re still knee deep in a terminal saviour complex. Pathetic.”
Ren doesn’t rise to the bait, “So this is a dream, then?” He focuses on instead.
“Of course it is,” the other deadpans, “Where else could you be having conversations with
dead men?”
“You’re dead?”
“Of course I am.” The man scoffs. “Or maybe I’m not? Who’s to say? If you can’t remember
me, then maybe it never happened.”

Ren’s eyes widen, and he pulls at his gloves, “So you’re just in my head, then?” He frowns,
“Why would someone in my head know more than me? Are you a cognition or something?”
The man barks a laugh, “Not in the normal sense, at least, but maybe you just know more
than you think. Or maybe not. Maybe none of this is real.”
Ren tilts his head, “I thought we already established that this was a dream?”
He can’t see the other’s eyes, but Ren’s pretty sure he just rolled them, “And since when were
those two mutually exclusive? You spend your time diving into the physical manifestations of
the hearts of others, and you can’t handle someone in your head telling you about things you
can’t remember?”
Ren squints, “Those two things are pretty different,” he narrows his eyes even further, “And
you haven’t actually told me anything yet.”
“Yes, and I’m going to keep it that way.” The other turns away, “If you can’t remember on
your own, then it won’t do any good for me to just tell you.”
“So what should I do then?” Ren asks, but he doesn’t know what about.
The other snorts, “How should I know? I’m just in your head, right? You’re clever, Joker, you
can figure it out.” Ren isn’t certain, but he swears he heard the other’s voice turn almost
fond.
Ren just hums in lieu of a reply.
“In any case,” the other continues, undaunted, “Isn’t it about time you woke up?”
Ren smirks, “Is it?”
“Don’t be cute,” the man says, and snaps his fingers-And Ren wakes up, Morgana still snoring at his side.
He shoots up, grabbing for his probation diary to quickly write what he can remember down
before it slips through his mind like a sieve.
As Ren quickly scrawls the key points, he scowls as he loses more and more details, ending
up with a mess of uncoordinated notes: Weird guy? Was in Mementos. Can’t remember
something? A dream but still real. Something to do with visions?
Ren angrily runs a hand through his hair as he runs out of points to write. Maybe the dream
didn’t even mean anything. Maybe he’s just getting worked up over nothing.
Is that truly how you feel? Arsène says, and Ren can almost hear the raised eyebrow.
He scowls. No, no it isn’t. That dream had the same feeling as the weird visions he’s been
having- just… to the left a bit. Usually his sense of self is a bit off in them- he’s still ‘Ren’,

but he knows that he knows more, without actually knowing anything. In the dream he was
just Ren. Normal Ren who has no idea what’s going on.
Ren feels like the universe heard his plea to stop fucking with him and decided to double
down in retaliation.
He looks at the floor as the light streaming into his bedroom slowly gets brighter, and sighs.
He tries to make it a policy to not wake up before noon on Sundays, but Ren doubts he can
get back to sleep like this.
Flipping his journal shut, he starts the day, and forgets the dream.

That, and the slightly less altruistic reason that her pushing back her exams was what caused

jealousy swirling to form some formless mass of what they believed her to truly be like.

Running into Maruki last month was one time too many, Sumire thinks, and she doesn’t have
anything to say to the man. Or, more accurately, she doesn’t have anything to say to the man
in a calm, measured, voice and without digging her nails into her palms so hard that her

So, she avoids him. She isn’t on the list of students who have to have mandatory counselling

doing pretty well, if you can. “That’s amazing, Amamiya-kun, I’m glad. You seem to have an

And he only needed to rip off half his face to do it. Somewhere, Arsène chuckles. Ren tilts

“Maybe, but what if it doesn’t have to be?” Maruki’s eyes gain an unreadable gleam.

you would make?
What if you couldn’t live without it?
What if there were no strings attached?

intrigues him, even beyond all its strange overlap with the concept of the Metaverse.

“I accept,” Ren says, and Maruki smiles wider,
“Great!” He nods cheerfully, “We can still meet up for counselling sessions, of course, but we

Akechi takes a deep breath.
In.
Out.
In.
Out- He can’t keep standing in front of this door all day. It’s been a while since he’s had one

“Enter,” is the reply, thrown out as carelessly as one would toss trash.
Fitting, given the man speaking it.

Akechi opens the door, coming to stand in the centre of the room a respectable distance from

Who the fuck is he kidding? Nothing could prepare him for these conversations, so he just

The fucker isn’t even looking at him, and Akechi’s been standing here for at least thirty

The piece of shit takes a long inhale of oxygen he doesn’t deserve, and finally turns to look at

Ah. So he’s already in a bad mood.
Akechi is very well versed with the ins and outs of how Masayoshi Shido likes to conduct his

“Akechi.” Shido says, and ah, that’s a bad start, “I take that you heard of that… calling card

Akechi bites the inside of his mouth. Shit. “I was given clearance to investigate the initial

What a joke. Akechi hopes that it’s true.

Fucker did that on purpose. “Yes, Shido-san?”

“This case is absurd.”
“I agree, Sae-san.”
“It’s completely ridiculous. I can’t believe the director thought this was a good idea.”
“Absolutely, Sae-san.”
“It’s not even considered a real case yet, and he’s still wasting our time with this.”
“Mmhm.”
“It’s,” Sae pauses, turning to look at Akechi properly, “Are you even listening, Akechi-kun?”
Akechi tries to hide his smirk. He must fail, because Sae glares at him, “Of course I am, Saesan. I just thought it might be a bad idea to interrupt you.”
The two of them are walking through central street, making their way to the conveyor belt
sushi place that they usually frequent. The director recently assigned the two of them to the
unofficial Phantom Thieves case- an act which has thoroughly pissed off the both of them;
Sae, because it is, at this point, a colossal waste of time, and Akechi, because this is yet
another case where he now has to tread the thin line of ‘making connections within the case’
without revealing any information at all.
He has to do that with a lot of his cases. It’s starting to get a bit dull.
Sae rolls her eyes, “I see that this isn’t bothering you.”
“Of course it is. I just believe that you’re complaining enough for the both of us.” Akechi
says. And also because if he lets himself start complaining, they’re going to be here all week.
And because it’s very funny to rile Sae up.
Sae huffs, “If you don’t have anything valuable say…”

“Of course I don’t.” Akechi deadpans, allowing himself to indulge a bit, “And neither do you,
because this case is a fruitless endeavour with the information available to us.”
Sae snorts at that, “We’re in agreement then. We can at least review the facts over dinner,
though.”
Akechi nods, satisfied at the prospect of free food. He thinks that Sae’s a bit of a cheapskate
for limiting the both of them to just conveyor sushi, but he’ll take what he can get.
The two arrive in the restaurant, taking a seat in one of the booths and spreading their files
over the table. Sae clicks her tongue at the grand total of two pieces of information they have
to work with. A photo of the calling card, and transcripts of the various interrogations that
Kamoshida has undergone after his arrest.
“I truly have no idea why the director is wasting everyone’s time with this.” Sae mutters to
herself.
Akechi would agree with her, if he didn’t know exactly why the director is wasting their time
with this. Likely, Shido gave him the order to pour some resources into investigating, because
the bald fuck is convinced that the Phantom Thieves have something to do with cognitive
psience, and as such is acting paranoid.
He’s right, technically, but it doesn’t stop Akechi from gripping his chopsticks a little too
hard from supressed frustration.
It also doesn’t stop him from worrying about the implications of all this.
Between Yoshizawa and the thieves, an alarming number of people have all gained access to
the Metaverse at once. Akechi got the Nav nearly three years ago, so why are new people
suddenly getting it only now? Is there even a pattern to it? Akechi wasn’t anyone that could
be considered ‘special’ before he awakened his persona, so there’s already no precedent for
unique requirements, but it still irks him that a bunch of random high schoolers have
stumbled into this power on a whim.
Akechi grips the chopsticks a little harder.
And, speak of the devil- a text buzzes on Akechi’s phone. He sighs; it’s Yoshizawa, sending
him an inane text about her day. She’s been doing that a lot ever since their deal, just sending
a bunch of unnecessary quips and photos. Akechi can only brush her off so many times
without possibly putting their deal in jeopardy, so he shoots off a text that could be read as
‘interested’ and puts his phone back down to look over the files once more.
Akechi notices Sae giving him a look out of the corner of his eye.
“You didn’t look very happy to get that text.” Sae comments with no particular intonation.
“Ah, my apologies,” Akechi says with a placating smile, “I didn’t mean to get distracted from
work- it won’t happen again.”

Sae gives a weary sigh, “That isn’t what I meant, Akechi-kun.” She straightens some of the
papers, and Akechi resists the urge to roll his eyes, “I just meant that I’ve never seen you get

Akechi shoves his phone into his pocket, “How are you so sure that it wasn’t for work, Saesan?”
“Because you never react to more work,” Sae says with a smug air, and, oh, doesn’t she think

Akechi actually rolls his eyes this time. Oh well, Sae can deal with some sass. “You’ve been
cataloguing my facial expressions, then?”
“There’s not a lot to catalogue.” She returns with equal sass, “So is that a friend, then?”
Akechi internally prepares himself for a long interrogation. Sae is almost as persistent as he
is. But the mother-henning would be better spent on Sae’s actual sister, he thinks.
“It was.” Akechi stiffly admits, hoping that maybe honesty will get her to leave him alone,
“I’ve made an acquaintance, recently. They seem to enjoy taking up my time.”
Sae hums, “Well, it’s good to see you make some actual friends your age. I was starting to get
worried.”
Is it your business? Akechi thinks, “And why is that, Sae-san?” he says pleasantly.
Sae gives him a confused look, “Why wouldn’t I be? You’re a teenager working for the
police, and I’ve never seen you interact with anyone other than co-workers.”
A misplaced sense of maternal instinct and guilt, then. Akechi can work with that, “I assure
you that I can take care of myself.”
“You’ve said that before,” Sae says, and must she look so smug? “As independent as you are,
Akechi-kun, surely it isn’t that insulting to have someone worry about you.” Akechi’s silence

You don’t ever complain when I take you out for sushi, and that’s my way of making sure

Akechi probably should have figured out that Sae had an ulterior motive for giving him free

Sae chuckles at that, “Well, you’ll have to play the game a while longer, then. I can’t afford
the good stuff.”
Akechi finds himself laughing as well, to his annoyance. Of all his co-workers, Sae is the

Apparently these bonds are not something he can make a choice in; Akechi thinks as he starts

Maybe it’s to do with trust? As much as he insists that he doesn’t trust Yoshizawa, he did
certainly give her something resembling it when they made their deal. And with Sae, he
didn’t fight her as hard as he could have on her prying. Is that trust? He doesn’t think so. So
what is it, then?
Maybe it’s random, he thinks with a stab of annoyance. Of course supernatural bullshit would
have a different prerequisite for every time it activates.
He has two of these bonds now, though. And considering that they only exist as an echoing
voice in his head, he doesn’t think he can just get rid of them as he would a piece of trash.
Akechi sighs. In for a penny, in for a pound. He may as well see where this leads.
A sunk cost.
A SLIPPERY SLOPE.
Time will tell.

Haru giggles, “Well, at least we’re done for today.” She picks up her bag, moving to sit on
one of the benches to the side. Sumire follows suit, taking out her lunch from her bag. She

stifles a laugh- she never had this kind of familiarity with Akechi last time, but now that he’s
one of her few friends, and the only person who she can talk to about the Metaverse, she’s
been bothering him all the time for things that aren’t even necessarily relevant.
It might be her desperate attempt to lessen the gap between herself and the detective, by
forcefully making herself a part of his day. She isn’t sure if it’s working, but until Akechi
snaps and tells her to piss off, she’ll keep at it.
“Who are you texting, Sumi-chan?” Haru asks, taking a bite of her own lunch.
“Oh, I just made a new friend.” Sumire says, letting a smile properly take her face, “I

doesn’t forget about me, I guess.”
Haru laughs, “You seem close, then.”
Sumire blinks, “Oh, not really,” certainly not now. She hopes so, though, in the future. “We,

friendship experience- you have me.”
Haru smiles in return, “Thank you, Sumi-chan.” She sighs. “In truth, you’re actually the first
friend that I’ve had in a while. Or ever, really,” she tucks some of her hair behind her ear

Sumire nods for her to go on, and she smiles gratefully, “Most of my friends in elementary
school were either the children of my father’s business partners, or they would find out I was

good word’.” She huffs, and looks down at her knees, “So I suppose from then onwards I just

friend for what was in it for them.”

Sumire presses her lips together, “That sounds lonely…”
Haru gives a sad smile, “It is, isn’t it? I guess I’m jealous that you seem so good at making
friends everywhere you go. I’ve seen you talk with some of the second years and Niijima-san
a lot, and now your new friend you were texting earlier.”
Sumire chokes a laugh, “I’m definitely not as good at making friends as you think I am,
senpai.”
Haru gives a teasing laugh, “Really? It seems to me like you have a whole crowd!”
Sumire pulls at her ponytail, “I really just got lucky all those times,” Already knowing what a
person is like does wonders for first impressions, Sumire has found, “When my sister was
still alive, she was basically my only friend. Any friends that I made were because Kasumi

Haru tilts her head, humming, “There’s a social phenomenon that I’ve heard of- it’s called
‘tall poppy syndrome’.” Sumire cocks her head in a gesture to continue, “It’s basically the
urge to ‘mow down’ any ‘tall poppies’ in society; when someone is noticeably unique or

sounds like what’s happening with you, Sumi-chan.”
Sumire gives a weak laugh, “Does that phenomenon come with the knowledge on how to

Haru smiles, “Not really, no. It’s kind of just a facet of society, I think. The sky is blue, the

“But?”
“I think that for people to ‘not be like this’, there would be a lot of things that we’d have to

Sumire’s eyes widen, and she thinks about wishes and ideal realities, of people remodelled to

“Right,” She says, voice suddenly firm, “If you take away jealousy, then you’d probably have

Sumire flushes, “I’ve just had some reason to think about it before.” She hates how easy it

She’s supposed to be better than this- especially now that she’s actually managed to do

Four days after Akechi initially made his deal with Yoshizawa, he heads back to Mementos to
start on the targets he was interrupted on. He’ll just do the interrogations today- he’s in a rare,
good mood and doesn’t feel like ruining it.
His instructions are to ask each of them if they’re hiding any particular information from the
larger conspiracy in the real world. These kinds of check-ups are pretty common, as a
conglomerate group of power-hungry egomaniacs is likely to collapse in on itself when
people take turns backstabbing and betraying the larger cause. Or, more accurately, betraying
the head of the cause- any other self-sabotage is almost actively encouraged.
All this to say that Shido likes assurance, and the cognitive world can give it to him. Those
below him can trade and deal as they please, so long as he remains unaffected.
The first guy was a bust. Just kept rambling about how much he hates one of his co-workers,
no secrets to be found other than a miniature soap opera unfolding in some guy’s workplace.
Akechi pulls open the second distortion to try for round two, stepping through with practiced
calm.
“Kaito Takahashi,” Akechi calls out into the carved space of conscious.
“Who- who are you?!” Takahashi’s shadow hisses, whirling around, “The black mask! Have
you come for me as well?” The shadow starts to bubble pre-emptively, steaming at the edges.
Akechi holds up his hands in a placating gesture, “Now, Takahashi-san, let’s not jump to
conclusions.” He squats in front of the shadow, resting his chin against his hand, “I’m just
here for a chat. Your boss wants to know if you’ve been hiding anything.”
Unfortunately, said boss never tells Akechi what he’s looking for. The logic there seems to be
that if a shadow is actively hiding something, they’ll spill whether they’re asked directly or

not; and if they don’t spill, then Akechi will never know what the problem may have been in
the first place.
A lovely restriction of information. And a real pain in the ass.
A cackle spills from the shadow’s lips, “I see. He wants to know how the research is going,
huh? He already knows that we aren’t getting anywhere!”
Akechi freezes, a sense of dread prickling where his personas hide, “Research?” He says
flatly.
“I’m at the top, you know?” The shadow drawls, “The only one in my field left- Shido got rid
of everyone else, and now I’m the last man standing! It means I have to be special, right?”
Akechi nods numbly, “Right.”
“Cognitive psience is a field filled to the brim with potential!” The shadow continues, and
Akechi digs one of his gauntlets into his leg, “But Shido won’t give us anything to work with!
I read that old research from a few years back, but he won’t even let us try to make the same
conditions- if we could get a hold of the subject they used for all that -or found some new
one- then we could actually start making some strides!” The shadow’s face twists into a
snarl, “But all we get are unreasonable demands to ‘make progress’ when we barely get
enough funding to scrape by!”
Somewhere, Akechi thinks that he could end this here. If this man truly is the last cognitive
psience researcher with funding that has been allowed to live, then he could do what he does
best and ensure that research never gets anywhere ever again.
He’d know it was you.
Akechi can’t tell if this interrogation is a threat, a reassurance, or a taunt. A threat, to remind
Akechi that he is ultimately replaceable. A reassurance, because Akechi can’t be replaced if
there’s nothing to replace him, and it sure seems like these researchers are coming up empty.
And a taunt, toDON’T. NOT HERE.
He won’t. He can’t. Not here.
He needs to leave. This place isn’t helping.
“To clarify,” Akechi says, interrupting the shadow’s ranting by pointing his gun at its head
and flicking off the safety, “There’s nothing you’re hiding from Shido other than exactly how
much you hate his guts.” He states more than asks, desperate to wrap this up.
The shadow nods mutely, trembling as it eyes the gun pointed at its forehead.
“Good.” Akechi says, and whirls around to leave the pocket of distortion.

Akechi collapses against the side of the subway tunnels. It isn’t exactly fresh air, but it will
have to do for now.
We have to go. We can do this once we’re back, Bird.
Akechi nods shakily at nothing, taking off his helmet. Fuck, he can’t breathe in this placeHe crushes a Goho-M in his palm, hitting the ground running as he’s thrown back to the top
layer of Mementos, ducking into an alleyway as he hisses at the Nav to deactivate, taking a
shuddering breath of the crisp evening air as he slumps against the cool bricks.
Okay. He’s okay. He can make it back like this.
Akechi slowly straightens out his dishevelled appearance, walking out of the alley to make
his way back to his apartment.
So much for a good fucking mood.

Ren looks over his shoulder, feeling the prick of being watched raise the hairs on the back of
his neck.
“Something wrong?” Morgana pops his head out of the bag.
Ren hums, “Not really…” he trails off, and pauses when he sees Niijima hiding around a
corner, peeking over a thick manga. Ren narrows his eyes. Does she… know that she’s
holding the book upside down?
Ren walks up to her awkwardly, giving a small wave, “Hey there, prez.”
Niijima flinches, clearly not expecting Ren to have addressed her, “Oh. Hello, Amamiya-kun.
How are you today.” She doesn’t sound like she’s asking a question; which probably makes
sense if she’s been stalking Ren all day.
“Fine,” Ren answers anyway.
“Good,” Niijima intones flatly. She shifts uncomfortably, still holding the Manga a little too
close to her face, “Well, um…”
Ren decides to put her out of her misery, “So, is there a reason you’ve been stalking me?”
“Stalking?!” Niijima splutters, affronted, “It’s not- well, I-” she deflates, and Ren can see the
cogs turning in her head on how to salvage this.
“It’s fine,” Ren lies, he’s actually kind of annoyed, but at least it’s funny, “You’ve been
tailing me for a while though. See anything interesting?”
Niijima scowls, “Surely you must understand why your group of friends is suspicious. I
mean, the delinquent, social outcast, and criminal transfer student all become friends after

being targeted by Kamoshida?”
Ren frowns at the implication laced in her words, “Can a bunch of people not just be friends?
You said it yourself, we’re all outcasts, so it’s only natural that we’d gravitate towards each
other.”
Niijima just stares him down, and Ren doesn’t blink in turn. He can feel Morgana shift
uncomfortably at the tense atmosphere.
“Why are you so desperate to catch the Phantom Thieves anyway?” Ren breaks the silence.
“Do you even know if they’re real? And if they are, they dealt with Kamoshida, right? Isn’t
that a good thing?”
Niijima sighs, “If they aren’t real in the ‘stealing hearts’ sense, then they still threatened a
teacher, bad person or no.” She huffs, “And there’s no guarantee that this group is good with
only one example of their behaviour. And I never said that I wanted to catch them to turn
them in.” Ren tilts his head questioningly, “I would want to confirm their intentions first.”
She finishes matter-of-factly.
That’s interesting. Ren hopes that she isn’t just bluffing- it would be convenient if all it takes
to placate Niijima is to prove he isn’t trying to take over Japan. He could probably just show
her his exam scores and insist he doesn’t have the brains to even try.
(He usually does way better on exams, but he got a bit distracted from studying when the
Phantom Thieves got founded.)
Ren gives a small smile, “If you want to tell if they’re good people, then maybe stalking your
prime suspects isn’t the way to go.”
Niijima narrows her eyes, “Is that a confession?”
“Of course not,” Ren grins, “I just think that when you find some better suspects, they might
not react as well to being tailed as me and my friends do.”
“Right,” Niijima says disbelievingly, and Ren chuckles.
“Surely you understand why I’m desperate to find these thieves,” she continues, “I know that
I failed as student council president in regards to the Kamoshida incident. I just don’t want to
ignore a possible threat to the student body again.”
Ren nods, understanding. “Is that the only reason, though?”
Niijima rolls her lips, pausing, “Well, if you truly aren’t related to the Phantom Thieves, then
it shouldn’t concern you, should it?”
Ren hums, as Morgana shifts to give him a look, “I suppose so.” He tosses out a casual wave,
“See you later, prez.”
“Of course,” Niijima mumbles, “See you later.”

Ren turns and leaves, satisfied in having discouraged her to follow him for the rest of the day.
Good- he needs the space. He has a calling card to send.

Chapter 11
Chapter Summary

Sumire tries for some budget subterfuge, and Akechi deals with the arcana.

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

Sumire nearly drops her phone when she gets a text from Akechi in the morning- both out of
shock that he would willingly text her and shock at its contents.
Akechi: A calling card was sent to Madarame last night.
Akechi: It was discovered this morning at his exhibition.
Sumi☆: !!!
Sumi☆: if they sent it yesterday, then I think theyll go to the palace straight after school
Sumi☆: thats what they did last time
Her texts get marked as ‘read’, and Sumire puts her phone away. She’s pretty confident that
the thieves will stick to the pattern of stealing treasures after school. As funny as it sounds in
practice, she thinks that it does actually make sense- it would basically be waving a neon sign
saying ‘we’re up to suspicious activities’ if the thieves were to skip school the day after a
calling card is sent.
But- oh, wait.
She never tried to guess Madarame’s keywords. She might have to run to tail the thieves after
school. At least she knows where their hideout is at the moment.
Pushing those thoughts for later, Sumire packs the bare minimum for school so she won’t be
weighed down during her impromptu palace escapade, foregoing grabbing her gymnastics
things knowing that she’ll have to skip practice this afternoon.
Sumire, much like when she saw Kamoshida’s calling card, can hardly pay attention to
school that day. During lunch, she remembers to send off a quick text to her coach with some
excuse of how she’s not feeling well enough to attend practice in the afternoon.
Once the bell rings, she shoots off to the Shibuya accessway, and waits as inconspicuously as
she can for all the thieves to arrive. They, thankfully for her nerves, arrive pretty quickly, and
set off on a path through central street. Sumire follows them to the entrance of a run-down

looking shack in a richer part of Shibuya, and edges as close as she can when she sees Ren
pull out his phone and look to the group for confirmation.
“Everyone ready?” She hears him say, to a chorus of confirmation.
The world shifts, and Sumire staggers as she takes in the sight of a museum coated bottom to
top in shining gold, spotlights illuminating giant murals, all signalling the ruler’s design of
fame and fortune. She goes to shield her eyes as the gold reflects and fragments the light
painting the building and street.
Sumire looks back, and sees that the cognitive space tapers off just a few blocks down the
road. She never explored the area surrounding Kamoshida’s palace, so she doesn’t know how
far outside the castle it stretched, but it’s definitely disconcerting to see the road and houses
crumble into negative space.
Sumire turns back to the monstrosity of a palace, and sees that the thieves have already leftprobably warped to the safe room closest to the treasure. She takes a running start, and starts
climbing the blocky exterior of the building, hopping from ledge to ledge, thanking
Madarame’s cognition for having a much easier climbing surface than sheer castle walls.
Learning her lesson from last time, Sumire doesn’t bother asking the panicking security
shadows for directions, instead choosing to move deeper within the mass of the palace,
hoping that she’ll stumble upon the centre.
Sumire skids to a halt as she sees the thieves hopping down the side of the larger museum
building, stopping in a courtyard in the centre. They all huddle around what Sumire can only
assume is the treasure, opening the wrappings to take a look. That was fast- did they fight
Madarame already? Or did they circumvent the fight entirely?
The question is answered for her as she sneaks a bit closer along the outside of the courtyard,
as Madarame’s shadow appears, flanked by some lesser security shadows, reactivating
several lasers scattered in the space, forcing the thieves to stagger back.
“Madarame!” She hears Fox call, brandishing his sword and pointing it at the shadow, who
simply cackles in response.
Sumire inches closer as they argue back and forth, Madarame revealing what she guesses
must be the real treasure, taunting the thieves for falling for the fake.
Some more shouts, as Sumire ducks behind a nearby ornament, and the fight begins.
Madarame’s shadow bubbles and twists into four paintings, depicting eyes, a nose, and a
mouth, that all twitch and spin as both sides begin their assault.
Much like last time, Sumire is in no rush to interfere. The thieves handled this fight last time,
and they can do it again. It doesn’t stop her from flinching and shifting nervously when
Panther gets doused in black paint, throwing her stumbling to the floor, as the other thieves
desperately try to get her back in the fight.

After Joker throws out a final attack, the paintings fall, and Madarame’s regular form takes its
place. Sumire almost breathes a sigh of relief, before the shadow cackles again and summons
four elemental copies of itself, targeting the thieves’ weaknesses in a round of attacks.
Two can play at that game though, Sumire thinks, as Joker calls out different orders and sets
up a chain of baton passes, alternating the finish between Fox or Skull’s powerful physical
attacks on the main shadow.
Eventually, Madarame staggers to his knees, unable to keep summoning copies of himself.
Sumire watches as Fox marches forward and snatches the treasure from Madarame as his
crumpled form blubbers apologies and begs them not to kill him.
“Swear, that you’ll repent,” Sumire hears Fox growl, and Madarame nods hastily as the
palace around them starts to shake and crumble.
“Wait!” Madarame’s shadow calls as the thieves all rush towards Mona for their escape,
“What about the other one, though?! The one in the black mask!”
The thieves all yelp words of confusion, as Sumire freezes. Her… her own mask is black, so
could he be…?
But, no, she’s never even been in this palace before, let alone met Madarame in the real
world, so who-?
Ah, right. Crow has more helmet than mask, but it certainly can be classified as ‘black’ with
its onyx sheen. So then was Akechi in this palace before? Did he scope it out when Sumire
told him who the thieves’ next target was?
But, wait. The thieves don’t know that. All they know is that someone with a black mask has
been trapsing around the Metaverse without their knowledge- and has encountered Madarame
in the past.
Shoot. She may have waited too long.
Her decision to not join the thieves just yet has been solidified over the past few weeks- from
her conversation with Akechi about her right to not forgive those who have wronged her and
later her striking a proper deal with him, she had no intention to call upon the thieves’
strength until later.
But now, she might not even have that option. When she finally asks for help- who’s to say
that they won’t be suspicious of her? The longer she waits the more this will get worse, but
she can’t just join them now, especially now that she’s found a tentative ally in AkechiSumire is quickly snapped out of her musings as the palace is shaken with the force of an
earthquake, and the ground cracks beneath her. She sprints towards the exit, vaulting over the
crumbling rubble, and gets spat back out into the real world behind the cover of two houses,
out of sight from the thieves.

She clutches her chest as she catches her breath, flinching violently when she hears a voice to
her side.
“I take it you went to witness that fight as well?” Sumire whips around and sees Akechi, not
nearly as dishevelled as she is, leaning against the wall beside her.
“When did you get here?!” She tries not to squeak, but fails as her voice cracks.
“You were the one who told me when the thieves were most likely to infiltrate.” He says
lightly, gesturing to Madarame’s shack behind them, “So I thought I’d take a look.”
“Have you already been to this palace before?” Sumire regathers herself, seeking an answer
to Madarame’s words earlier.
“Is this part of our information exchange?” Akechi asks flatly, and Sumire stutters on a nod,
“In that case: Yes, I have.” He lifts a hand to his chin, seemingly considering his question,
“You said there were five thieves. I did see five members in there, and I could probably
identify them all easily except for one. Who was the… cat? Thing?” Akechi says, not fully
masking his bafflement.
Sumire giggles into her hand, “Yeah, that one tripped me up as well. That’s Morgana, or
Mona in the Metaverse. He only looks like that in the cognitive world, I’m pretty sure. In the
real world, he just looks like an ordinary cat.”
Akechi hums. “Absurd.” He scoffs. He pauses, then shakes his head, “How does he
communicate in reality?”
“I think the trick is if you’ve heard him before in the Metaverse, then you can hear him speak
like a normal person in the real world,” Sumire says uncertainly, “If not, I think you only hear
meows.”
Akechi nods, seemingly considering as he looks into the middle distance, “A change in
cognition, then? How fascinating. And ridiculous.” He adds with a sneer.
Sumire feels her lips hitch up in a teasing grin, “You really hate the idea of a talking cat,
huh?”
Akechi sighs, “It’s more a matter of principal. As whimsical and wonderland-esque as the
Metaverse may seem, it has, up until this point, operated on a series of identifiable rules.
None of which,” he scowls, “Included a talking cat.” He shifts, looking back at the ground,
“You get a question, by the way. I technically asked two.”
Sumire blinks, not having expected him to keep track, “Okay, um,” what to ask? “You were
paranoid, before, about someone messing around with the Metaverse. You said that we were
probably okay, but what about the thieves?”
Akechi stiffens at her question, and Sumire almost takes it back before he clears his throat
and answers, “The thieves were already playing with fire just from the calling card for that

gym teacher. But this?” He points again at Madarame’s shack, “This is sure to attract the
wrong kind of attention.”
Sumire nods, worrying her bottom lip between her teeth, “Is there anything we can do to…
take the heat off?”
Akechi gives her an unimpressed look, “I’m going to give you a pass on that question- what
do you think?”
Sumire sighs, shoulders slumping, “Yeah, probably nothing…”
“Not unless we want to put ourselves in danger, no.” Akechi agrees.
She frowns, thinking back to the last timeline. She was told when she first asked to join the
thieves that it was too dangerous- is this when that danger began? Did they just accidentally
get involved with the wrong people? How much of all this was (and will be) coincidence?
Akechi pushes himself off of the wall, smoothing down the front of his school blazer, “Well,
if that’s all.” He takes out his phone, taking a few steps back, and whispers, “Mementos.”
The world warps where Akechi stands, leaving empty space in his place. Sumire blinks,
having only managed to raise her hand in a half wave of goodbye before he left.
“Oh.” She says dumbly into the empty air. She… never thought to use Mementos as a way to
get around. That could be useful- though using it right now might just annoy Akechi for
following him.
Choosing the less fancy way to travel, Sumire peeks out from behind the corner of the shack,
and ducks back into the street when the coast is clear.

Much like the last timeline, when the school cleanup rolls around on May 30th, Sumire opts
to suck it up and go. She should really take the time she’s been given to practice her new
gymnastics routine -as she’s had to set aside time for thieving-adjacent activities- but she was
once again swayed by the resentful whispers of her classmates, spitting venom at her for
things she can’t control.
Although, Sumire’s dour mood evaporates when she sees that she’s been put in a group with
Haru, along with two other students- one first year and one second year.
Haru hums, surveying the section of Inokashira park that their group has been given to clean
up. “I think we should focus on just collecting the biggest pieces of trash first, and then work
our way down to the smaller things so that we don’t get lost in the weeds.”
Sumire and the rest of the group nods, and they each split off to get started.
The second-year boy picks up a discarded umbrella, and turns to the group excitedly, “While
we’re doing this, did any of you guys hear about the calling card from the Phantom Thieves
that was sent to Madarame? Y’know, that artist?”

Sumire perks up as Haru and the other first year give the boy a questioning look. Actually,

Again, Haru and Mishima speak in unison,
“Like an intern?” Haru asks.

Sumire must spend too long looking like she just got caught, because Mishima’s eyes

The other first year, who has yet to contribute, gives Sumire a mildly impressed look before

Haru giggles, “I didn’t know that the person you were texting all the time was a celebrity,
Sumi-chan.” Mishima whips to look at Haru with an alarmed expression.
“It’s not like I text him all the time,” Sumire protests, because she really doesn’t, “I just don’t

Haru seems to be contemplating something, as she tilts her head, and Sumire takes the

“Well,” Haru seems to snap herself out of it, “Lets get finished up here quickly so we can

Sumire sits down at her desk again after school, opening her notebook that is very slowly
turning into a conspiracy board and staring down at it.
She feels like she’s gained a lot of new information since making a deal with Akechi, but
simultaneously it feels like she’s learned nothing at all.
Starting with the obvious, she marks off that Akechi gained his persona in some
indeterminate time before all of the other thieves did. This was definitely one of the bits of
information she was most worried about finding, so she’s glad that’s out of the way. She also
marks down properly that she was correct about when Yusuke joined the thieves.
Now onto the more concerning information.
Akechi’s… aggressive reaction to Sumire confronting him in Mementos was unexpected at
first -though maybe she should have seen it coming- but what stands out to Sumire most is
why. Akechi mentioned that he knows someone that used to research cognitive psience, and
his reaction suggests that he’s not a fan of the idea of it continuing or being used.
The only person that Sumire knows who researched cognitive psience is Maruki. And
Futaba’s mother, she’s pretty sure someone mentioned, but given that she’s been dead for a
while now, Sumire doubts that’s who Akechi was worried about.
But, during January, Akechi never gave any indication that he had met, or even heard of,
Maruki before the false reality. So that probably rules him out, too.
Shido. Sumire realises with a start. Some of the memories in Maruki’s palace talked about
how it was Shido who cut off Maruki’s research, so the man must have a hand in the field
somewhere.
Is this the missing piece for why Akechi requested the thieves to target Shido? Some
unnamed grievances about cognitive psience? Maybe Akechi figured out in the last timeline
that Shido is responsible for the mental shutdowns and psychotic breakdowns because of the
knowledge that he already has about the cognitive world, and eventually went to the thieves.
Sumire doesn’t actually know how mental shutdowns and psychotic breakdowns are caused;
If Akechi was so shocked about seeing someone else in the Metaverse, then maybe they can
be caused in the real world? Like how Maruki used his power before January?
She also notes down Akechi’s words after Madarame’s palace; that the thieves are ‘asking for
trouble’ by having targeted Madarame. Is it because there’s something special about
Madarame in particular? or is whoever Akechi’s so wary about just on the lookout for any
possible cognitive-psience-related incidents?

Sumire sighs, looking at her negligible amount of new information. She’s got a whole lot of
theories and not a lot of facts, and with how adamant Akechi has been about sticking to the
terms of their deal, she doubts that he’d be willing to spill without Sumire offering some kind
of equal exchange. Which she doesn’t really have. She doesn’t even know who the thieves’
next target is.
Sumire half-heartedly searches up some of the key players on her phone- nothing about Shido
other than a suspiciously spotless political history, Maruki doesn’t have a wiki page, and
there’s next to nothing about Akechi’s life before he came into the public eye.
Except- oh. Hold on. Sumire checks the date and blinks. Akechi’s birthday is listed as June
2nd online. Which is tomorrow.
Sumire makes an impulsive decision, and quickly opens her messages to Akechi.
Sumi☆: hello Akechi-san!
Sumi☆: I heard about a darts place in Kichijoji, do you want to come check it out with me
tomorrow?
She stares at her phone waiting for a response. She knows that Akechi enjoys Penguin
Sniper- he said as much in January when the whole group went to play billiards. Sumire can
count the number of things Akechi has admitted to genuinely liking on one hand, so she
knows he really means this one.
Hopefully, the choice of venue will convince him to hang out with her. It’s his birthday, she
wants to do something nice.
She watches as three little dots appear as Akechi types something.
Akechi: May I ask why?
Sumire frowns. Not unexpected, really. It just means that she’ll have to break out the charm.
Oh?
She has plenty of charm.
Sumi☆: you seem like the kind of person who likes darts, is all!
Sumi☆: we could also exchange some more information as we play?
She adds the second text on as an afterthought, hoping that maybe it will entice him
somehow.
Three dots appear again.
Akechi: What time?

Sumire pumps her fist in the air and spins around on her chair, hurriedly typing out a
response.
Sumi☆: meet at 5?
Sumi☆: the place is called penguin sniper.
Akechi: I’m aware. I suppose that I’ll see you there, Yoshizawa-san.
Sumire smiles at the response. Even if it is a slightly frosty acceptance, it is an acceptance,
nonetheless.
She should look up some dessert places in the area, too. It wouldn’t be a good birthday
celebration without cake.

Akechi has his suspicions about why Yoshizawa texted him yesterday -none of which are
particularly favourable- but he decided to humour her, nevertheless.
He isn’t quite sure why he bothered, looking back on it, as he walks up the steps to Penguin
Sniper. He could have very easily brushed her off claiming a prior engagement, but
something possessed him to agree.
He passes through the door, and immediately sees a head of red hair standing by one of the
dart boards on the far side of the room, playing a solo game as she waits.
Akechi walks up behind her, not making his presence immediately known. He watches as she
throws one of the darts, landing on the seventeen. She looks proud at this, and Akechi stifles
a sigh.
“May I ask the real reasoning as to why you invited me here?” Akechi finally speaks up.
Yoshizawa jumps, and whirls around to look at him, “Oh! When did you get here?”
“Just now,” Akechi lies smoothly, leaning against a nearby pillar. “I hope you weren’t waiting
long?”
“Oh, I came early on purpose.” She admits, “Because, um…”
Akechi holds no strong feelings either way as to why she would waste her time, other than
for how it baffles him. “Are you going to answer my first question?” He interrupts her.
She starts, “Oh, well,” she twists some of her hair in her fingers, “It’s your birthday?”
Akechi lets out a weary sigh as his suspicions are confirmed, “Why?” he says bluntly.
“Why…?” Yoshizawa pauses, her eyes widening as she catches on to what he’s asking, “Why
wouldn’t I?”

“Because there’s no reason to?” Akechi raises an eyebrow. “Our deal is already solidified;
you don’t need to try and win me over.”
Yoshizawa looks confused, “Well, if we’re friends, I thought…” she trails off, face flushing.
Akechi sighs again, not bothering to correct her assumption, and resets the darts board, “I’m
already here, so we might as well play. Can you play 701?”
Yoshizawa starts, looking alarmed, “Well, maybe, but-”
“Great.” Akechi sets up the game for 701, “Competitive or team game?”
Yoshizawa looks a little lost as Akechi continues to barrel through the conversation, “Um,
team?”
“Shall I start?” He holds up one of the darts, and she nods mutely.
Akechi takes his first turn, successfully throwing three bullseyes. He wasn’t too concerned,
but he hasn’t played in a while, so he played a little more carefully than he would have
normally. He recollects the darts, and turns to see Yoshizawa holding her hand out in a highfive as he goes to pass the darts to her.
He stares at her flatly, but at her enthusiastic nodding he eventually relents and claps their
hands together. She collects the darts with some light cheer and goes to take her turn.
Akechi can tell that Yoshizawa is also shooting for bullseyes, but she only barely manages to
land one, with her other two shots going wide and landing on unfortunately small numbers.
She collects her shots and turns to Akechi for another high-five.
“You aren’t very good at darts.” Akechi comments flatly instead, leaving her hanging.
She deflates, and huffs, “I was trying to tell you that before. But you insisted we play 701, so
I tried my best.”
Akechi tilts his head, narrowing his eyes, “Why did you suggest we go out for darts in that
case?”
“Well, you like it, right?” She says earnestly, “And it’s your birthday, so it’s only fair we do
something you like.”
Akechi would be lying if he said that Yoshizawa doesn’t confuse him in every conceivable
way. Her insistence on their supposed friendship is one thing, trying to actively upkeep it is
another.
There’s also the manner of how she seems completely unperturbed by everything about him.
There were no questions as to what he’s doing in the Metaverse, and barring when he held a
sword to her throat, she’s completely unbothered that Akechi has forgone the mask of
politeness around her.
If anything, she seems to almost prefer it. An absurd thought that Akechi discards.

Akechi is aware that many people place stock in birthdays, though he is not one of them. He
supposes being a year older isn’t bad, but he’s given no indication to Yoshizawa that this is
something he cares to celebrate.
So why is she going out of her way for this?
Akechi supposes that, theoretically, Yoshizawa could just be like this. A generous person,
whatever that means. It doesn’t stop him from waiting for the other shoe to drop.
The Magician arcana hums. Akechi sighs.
“Your posture is wrong,” he says, and Yoshizawa looks confused, “When you’re throwing the
darts,” he clarifies, “You need to keep both your arm and feet in line with your shoulders.”
He picks up a dart to demonstrate.
Yoshizawa blinks, and quickly picks up a dart to copy his posture. Akechi motions for her to
stand in front of the dartboard to take a shot, and she obliges. She doesn’t hit the bullseye, but
she does get a lot closer than her previous shots.
“Better,” He tells her, and she lights up.
“Thank you, Akechi-san,” she says, smiling. He gives a short nod in response.
They continue their game, resetting the board now that the turn order has been thrown off by
Yoshizawa’s practice shot. They aren’t on track to win, but they are getting closer than
Akechi thought they might.
Yoshizawa looks contemplative, “I think that I wanted to celebrate your birthday because I
thought that you wouldn’t celebrate it otherwise.” She eventually says, and Akechi turns to
look at her, “And I always enjoyed celebrating my birthday with my sister, so I thought you
might enjoy it too if you spent it with someone.”
Akechi doesn’t say anything to that, but she doesn’t seem to mind, simply turning back to the
dartboard to take another shot.
(If she knew what you are, she would hate you)
He knows. And he hates that she could find out so easily, but won’t. Because she’s too kind,
too trusting, not shrewd enough to see the wolf in sheep’s clothing even after he’s already
bared his fangs.
He can’t let himself get too close, but Yoshizawa seems more than content to close the
distance for the both of them, and there’s nothing he can do about it.
He doesn’t want this; he insists to the void of his mind. His personas don’t respond.
The Magician arcana grows to its second rank.
***

When Akechi leaves Penguin Sniper later that evening, with Yoshizawa on his tail, insisting
that they go to get cake, he nearly stumbles as a migraine builds behind his eyes.
It doesn’t feel like the normal ones, thoughIt’s a quiet afternoon. Yet, he still feels a sense of dread. Twelve days. Twelve days until this
farce comes to an end, and the tentative bond he’s built (Which one? Isn’t there-) will be
severed.
He’s happy. He thinks.
He can’t help but feel unsatisfied.
He asks the other a question, deadly serious, despite knowing he won’t get a serious answer.
He just wants to know, to confirm in complete certainty, that there’s no way for the two of
them to be, other than on the opposite sides of a war that only one of them is fighting.
He’s surprised. The other doesn’t brush the question off, but gives a dodgy answer,
nonetheless. The other spouts some pretty sentiment about how they’re rivals, first and
foremost.
That’s all the confirmation he needs. Rivals is practically synonymous with enemies, and
that’s what they will be.
But, Akechi thinks, the other never actually said that.
It’s almost as if he really thinksAkechi shakes out of it.
Patterns upon patterns, and he’s not sure he likes any of them. Cryptic visions combined with
headaches least of all.
“Are you alright, Akechi-san?” Yoshizawa turns and asks, concern painting her face.
“Just fine,” he responds, and he doesn’t know if it’s a lie, turning to continue down the road.

Ren doesn’t quite realise he’s dreaming at first.
Ren turns to the other boy there, clad in black and face almost completely obscured.
“Well?” The boy says, “I presume you had a reason for dragging me to Mementos.”
“Yeah,” Ren agrees, starting to walk into the subway tunnel, “You wouldn’t have agreed to
hang out with me otherwise.”
The other scoffs, “Seriously? And here I thought you actually had something important to
do.” Ren can’t see it, but he’s pretty sure the boy just rolled his eyes, “What are you planning,
then?”
Ren thinks about the glove in his pocket, and ignores the hole it burns, “We’re going to have
a competition,” He twirls his gun in his hand, “We’re going to see who can destroy the most
shadows in this area of Mementos.”
The other sighs, “If you were looking for competition, why not just ask for a game of
billiards? I still haven’t played against you with my left hand.”
“I already tried that,” Ren says, annoyed, “And you brushed me off.”
The boy hums, unrepentant, “I suppose I did. Then, in that case, why didn’t you get the hint?”
Ren turns and grins at him, “Well, I could take a hint, or I could get more creative,” he
gestures to the tunnels, “And I would say it paid off, since you’re here.”
The other sneers, but stays quiet as he stalks off further down the tunnels. Ren smiles as he
passes, proud at having outplayed him.
“You realise that none of the shadows in this area will pose much of a challenge, right,
Joker?” The other eventually speaks up, and Ren smirks.

“Exactly,” he says, and he watches as the boy pauses, allowing a manic grin to slowly crawl
onto his face.
The other lets out a low cackle, “Well then, you’d better keep up.”
Ren snaps out of the (memory? Vision? Dream?) and promptly realises that he still hasn’t
woken up.
He can see the other figure turn and look at him, “Oh. You still don’t remember.”
Ren’s dreamed about this before, hasn’t he?
As though he can hear Ren’s thoughts, the other smirks, “Do you just forget about all of this
whenever you wake up? No wonder you’ve made no progress.”
“You could help.” Ren points out, shoving his hands into his pockets. There was a glove
there, in the dream, but he can’t feel it now.
“I could,” the other says, and then he turns to keep walking.
Ren jogs to catch up, “That just now,” he gestures vaguely around them, “Was that what I’m
forgetting?”
“In part.” The other says, not turning back around.
“So did we know each other?”
The other stops walking, and finally turns around, “You assume that this is taking place in

Ren sits in class, ignoring Ushimaru’s lecture and nervously tapping his pen against one of
the pages of his probation diary.
After they fought Madarame, Ren has been cooking up theories about who the black-masked
persona user the shadow mentioned could possibly be, and has come up with nothing. In all
likelihood, they’ve never met. Tokyo is a big place, and Madarame has interacted with
countless people in his day-to-day life. And even then, there’s no guarantee that whoever the
Black Mask is has actually met the artist in the real world- they could have just interacted
with his shadow exclusively.
Ren also isn’t sure what to think about the possibility of another person with access to the
Metaverse. He got the Nav seemingly randomly, so could it be that there are other
unfortunate people who got thrown into the Metaverse by pure chance?
Ren scribbles down some notes on the page, frowning at some gibberish he must have written
a few weeks earlier. Had he been trying to remember a dream? He can’t make any sense of
the notes, so it mustn’t have been that important.
Or, was-?
He thinksRen loses his train of thought.
Sitting up as his classmates shuffle to make their way home as their final class wraps up, Ren
throws his diary back in his bag, as Morgana settles back in over the top of all his belongings,
and he checks his phone to see if he has any texts from his confidants.
Exiting the school’s gates, Ren stifles a yelp as he bumps into someone in the Shujin
tracksuit, causing them to drop what they’re holding.
“Oh! I’m sorry!” A girl’s voice says, and Ren pulls himself back together.
“No, sorry, that was my fault,” he says to the girl with fluffy pink hair, moving to pick up the
bag of soil that she dropped.
She takes the bag back into her arms, “Thank you so much,” she says with a small smile, “I
usually don’t move these by hand, but since there weren’t that many, I thought I’d save the
time.” She shuffles on her feet, “I’m Haru, by the way, a third year. What’s your name?”

“Oh,” Ren blinks at the lack of a family name given, “I’m Ren.” He decides to return the
sentiment. Maybe she’s just friendly?
“It’s nice to meet you, Ren-kun.” Haru says brightly, though Ren thinks that she seems
almost tentative.
“Likewise,” he offers a smile in turn, “Do you need any help with the rest of those?” He

“That would be lovely, thank you!” She says, and points to a small pile of them a short
