Ren nods, and spends some time with Haru, moving various gardening supplies to different
places, grateful for the muscle that his Metaverse excursions has given him.
Eventually, Haru wipes her brow and huffs, “All done!” She turns to Ren, “Thank you so
much for helping me, usually I get Sumi-chan to help me out with this, but she was busy
today.”
Ren cocks his head at the name, “Sumi?”
“Oh, right,” Haru laughs, “Sumire Yoshizawa, the first-year gymnast. She’s an unofficial
member of the gardening club.”
Yoshizawa, huh? “I’ve heard of her,” Ren admits, and tugs on his fringe, “I don’t think she
likes me much, though.” He admits.
Haru blinks, “Really?” She laughs a little, “You must have really done something for that to
happen.”

Haru pauses, “Rumours?” She jumps, “Oh! You’re the transfer student everyone’s been
talking about.”
Ren grimaces a little harder, “In the flesh.”
She laughs into her hand, “You don’t need to sound so nervous; I don’t believe any of the
rumours or anything,” Ren relaxes and smiles a bit, “But I wonder why Sumi-chan doesn’t
seem to like you then? She isn’t the type to care about that kind of thing,” Haru trails off, lost

today. If you ever want to help out again, I spend most of my time around the gardens.”

Ren nods affirmatively, “I’ll keep an eye out.” He says, as he turns to finally leave the school.
He feels like Haru is someone he might be able to form a bond with, having felt the pull of a
possible arcana during their conversation, as Morgana mumbles “Gardening, huh?” to his

Ren senses his bundle of arcana thrum warmly in his chest, and pauses when he feels an extra
one sitting in their midst. Is it a precursor to his bond with Haru? He didn’t realise he was
that close to forging one- this feels like a full-on bond.
He tries to sense what arcana it is, and comes up empty. He also doesn’t hear the whisper of
who it belongs to like he does with his other confidants.
Ren frowns to himself, and brushes it off. It’s probably nothing. Nothing important, at least.

When Akechi sees Madarame’s confession live on June fifth, his first thought is Fuck, I have
to do something about this, followed by the realisation of the sheer amount of myriad
different ways he has to ‘do something’ to appease the various demanding authority figures
in his life.
Starting, it seems, with Sae Niijima, who is furiously pacing and collecting papers from every

Akechi has also been assigned properly to the case, a fact of which he was warned of via
Shido’s vague threats. He’s very glad that his deal with Yoshizawa prepared him for this
development with Madarame, otherwise he might have snapped.

make him the subject of her ire.

“That’s alright,” Akechi finally speaks up, “I don’t need anything.”

stiff.

He can feel the Moon arcana grow to its second rank.

“The Star means inspiration and hope, mostly.” José says matter-of-factly, “The arcana your

“Oh, nothing just yet. Just talking with you has already been plenty interesting. Although,”

Akechi nods and stands out of the way of the reactivated car.
José speeds off, drifting around a corner as he sends the surrounding shadows fleeing. Akechi
stares for a minute, lost in thought.
The Velvet Room insisted that bonds are not something he should be dabbling in. Akechi
already resolved to ignore that out of spite, but having another claim that bonds are in fact a
necessary component to his existence gives him pause.
He doesn’t enjoy the claim that he was ‘doing it wrong’, or whatever José said, though. He
doesn’t need these bonds. They’ve yet to give him anything other than a headache. He’s
survived the past few years without them just fine.
But, even though they’ve yet to present any benefit, they also haven’t hurt yet, either. Akechi
remains unopposed to the idea of seeing where this leads.
Hm. He should write down a list of questions to ask José, for their next meeting.

“So, um,” She says to Akechi, who is sitting eerily still on the bench opposite from her.
“Explain.” He says, words clipped, “What you are talking about.”
Explain. She can do that.
Right?
She’ll start with the overview.
“Okay, so,” Sumire huffs, “The reason that my awakening story had a bunch of holes in it is
because I actually awakened in October. Last year. Well.” She wrings her hands together,
“This year, but before time looped.”
Akechi takes a long breath, the picture of calm, “And then?”
“Well, I didn’t really interact with the Metaverse again until January of next year,” Sumire
continues, glad that he’s saving his disbelief for after she finishes, “Basically, there was this
whole thing where uh- do you know my school counsellor? Takuto Maruki?” He gives her a
flat look that says ‘no’, “Uh, well, anyway, he used to research cognitive psience, and he
became a persona user at one point. But not fully until Christmas Eve of this year.”
Akechi gives her yet another look, and she shrugs, “I don’t really get it either, but, basically,
he also got the power of a god,” she blanches slightly as Akechi pushes up his visor to scrape
his hands down his face, “I’ll, uh, loop back around to that one- but he became a god, and he
was obsessed with using his unique persona power of actualisation to force everyone into a
perfect reality. And,” she sighs, “We couldn’t stop him in time.”
Akechi looks up, “We?”
Sumire nods, trying to smile, “You and I joined the Phantom Thieves to try and take Maruki
down.”
Akechi’s face is still carefully neutral, “I see. And how is it that we failed? Why did only you
get sent back in time?”
Sumire bites her lip. This is definitely what she was hoping to avoid. It was only a
hypothetical before, but now she actually has a stake in Ren and Akechi’s friendship.
She doesn’t even know why Ren did what he did yet, so…

She can leave telling him until after she figures it out. And until Akechi knows Ren enough
to have his own opinion.
“We ran out of time.” Sumire says, voice carefully level, “There was a deadline, and we
didn’t make it.” Akechi nods for her to continue, “And as for why I’m the one who got sent
back? I… have no idea.” She shrugs helplessly, “What happened gets kind of blurry. But, I
was alone at the time. I know all the other thieves were in one place together, and I’m not
sure where you were.”
Akechi nods, “Alright. A perfectly believable story.” He cocks his head, “Anything to prove
it?”
Sumire breathes harshly through her nose, pressing her lips together, “José could tell that
time had looped. You can ask him?”
Akechi nods again, poker face still going strong, “I will do that.” He brings a hand to his
chin, “How about you tell me something else? Who is going to be the thieves next target? It
isn’t immediate proof, per say, but it will become evidence in your favour later on.”
Sumire laughs nervously, “Well, I can’t actually remember his name, is the thing.”
“Of course.” Akechi deadpans.
“But I remember that he was a mafia boss!” Sumire says quickly, “And I can tell you all the
other targets, too.”
“Well, ‘mafia boss’ narrows it down.” Akechi says sarcastically, which Sumire thinks is a bit
unfair, “Go on, then. Predict the future.”
“Well, after the mafia guy, I don’t actually know if the thieves took anyone down in the
cognitive world, because they went after Medjed.” Sumire tugs on her ponytail.
Akechi hums, “An anonymous hacker group. How did they deal with that one?”
“One of the future thieves is an amazing hacker.” Sumire smiles slightly, “She hasn’t joined
yet, but she will by August, I think.”
“I see.” Akechi waves his hand, “Who’s next, then?”
“Kunikazu Okumura.” Sumire says confidently, “But, um, something went wrong with him.
He ended up having a mental shutdown after he was sent a calling card. But it wasn’t the
thieves’ fault!” She hastily adds.
Akechi lets out a small huff of breath, face still. “Well, that’s something to look out for, then.
Who was next?”
“Sae Niijima,” Sumire says, and Akechi’s calm drops for open surprise, “I think that the
thieves were trying to avoid being arrested, since they were framed for what happened to
Okumura.”

Akechi folds his arms and looks into the middle distance. “She doesn’t even have a palace
though, so…” He mumbles to himself. After a moment, he bites his lip, as though he’s
realised something.
“Her palace was a casino,” Sumire says quietly, “I managed to see that one.”
Akechi nods, considering, “That isn’t entirely surprising.” He says with an unreadable tone.
Sumire frowns, but moves on, “Um, after her was Masayoshi Shido-”
She’s cut off as Akechi coughs suddenly, going very still and face painted with alarm.
“Seriously?” He hisses, and Sumire nods awkwardly.
“He confessed to being the one behind the mental shutdowns and psychotic breakdowns,”
She says, and Akechi’s face goes blank again, “And I remember you mentioning that you had
asked the thieves to target him? But I’m not really sure what happened, since I wasn’t
properly involved until Maruki came into the picture.”
Akechi nods, face unreadable, and Sumire shifts uncomfortably.
“Was, um, Shido the person who you were afraid of researching cognitive psience?” She says
tentatively after a beat, “I know he had something to do with it, since he shut down Maruki’s
research a few years ago, so…”
Akechi’s head snaps up, like he had been in thought, and he gives a jerky nod.
“There’s no point in keeping it from you since you already know,” he says smoothly, “But,
yes, I was concerned about Shido’s involvement in the cognitive world.”
Sumire wrings her hands in her lap, “Did you already know he was behind the shutdowns and
breakdowns?” She asks with genuine curiosity.
He gives her a searching look, before nodding slowly, “Yes,” He says, “I did.”
Sumire nods. There’s probably a reason Akechi has been unable to deal with Shido in both
the real and cognitive worlds, she thinks. Shido is a powerful politician in reality, so that’s
definitely an ordeal to take him down there. And in the cognitive world, it’s quite the ask for
one person to take on a palace alone.
And, Sumire thinks with dawning understanding, Akechi doesn’t know how to change hearts.
“Well,” Akechi says suddenly, startling Sumire out of her thoughts, “I think that’s enough for
today.” He gives her a sharp look, “But this discussion isn’t over.”
Sumire nods nervously, “Okay.” She worries her lips together, “Do… do you believe me?”
She asks quietly.
Akechi looks her up and down, “I can’t say that I’m fully convinced just yet,” he says slowly,
“But you do have a lot of information that would have been extremely hard to obtain with

events as they are now. And I’ll speak to José, as you suggested.” He finishes, and Sumire
breathes a sigh of relief and finally lets a warm smile break out on her face.
“Thank you, Akechi-san.” She says, and Akechi turns away.

Akechi and Ren rank up some confidants.

Chapter Notes

Akechi doesn’t want to admit that Yoshizawa has thoroughly thrown him for a loop, but she
definitely has.
The worst thing is that she’s probably telling the truth.
The information that she was able to provide goes beyond just educated guesses, and the fact
that she still doesn’t know what Akechi does means that she likely doesn’t actually have
intimate knowledge of the conspiracy, which would have been Akechi’s first explanation as
to why she has all this information.
But, alas. Time travel.
Medjed, Okumura, Sae, Shido, and Maruki. All the names that Yoshizawa was able to
provide are… concerning to say the least.
Medjed, because the only way for the thieves to take them down would be for them to have a
highly competent hacker on their team, as Yoshizawa already confirmed.
Okumura, because he died by mental shutdown before he could have a change of heart.
Akechi knows what his job is, and has no delusions as to who was (and likely will be)
responsible for the man’s death. If Shido is willing to assassinate one of his biggest
customers, then he’s either very paranoid or overly confident. Neither spell good things.
Sae, because much to Akechi’s chagrin, he has a modicum of fondness for the one coworker
he can tolerate. She doesn’t deserve to be in the firing line of the conspiracy, nor does she
deserve to have her heart ripped out and made hollow like the thieves’ other targets.
He also wants to see what the Moon arcana can do for him, and if Sae is indisposed that
might be a problem.
Maruki, because the implication of becoming a god is horrifying, and the further information
that he was (is?) obsessed with ‘making everyone happy’ in some ideal reality makes Akechi
want to claw his skin off. He actually believes Yoshizawa when she says that Akechi
willingly worked with the thieves to take the counsellor down, just out of necessity to avoid
whatever fresh hell would be the alternative.

What he doesn’t believe, however, is that he would ask the thieves to target Shido instead of
destroying the man himself.
The past three years (longer, if he’s being serious) Akechi has been devoted to the sole
purpose of making Masayoshi Shido acknowledge exactly what he deserves, to be subject to
all the suffering that he subjected Akechi’s mother to. He wants the man to break beneath his
heel, for him to watch as his delicate tower of hubris crumbles in his hands, to be the small
leak that sinks a great ship.
And Akechi wants Shido to know exactly who his downfall was orchestrated by.
In his head, that’s all Akechi is. A goal. There is no after, no alternative in his head, because
in his mind there is nothing else he could possibly want to live for other than making sure
Shido gets what’s coming to him.
(He feels Robin and Loki shift in an unidentifiable emotion)
So the idea that he would pass such a goal on to someone else, especially the thieves, of all
people, is something he cannot allow to pass.
Maybe he failed, last timeline. Maybe there was some unforeseen obstruction that undid
years of work that forced Akechi to move the goalposts.
Well, not this time. He’s still in the game, and he intends to win.
Beyond that, though, Akechi thinks as he slips into Mementos, is the issue of why Yoshizawa
was sent back in time.
Apparently they all failed to fight Maruki. ‘Ran out of time’, she said.
Akechi thinks about Amamiya, his steel will and unmovable sense of justice. He’s only
properly met the boy once and Akechi already knows that he wouldn’t go down without a
fight.
So it’s somewhat satisfying to hear that he went down anyway. Justice only got him so far,
and reality had crumbled around him before Yoshizawa got sent back to clean up his mess.
Akechi steps out into the subway tunnels, and sighs. He came down here to speak to José, but
he really doesn’t want to wander around for a few hours trying to track him down.
Akechi calls Robin to the front of his mind, who hums cheerfully, and sends out a widespread
scan of the area. He gets back the information of shadow locations, strength, and the
occasional weakness, but nothing on the kid.
Akechi frowns. José isn’t anywhere near him, then.
Although, could it be possible that he doesn’t actually have to go looking for him? If José can
sense the arcana that Akechi has, then…

Akechi closes his eyes, and focuses on the Star arcana. He can feel it resonate warmly in his
chest, whispering a small ‘rank one’ in the base of his mind.
Sure enough, Akechi hears the rumbling of a car in the distance.
“Hey, mister!” José waves from the driver’s seat, “You were calling, right?” he laughs, “It
kinda tickled.”
“Apologies,” Akechi says reflexively, and also because having a metaphysical bond give off
a physical sensation sounds unpleasant.
“It’s fine,” José says, blinking, “It’s sort of like… hm. Remembering that you exist? And how
that’s nice? That’s how it felt.” He nods confidently.
“Sure,” Akechi says, itching to get to the point, “A question, do you know Yoshizawa? The
girl with the black mask and red hair?” He adds when he realises that José seems averse to
calling people by their names.
“Hmm.” José scrunches his face, “Oh! Yes, that lady. She was very strange.”
“Why so?” Akechi says, moving closer to the car.
José hops out of the driver’s seat in the space next to Akechi, “Well, I’m not sure if I can tell
you…”
“Has time looped?” Akechi interrupts, wanting to skip the dilemma on confidentiality.
José’s eyes widen, “Oh, do you remember too?” He frowns, “But, I can’t see…”
“I don’t remember.” Akechi says flatly, “Yoshizawa informed me that she travelled through
time after a world-ending event sometime next year. Is this true?”
José nods far too cheerfully for someone confirming the end of the world, “Yup! She’s so
strange because it’s usually wildcards like you or the other mister that person chooses for this
kind of stuff, so something must have happened for him to choose her.”
So Yoshizawa is an anomaly, then. And Akechi would bet a fair amount that the ‘other
mister’, is Amamiya. Akechi saw the thief swap through at least six different personas in
Madarame’s palace, so he definitely fits the bill of ‘wildcard.’
Hm.
Yoshizawa said she was alone when time looped. So she wouldn’t know if something had
happened to him or Amamiya, who are apparently the two preferred candidates for such time
travel situations as these.
The implication that there are procedures for this is worrying. How often does reality need to
be reset?

“Hey, mister,” José interrupts Akechi’s thoughts, “You want to further our deal, right? Since I
told you something, can you tell me something about humans?”
Akechi nods slowly, “Of course. What do you want to know?”
José scratches his head, and hums, “How about… Oh! Why is it that you act differently
towards me than you do the other things in this place? You really hate the shadows here.”
Akechi schools his expression to not seem so taken aback. He didn’t expect a personal
question- though he supposes it’s fair game since he’s human himself.
He probably should have made the terms of their deal more specific.
“Because we have a deal, and I do not wish to harm our future endeavours.” Akechi
eventually settles on, satisfied at it being completely accurate and impersonal.
José looks thoughtful, “So humans act differently towards people that they want something
from?”
“Yes.” Akechi says, and leaves it at that.
“Oh.” José says, face scrunching again. “Is that why you don’t like humans, mister?”
Whatever third eye bullshit this kid has is very annoying, “What gives you that impression?”
Akechi says anyway, just to be coy.
“Well, some of the shadows that you’ve killed down here belong to people, and that hurts
them.” José states matter-of-factly, “Did you know?”
“I do.” Akechi says blankly.
“Oh.” José frowns, “That’s why I think you don’t like humans, then. Why do you like hurting
them, though?”
Akechi scoffs, his unaffected demeanour cracking, “It’s not like I do it for fun.”
José looks more confused, “Then why do you do it?”
Akechi sighs, “Sometimes, humans do things they don’t want to do because it gets them
closer to something they do want to do.”
“Oh, okay, I think I understand,” José says, not at all looking like he understands, “That’s all
I wanted to ask for now. Do you need anything else?”
“No, that’s all.” Akechi says pleasantly, trying to patch up the crack in his mask.
José doesn’t seem to care, though, as he cheerfully hops back in his car.
Akechi feels the Star arcana grow to rank two.

“Oh!” José grins, “I wasn’t sure if that would happen yet, but I guess we talked enough?” He
gives a wave, “I’ll see you later, mister! If you need to talk to me, you can just do what you
did earlier to call me.” With that, he peels off before Akechi can respond.
Akechi leans against the wall, and flips up his visor to pinch the bridge of his nose. Are all
arcana rank ups going to be this exhausting? Between Yoshizawa and José, he thinks that
they certainly are.
Time travel is real, and he has some kid questioning his motivations for why he does what he
does. What a day.

When Sumire gets a text from Akechi two days after she admitted to time travel, saying that
he’s confirmed her claims, she has to stop herself from jumping with excitement.
She has someone who knows. And believes her. She doesn’t have to tiptoe around the issue
anymore.
An excellent development. Ella hums in the back of her mind.
This is amazing, Sumire thinks. Even though Akechi is an all-around secretive and cagey
person, she doesn’t think she could have asked for someone better to be her friend in all this.
And he believes her.
Sumire thinks that she probably isn’t going to get over this for at least a few days.
She checks her phone again, and sees that she has another text from Akechi, requesting she
look into who the thieves’ next target may be. That shouldn’t be too difficult- if all else fails
she can just tail them again.
Sumire smiles. She had been giddy when she managed to corner Akechi in Mementos, and
now that she doesn’t have to lie to him, she feels even better. Maybe he’ll even stop
pretending that they’re only working together because they made a deal.
And also because Sumire doesn’t really have any more information to give. She kind of
already dropped the biggest bomb she has.
Except, she thinks with a twinge, the exact truth behind why they failed to stop Maruki.
She’ll hold onto that one until she figures it out. And maybe until she manages to get over her
issue with Ren.
She bites her lip, and stops thinking about that.
She wonders if Akechi is going to be more forthcoming about what he knows from here on
out. The optimistic part of her hopes that he’ll sit down and explain to her everything that he
knows, outlining everything to do with cognitive psience and the key to how they can fix
everything that went wrong last timeline.

The realistic part of her reminds her that he’s probably only going to tell her things as they
become immediately important. She remembers how Akechi would clam up in January
whenever she asked anything a little too personal, only to be dismissed with a frosty ‘none of
your business.’
So, yeah. She’s probably not going to get anything too big out of him just yet.
But, they weren’t that close in January. So, maybe, if she becomes closer friends with him
and proves he can trust her, then he’ll open up.
Sumire sighs to herself.
From what she knows about Akechi, that’s going to take a lot of work.
But, what kind of friend would she be if she doesn’t even try?

Akechi isn’t sure what he’s doing, exactly, killing time outside of Penguin Sniper.
Are you at least going to play a game?
STOP WASTING TIME. GO DO SOMETHING INTERESTING.
Akechi supresses an eyeroll, knowing that his personas will get the message anyway. They

Akechi hums, “I’m afraid I wasn’t doing anything particularly interesting.”

SAE STILL HASN’T.

right? But you played that game with your right hand.” He looks Akechi in the eye, a

And, well, that’s what he was looking for, no? Akechi smooths his wide smirk into a pleasant
little quirk of the lips, and hums.
Maybe Amamiya deserves more credit than Akechi was initially willing to give him.
***
Ren doesn’t understand what Akechi wants from him, which is a first for any of his
confidants.
For all the smoke and mirrors that the detective seems to throw to obstruct his own
intentions, he’s remarkably apt at seeing through them to get Ren to talk.
Seriously, Ren doesn’t think he’s spoken this much in one conversation in a damn while.
It’s satisfying, Ren thinks, facing someone who uses all the same tricks he does. If Ren didn’t
know any better, he’d think Akechi was trying to rank up a confidant of his own.
This would all be far nicer, of course, if Akechi were not the detective investigating the
Phantom Thieves. Ren doesn’t care, personally, but if he has to hear Morgana bitch about
how dangerous talking to the detective is one more time, he might lose it.
That’s nothing to say on how much Ryuji has been grouching since the TV station. Ann and
Yusuke have been a bit more laid back, but they still seem put off by Akechi’s comments.

Ren hates to admit that he thinks Akechi might have a point. For someone that doesn’t know
about the Metaverse, the concern about the thieves’ intentions seems warranted.
That makes Ren want to prove him wrong even more.
Ren knows that it’s probably a bad idea to get close to the person who’s investigating him,
but, what was the saying? Know thy enemy? Something like that.
For some reason, something in Ren twitches at calling Akechi an enemy.
The detective has finished clearing up the billiards table, and gestures towards the exit.
“Hey,” Ren says as they start to leave, “When we do this again, don’t hold back.”
Akechi gives him a look over his shoulder, and a breathy chuckle escapes his lips. Ren
frowns at the dismissal.
“How about this?” Akechi says as the two walk down the steps, startling Ren, “If you can
beat me while I’m using my right hand, I’ll face you with everything I have.”
Ren blinks, then breaks out in a grin, “It’s a deal.”
Akechi smiles back, revealing nothing, and they both go to leave the billiards hall, and Ren
can feel the Justice arcana rank up.
As he lets Morgana hop back in the bag once he finds the not-cat still sulking in an alleyway,
heRen isn’t shocked that there’s a gun pointed at his chest, he’s just shocked that it’s happening
now, rather than a few days later.
His feigned surprise morphs into genuine curiosity as the other keeps talking, and Ren feels a
buzz under his skin that he always feels when talking to the other.
Now he’s interested-Has a vision, apparently.
At least they aren’t giving him migraines, anymore. And they only did that once, he reminds
the nagging voice in his head.
He still shakes his head a bit, trying to clear the smoke.
“Hey, are you alright?” Morgana chirps, “Did you have fun with Akechi?”
Ren waves his hand, “I’m fine. And yeah, Akechi was great.”
Morgana gives him a disbelieving look, “Really?”
Ren sighs and places a hand on his chest, “When will my closest friends ever believe me
when I tell them something?”

Morgana looks a bit guilty at that, “I just don’t get why you want to hang out with him, s’all.”
“You haven’t met him properly,” Ren reassures him, “He’s pretty interesting when you give
him a chance.”
“’Interesting’ is a pretty weird description of someone you’re supposed to like hanging out
with,” Morgana points out. “And you’ve only met him a few times.”
“I’ll just have to get to know him better, then.” Ren says with a smile, and Morgana yelps at
having been played.
Either way, now that Ren has a confidant with Akechi, there’s nothing that’s going to stop
him from getting closer to the detective. Ren will get stronger the more he speaks with him,
after all.
I’m sure that’s the only reason. Arsène chimes in with no small amount of sarcasm.
Ren pouts. Can’t one person be on his side for this?
***
That one person, Ren thinks a few days later, is not Mishima.
Well, he didn’t expect it to be, but it’s still kind of weird listening to one friend bash another
friend.
…Is he friends with Akechi? Ren feels like if he asks, he’ll just get brushed off with some
pretty laugh and not get an answer.
Ren comes back to earth as Mishima finishes his rant, “And, I mean, just the nerve of him!
What does he know?”
Ren shrugs, not particularly wanting to get in the way. Mishima’s just passionate, he thinks.
Maybe a little too passionate, but he can’t fault the guy for being thankful when he doesn’t
have to suffer Kamoshida’s abuse anymore since the thieves made him confess.
Ren wishes he knew how to put into words that Mishima doesn’t owe him anything, though.
“Everyone says he’s such an ace detective, but they’ll be singing a different tune once the
Phantom Thieves prove their justice…” Mishima grumbles, and Ren winces at the reminder
of the deadline the thieves are on right now.
Makoto’s really giving them a tight deadline with just two weeks. They don’t even have the
guy’s name yet- they’ve only just proven that he actually exists by cornering some
classmates.
Maybe Akechi would have information on the mafia? Ren shakes his head at the stupid idea.
Way to get caught, dumbass.
“He even has famous friends, and stuff.” Mishima huffs, “I bet he has girls all over him.”

Ren doesn’t recall when the conversation took this particular turn, “Famous friends?” He
questions instead.
“Huh?” Mishima snaps out of his monologue, “Oh, right. You know that first year gymnast,
Yoshizawa? She mentioned that she found out about Madarame’s calling card because
Akechi told her.”
Ren frowns. He wasn’t expecting this coincidence. “Why would Akechi tell Yoshizawa
something like that?”
Mishima nods enthusiastically, “I know, right? And it was before the calling card was
announced publicly, too.”
Ren frowns harder. That’s… weird. Akechi doesn’t seem like the type to go around telling
people confidential information on a whim. And why Yoshizawa? Did she specifically ask?
He keeps hearing about Yoshizawa from people. Ryuji and Ann have mentioned her in the
past, and then Haru, and now Akechi apparently knows her? He hasn’t even properly met her
yet, but she doesn’t seem to like him, but gets along well enough with everyone else.
Well, discounting the jealous whispers Ren’s occasionally heard in the hallways at Shujin.
After Ren has said his goodbyes to Mishima, he spends his commute trying to wrap his head
around the mystery that is the red-haired girl.
…didn’t he see her at the Wilton hotel? She was there while the thieves were having their
first official meeting- not that they knew that until after their encounter with the jerk at the
elevator.
She also showed up at Leblanc once, too. That was the first time that Ren had ever seen her.
Ren can come up with a lot of paranoid theories for these coincidences surrounding
Yoshizawa, but none have a particularly solid standing. His top one is that she suspects him
of being a phantom thief. Which, well, she wouldn’t be wrong, but Ren doesn’t know how
she would have figured that out before their first calling card was even sent.
It’s probably nothing, he reassures himself.
…
He feels like he’s missing something.
***
Ren doesn’t have any epiphanies about Yoshizawa when he falls asleep, but he does dream.
He’s sitting at Jazz Jin, absent mindedly swirling his drink with a straw, letting the silence
rest as the other boy makes no move to start a conversation, content to take in the live music.

Ren isn’t sure why the other invited him out today, especially given what’s supposed to
happen in a few days. And what he declared a week earlier. Ren had to borderline bribe the
other to come to the jazz club just a few days before, and now he’s inviting Ren unprompted?
He doesn’t buy it. But he also can’t bring himself to complain. It’s nice, to have a break from
the knowledge that it’s all going to go to hell in a few days.
“Are you prepared?” The other speaks up suddenly, “To send the calling card, I mean.”
Ren gives a small smile, “I should be asking you that, shouldn’t I? I’ve done this five times
already.”
The other chuckles, but it feels a bit hollow, “I suppose that’s true.”
They fall into silence again. It isn’t uncomfortable, necessarily. There’s just nothing to say.
Ren is the first one to crack, this time, “You said that we’d probably have to stop meeting up,
after this. Does that really have to happen?”
Ren knows why that can’t happen. He knows that he’s playing with fire just for asking. But, he
wants proof. Proof that the other really wants this.
It’s futile, he’s aware, but he’s desperate.
The other hums, considering the question, before a sad smile dances across his face, “I think
that our friendship was never going to be anything long-term.”
Fucking liar. Or, maybe not a liar, but coward anyway.
Maybe Ren’s being unfair. He hates this.
“Sure.” Ren says, trying not to sound too angry. The other looks almost disappointed. For
what, Ren isn’t sure.
Ren forgets why he’s so upset, and remembers what these dreams are about.
When Ren blinks, Crow is sitting where the other boy sat, looking thoroughly out of place in
his black and blue bodysuit and helmet while they both sit in the warm lighting of the… jazz
club, was it?
“And so you return.” Crow says dryly.
Ren smiles awkwardly, “Did you think I wouldn’t be back?”
“I figured you’d return to further the arcana, at least.” Crow says, looking at the table.
“Is that something that I do subconsciously?” Ren wonders aloud, “Because you were right,
I don’t remember any of this when I wake up.”

Crow snorts. “Of course I’m right. I’m the one who has to be stuck in your head, so I know
how it works.”
Ren raises an eyebrow, “So you aren’t a figment of my imagination? Are you trapped here?”
“Who knows?” Crow shrugs. “I’m here, and I know you, but maybe the reason I know you so
well is only because you perceive me as someone with that knowledge.” He gestures vaguely
with his gauntleted hands, “The power of cognition, and other such bullshit.”
Ren laughs, and leans back in his chair, “So you aren’t trapped, then? I’d feel pretty bad, if I
was keeping you here because I can’t remember something.”
“I can’t leave, if that’s what you’re asking. But that might just be due to the nature of my
existence rather than you actively holding me here.” Crow lets out a bark of a laugh, “Well
now, isn’t that familiar.” His words gain a sardonic edge.
Ren frowns, “You know I don’t get the joke.”
“Give it time.” Crow deadpans, “And it’s not a joke. Not a funny one, at least.”
Ren isn’t sure how to respond, so they fall into silence.
Ren looks around the set piece for this particular memory. It’s not anywhere he recognises,
and he wasn’t able to properly see who his companion was, either. He looks at Crow out of
the corner of his eye, who isn’t being nearly so subtle in his own staring.
“The person in the memory,” Ren starts eventually, “Was it you? It was you last time.”
Crow tilts his head slightly, “It was.”
“Why couldn’t I see your face?”
“Cognition, probably.” Crow shrugs, “My own identity falls under the bracket of ‘implied
knowledge’ that you gain when experiencing a memory, and doesn’t translate when you snap
out of it.” He grins, “So I’m afraid I’ll have to remain a mystery a while longer.”
Ren rolls his eyes, “You were acting different, in this memory.” He points out.
“I was less of an asshole, you mean?”
Ren shakes his head, “Well, sort of. You seemed more… not you.”
“Perhaps.” Crow says, ever unhelpful, “These memories aren’t in chronological order, so
some inconsistencies can be attributed to being at different points in our relationship.”
Ren heaves a sigh, “If you want me to remember, you could stand to make it less convoluted.”
“Blame yourself.” Crow scoffs, “It’s your fucked up mind that’s throwing these together.”

Ren presses his lips together, and takes that as his cue to reflect more on what he saw, trying
to pick it apart.
He sighs and rests his head on the table, thoughts turning to the real world. There’s been no
indication as to how this all fits into the Metaverse and palaces, other than that he and Crow
have apparently interacted in the Metaverse before, and Crow is definitely a persona userRen realises something, feeling like an idiot, and sits up suddenly.
“You look like you’ve had an epiphany.” Crow says at Ren’s sudden start, “Spit it out.”
“There’s someone in the Metaverse that we’ve been told to look out for,” Ren says slowly,
piecing some things together, “We’ve been told to keep an eye out for a persona user with a
black mask, and, well,” Ren gestures at all of Crow, and the other smirks.
“Yes?” Crow prompts, just to be a shit.
Ren cuts to the point. “Are you the person Madarame mentioned?”
“There’s no limit on how many people can have a black mask, Joker.” Crow says flatly,
dropping his amused tone, “And didn’t I already tell you that I’m dead?”
Ren does remember that, now. The throwaway line Crow had said when they first met slipped
Ren’s mind for a while, but he frowns as he considers the implications of remembering who
Crow is while he’s dead in reality.
“Great.” Ren deadpans, and glares at Crow when the Aeon arcana hits rank two. Crow just
smirks in response.
“Well,” Crow says as the sound of breaking chains fades, “That’s another one. Feel
enlightened?”
Ren leans back and grumbles, “You know I don’t.”
“Save it for next time, then.” Crow leans forward, and snaps his fingers-And in the real world, Ren wakes up.

Akechi waits in the hallway to Sae’s apartment, pretending to check his phone as he waits for
Sae to grab her things.
Makoto is standing in the hall as well. Akechi assumes it’s so that she can see her sister off
when she leaves, but right now her presence is only creating an awkward silence.
Akechi decides to humour her, “How are things at school, Niijima-san?”
Makoto starts at having been addressed, “Oh. Um. It’s going fine.” She says stiltedly, “I have
a lot of student council work at the moment, so I’m kind of busy.”
“I see.” Akechi says, and an idea forms, “I’m curious, you overheard how Sae-san and I were
talking about how the Phantom Thieves are likely Shujin students, right?”
Makoto stiffens, but eventually nods.
“Any insights? I’d say you have better intel than we do.” Akechi says with an interview
smile.
Makoto smooths out her skirt, “I’m afraid that I don’t know anything that you wouldn’t
already know.” She says smoothly.
“Of course.” Akechi widens his smile, “But I’m surprised. I would have thought that
someone like you would be itching to catch the thieves yourself.”
Makoto scowls, “And what is that supposed to mean, Akechi-kun?”
“Nothing at all.” Akechi says with an air of nonchalance, “I just thought that someone as
people pleasing as you would be desperate to assist the Shujin administration in their
investigation.”
Makoto’s face twitches as she clenches her fists, “If you must know.” She says tightly, “The

“And yet you’re doing it anyway.” Akechi hums as Sae finally exits her room with a stack of

“We’re going now, Makoto.” Sae says curtly, shoving on her heels, “I probably won’t be back
until late, so don’t wait up.”
“Got it.” Makoto says weakly.

back while Sae isn’t looking.

As Akechi and Sae look over all the files they have, Akechi considers what Yoshizawa has
told him.
Sae Niijima will eventually grow a palace. A casino, Yoshizawa had said. A place for
gambling and debauchery. Akechi can guess the symbolism there- as casinos are often rigged
in favour of the house, prosecution within Japan has a ninety-nine percent conviction rate.
Prosecutors, if they wish to succeed in their field, must live up to these standards.
Especially people like Sae, who has the misfortune of being a woman in a male dominated
field.
Akechi has never seen direct evidence that Sae has fudged her cases. But, with how many
people are often in on such fabrications, that doesn’t mean much. The trail would have been
scrubbed long before Akechi would even have the chance to follow it.
Of course, Akechi is part of the problem. He’s lost count of the number of times that he’s sat
at a board meeting of other conspiracy members, all discussing fake evidence as though it
were entirely real.
He finds it disgusting. He doesn’t accept it, but he has bigger fish to fry. If he wants to stay
alive, then he won’t challenge it. It’s a kind of apathy that has come to permeate many
aspects of his life.
Sae, on the other hand, has no such sword of Damocles. If Yoshizawa is correct, then Sae will
fall victim to delusions that fabricating evidence and forging testimonies is necessary,
whatever that means in her context.
Akechi wants to avoid that, if possible. But he doesn’t know how.
(He also draws a blank when he considers why)
“It’s interesting,” Sae hums, interrupting Akechi’s thoughts, “Both these ‘changes of heart’
and the psychotic breakdown incidents, and to a lessor extent the mental shutdowns, all
involve people with no prior relevant medical records suddenly having a dramatic shift to
their body or personality out of the blue.”

Akechi raises an eyebrow. Leave it to Sae to draw a connection between the incidents even
without knowledge of the cognitive world.
“Are you suggesting that these phenomena are perpetrated using the same methods?” Akechi
pushes.
Sae lets out a long breath through her nose, “Possibly. Don’t you think it’s odd that none of
these incidents have an obvious perpetrator? The mental shutdowns happen almost at
random; the psychotic break victims can’t recall what they were thinking at all while the
incident occurred; and the change of heart recipients both claim that they never spoke to
anyone that could have been a possible cause. They only saw the calling card and were later
overcome with an all-encompassing sense of guilt and urge to confess their crimes.” She
huffs.
Akechi nods. It is, as always, very interesting to see where Sae’s mind can go.
Shall we give her a nudge?
IN WHICH DIRECTION?
Flip a coin.
“That is technically true, Sae-san,” Akechi settles on, “But the changes of heart have had
prior forewarning, while the mental shutdowns and psychotic breaks have, as you said, been
happening completely out of the blue.”
The coin has landed on its middle, it seems.
“That may be true…” Sae mutters, “But what if…?” She presses her lips together, “Surely
you have to see how these incidents are similar. They’re both scenarios of people changing
suddenly, when there’s no reason.” She cuts off with a short sigh.
“I suppose that’s true.” Akechi concedes. He would probably have a much better time
deflecting if he had remembered to get Yoshizawa to tell him how changes of heart work.
He hums, “So you believe that they have similar methods. Are you implying that they have
the same perpetrator?” He ventures.
Sae huffs, “It’s too early to tell.” She says, resigned, “The M.O. is different enough that it’s
hard to link them just yet.”
Akechi nods, satisfied with her roadblock, and goes back to looking over his own files.
Sae clicks her tongue, “I can win this case. I know I can. The director wants a suspect? I’ll
give him one.”
And there, Akechi thinks, is Sae’s sword of Damocles.
Not the threat of death, no- but rather the fear of being let go, the desperate need to prove
herself, and the all-consuming jealousy of her peers.

Akechi has successfully found the ‘how’ of how to prevent Sae from forming a palace. He
just needs to convince her that winning is not all there is to her life, she has other things to
live for, other such platitudes.
Unfortunately, the ‘how’ is borderline impossible for Akechi to accomplish. He would be a
hypocrite, for one, and unless he wants a knife in the back he’d have to convince her subtly
enough that nobody catches wind of his meddling.
So, no dramatic speeches, no obvious hints, and all around, no way to stop Sae Niijima from
barrelling down her path of obsession with success.
How far will she go, Akechi wonders? He vowed a long time ago that he would do anything
to achieve his goals (Loki grins somewhere behind his ribs), but will Sae vow the same?
Does she have a breaking point?
He hopes she won’t find it. By then it would probably be too late.
Akechi wonders if in the last timeline he tried to protect Sae. If she had a change of heart
after Okumura was murdered, then would Akechi not have been ordered to do the same to

He doesn’t know. And unfortunately, neither does Yoshizawa.
(And if he can help it, she won’t find out.)
As Akechi and Sae wrap up their business, he feels the Moon arcana grow to rank three.

On Wednesday, Akechi resigns himself to the fact that he’s wasting time.
The police department is clearly hoping that he’ll miraculously uncover all the information
they need to find the identities of the Phantom Thieves through his investigation.
Unfortunately for them, Akechi already knows who the Phantom Thieves are, having recently
properly looked up their names, and until he figures out what to do with them, he has no

He doesn’t want to sell them out to Shido, because that would spawn myriad questions about
why they have access to the cognitive world, and Akechi doesn’t want to shoot himself in the

Another, quieter, part of him admits that he doesn’t want to sell out the thieves before his
curiosity is sated. Amamiya would be less interesting to speak with if he’s dead.
Akechi knows that his deal with Yoshizawa is… slightly deceptive. Her primary goal is to
prevent the world from succumbing to Maruki’s ideal reality, and from what Akechi can tell,

She has assumed that Akechi shares this goal. Which, well, he does- it’s just not his focus.

was tasked with investigating Shujin for more information on the Phantom Thieves case,”
Akechi ignores how Takamaki and Sakamoto stiffen. Seriously, how were these people not
caught immediately? “But given that I’ve already investigated Shujin in the past, and the
police have collected all relevant witness statements, I must admit that my presence here is
something of a waste of time.”
Morgana pops his head out of Amamiya’s bag, “So he’s just sitting here? I told you he was
weird, Joker.”

Akechi widens his eyes as the thieves all turn to shush Morgana, “You bring your cat even to
school, Amamiya?”
“Well, I am a delinquent.” Amamiya smirks.
Akechi sighs, playing along, “Rather tame for an act of rebellion, don’t you think?”
“Sure,” Amamiya shoves Morgana back down into the bag, “But you should hear the
rumours. Apparently, I’ve killed a man.” He gives a wide grin, and Makoto gives an
exasperated sigh.
“My, is that a confession?” Akechi quips, smiling back, “A rather tragic way to get arrestedjust admitting your crimes to a detective.”
“Uh- he’s joking!” Takamaki interrupts hurriedly, thwacking Amamiya on the shoulder.
“As was I,” Akechi carefully tilts his lips into a frown, “I’m sorry if my presence is making
you uncomfortable, you seem rather nervous.”
“Uh, well- it’s just-” Sakamoto stutters, before settling on fixing a glare at Akechi.
“It’s nothing at all, Akechi-kun,” Niijima interjects smoothly, “We were just looking for a
place to spend lunch and were a bit shocked to find you here. You don’t go to our school,
after all.”
Akechi hums, and gestures to the otherwise empty table, “Well, don’t let me stop you. It’s not
as though I’m working on anything confidential.”
“What are you working on?” Amamiya says before Makoto can make an excuse to leave.
“Math homework.” Akechi says flatly. Amamiya nods in commiseration, a smile tugging at
his lips.
“If you ain’t working on anythin’ important, then why stick around?” Sakamoto says, as
Takamaki goes to elbow him.
“Don’t be a dick!” She hisses, and Akechi holds up his hands placatingly.
“No, it’s fine,” he hums, considering, “I suppose I’d rather not return to the police station to
tell my elder coworkers outright that they’re wasting my time, so I’m waiting here instead, so
that I can at least pretend I gave it a good shot instead of actively disobeying orders.”
Makoto raises her eyebrows. Akechi gives her a perfect smile in return. She can judge him all
she likes, he thinks- she’s the one who’s spending time with thieves.
“Colour me surprised, detective,” Amamiya pipes up again, “I didn’t think you were the type
for malicious compliance.”
“My personality contains multitudes.” Akechi deadpans, and Amamiya lets out a proper
chuckle at that.

“Anyway.” Makoto interrupts, shooting Amamiya an unimpressed look, “I think we’ll be
leaving now, Akechi-kun. Good luck with your work.”
“Goodbye,” Akechi nods, and waves to Amamiya as he leaves, getting a nod in return.
The other thieves hurriedly file out, until only Makoto remains. Akechi raises an eyebrow at
her as she stays in the room. She ignores him, and heads to one of the filing cabinets to grab
some papers.
He definitely deserves the cold shoulder, especially given what he said to her the other day.
He usually isn’t so forward in insulting her, but she seems to have finally gained the courage
to fight back.
Maybe she really has awakened a persona.
“Have I done something to offend, Niijima-san?” He says, just to be an asshole. He chuckles
lightly as Makoto whips around to glare at him, “Don’t worry, I’m not that dense. I realise
that I may have been overly harsh the other day.”
“You think?” Makoto mutters, and puts the files she’s grabbed onto the table to quickly sort
through them.
Akechi is content to leave it at that, but looks up when she speaks again, “I told the principal
that I wasn’t going to investigate the Phantom Thieves anymore.” She says, and Akechi tilts
his head, “You were accusing me of being a pushover, right? Well I’m not anymore. I’m in
control of my life, now.”
Akechi hums, letting his face fall into neutrality, “If you’ve truly grown as a person, then you
shouldn’t need my approval, right?”
Makoto surprisingly smiles at this, and huffs a laugh, “I guess that’s true. I suppose I just
wanted to prove you wrong?”
It’s Akechi’s turn to smile at that, a bit sharper than he would normally allow, “Well, I can
certainly understand that.”
Makoto keeps smiling as she goes back to quickly grabbing what she needs.
Definitely a persona awakening, Akechi thinks. Makoto has finally found her spine, it seems.
Akechi finds that he much prefers that she’s more self-assuredI am thou, thou art I
Thou hast acquired a new bond.
It will lead thee closer to freedom, by traversing the hidden depths of one’s soul.
Through the forging of the High Priestess arcana, thou hast gained a glimpse of the power of
rebellion, and hast begun to uncover thine own truth.

That was not what he was going for with that train of thought. He still doesn’t actually like
Makoto that much. Akechi didn’t realise that growing to tolerate someone’s character was
grounds to form a bond, but he really should have expected this by this point.
Makoto gives a short nod as she leaves the room properly, and Akechi sighs.
The thieves are idiots, and that’s when Akechi’s being charitable. Makoto should throw some
book smarts into the mix at least.
Akechi shoots off a text to Yoshizawa, inviting her to eat lunch in the student council room
and talk, and goes back to his work.

Sumire rounds the corner to head towards the student council room, nearly tripping as she
sees the thieves loitering in the hallway, ducking back behind the corner so she can
eavesdrop.
“What the hell was that about, man?!” She hears Ryuji hiss.
“What was what?” Ren answers nonchalantly.
“He means,” Ann says, “Are you friends with Akechi-kun, Ren? That’s what it sounded like
in there.”
Sumire leans a little closer around the corner to hear them better.
“I think so,” Ren says, uncharacteristically unsure, “I want to be, I think. He’s pretty
interesting.”
“I think you’ve upgraded from banter to flirting.” Morgana pipes up with a groan.
“It’s not-” Ren starts.
“What?!” Ryuji cuts across him, far louder than he probably should be, drawing the attention
of the various other students in the surrounding area.
“It’s not flirting.” Ren finishes, “Where’s Makoto, anyway?”
“I think she stayed back to grab some stuff from the student council room.” Ann chimes in,
apparently happy to change the subject as Ryuji continues to splutter.
Sumire’s eyes widen at the mention of Makoto. Already? She had pencilled in Makoto as
joining for Sae’s palace, but did she join for Kaneshiro?
Sumire’s thoughts are interrupted as Makoto’s voice cuts in, “Sorry, everyone. I was just
picking up the papers we were going to look at.”
“Not a problem!” Ann chirps.

“But man,” Ryuji sighs, “Seriously, what the hell was Akechi doing there, anyways?”

“Yeah, I guess that’s true,” Ryuji says.
“Is it, though?” Makoto says with a tinge of worry in her voice, “If he’s neglecting gathering
more information on the Phantom Thieves, what if that means he thinks he already knows

There’s a tense silence as Sumire hears several sharp breaths, and nervous hums.
“We’ll have to be careful around him.” Morgana declares, “He may act innocent enough, but
I don’t think we should underestimate him.”
“Right.” Makoto says, and Sumire ducks a little further away as the thieves’ footsteps get
closer.
She waits until the thieves are a few paces away before slipping into the hallway they were
previously occupying, and she opens the door to the student council room.
Akechi is sitting at the table in the middle of the room, staring down at a textbook with a

him, closing the textbook with a thump.
“Was Niijima a member of the thieves, last time?” Akechi says as soon as she sits down.

Akechi hums, an unreadable expression passing over his face, before he looks up, “A fair
assumption, I suppose. It isn’t completely unfeasible that Niijima would join to take down

Kaneshiro, though. She is Student Council President, and the phishing scams have been

Akechi gives her a withering glare, and she laughs even harder.

“Aren’t you going to eat lunch as well?” She asks tentatively.
Akechi’s eyes flick up, before he looks back down, “I already ate.” He says dismissively.
Sumire narrows her eyes, “What did you eat?” she pushes.
Akechi sighs, “An apple, Yoshizawa, does it matter?”
Sumire frowns further. She sighs through her nose and hauls her bag into her lap to go

Something in her tone must work, (Or maybe he’s just hungry from only eating a pittance for

Sumire frowns as well, “I take there’s not a lot we can do about that?”
“Not particularly.” Akechi confirms, “And even if the thieves dropped Kaneshiro, targeting

Akechi hums softly, “Maybe.”

The day after his trip to Shujin, Akechi finds himself tapping on the Metanav.
“Sae Niijima.” He says, “The prosecutor.”
No candidate found. The Nav chirps.
This, Akechi already knows.
“Mementos,” He amends.
Candidate found. The Nav confirms, and this Akechi already knows as well.
He hasn’t checked. He knows most people have shadows. Actually, he’s pretty sure everyone
has a shadow- he’s never encountered someone who doesn’t.
Well, except for himself.
And, more recently, Yoshizawa and the Phantom Thieves. But that goes to show it’s likely a
persona thing.
All this to say, he didn’t think it pressing to see that Sae has a shadow in Mementos. She was
fairly high up in the subway system, too, so he figured it wasn’t his place to go question her
psyche when she wasn’t that distorted.
That has changed. Sae’s actually lower down, now, and with Yoshizawa’s portent of the
casino palace, Akechi is itching to take a look at how far gone the prosecutor is.
Call it a professional curiosity.
(The Moon arcana hums.)
Akechi stalks his way through the pulsing subway tunnels, keeping Loki constantly at his
side. It’s been a bit of a trek, and he’s far down enough that the shadows have stopped
cowering from him. He still destroys them fairly easily, but the fact that he has to bother with
them to begin with is starting to piss him off.
Thankfully, Sae’s pocket of distortion isn’t much further. Pulling back the curtain, Akechi
dismisses Loki to avoid appearing threatening. He’s only here to talk, after all.
“Sae-san?” He calls out into the space, and golden eyes whip around to pierce into his own.
“Who are you?” Sae hisses. To her credit, she does sound far less aggressive than many of
the other shadows that Akechi has faced in the past. Though, that might be more indicative of
the kind of people Akechi has been sent to target rather than of Sae herself.
“I just want to chat.” Akechi holds up his hands in surrender, and telegraphs his movements
clearly as he goes to sit on the ground.

The shadow narrows her eyes, and sneers, “You still haven’t answered my question.”
“Who I am doesn’t matter.” Akechi says. If Sae hasn’t already recognised him he sees no
reason to make her paranoid in the real world, “I just want to know how you are.”
She scoffs, “How I am? How I am doesn’t matter. I’ll keep going until I succeed.”
There’s some more familiar shadow talk. “What does success look like to you?” Akechi
prompts.
“Like winning.” Sae says frankly, “The only worth anyone has in this society is how they can
provide for it, and I’m going to prove just how much I deserve to be here.”
“I see.” Akechi says quietly, not breaking eye contact.
He thinks it should concern him, how much he understands Sae’s distortion. He can’t bring
himself to care, particularly. You have to do what it takes to stay alive, and the surest way to
do that is to claw your way to the top and make sure you stay there.
Goro Akechi was taught from a young age that people don’t have worth if they don’t have
use- and he can see before him that Sae Niijima was taught the same thing.
Or maybe she learnt it on her own. She grew up in a loving household, after all.
Akechi huffs a short breath, and slowly gets to his feet. Sae doesn’t break her stare.
As he turns to leave, Sae calls out, “Akechi-kun.”
Akechi turns slightly, “So you do recognise me.”
“Not at first.” She admits, “But I can feel the arcana. The Moon, is it?”
Akechi nods, and she snorts and turns away. “I should probably be insulted, given what that
one means.”
“Care to enlighten me?” Akechi turns fully to face her.
“The Moon represents self-deception and insecurity.” The shadow recites, “It spells bad
things both upright and reversed.”
Akechi smirks, “I didn’t take you for a fan of tarot, Sae-san.”
“My real self isn’t.” She says flatly, “I think I only know because of the bond. Interesting,
isn’t it?”
“Indeed.” Akechi agrees, and he turns again.
He pulls open the curtain of distortion, and begins to step through.
“Akechi-kun.” Sae calls out one last time, “Take care of yourself.”

Akechi pauses, but does not respond as he leaves.

When Sumire was seven years old, she and Kasumi made a promise.
“We’ll be the top of the world, Sumi!” Kasumi said, a wide grin splitting her face.
Sumire had nodded eagerly. Anything her sister wanted was something she wanted as wellKasumi was so amazing, how could she not make all the best decisions? They used to
practice hard at their sport because they would get ice-cream afterwards, and then they grew
to truly love it beyond just the reward.
Kasumi kept practicing for the thrill of it all, Sumire thinks. She can tell how much her sister
loved the flips and jumps and stretches all combined in a dance, showcasing the potential of
the human body.
Sumire kept practicing because she didn’t want Kasumi to leave her behind.
That isn’t to say that Sumire doesn’t enjoy gymnastics, far from it, but her latent motivation
for her life’s goal laid in the fact that Kasumi wanted it, so she did too.
When Sumire was thirteen years old, she started to believe that she would never catch up to
Kasumi.
Kasumi was so kind about it, of course, but that just made Sumire all the more aware of how
she was inferior. Her self-worth and entire motivation in life was tied to her sister, but when
she began to resent her for how perfect she was, Sumire couldn’t help but resent herself, too.
How dare she, the lesser twin, be angry at Kasumi for being better than her. This was her own
fault, she thought, there must be something wrong with her.
Then, the day before Sumire turned fifteen, Kasumi was hit by a truck trying to protect
Sumire, and her whole world fell apart.
In the time before she saw Doctor Maruki for the first time, Sumire felt like her entire reason
for existing had evaporated. Her motivation for gymnastics, her entire being had been based
on Kasumi’s shadow, and now there was nowhere to hide. Just Sumire Yoshizawa against the
world she had only ever seen through Kasumi’s eyes.
She got nowhere, in trying to make herself feel better. She was rapidly failing at gymnastics
because she couldn’t bring herself to try, and that only made her feel worse- because if she
wasn’t dedicating herself to her and Kasumi’s dream, then why the hell was she even here?
Then she met Doctor Maruki, and the year slid by like a dream.
Kasumi Yoshizawa would never let something as small as the death of her younger sister get
in the way of her goal. So she practiced, and practiced, and practiced some more. And got

absolutely nowhere, because she was working on an assumption of how her body should
move when that wasn’t the body she had.
Maruki could make Sumire believe she didn’t exist, but he couldn’t hide all the little ticks in
her brain that made her struggle, and he certainly couldn’t completely alter her physiology to
make her body make sense.
And then, Sumire Yoshizawa woke up. And all the little confusing feelings and
inconsistencies from the last year suddenly clicked. Her confusion left her as rapidly as her
motivation for everything else did, and Sumire begged to go back to being Kasumi.
She got over it. What an insult it would be to Kasumi, Sumire thinks, if she were to go about
pretending that her sister never died. To waste the life that Kasumi had given in Sumire’s
stead.
So Sumire became motivated again. Her want to fulfill her and her sister’s dream suddenly
became sustainable, because she knows who Sumire Yoshizawa is now, and she’s someone
who can reach the top of the world.
But, Sumire thinks as she follows Akechi into Mementos, is it truly sustainable?

The thieves are making excellent progress through Kaneshiro’s bank, Ren thinks.
A healthy combination of their new team member, José’s wishing star granting them some
extra power, and Ren finally getting the hang of the whole persona fusion thing, have all

amounted to the Phantom Thieves tearing through fights with minimal damage and some
serious overkill.
And, Ren shoving his pockets full with more money than he’ll ever know what to do with.
He gives a lot of it to Yusuke, but he fears that the artist is just going to spend it on art
supplies rather than food.
The euphoria of his team’s sudden boost in power is almost enough to distract Ren from the
ebbing sense of dread about the other Metaverse user.
He also feels like he’s forgetting something, and that mystery bond hasn’t gone away, even as
several others join its rank. Ren feels like it’s gotten stronger, weirdly, which he thinks should
be a bit difficult given he doesn’t even know who it belongs to.
So, Ren’s paranoid. He keeps looking around wildly with third eye, glaring holes into
particularly dark pockets of the bank.
It’s getting to the point where the other thieves have noticed his unrest, and are shooting
questioning and sympathetic looks as he waves them off.
Eventually, Makoto seems to get fed up with his fidgeting, “Joker? Is there a problem?”

Ren grins to himself, and walks up to Akechi, who’s currently zoned out, staring at nothing.
“Are you busy, detective?” Ren asks, and tries not to feel too satisfied as Akechi startles.
“Amamiya.” Akechi blinks, “I’m not busy, no. Do you need something?”
Ren rolls his lips at the implication that he would only seek Akechi out for a tangible benefit,
“No.” He corrects, “I was wondering if you wanted to hang out.”
Akechi’s face stays neutral as he stares Ren down, “I see. I had actually been intending to
invite you out to a café nearby that I wanted to try, but someone else beat me on the
initiative.”
“You’re popular, then?” Ren grins sheepishly.
Akechi makes a noise that sounds very suspiciously like a snort, “Not exactly. It was just
coincidence.”
Ren twists his fringe between his fingers, “We could still go there, if you want.” He shrugs, “I
can’t seem to remember any laws that forbid someone from going to the same café twice.”
Akechi gives him a look that seems distinctly unimpressed, “No, I suppose not.” He
deadpans, before a perfect smile slams onto his face, “I suppose if you’re inviting me, then
you’ll be paying?”
Ren ignores a wave of déjà vu, “You’re lucky I’m a gentleman, detective.” He turns to start
walking, before realising he doesn’t know where they’re going. The corner of Akechi’s
mouth twitches upwards before he falls into step to lead the way.
Akechi leads him to a modern-looking café, and they both take a seat and order coffee.

“So what’s so special about this café that you wanted to try it?” Ren says, peeking over the
dessert menu in his hands.
“Nothing, really,” Akechi admits, “It’s just that interviews often ask me about current trends,
and I need to have opinions prepped.”
Ren scrunches his face, “How is that relevant to detective work?”
“It isn’t.” Akechi says flatly, not looking up from his own menu.
“That sucks.” Ren commiserates, eyes flicking to the side as he looks down.
Akechi hums, tilting his head up slightly, “It does, a bit.”
Ren raises his eyebrows expectantly, hoping he’ll continue, and frowning when Akechi
leaves it at that.
Akechi’s a bit hot and cold, he thinks. Ren can’t tell when he’s stumbling into a
conversational pitfall that will cut the detective off short. He isn’t sure if he wants to push,
either. For all Akechi has taken permanent residence in a corner of Ren’s mind, they’ve only
really met a few times, so he doesn’t know what etiquette he has to employ here.
…
Fuck it.
“Is there something stopping you from keeping the interviewers on track?” Ren asks
surreptitiously, leaning his cheek against his hand.
Akechi raises an eyebrow, “I suppose you got a rather charitable impression of my interviews
that day at the TV station.” He sighs, “That was an outlier, I’m afraid. Most of the time I’m
never asked about any specific casework, and more about myself.”
“Oh.” Ren hums, “Why do you have to keep up with trends, though? Can ‘yourself’ not just
say that you’re unfamiliar with what they’re talking about?”
Akechi gives him a look that borders on exasperation, “I’d prefer to be in control of the
image I present on television. The personality I cultivate for media purposes is much more
palatable than what’s underneath, I find.”
Ren frowns. He doesn’t like how matter-of-factly Akechi said that. He shrugs awkwardly, “I
think I’d like the real you, as well. Whatever he’s like.” He says quietly.
Akechi pauses for a moment, before pasting on another pretty smile, “That’s very kind of you
to say, Amamiya.”
Ren slumps in defeat, and nods weakly, going back to his menu.
Akechi shifts, “What makes you think I’m not being real right now?”

Ren looks up, and smirks, “Because you act nearly exactly the same here as you do on TV.”
Akechi returns the smirk, though it’s a shade more sardonic, “Then you haven’t seen me on
TV very much.”
“Of course,” Ren sighs dramatically, leaning back, “You’re only at your truest when dissing
the Phantom Thieves, how could I forget?”
Akechi lets out another suspiciously snort-like sound, and covers his mouth, “An interesting
conclusion to jump to, but I concede not an entirely inaccurate one.”
Ren grins, leaning forward, “Then I guess we’ll just have to debate some more, if I want to
see the real you.”
Akechi pierces him with a sharp look, “Why is that you seem so invested in that?”
Ren goes to answer, but stops short.
He’s identified that the desire is there, but he’s yet to ascertain why.
The itch returns, and the curiosity with it.
What is it that makes Akechi different?
“I think,” Ren says slowly, “That it’s because we’re similar.”
Akechi tilts his head, “That’s an awfully vague answer.”
Ren shrugs, “It’s all I’ve got.”
“Ha.” Akechi breathes, and then shakes his head, “I have to say that I’ve felt a curiosity
towards you as well. Maybe you’re just magnetic?” He says, voice gaining a teasing edge.
Ren grins, “You sure you aren’t the magnetic one?”
“Who knows?” Akechi leans back, and folds his arms, “Maybe it’s fate.” He says softly.
Ren looks Akechi up and down, before smiling genuinely, “Yeah,” he huffs, “Maybe.”
(Both Ren and Akechi feel the Justice arcana reach rank three)

Sumire doesn’t know how she got into this, but she can’t decide whether to laugh or cry.
For being a time traveller, Sumire has experienced shockingly little in the way of repeated
interactions. For the most part, aside from school classes, she hasn’t had any people come to
her with things she’s already heard before.

And that is why it’s so hilarious to her that -even in wildly different circumstances- Akechi
has still managed to drag the three of them on an awkward café date. She didn’t realise it was
awkward last time, but now she knows how much Akechi thrives off of schadenfreude, it’s
clear he’s setting this up on purpose.
She has to stop herself from dissolving into giggles every time she catches a glimpse of
Akechi’s entirely too self-satisfied smile.
She also flinches every time she looks at Ren.
Sumire hates how easy it is to just start talking to him like nothing’s wrong.
On his end of things, there isn’t anything wrong, she reminds herself. She’s probably weirded
him out with how hot and cold she’s been, actually.
You’re supposed to be angry; she reminds herself when she almost starts some idle chatter
with him.
He doesn’t remember you; she reminds herself again when she almost points out something
they did together last timeline.
Akechi keeps throwing her looks. She hasn’t explained any of this to him, after all. He’s
probably put two and two together on the fact that Ren is the person she takes issue with in
the thieves, but has no intention of telling him exactly why until she gets through her to-do
list of ‘things to address’ first.
Maybe Akechi will just assume that she resents Ren as the leader because he failed to
infiltrate Maruki’s palace before the deadline, or some other conclusion based on the lies
she’s told.
She needs to figure this out, she thinks for what must be the tenth time this week. She still
hasn’t made any progress, of course.
Sumire catches Ren’s eyes again, and the man looks bewildered. Understandable, considering
the battle going on in Sumire’s head, and how Akechi seems caught between his interview
personality and his real one.
He’s sticking to his TV smile, mostly, but he’ll occasionally shoot Sumire a sharp look or
phrase that must make for an odd picture for people not in the know.
Such people including Ren, of course, who still hasn’t managed to mask the utter confusion
on his face.
Sumire bites her lip.
Her instinct is to get far, far away from Ren. She doesn’t trust herself not to do something
rash, like lash out. Or forgive him, like the old Sumire would have done in a heartbeat.
She wonders if the new Sumire is really any different.

Is it growth, to hold a grudge? Where does the betrayal to herself lie? Is it in chaining herself
to the past or in ignoring it entirely?
Ella thrums warmly, reassuring. Sumire smiles to herself.
She’s still angry, then. Ella can confirm that.
Sumire wonders if there’s something wrong with her, that she enjoys the company of a
murderer more than someone who had done so much to help her in the past.
Akechi has done a lot to help her too, though.
Hm.
Maybe, Sumire thinks to herself, she’s just selfish. Maybe that’s why she’s finding it hard to
care.
She shakes the thoughts out of her head, and focuses back on the present.
The conversation is definitely more awkward this time around, now that Ren is the one most
out of the loop in this situation. And, unlike Sumire last time, he has the awareness to realise
that he’s missing something, and is thus making no attempt at furthering the conversation.
Akechi isn’t helping, as usual- but he also isn’t making it any worse by asking Sumire any
out-of-the-blue questions to try and poke something out of Ren, so there’s that.
Sumire sighs quietly to herself.
This is a mess.

Akechi can feel the thrum of the Devil arcana before he even enters the room.
It makes him sick. He has a sudden violent urge to claw the skin on his chest off just to get a
shot at ripping out one of the tangled threads worming its way through his arteries.
He ignores it. He has gloves on, so he wouldn’t get very far anyway.
Instead he doesn’t smile, doesn’t frown, doesn’t do much of anything as he closes the door

you’ve let things get this far.”

Akechi almost bristles at the implication that this is all his fault. He doesn’t though.

Shido’s wrath, this time.

prepared speech, “But I’ve managed to locate them in the Metaverse, now. I don’t have their

No?
Akechi closes his mouth.
This is a deviation.
“You’re lucky, Akechi,” Shido says, sitting down and leaning forward, “That I’ve come to

“That’s what I just said.” Shido snaps, “Have you heard of Medjed, Akechi?”
Of course he fucking has, “Yes, sir.” He says.
“These thieves are a danger to us, but they’re also a danger to themselves.” Shido says

It’s too bad that a hacker will join the thieves in the future. Shido’s destructive plan might

Oh.
Maybe the thieves never needed a hacker, then.
Akechi fucking hates where this plan is going. He doesn’t think about why.

Akechi is starting to get the bigger picture.

The Phantom Thieves, led by Ren Amamiya, stumble their way into another world and
accidentally awaken to a mysterious power.
And just so happen to find a guide with all the answers they need.
They discover they can take down a disgusting abuser, and a series of misfortunes pushes

They succeed, and no one gets hurt.
(Because they have a fucking guide.)
They decide that they’re justice incarnate, and start taking the requests of anyone with a sob

There’s a bit of a gap in what Akechi knows here.
Somehow, they find Shido. They probably figure out what Akechi does, too. They take down

And then their school counsellor becomes god, or whatever.
“It’s an excellent plan, sir.” Akechi says, because there’s nothing else he can say.
