Akechi lives, and has always lived, his life in a constant state of anticipation. Anticipation for
the day that it will all be worth it, every promise fulfilled, every sacrifice not in vain, every
potential regret snuffed out, and, well,
This bond only makes him all the more eager.
Perhaps it does serve a purpose.
***
The Devil arcana had fucking better serve a purpose, Akechi thinks later when he rips his
mind out from under the water, because otherwise he’s going to claw his skin off.
Maybe he won’t do anything that extreme. He could always claw off a shadow’s, instead.
José insisted quite fervently that bonds serve to grow a wildcards power, change fate, and
other such bullshit. Akechi has decided to put this to the test.
Which is how he finds himself leaning leisurely against the railing of a luxury cruiser in
Shido’s head, staring disinterestedly at the city drowned in bloody waters.
Akechi’s theory is this: if Sae Niijima’s shadow was able to sense that she represents the
Moon to him, then it isn’t a stretch to believe that the arcana can affect the cognitive world in
an undefined way. Akechi wants to see how that extends to palaces, if at all.
He has no intention of seeking out Shido’s shadow. The fire that Akechi would have to play
with is far too great- the chances of him accidentally influencing Shido’s real-world mind are
too high, especially if the shadow can recognise him through vibes, apparently.
Akechi kicks off the railing, and shoots the door handle instead of turning it, kicking open the
entrance to the foyer. None of the cognitions spare him much of a glance, too absorbed in
their chittering laughter and airy small talk to care about the black masked intruder storming
past them with murder in his eyes.
Maybe he’ll terrorise the creeps around the pool deck. That’s always some good stress relief.
An outsider’s perspective on Akechi’s actions may question why it is that he’s waited two
years for his revenge instead of simply tearing through Shido’s head the second he found the
other world.
The answer can be split into two parts. The first: when Akechi first awakened his powers, he
couldn’t have made it ten steps in the front door without being turned into a bloody, pasty,
adornment on the carpet.
Then, even as Akechi got stronger -and he got stronger fast- Shido’s palace adapted. A side
effect of knowing the man in the real world, Akechi assumes, combined with Shido’s active
knowledge of the cognitive world’s existence. Shido’s palace is designed to keep Akechi, and
Akechi specifically, out. Cognitions are uncooperative, Shadows target him with unchecked
aggression, and a lurking presence in the darkness rains bullets down from above with all the
accuracy of an experienced sniper.

So, for the outsider asking why Akechi hasn’t hurried the hell up- the answer is that he’s
tried.
The second part to the answer, is that Akechi craves a very specific type of revenge.
Many people would consider death too good for scum like Shido, and Akechi happens to
agree. He still intends to kill him, of course, but he’s going to make sure it isn’t quick. The
higher Shido is when he falls, the longer he’ll have to contemplate exactly how pathetic and
worthless he is before he hits the pavement.
Goro Akechi is a patient man. He can wait.
Doesn’t stop him from bitching about it, though.
Akechi spins and kicks and slashes through the shadows cornered in the narrow hallways,
taking the fastest route through the ship to make ground. He’s not headed anywhere in
particular- he’s only here to test his theory.
So far, there’s no indication that Shido’s palace is any easier than before.
Fuck.
“Fuck!” Akechi hisses as he wrenches his blade out of a shadow’s dissolving corpse. What’s
the hell is the point of dealing with this fucked up bond of it isn’t even doing anything for
him?
“Are you having fun?”
Akechi freezes at the voice.
“You’re starting to raise the alarms, you know. The captain won’t be happy if the news
reaches him.”
Akechi knows that voice, he knows it well, becauseAkechi spins, and is met with the blank stare of his own face.
The cognition tilts its head and gives a passive smile, “I usually let you get away with a lot,
but I’m afraid that the carpet is starting to stain.” It raises a hand and gestures at the black
ooze that hasn’t fully evaporated with the rest of the shadows’ bodies.
Akechi swallows. HeA sneer- his own face. Akechi hates how this thing is using his face. Maybe it’s narcissistic of
him for that to be the thing he’s focusing on, but it’s all he can think about.
It’s all he can think about, because if he were to think about anything else, he would have to
think about the other’s shouts from behind the bulkhead door. He’d have to think about how
much everything hurts. He’d have to think about-

He’d have to start wondering if death will hurt, more than he’s in pain now. If there’s
anything after. If there’s a hell, then he surely has VIP tickets.
He hopes that the other can forgive him for this, and he firesAkechi blinks, shoves that out of his mind for later, and continues to stare down the cognition
wearing his skin.
It’s… accurate. Unnervingly so. Akechi isn’t sure what that says about what Shido thinks of
him.
“Are you going to say anything?” The cognition drawls, “You were so loud before.”
“What are you?” Akechi finds his voice again.
“What am I?” The cognition gives him an innocent smile, “I’m you, of course.”
“No you’re not.” Akechi spits, “You’re what he thinks of me.”
The cognition shrugs, and sighs, “I suppose that’s true. But the captain is very perceptive,
you’ll find.”
Akechi points his sword at the cognition, “Why have I never seen you before?”
“You’ve never caused this much trouble before.” The cognition points out, “Normally I’d let
the cleaner deal with you, but you seem to have torn through him in your little tantrum.”
Akechi might remember that. He wasn’t paying a lot of attention to what he was killing.
“So, what?” Akechi steps closer, “Are you here to try and kill me?” He tenses his muscles,
preparing to make the first move.
The cognition’s eyes widen in faux shock, “Goodness, no! Unless,” it smirks, “You plan on
inconveniencing the captain. It’s my job to deal with problems like that.”
Akechi doesn’t untense. He doesn’t trust this thing at all.
It was always reasonable to assume that there would be a cognition of him on Shido’s ship.
He’s the one keeping the thing sailing, after all. But after encounters with nearly every other
member of the conspiracy, and no sign of him- Akechi figured that Shido envisioned him as
another one of the drowned bodies in the blood-filled sea.
Great. Another reason to hate Shido, and a loose end that Akechi didn’t need to worry about.
But now, staring himself in the face, Akechi is abruptly realising that he may be a
countermeasure to himself.
“I’ve never seen you on this ship before.” Akechi pushes again, “Where have you been
hiding?”

“In your blind spots, mostly.” The cognition says flatly, “None of the other sycophants on this
ship are treacherous enough to be worth my time. It doesn’t matter if I’m in full view of
them.” Its smile stretches unnaturally, “For intruders like you, on the other hand?”
Akechi fails to stop the shock from twitching on his face as he realises the implication to the
cognition’s words, “You aren’t a guest on this ship.” He states more than asks.
The cognition claps his hands together, “Ding ding ding! That’s right! I don’t need to be
bribed like everyone else. I’ll do the captain’s bidding either way.”
Akechi uses a great deal of self-restraint to not shoot the cognition then and there. “How do
you get around, then?” He grits out past his clenched teeth.
“The same way you do, probably.” The cognition says cheerfully, “It doesn’t matter if any of
the guests see me.” He repeats, “They either assume I’m one of them, or they’re so
pathetically easy to kill that it doesn’t matter anyway.”
Akechi steps closer, sword still pointed threateningly, “If you’re here because I’ve been
causing trouble, then why the fuck are you stopping to chat?”
The cognition grins, andI am thou, thou art I
Thou hast acquired a new bond.
It will lead thee closer to freedom, by traversing the hidden depths of one’s soul.
Through the forging of the Tower arcana, thou hast gained a glimpse of the power of
rebellion, and hast begun to uncover thine own truth.
“Well, I figured I’d ask nicely first.” The cognition chuckles lightly, “All I’m good for is
murder and a pretty face, right?”
“Fuck off,” Akechi spits as he’s still reeling, and crushes a Goho-M in his hand.
He reappears on the front deck of the cruiser, clenching his fists and grinding his teeth.
Fucking hell.
Akechi thinks it’s rather concerning, that his fate is supposedly tied to a figment of a figment
of Shido’s imagination.
Akechi doesn’t admit to fear very often. Usually, he’ll shove down anything that can be
labelled ‘hesitation’ so far that he forgets it exists entirely. It’s effective, when he needs to get
things done.
Don’t think about the weight of a gun in his hand, don’t think about how this is killing him
slowly from the inside out, don’t think about how the person on the other end might have had
something to live for.

Everything he destroys, is trash, scum- things that deserve the fate delivered by Akechi’s
hand. They should have seen the sword of Damocles gifted to them alongside their
acquaintance with Shido, so who’s truly at fault?
Shido, mostly.
(He can’t kid himself; Akechi knows he’ll deserve the best seat in the frozen lake at the
bottom of hell)
Perhaps it is his own perception of himself as an unbiased, unrelenting killer, that makes
Akechi fear a mannequin styled to bear his own face.
No one is safe from the judgement wrought by the conspiracy’s assassin, least of all Akechi.
(Only good for murder and a pretty face, The voice of the cognition repeats in his head.)
He needs to be more careful.
The Tower arcana doesn’t make him feel as sick as the Devil does. It’s filler, to him. He
doesn’t care what Shido thinks of him, so long as he doesn’t catch on to his plans.
…
That, he chuckles wryly to himself, unfortunately encompasses a lot about how he needs to
be seen.
That doesn’t mean he cares.
The Tower arcana buzzes, and the hair on Akechi’s neck pricks as he feels himself being
watched yet again.

“Right,” Akechi adds, as an afterthought.

“Hey.” Ren says.
Akechi looks up from his phone, “Hello,” he says, some amusement creeping onto his face.
“You, uh, look nice.” Ren stutters, because he does. Akechi in a yukata and ponytail is

Akechi blinks, taken aback, before a TV smile slams down on his face, “Thank you,
Amamiya.” He says with no particular intonation.
“I’m being serious,” Ren says quietly.
Akechi tilts his head, some of the mask dissipating, “I didn’t mean to insinuate you weren’t.”
Ren nods, and their conversation peters out.
After a beat, Akechi’s eyes flick to him again. “You look nice too.” He says, and Ren gapes.

He clamps his mouth shut when he realises he must look like an idiot, “Uh,” he says
intelligently, “Thanks.”
Akechi’s eyes glimmer teasingly, “I’m being serious,” he echoes.
“I don’t really look any different from normal,” Ren looks down, resisting the urge to reach

“You aren’t wearing your glasses.” Akechi points out, “I’ve never seen you without them.”
Ren instinctively goes to readjust the glasses that aren’t there, “Uh, yeah. They’re actually
fake.”
“Hm,” Akechi pierces him with a look, “I thought as much. The lenses didn’t reflect the same

Ren grins, “You’re the detective, you tell me.”
Akechi huffs a laugh, “I’ll have to get back to you on that one. Give me some time to collect

Ren chuckles, before his brain catches up to what Akechi said.
“You think I’m charming?” Ren blurts.
Akechi pauses, and then turns to fix Ren with an exasperated look, “I was implying that you
think you’re charming.”
Ren lets his grin grow wider, “Those two aren’t mutually exclusive.”
Akechi sighs in a show of dramatics, “And yet you still aren’t charming.”
A startled laugh escapes Ren’s lips. He goes to retort, but he’s cut off by Haru’s sigh from the
other group.
“I’m sorry everyone, but I think I need to get going.” She says, putting her phone away after

Akechi nods, “I wouldn’t mind one. Thank you, Haru-san.”
Haru nods cheerfully, “Great! I’ll get us picked up near the station. Goodbye everyone!” She
waves to the thieves, and falls into step with Akechi and Yoshizawa. Akechi throws Ren a
short wave as he leaves, and Ren returns it and smiles.

After the trio are out of sight, Ryuji throws up his hands, “That was so effin’ weird!” He

“How so?” Yusuke frowns.
“I’ve seen Haru-san around once or twice,” Makoto muses, and she frowns, “But those three
seem like such an odd trio to be friends.”
“I mean,” Ann shrugs, “I’ve met Sumire-chan a few times, and we’ve all met Akechi-kun
once or twice at least, but it’s not like any of us know them that well. So we can’t really say if
it’s weird or not. Like,” She laughs sheepishly, and twists some of her hair around one of her

Ren nods in agreement, a small smile tugging at his lips, but Morgana pipes up, “Akechi
always acts weird when he’s near us. And he was definitely off this time, too.”
“Right,” Yusuke hums, “It did seem odd that he was aware of my name. Though, his excuse
was also perfectly reasonable.”
“Man,” Ryuji cuts in, “When Sumire said she was going to this festival, I didn’t think she
meant with Akechi.”
“She can be friends with whoever she wants,” Ren says noncommittally.
“Well, yeah, but-” Ryuji backpedals, and then huffs, “I just think he’s a dick.”
Ren shrugs, not particularly enthused to debate this with his friends yet again, “He’s not so
bad.”
“Anyway,” Makoto thankfully interrupts, “We might just be being paranoid. There’s nothing
about those three that screams ‘odd’ other than being slightly unexpected.”
“I think you’re right,” Ann nods, and then grins brightly, “And Haru and Sumire are such
sweethearts, too!”
“They are rather pleasant to converse with.” Yusuke says, smiling.
“Yeah, Sumire’s great.” Ryuji says sunnily.
Morgana hums, “She doesn’t seem to like Joker much.”
Makoto gives Ren a confused look, “Really? How come?”
Ren shrugs, “Dunno,” he says, helpfully.
“Helpful.” Ann deadpans, unhelpfully.
Ren grimaces, “I really don’t know. She likes all of you, at least.”

The other thieves exchange looks, and all give weak shrugs. Ren takes that they’re just as
clueless as he is.
Ren defended the group earlier, but that doesn’t stop him from wondering. He’s been running
into Akechi and Yoshizawa a lot lately, and the two are trying their damndest to ensure they
come as a set. Throw Haru in the mix, and Ren is left with a lot of questions.
Three people hanging out is not inherently nefarious, he reminds himself. Three people who
he keeps running into is not odd, especially when he actively seeks one out and he’s only met
another twice. Three people hanging out does not mean they know that Ren and his friends
are the Phantom Thieves.
Maybe, if he keeps telling himself that, he’ll stop feeling like he needs to check over his
shoulder.
It’s probably his paranoia from all the mysteries in the Metaverse that’s making him extra
afraid of anything slightly unexplained in the real world.
That, and Akechi is a detective trying to catch the thieves. Ren tries to ignore how he’s the
least worried about that.
The black mask, strange dreams, inexplicable visions, standoffish girls, and strange trios.
Ren sighs. When can he catch a break?

The fireworks festival was… fine. Akechi didn’t hate it. The annoyance he felt at the rain
was definitely tempered by the fact he knew that simply being there was pissing off Haru’s
fiancé.
He doesn’t particularly enjoy crowds, and he’s glad that neither Sumire nor Haru called him
out on how tense he was, or how he spent more time than strictly necessary eyeing their
surroundings with frantic paranoia.
They didn’t mention it, or they didn’t notice. Either way, he’s grateful.
The reason he was late is actually because he spent longer than he realised on trying to
determine whether a ponytail and change in outfit would be enough to disguise him. It was,
so he was nervous over nothing, it seems.
Running into Amamiya and the other thieves was an interesting turn.
He’s been running into Amamiya a lot, lately. He thinks he should be more annoyed than he
is, but unfortunately the younger boy has a sort of magnetic charm that Akechi is struggling
to ignore (not that he’d ever admit that to Amamiya). It’s the kind of charm that Akechi
figures vigilante leaders would need to have.
Or cult leaders. But that’s neither here nor there.

Something in him curdled at how easily Sumire and Haru were able to speak with the thieves.
They accepted the two with open and friendly arms while Akechi was forced to make his
presence unobtrusive.
Of course they’d like Sumire and Haru, a more rational part of Akechi thinks, neither of them
are the detective threatening to arrest them.
Another, perhaps less rational, part of Akechi is sharp, and furious, and jealous. He always
has been.
He feels the warm hum of the arcana nestled in his heart, and he know that these bonds are
going to ruin him.
He didn’t care, before. He’s never cared that he can play people like a fiddle but could never
service the instrument. It didn’t matter. Most people can’t tell the difference, and he’s never
cared to correct them.
But now, when he felt the slight pull of the Magician, Strength, Justice, and High Priestess,
all in tandem, he suddenly wished he was more. That he could be so effortlessly personable
as all of them. He could never be one of them, for all the reasons on earth, and where he was
once numb it now hurts, the threads of bonds cutting his insides like wires.
So, when Amamiya chose to speak to him instead of anyone else, if Akechi felt endlessly
smug (And endlessly relieved) that the Phantom Thieves’ precious leader chose to speak
with him instead of his friends, well, that’s his own business.
Just after Haru had dropped both Akechi and Sumire in Kichijoji, Sumire had pulled him
aside and asked if they could meet in Mementos at some point. She seemed weirdly nervous;
in a way she rarely is around Akechi anymore. The times when Sumire had acted like this
was when she was hiding something, so Akechi assumes she has something to get off her
chest.
So, he felt the Magician arcana glow warmly, sighed, and agreed to meet.
Which leads to now.
“So, what is it that you wanted to tell me, Sumire?” Akechi turns and looks at her, folding his
arms.
Sumire blinks, “Oh, uh, you could tell?”
“You aren’t a particularly accomplished actor.” Akechi says dryly.
Sumire winces, “Yeah. I’m starting to figure that out.”
Akechi tilts his head and snorts. “Well?” He prompts, “Spit it out.”
Sumire bites her lip and looks at the floor, “Right, um,” She breathes in deeply and huffs,
“So, after you told me that the thieves had sent Kaneshiro’s calling card, I followed them in
like I did with Madarame.”

Akechi nods slowly, “I had assumed you would. That’s why I told you about the calling
card.”
“Yep,” Sumire laughs nervously, “So, just after they fought his shadow, he, um, told them
some stuff?”
She seems to be losing her nerve as she trails off. Akechi sighs, not eager to make this trip a
waste of time, “Are you going to get to the point.”
“I- I’m getting there,” Sumire says, voice pitching upwards, “Kaneshiro, he talked about
another Metaverse user, like Madarame did, and he, um, said that,” she pauses and takes a
breath, “He said that the other Metaverse user was responsible for the mental shutdowns and
psychotic breakdowns.” She finishes, and finally looks Akechi in the eye.
Ah.
Ha.
It’s hilarious, really, that it took someone saying it outright for Yoshizawa to finally put two
and two together.
Akechi can’t stop as a short laugh bubbles past his lips, nor can he stop when several others
follow, until he’s doubled over, cackling, as Yoshizawa’s eyes widen in something that might
be fear.
Good.
He flips up his visor, still laughing, to flick away the tears that have formed in the corner of
his eyes.
“Would you look at that?” Akechi drawls, “You bet on a murderer. There’s an irony here,
somewhere, that you have the power of knowing what happens and still managed to fuck it
up.”
Yoshizawa opens her mouth, but Akechi cuts across her before she can talk.
“What was your game in confronting me here?” He snaps, “Appeal to my good will? Ask
politely that I stop? Kill me?” Yoshizawa looks horrified, and Akechi smirks, sharp as a
knife.
“No!” She exclaims, finally getting a word in, “I just want to hear your side to all of this. I
would never hurt you.” She insists, finding her spine.
Akechi covers his mouth as his shoulders start to shake again, “This is rich,” He spits through
wheezes, “Are you not even going to try and stop me? You remember how Okumura died last
time, right?” He sneers, “Unless the thieves are major fuckups, then that was all me.” His grin
turns sardonic, “So are you going to let me get away with it?”
Yoshizawa stares, shell-shocked, as Akechi draws his gun and points it between her eyes. She
stumbles back, eyes wide with alarm.

“Go on.” Akechi hisses, “Try and fight me. You can at least say you tried, when you lose.” A
lopsided grin pulls at his lips, “Unless, don’t tell me, are you really that loyal?” He barks
another laugh, “Do you really want to become an accessory to murder because of some deal?
Because of your misguided assumptions that we’re friends?”
Yoshizawa’s eyes flick towards the gun, then back to Akechi’s face, “We are friends,” she
says firmly, the waver in her voice betraying her lack of confidence.
“Sure.” Akechi says flatly, “And that will definitely stop me from pulling the trigger.”
Yoshizawa swallows, “Akechi, please, I just want you to tell me what’s happening.” She
shoots him a desperate look.
Akechi smiles, and lets Loki manifest, hovering behind him.
“What was your goal? Really?” Akechi snarls, “The thieves definitely figured me out last
time, they’d have to, if they took down Shido. So what stupid little part of your head looked
at how much they hated me and made you think that approaching me was your best choice?”
“They didn’t hate you!” Yoshizawa exclaims, “They didn’t hate you, so there’s no way
you’re all bad.” She takes a shaky breath, “You’re my friend- last time, and this time too.
So-”
Akechi tilts the gun and shoots at her feet, forcing her to jump back with a yelp, “Spare me.”
He growls, “I don’t give a shit. You won’t stop me, and you couldn’t if you tried.”
He sends Loki to crash his sword into the ground, causing Yoshizawa to jump even further
back.
She looks on the verge of tears, “Please, I-”
“Get the fuck out, and I might let you live,” Akechi hisses quietly.
Yoshizawa looks up, lips pressed together, and gives a shaky nod. She takes a few tentative
steps back, before dashing away, around a corner and out of sight.
Akechi clenches his jaw and bites his lip. He doesn’t move until he’s sure she’s gone.
Inexplicably, the Magician arcana reaches rank five.
As Akechi feels the bond grow stronger, he inhales sharply and throws his sword at the wall
of the tunnel with a shout.
Fuck, is that bond just going to sit there? A reminder of what he can never have?
Akechi looks inward, at the threads bundled like yarn, and muffles a scream as he nearly
breaks his fist on the tunnel wall.
Bonds would be his strength? What a fucking joke. What saccharine bullshit, preached by
those who have no idea what they’re talking about.

If his bonds don’t betray him, then he’ll betray them, because it’s the only thing he can do.
The only thing he’ll ever do, when presented with the choice.
It’s telling, Akechi scoffs to himself, that all of his bonds are either people who will no doubt
be collateral for his revenge, or the twisted scum who made his path necessary in the first
place.
The only exceptions are the things that aren’t human. And, well, even then.
The bundle of thread becomes taught wires yet again, and Akechi chokes,
Well, fine.
He’ll go back to how he’s always done it.
It doesn’t matter. He’s played the game perfectly before, and he can do it again.
This was a minor setback. That’s all.

Sumire reaches the top of Mementos, and collapses against the wall, sliding to the floor and
pulling her knees to her chest.
She should move. She needs to get out of Mementos before Akechi comes through here to
leave.
A sob wracks her chest, and she furiously wipes her eyes, trying to get it together.
“C’mon.” She whispers to herself, “C’mon Sumire, stop- crying.”
She sniffles some more, and tries not to think about how it’s all gone wrong.
She’s alone. Again. She’s accidentally chased Akechi away, because he wouldn’t even give
her a chance to try and explain herself.
He didn’t try to explain himself, either.
Sumire presses her hands together, frustrated. Is Akechi really so paranoid, that he would just
drop her the second that she tried to figure him out?
He even threatened to kill her, whichSumire, well, sheShe doesn’t buy it.
Maybe it’s wishful thinking. Maybe she’s being wilfully ignorant. But she doesn’t believe
that Akechi would have tried to kill her.

So, what? She thinks to herself. Does she just try to get through to Akechi again? Take a
gamble that she’s right? She… really can’t see that going well. Sumire doubts that he’ll kill
her, but he’s definitely not above beating her up.
She definitely can’t go to the thieves. They’ll think she’s the one killing people. She could
avoid that, maybe, by pointing the finger at Akechi, but Sumire’s trying to gain his trust, not
shatter it entirely.
She fells Ella buzz warmly, taking a stand.
Right. That’s right.
She doesn’t know if it’s the right thing to do, but she won’t give up on Akechi just yet. She
won’t throw him to the wolves just to make her life easier.
She can fix reality this way, or not at all.
Sumire thinks, and considers the time she has left.
January is definitely her cut off. She needs to have figured out what went wrong by then, and
either have already fixed it or know how to.
The thieves already have everything before January covered, she’s pretty sure. It was just
before Maruki’s calling card that Ren faltered.
But…
Even if the thieves have everything before January covered in theory, Sumire has definitely
altered events with Akechi. She doesn’t doubt that he’s important in the coming months, and
what if the thieves can’t handle that?
What if Akechi can’t handle that?
She needs to figure out a way to get through to him, quickly.
Sumire figures that her cut off for that is October, when Okumura dies. She doesn’t want
Haru to have to suffer that, and she thinks taking a body off the pile can only mean good
things for Akechi.
So, she has two deadlines. She can work with that.
She can’t make any progress on the October one just yet, but…
Sumire thinks again about what happened in early February, last time.
Why did Ren take the deal? He was so confident before. He promised Sumire, he promised
everyone that they’d all work together, that they wouldn’t falter in destroying the perfect lives
Maruki was offering them.
Through her spite and anger, Sumire can acknowledge that something doesn’t quite click.

Did Maruki offer him something? Manipulate him? Did he really falter at the last second for
no reason? Did he suddenly believe that everyone really would be better off in Maruki’s
reality? Ren didn’t even get a wish, soSumire stops.
Is that really true?
She, and everyone else, had assumed that because Ren was never taken under Maruki’s
delusions, he never had a wish. Sumire, while she still desperately clung to her life as
Kasumi, had been furious that Ren would try and drag her back to reality when he couldn’t
possibly understand what she was going through. She had snapped out of that, of course, but
what ifWhat if he didn’t understand, until Maruki told him exactly what he would be giving up?
That’s… a possibility.
But what would Ren wish for? What would he want so desperately that he would succumb to
the false reality?
We may have to spend some time with him. Ella points out.
Damnit.
Sumire huffs. If she has a goal, she can do it.
Easy. This will be easy. She just has to get Akechi to listen to her, and then figure out Ren’s
deepest and most secret desires.
Okay.
She just has to talk with them.

He has to say though, of all their post-heist celebrations, this one takes the cake. The buffet

It’s an absurd theory.
The suspicion doesn’t go away.

Ren frowns at the others serious tone, “What is it?” He asks softly.
“No matter what happens tomorrow, you won’t falter,” The other says sternly, “Whatever
bullshit gets thrown around, whatever tricks that madman tries to pull, promise you’ll still
fight this reality.”
Ren presses his lips together, and tries to figure out where this is coming from.
For lack of an answer, Ren smiles warmly, “I promise,” he says, and he’s sure he means it.
The other nods stiffly, “Good.”
And then, Ren snaps to the present, still asleep, and a lot of things suddenly fall into place.
Ren turns to stare at Crow, now in his Metaverse attire.
Crow folds his arms, and huffs, “What?”
“The jazz club,” Ren starts, “I saw it in one of these dreams,”
Crow gives him an unimpressed look, “Uh huh.”

“And the aquarium,” Ren says, thoughts going a mile a minute, “That got brought up in one
of these memories, too.”
“Congratulations on your observational skills,” Crow says dryly.
“Fuck off,” Ren glares, “I know who you are.”
A knife sharp smirk cuts across Crow’s face, “Oh? Do tell.”
“Akechi, right?” Ren steps forward, “He invited me to the aquarium, and he’s the one that
showed me the jazz club.”
Crow regards him for a moment, before spreading his arms out wide, “Guilty as charged,
Joker.”
Ren stares, reeling.
“But,” Ren starts, opening and closing his mouth, “You said you’re dead. Akechi’s not
dead.”
Crow shrugs, inspecting his hands.
Ren rolls his eyes, and keeps thinking aloud, “One of these memories happened in the attic,”
he continues, finishing the revelation that got cut short last dream, “But I’ve only ever been
in Leblanc’s attic this year, let alone lived there.”
“And?” Crow tilts his head, “What have you figured out?”
Ren tugs on his gloves, as his mind struggles to come to a conclusion- because it’s ridiculous,
what he’s thinking, completely impossible.
All of this is insane, but“Are these dreams… prophetic, or something?” Ren murmurs, “Are you supposed to be from
the future?” He looks at Crow.
“I don’t know. Are you a seer?” Crow says disinterestedly.
“Help me out here!” Ren snaps, “What, are you going to die in the future?”
“The future is hardly set in stone.” Crow says, finally looking up again, “But you’re still
missing something.”
Ren bites his lip, and wracks his brain for what the hell Crow could be talking about.
“The memory with the phone call, in the attic,” Ren says slowly, “You didn’t call me, in the
real world.”
Crow nods for him to continue.

Ren presses his lips together, “But, I don’t remember these dreams enough to have made that
kind of change, if the timeline’s set, or something.”
Crow folds his arms, still staying silent.
“So,” Ren cuts himself off. He huffs angrily, and throws up his hands, “You’re not helpful,
you know.”
“So I’ve been told,” Crow deadpans, “If you can’t figure it out, I can’t tell you.”
“Fuck, is it an alternate reality?” Ren says, running his hands through his hair, glaring as
Crow snorts, “You don’t get to laugh. You can’t tell me, or you won’t?”
“Is there a difference, given the nature of my existence?” Crow ponders aloud, unhelpfully.
“Right, cognition. Whatever.” Ren crosses his arms, frustrated, “You don’t act like Akechi.”
He points out.
“From what you’ve seen in reality, sure.” Crow hums, “But I’m your cognition based on
what you’re forgetting, so who’s really acting out of character?”
Ren shrugs, feeling petulant, “So basically, all these dreams are useless, because nothing that
happens in them is sure to happen in the real world.”
“Is that what you really think?” Crow says, contemplative.
Ren bites his lip. Is it?
These dreams aren’t prophetic, but his cognition is definitely implying that they’re important.
Akechi isn’t dead in reality, but could he be in danger? Is it up to Ren to save him, using the
knowledge granted from the Aeon?
A bit fucking difficult, Ren grouses, when he can’t remember any of this stuff when he wakes
up. The only thing these dreams have given him in the waking world are a series of vibes, and
a vague suspicion towards Yoshizawa that she might be the black mask.
Ren catches on that thought.
“Wait, fuck, are you the black mask?” Ren turns to Crow again.
“Haven’t you asked this before?” Crow sighs.
“Yeah, and you dodged the question by saying that you’re dead,” Ren narrows his eyes, “But
you aren’t, so you’re still a candidate.”
Crow shrugs, “My answer remains largely the same. There isn’t a monopoly on the colour of
someone’s Metaverse outfit. I could be one of many who happen to be sporting black masks.”
Ren scowls. That’s a valid point.

Crow chuckles, “What’s all this hostility, Joker? You seemed so torn up at the idea of my
death last time.”
Ren kicks at the floor, “I’m just,” he huffs, “Confused. About all of this.”
Trying to fit all of this together is like trying to do a puzzle without the corner pieces. And the
picture is just a flat colour. And there’s a thousand pieces.
And Ren’s blindfolded, too, just for good measure.
“I don’t want you to die.” Ren says softly. He dreaded the idea of Crow’s death before, but
now that Ren knows who he is- and he has a chance to avoid it?
He hopes he has a chance to avoid it.
“You’ll figure it out.” Crow murmurs, andAs the Aeon hits rank five, Ren wakes up, with no memory of his newfound resolve.

Chapter End Notes

Boy oh boy.
/Now/ that canon divergence is starting to hit. Sumire doesn't know much about the
thieves pre-Maruki, but she's /pretty/ sure this wasn't supposed to happen.
In regards to the door in Okumura's palace- though it's never stated in-game, I suspect
that there's another way to get around cognitive locks in palaces beyond meeting the
requirements or altering the ruler's cognition. I would assume that in canon, neither
Madarame nor Okumura would be thrilled about letting Akechi further into their
palaces, and yet he /definitely/ got pretty far into Okumura's, and it's implied he scouted
all of Madarame's.
The solution that I've made up here is essentially 'brute force', a method which the
thieves haven't thought to try, but Wakaba and Akechi definitely would have. I would
consider the downsides to such a method would be /drastically/ increasing the security
level in the palace, and maybe setting the real-world ruler on edge. Akechi would never
attempt brute force in a palace like Shido's- too much risk involved there.

opening and closing her mouth, thinking of what to say.
She can’t say that she should have seen this coming, because she doesn’t know how she
could have.
“…why is it that you want revenge?” Haru eventually asks, tentative.
Akechi looks like he’s about to snap at her, before he deflates, “…My mother, mostly.” He
admits quietly, “She… well. It’s not important.”
Haru hums softly, “I see.” She looks contemplative for a beat, “…Do you really want to be
doing this, or can you just not stop?”
Akechi narrows his eyes, “What?” He doesn’t really seem to be asking.
“Do you really not care, or do you not have a choice?” Haru continues anyway, ignoring the
warning laced in Akechi’s tone, “What are the consequences if you tried to quit?”
Akechi’s lip curls again, as he glares down at her.
Haru meets his gaze calmly, and nods, “So you’re trapped, then.”
“What the hell do you know?” Akechi spits, sneering, “Does it matter if I don’t have a
choice? It was always my choice to start this, and even if I could leave now, I wouldn’t.”
Sumire looks up at him pleadingly, “Is that really true? How old were you when you first…?”
Killed someone, she doesn’t say.
Akechi gets the idea anyway. “…Fifteen.” He says, not looking at her and quietly enough that
she almost doesn’t hear it.
Sumire shifts forward, “When you were fifteen, did you really want to become a murderer?”
Akechi just stares at her, face impassive once again.
Haru looks between them, back and forth, and her eyes gain a calculating gleam, “The way I
see it,” she starts, turning to Akechi, “Is that the faster you get your revenge, the faster you’ll
be free, right?”
Akechi blinks, “What?”

“So,” Haru continues, a smile spreading on her lips, “If Sumi-chan and I helped you, then

some bullshit-”
Haru cuts him off, “No, but we can figure out ways that you won’t have to kill as often, and
keep you safe while we’re at it.” She smiles up at him cheerfully.
Sumire nods quickly, trying to hide her shock, “Right!”
“We’re your friends, Akechi-kun,” Haru says seriously, standing up and taking a step

“So am I.” Sumire says confidently, quickly moving to stand beside Haru.
Akechi stares at both of them, shock and confusion painting his expression. He bites his lip,
and then scoffs at the ground, “…You’re both ridiculous.” He says softly.
Sumire beams, “Is that a yes, then?”
Akechi rolls his eyes, “Do whatever the hell you want.” He says flatly, and Sumire knows he
means yes.
“Wonderful!” Haru claps her hands together.
Akechi pinches the bridge of his nose, exasperation catching up to him, “How do you even
plan on doing anything? You don’t know anything about the Metaverse, and neither of you
know anything about the inner workings of the conspiracy.”
Haru’s smile is unabating, “Well, that’s where you and Sumi-chan come in! I’m sure we can
all share our knowledge.” Akechi shoots her a glare, and she barely blinks.
Sumire pauses, “Also, wow, a whole conspiracy?”
“Having second thoughts?” Akechi deadpans, resigned, like he already knows the answer.
Sumire grins, “Not a chance!”
Akechi sighs wearily, “I’m starting to get that, yes.”
Sumire huffs a delighted laugh. She’s practically on cloud nine after how well this went in
comparison to last time.
She fixed her mistake. She’s got Haru on her side. She can help.
Haru speaks up, “Well! It’s getting late, and we’re all tired, so how about we head home, and
meet up soon to discuss more?”

Sumire nods gratefully, aware of how late it’s getting, “That sounds good! Oh, and Harusenpai, you can leave the Metaverse with the app that should have just appeared on your
phone.”
Haru blinks, “An app?” She takes her phone out of her pocket and scans the homepage,
“Oh!” She exclaims, “There is one here. How strange, another world accessed through a
phone app… “
“Yes, yes,” Akechi cuts across, waving his hand dismissively, “it’s all very weird. I’ll be
leaving, now.”
Sumire gives him a sympathetic glance, “Tired?”
“Fucking exhausted.” Akechi says, turning on his heel and stalking off.
(Meanwhile, in Akechi’s mind, he hears the breaking of chains,
I am thou, thou art I
Thou hast acquired a new bond.
It will lead thee closer to freedom, by traversing the hidden depths of one’s soul.
Through the forging of the Fool arcana, thou hast gained a glimpse of the power of rebellion,
and hast begun to uncover thine own truth.
When the world settles back into place, he’s confused, at first.
The Fool? With who? He already has the Magician and Strength with Sumire and Haru
respectively, so who could this represent?
He gives the bond an experimental tug, and raises his eyebrows at the veritable chord he gets
back in response.
The three of them, then.
He smirks wryly to himself. The Fool, hm?)

While Akechi makes his way through the top layer of Mementos, he hears a voice call out
after him.
“Akechi-kun!” Haru calls, jogging after him.
Akechi sighs, and turns around. “Is there a reason you’ve chased after me now, Haru-san,

sound too curt, despite having given up on his mask of pleasantries.

Haru giggles, apparently amused by his attempts, “I just wanted to continue our conversation
from when you helped me buy gardening supplies.”
Akechi raises an eyebrow, “Oh? I was under the impression that you hated that particular

“Well, I was a bit uncomfortable when you pushed it.” Haru admits, wringing her hands

Was he? A good question.
There was a part of him, maybe, that felt… averse to the idea that he would have to hurt Haru

(Maybe, a part of him thought that if he made her realise she’d be better off, then the wound

Haru lets out a sad laugh, “Isn’t it? I didn’t care what my father had become, until I realised

Akechi cocks an eyebrow, “Do you?”
Haru’s steel deflates slightly, “Hm?”

Akechi scoffs, “Then why?”
Haru hums, considering, “If you have to have a reason for it,” She says slowly, “then think of

Haru frowns, and looks to be lost in thought, “…I would be upset, if you did that.” She says

Akechi shrugs. “You can try.”

Akechi snorts, “Tell me about it. I was lost as hell when I first awakened my personas.”
“Personas?” Haru cocks her head, looking confused.

Haru clasps her hands together, “They sound very cool!” She exclaims, sounding entirely

Haru’s smile turns sharp, and a little smug, “Well, I think I got the gist that there was more to

“Ah.” Akechi says dispassionately, “I must be slipping.”
Haru giggles, “I like this side of you, though.” She says as her cheer dies down, “I think

Akechi finds that unlikely. Sumire and Haru are just weird. “…Perhaps.” He says anyway, to
placate her.
He can feel the Strength reach rank four in his chest.
Haru gives him a soft look, like she knows he doesn’t believe her, “Well, anyway,” She says,
“I should probably head back. It’s rather late.”
Akechi nods stiffly, “Yes.” He throws up a wave, “I’ll see you later, Haru-san.”
Haru returns the wave, “You too, Akechi-kun.”

The day after, Akechi still feels restless.
How could he not, with everything that has been revealed against his will?
He thinks that both Sumire and Haru are absolute fools for simply nodding and smiling at the
revelation that he’s a literal murderer.
The concept of taking someone else’s life doesn’t shock him, or ignite a sense of dread like it
used to. That stopped happening a long time ago. That doesn’t explain why Haru and Sumire
are so desensitised, though.
They’d probably take a hint if they ever saw what happened to the people Akechi killed in
person, or if he killed someone close to them.
Perhaps Haru was right in her insights- maybe it’s their selfishness that allows them to sleep
soundly at night, despite having just damned themselves to being accomplices.
Akechi can’t quite comprehend why they would choose Akechi over literally any other
option, but he supposes that at some point he should stop complaining.
You won’t. Robin assures him dryly.
He won’t.
But, he can’t lie that with the new addition of the Fool arcana to his repertoire, he’s felt
calmer than he has in weeks. The newly spun thread holds all the others together, twisting
them in an orderly bundle, laying the foundations.
For what? The more conscious part of his brain asks. He gets no answers.
Akechi huffs to himself as he jogs down the steps of Mementos, waiting until he’s further in
to start pulling on the Star arcana.
He sits on the corner of one of the platforms, waiting, and doesn’t look up when he hears the
telltale sounds of José’s car, hauling stars and trinkets on its back.
“Oh, Mister!” José exclaims, jumping down from the driver’s seat, “It’s been a while! Are
you feeling better?”
Akechi narrows his eyes at the question, “What?”
“Well last time we talked to each other, you seemed really angry,” José points out matter-offactly.
Ah, right. The last time Akechi spoke to José would have been just after he formed the Devil
arcana. He’s still not happy about that.

“And then,” José continues over Akechi’s thoughts, “I could feel you trying to push your
bonds away.” He laughs, “Well, I could feel you trying to push my bond away, but I couldn’t
think of any reason that I would have upset you, so I assumed you were doing it to
everyone.”
Akechi snorts. “That’s a rather simplistic assumption to make.”
José frowns, “But if I didn’t do anything to upset you, then why would you only be mad at
me?”
Akechi shrugs, “Human emotions aren’t quite as neat and tidy as you’re attempting to
categorise them as. Though,” he continues, when José looks downcast, “Your assumption was
correct, this time.”
José brightens, “Oh! I’m glad I got it right!” He scratches his head, “Humans sure are
complicated, though. Every time I learn something more, I just get more confused. How do
you humans all understand each other?”
“We don’t.” Akechi says flatly, “We think we understand things, but we’re all just as clueless
as you.”
José hums contemplatively, “Then… if you can’t understand each other, can you at least
understand yourself, Mister?”
Akechi goes to respond with a resounding ‘yes’, before he cuts himself off. He would argue,
ordinarily, that persona-users, by nature, have a far stronger sense of self than the average
person. Their core being is condensed into one representation, drawn equally from their own
heart and the hearts of the collective unconscious.
But, well, Akechi doesn’t have one persona. His soul didn’t even have the decency to awaken
at different times, so that he could at the very least attribute the fractured aspects of himself
to distinct parts of his life.
But, no. He has Robin Hood and Loki, who both want revenge and justice in equal measure,
and they can’t even be consistent about it.
WHERE’S THE FUN IN BEING PREDICTABLE?
We would be consistent if you only deigned to listen.
Case and point.
Akechi wonders if Amamiya has the same problem, with his veritable menagerie of personas.
“No.” Akechi eventually admits. “I don’t.”
“Oh.” José frowns. “I guess you are a wildcard. So it makes sense that you might have
trouble wrapping your head around all that potential.”

“I’m really not feeling the effects of this so-called ‘potential’.” Akechi says dryly, “The only
thing these bonds have really given me is heartburn, so far.”
“Oh, well, that’s because you’re supposed to use it for-” José cuts himself off with a frown,
“Huh. I… can’t remember?”
Akechi resists the urge to roll his eyes. These extra-dimensional beings have a habit of being
spectacularly unhelpful. “Well, tell me if you ever remember.” Akechi says.
José nods cheerfully, “Will do, Mister!” He squints in Akechi’s general direction, “But, hey,
you’ve really started collecting those things! You’ve even picked up the Fool!”
Akechi raises his eyebrows at that, “Is there some kind of significance to the Fool arcana in
particular?”
“Well, the Fool represents beginnings,” José explains, “It’s really important for wildcards,
since, you know, ‘Fool’s Journey’, and all that. So it’s kind of weird that it took you so long
to get it. But, it means that your journey has finally begun! This one, at least.”
“I see.” Akechi says with a huff. Fate has a funny sense of humour, if it’s decided that
Akechi’s journey has only begun now, three years down the line, once he’s picked up a
couple of idiotic accomplices.
He wonders what the Velvet Room’s opinion of all this is. Nothing good, he assumes, since
they’re the ones that have so vehemently insisted he ignore the arcana to begin with.
It’s ill advised, but Akechi finds himself trusting José’s information more than the Velvet
Room’s by a wide margin- if only because of the hum of the Star, that grows to rank four as
he thinks about it.
José smiles brightly, “Hey! We just got closer. You’re making some pretty good progress on
strengthening your bonds, too.”
“I aim to overachieve.” Akechi deadpans, and stands up to leave.
“You’re leaving?” José tilts his head, and then gives a big wave, “Well, see you later, Mister!
I’ll tell you if I remember what those bonds are for specifically.”
“Glad to hear it.” Akechi nods, and begins walking back to the entrance of Mementos.
He sighs to himself. One of these days, he’s going to have to stop pretending he’s even trying
to push these people away anymore.

Ren stares at the dead woman currently happily chatting away with her daughter.
This is insane. He probably should have seen this coming, what with everyone acting strange
at the shrine. But, even then, who the hell expects dead people to just start walking around
again like nothing’s wrong?

No one’s even acknowledging it. Just cheerfully bantering over new year’s food and coffee.
The last, and only, time that Ren ever saw Wakaba was-In the battle at the top of Futaba’s pyramid, which Ren snaps back to when he gets a side full
of sphinx paw, knocking him to the ground.
“Joker!” Morgana calls out.
“M’fine,” Ren grunts over the sounds of battle.
“Don’t lose focus!” Makoto shouts, emptying the rest of her bullets into the sphinx’s wings.
Ren hisses as he hauls himself back to his feet, “Right,” he says, trying to play it off, “Sorry.”
That’s concerning, Ren thinks as he dodges a blast of wind. It’s been a while since one of
these visions has caught him at a bad time, or been distracting enough to throw him off while
he’s in the Metaverse.
And its contents, too. The exact details of these visions often flit through his mind quite
rapidly, conveying the emotion more than the scenario.
Dread, understanding, sorrow, fear- those kinds of emotions more often than not.
And that’s nothing to say on his dreams that he’s sure are linked to the Aeon.
But this vision? This vision was rather forthcoming on what it was trying to convey- Wakaba
Isshiki having a cheerful discussion with Futaba at Leblanc.
Which is absolute nonsense, because Wakaba has been dead for two years, and staring up at
the circling sphinx above them is the first time that Ren has ever seen the woman’s face.
Are the visions just that, then? Complete nonsense? Should Ren forgo the assumption that
these are related to the Metaverse and actually ask Takemi to give him some diagnosis for
oddly specific hallucinations?
Yeah, he doubts that one, he thinks, as he feels the Aeon’s pull. It almost feels as though it’s
asking Ren to give it attention, which pulls a short laugh to his lips as he dodges another slam
from the sphinx’s paw.
He’ll have to ask the Velvet Room. They had nothing to say last time he asked about weird
visions, but maybe the addition of a new and mysterious bond will loosen up their lips.

When Futaba crumples back into the real world after speedrunning her personal growth, she

She can feel the pleasant buzz of Necronomicon as she slowly drifts off, not even bothering

What? She whines internally. She’s in the real world, there’s no shadows here, she’s fineAnother ping.

That’s…
Futaba can’t be sure, but…

But now that her shadow has morphed into her persona, she gets a whole healthy heaping of

She gets a whole lot of the warm fuzzies from when the thieves probably insisted to her

Weird.
Well, Futaba thinks as the grip of sleep begins to claim her again, she’ll bring it up later.

Chapter Summary

The Velvet Room makes a move, and the black masks hash some things out.

Chapter Notes

Ren blinks.
He’s surprised, for a beat, because he’s pretty sure his eyes were closed just a second ago, and
it’s pretty hard to blink when your eyes are already closed. He stares up at the ceiling and
takes in the familiar velvet blue, and lets out a small sigh at the sound of chains that start to
filter in, and resigns himself to having to sit up.
He really needed that sleep, too. Well, at least he has the opportunity to ask some questionsassuming Igor lets him get a word in, that is.
“Trickster,” Igor starts, already a bad sign, “How fares your thievery?”
“Just fine.” Ren grumbles as he hauls himself to his feet, “Thieving’s great. I, uh, had some
questions actually.”
“Our purpose is to further your rehabilitation,” Justine explains dispassionately, “We will do
our utmost to aid you if necessary.”
“Unless your question is really dumb!” Caroline cuts in, “Sometimes stupidity can’t be cured,
inmate.”
Ren graciously doesn’t point out exactly how forthcoming, or lack thereof, the Velvet Room
has been with information in the past.
“Yeah, great,” he says instead, “So, remember how I asked about weird visions I’ve been
having before?”
“I do recall.” Igor says.

“Well,” Ren rubs the back of his neck, “They keep happening. A lot. And I’ve been getting
dreams too.”
“We already told you we have no idea what you’re talking about!” Caroline snaps.
Justine flips through clipboard, “Perhaps you should seek the counsel of one of your world’s
‘general practitioners’.”
Ren resists the urge to roll his eyes. Asking Takemi for help is definitely a last resort, in his
book. He doesn’t need the woman thinking he’s more insane than she already does.
“Yeah, okay.” Ren bites his lip, “But… I think they’re linked to this weird bond that I have?
The Aeon.”
Igor’s eyes widen, somehow, and for a beat Ren is afraid they’re going to tumble right out of
his head. He lets out a low hum, while the twins exchange confused glances.
“The Aeon,” Igor starts, “Synonymous with the Judgement, in some decks. When drawn, the
card calls for understanding and reflection of the path taken, and truths yet uncovered.” He
laughs, “A fascinating development, indeed.”
“Do you know who it belongs to?” Ren pushes, leaning forward, “I can tell who all my other
bonds represent, but this one always comes up empty.”
“You can’t tell who it belongs to?” Justine murmurs, looking confused.
An uncharacteristically contemplative expression passes on Caroline’s face, “That’s…”
“You would do well to be wary of this particular bond, trickster.” Igor declares, tapping his
fingers rhythmically on his desk, “For this arcana, normally so intwined with uncovering
truths, to be so shrouded in mystery- I can only portend that it may hold disaster, and a key to
ruin.”
Ren’s eyes narrow of their own volition. Be wary of this bond in particular? It seems
counterintuitive, when all the Velvet Room has preached in the past is to grow his bonds, and
whatnot. And- doesn’t it make sense for a bond about seeking truth to be confusing and
mysterious at first? Ren wants answers, sure, but he has to concede that from what Igor is
telling him, being left in the dark sounds particularly on brand for this arcana.
There’s a small pull from the Aeon in his chest, and Ren supresses a twitch in his lips.
Ren looks between the twins, who are both in the middle of having a conversation with facial
expressions alone. This isn’t the first time that the twins and Igor seem to have conflicting
knowledge, Ren thinks, as he remembers how the Strength has been progressing so far.
Huh.
Ren quietly resolves to disregard Igor’s advice.
“Got it,” Ren lies, “I’ll try and avoid it.”

Igor nods, satisfied, while Justine shifts.
“Your rank with the Aeon is almost halfway to completion.” She says, “How is it that you’ve
been strengthening it, without having any knowledge of who it belongs to?”
Ren shrugs, not wanting to reveal too much in front of Igor, “Sometimes I’ll wake up, and I
can feel that the bond has gotten a bit stronger. I’m not really doing anything.”
“Huh.” Caroline frowns.
“Girls?” Igor interrupts, “What is the matter?”
“Nothing, master.” Justine says blithely, going back to flipping through her clipboard.
Ren smiles to himself at the further confirmation that the twins are probably on his side. He
reaches up and tugs at his bangs, “Uh. Is that all?”
“Show some respect!” Caroline snaps, banging her baton on the bars. Okay, maybe they’re
not completely on his side.
“Rest well, trickster,” Ren hears Igor say as his vision fades.
***
In the same space, but also somewhere else entirely, Akechi opens his eyes to find himself
standing again within a blue-tinted courtroom.
He rolls his eyes. Great. Wonderful. He assumes that he’s going to get a lecture on the danger
of letting bonds into his heart, like he can control it in the slightest.
Akechi pastes on his nicest, fakest, smile and waits for Igor to begin his spiel.
“You have certainly done well to ignore our warnings, trickster.” Igor starts, voice booming
from his position on the judge’s plinth.
Akechi shrugs. He eyes where the twins stand behind the prosecutor’s desk. Usually, one of
them would have chimed in with words of assent by now. He raises an eyebrow when he sees
them both looking unusually stoic. Do they really believe his actions that serious? Or is it
something else?
“Well,” Akechi starts, “I’m weighing my options.”
“Once the bonds have taken root in your heart, it’s already too late.” Igor continues, “By
‘weighing your options’, as you say, you have chained your strength to those with fickle
goals and whims.”
Akechi chooses to ignore the part of him that agrees, for now. “I have also aligned myself
with those who are willing to help further my goals,” for whatever reason, “And I’ve yet to
see a correlation between my ‘strength’ and my bonds.” A statement which, of course, goes
both ways, but that’s hardly the point Akechi’s trying to make at the moment.

He sees the twins both make a face in the corner of his eye, while Igor continues like Akechi
never spoke at all, “I see you have acquired the Fool. You should know that this bond will
only restrict your path to the desires of those it represents.”
Akechi hums, “I’m sure.”
“You should listen to our master, defendant!” Buns finally snaps, “Don’t act like you know
better!”
“And what do you think?” Akechi turns to the twins, acting on a sudden hunch, “About the
arcana?”
“That is irrelevant,” Braids says flatly, “We in this room exist to serve your purposes. You
should heed our advice, when it is given.”
Akechi pointedly doesn’t react to her words. It is unlikely, he thinks, that they truly ‘exist to
serve’, or whatever other bullshit they want to peddle, when they take the metaphorical role
of prosecutors and judge against his defence.
The Velvet Room was never really this pushy before he started picking up the arcana. Their
visits to his dreams were few and far between, and they only spouted the same rotating set of
speeches- ‘don’t falter in order to avoid ruin,’ and whatnot.
Akechi has resolutely ignored the doors at the entrances to Mementos and palaces, too. He
entered one of them once, a few years ago, and when he found that it was just a one-wayticket to get talked at for ten minutes, never entered them again.
There’s no information that he requires from the Velvet Room, and if these dreams are any
indication, there’s really not a lot they need from him, either.
They only seem to care when he actively disobeys their vague advice- and, even then…
It is interesting, that the twins seemed to dodge the question.
“Well, I suppose that’s that, then.” Akechi says in a chipper voice, “Anything else to add?”
Buns rolls her eyes, “We wouldn’t have had to have this conversation at all if you had just
listened the first time, defendant.”
Then he’ll probably have to endure this conversation again, Akechi thinks, not particularly in
the mood to bend to the will of a bunch of strange beings with unknows agendas. He nods
blandly, anyway.
“Until next time, trickster.” Igor says, as Akechi feels the tug of sleep yet again.

Sumire hits the Nav on her phone, shifting into Mementos.
“Oh!” A voice exclaims at her side.

“Haru-senpai!” Sumire starts, “Did you just get here as well?”
Haru shakes her head, “Oh, no, I got here a few minutes ago, but I wasn’t quite sure where to
go.” She readjusts her hair sheepishly, “So I thought I’d just wait here for you or Akechi-kun
to show up.”
Sumire nods, “Well, I’m here! Let’s get going then.”
Haru smiles, “Wonderful. Um, where are we headed, exactly?”
“Oh, we’ll be going into Mementos proper.” Sumire explains as she starts walking.
Haru matches her step, “’Proper’? Does that mean there’s more to this place?”
“Yes, this above ground section isn’t really…” Sumire purses her lips together, “Well, it is
Mementos, but it’s all the above ground stuff, so it just looks like regular Tokyo, but without
all the people.”
Haru’s eyes widen, “Above ground?”
“All the interesting bits of Mementos are actually in the subway tunnels.” Sumire points at

Haru nods slowly, and jumps as her Metaverse outfit burns into place. She readjusts her hat,
“Well, I guess that’s as good a sign as any.”
Sumire taps her cognitively adjusted heels into place, “Yep! Though, that’s, uh, not quite
what I meant.”
Haru gives her a confused look, before she winces as the pulsing red veins signature to
Mementos come into view. “Oh…” She murmurs, looking lightly disgusted.
“Yeah…” Sumire commiserates.
“Took you both long enough.” An icy voice cuts in.
Sumire whips around, and breaks into a smile and a cheerful wave, “Hello, Akechi.”
Akechi scoffs, and Sumire assumes that he rolls his eyes beneath his helmet, “No need for

“I disagree,” Haru says, a strained smile spreading across her face, “I think being as pleasant

you’ll have to take it up with the collective unconsciousness of Tokyo.”
Haru giggles, “I’ll get on that, then.”

Haru nods slowly, “I see…”
Akechi turns back to the group, and shrugs, “I would say more, but someone has yet to

Whoops. She did promise to do that, didn’t she? “Uh. Sorry. I can get on that now…?”

Akechi cocks his head, “Are you really surprised?” He drawls.

Haru is successfully distracted, as she perks up, confusion painting her face, “And this

Sumire shakes her head, “Well, it’s usually in the centre of a palace, so really heavily

Sumire blinks, caught off guard, “Uh! I spied on the thieves for a bit when I first awakened

Haru gasps softly, “Does that mean you know who they are?”
Behind his visor, Sumire can see Akechi’s eyes dart to Haru before he continues walking in a
show of practiced nonchalance, “About that.”
Sumire laughs uncomfortable, “Um, yes. Do you remember the people we ran into at the

Haru stares at her, uncomprehending. When Sumire doesn’t elaborate, she blinks slowly, as
understanding dawns on her face. “…Seriously?” She mutters, resigned.
Akechi snorts, “I’m as amazed as you. Not that they’re stupid enough to be vigilantes- more
that they’ve yet to be caught.”
Sumire tilts her head, “…Aren’t you the detective on the case?”
“And isn’t your revenge plot kind of a form of vigilantism?” Haru chimes in.
Akechi stops walking abruptly. “Shut up.” He says in a low growl, and stalks off again,
movements stiff.
Sumire hides her smile behind her hand.
Haru giggles softly, before she recomposes herself. “I really can’t believe it…” she murmurs,
“I mean, Niijima-san? She always seemed so…”

“Stuck up?” Akechi offers, “Bending over backwards to accommodate the whims of

Sumire winces slightly. She wants to protest, but she does remember how quickly Makoto

Sumire blurts, no longer able to keep quiet about the absurdity of all this.
As is the case with a lot of the things that have come up this year, she probably shouldn’t be

Akechi gives her a look, like he’s asking why she’s surprised, “It’s a lot less shocking when

Sumire frowns, “So why does Shido even keep you around, then?” She realises as she says it

Sumire nods. Right, of course- Akechi isn’t just an assassin. She isn’t sure if that’s better or
worse, but at least not all of the things he has to do involve murder. It still doesn’t sit great

targets have or will end up dead.
(She mentally kicks herself, at that. She thinks that she shouldn’t be settling for ‘good
enough’, when she’s the only person in the world who knows bits and pieces of the future.
She just doesn’t know what to do,)

Haru nods placatingly, “Right, you did.” She frowns, “What is your plan, exactly? What’s

Akechi nods, “Something like that, I’d say.”

Haru hops off the bench delicately, “Me too… if my father is part of the conspiracy, then I’ll

This entire situation is a mess- Sumire knew this even before she knew the severity of it. She

If it ended badly, she thinks she might have spent way too long panicking and throwing
herself into self-fulfilling prophecy by trying to avoid what she may have perceived as ‘set

Of course, now she’s just panicking because she has no idea what she’s supposed to be doing.
But she can fix this. Both Haru and Akechi are smart- they’ll know what to do, even when
she hits a dead end.
…But what is it that she can do?
Sumire feels nervous that she’s yet to encounter anything to do with why she was sent back in

At some point during the night, not so long after he met with Haru and Sumire, Akechi
dreams.
Akechi glares down at the other boy, stiffly folding his arms as he waits for a response.
Fuck, this is what Akechi was afraid of. Of course the fate of the entire world is being left in
the hands of a teenager- because he’s just so special. Of course Akechi has to stand here and
beg, because he doesn’t even get to decide whether he lives or dies.
He’s not even real, and still, the other looks like the world is ending.
Which it will, if the boy is as much of a fucking moron as he’s making himself out to be with
this display.

“I want to hear you say it aloud,” Akechi eventually says, keeping his voice as level as
possible, “What do you intend to do?”
The other boy pales further, opening and closing his mouth like he’s choking on air. Akechi
presses his lips together in a sneer, and waits. He slowly breathes in the smell of coffee and
curry, directing his thoughts anywhere but what the hell he’s going to do if the other takes the
deal.
Will it hurt, to be tugged around on strings for the rest of his existence, so long as the other
wishes it? Will the madman let him have some semblance of himself, or will his insides be
scraped out and replaced with something more palatable?
Who is he kidding? Of course he won’t be allowed to exist as he is. He’s too much of a danger
to the sanctity of this reality- he’d tear it apart the second he got the chance, should he
remember that he’s trapped.
And, most importantly, there is no chance that Goro Akechi can truly exist in a perfect reality.
So, there’s that.
If only the other could see that, too- but instead he looks like he’s genuinely considering
taking this fucking deal.
“Are you going to answer?” Akechi drawls.
The other boy finally looks up, “Can you not give me one fucking second to think about
this?” He says, voice wobbling.
Akechi scoffs, “You’ve had one. Shall we repeat everything that’s already been said? You
have nothing to gain by taking this deal. You’d be betraying everyone, and for what?”
The other boy’s face twists, “’Nothing to gain’? Are you fucking kidding?” He takes a step
forward, and Akechi takes a step back.
“Have I been known to joke?” Akechi says lightly, then scowls, “That seems more your
prerogative. I have to say though, you’ve lost your touch. This farce isn’t very funny.”
The other looks to stop listening halfway through, looking back down at the floor with glassy
eyes.
“Shit,” The other chokes out wetly, “Fuck- Akechi, why didn’t you tell me?” His gestures
violently, “We could have figured this out!” He shouts.
“Figured what out, Joker?” Akechi hisses, “There’s nothing we can do.”
“Like hell there isn’t!” The other spits, and runs a hand through his hair roughly.
Akechi rolls his eyes. “Give it up, would you?” He snarls, “I get that your little complex
can’t handle the idea that you couldn’t save everyone, but you need to let this go.”

“God, fuck you.” The other says in nearly a whisper, “What is it about this that’s so hard for
you to understand?”
“There’s nothing to understand,” Akechi shoves his hand into his pockets, trying to make the
action seem final, “Now what are you going to do?”
“No, nonono, no, I can’t-” The other takes in a shuddering breath, “This isn’t fucking fair- I
thought,” He bites his lip, “Shit, I thought everything was going to be okay,”
“This is the real world, Joker.” Akechi says quietly, “Not everything works out.”
The other looks up sharply at that. “But it could.”
Akechi feels like he’s been plunged into ice, “Joker, don’t you fucking dare.”
“What?” The other challenges, something flashing in his eyes, “Don’t what?”
“Don’t trap me here.” Akechi snarls, taking a step forward. The other stands his ground.
The boy laughs weakly, “You really don’t get it, huh?”
“No, I don’t fucking understand why you’re hesitating- when you were perfectly fine
destroying this reality just yesterday!” Akechi runs a hand through his hair, “You-” he takes
a sharp breath, trying to steady himself, “Goddamnit, you promised!”
The other flinches, and tears start to well in his eyes again, “…I-” he cuts off, shaking.
“Joker.” Akechi says taking another step forward. He places his hands on the sides of the
other’s face, tilting his head up to look him in the eye, “You know what you have to do. There
is no choice here.”
The other blinks slowly, mouth slightly parted, before he swallows, and grimaces. “You’re
right.” He says softly, “There isn’t.” He tentatively places his hands over where Akechi’s are
resting, “I’m taking the deal.”
Akechi rips his hands away like he’s been burned. His instinct is to lash out, scream and claw
and shout until the other takes a fucking hint and makes the right choice.
But Akechi knows that won’t work.
He laughs bitterly, “Well, I have your answer.” The other has the good sense to look
ashamed. Akechi turns on his heel to leave. When he reaches the door, he looks over his
shoulder, “Our deal’s off.” His eyes flick downward, “I hope you know I’ll never forgive you
for this.”
He doesn’t give the other a chance to respond as he slams the door behind him, drowning out
the sound of the tinkling bell.
Fuck.

No. No, he can’t accept this. He won’t accept this.
He doesn’t need everyone else to do this.
Reality shifts and shimmers, and distantly Akechi can’t tell if it’s the dream or the vision that
swirls his sight.
He can see a towering structure, blinding white and clinical, andAkechi wakes up.
He sits up, fast as a bullet, clutching at his chest as he coughs violently.
He tugs at his hair, trying to centre himself as his vision blurs. He blinks rapidly, trying to
clear the kaleidoscopic colours that painted the end of his vivid dreamAs Akechi has that thought, he realises that the details have already slipped his mind.
God fucking damnit.
Akechi sighs heavily, scraping a hand down his face. Even if the details evade him, he still
remembers that he had a troubling dream- though that’s not really anything particularly new.
He half-heartedly scrounges for anything he could possibly recall, andHis bonds twist, and a butterfly net manages to snag whisps of smoke.
He remembers coffee. Or the smell of it, more accurately. Warm and rich, and definitely
better than anything he’s ever had before.
He remembers a knife to the back, though he can’t quite tell if it’s literal or metaphorical.
Who knows, maybe it’s both? That does sound like his luck.
He remembers glittering silver, pristine enough to be blinding, shifting in manufactured
imperfection.
What a pleasant dream. If he could remember it properly, he’s sure that he would hate it.
Akechi bites his lip. There are little fragments of something that keep filtering into his mind,
as of late. As of about April, he’d say if he had to hazard a guess.
April? Didn’t Sumire say that…?
Akechi bites his lip harder. Now that’s a thought. Between his visions and weird dreamsnone of them paint a very coherent picture. But they wouldn’t have to, if they’re whispers
from a year erased.
Didn’t José say something about how wildcards are usually chosen for all this time travel
business? What if he has a leg-up on remembering things because of that? If that’s what’s
happening at all, of course.

Akechi wonders if Amamiya might be experiencing something similar. That would be…
inconvenient, if that’s true. Akechi has revenge he needs to fulfill, and he doesn’t need yet
another roadblock.
Akechi flops back down, glaring up at the ceiling. He should ask Sumire more about all of
this.

Akechi almost does a double take when he see Amamiya standing outside of Penguin Sniper,
in the exact spot that Akechi himself tends to loiter at.
“Amamiya.” He says amicably, walking up to the other boy, “What are you doing here?”
Amamiya jumps at Akechi’s voice, head snapping up, “Uh.” He starts, “I wanted to spend
time with you, actually.” He rubs the back of his neck sheepishly, “You weren’t here, though,
so I thought I’d wait around to see if you’d show up.”
Akechi cocks an eyebrow, “Couldn’t you have texted me?”
Amamiya flushes, “I guess I didn’t think of that?”
Akechi chuckles politely, masking the rougher bark of laughter that attempts to claw its way
up his throat. He smooths out his smirk, “Well, I’m free right now. Is there anywhere you had
in mind?”
Amamiya hums contemplatively, and twists his fringe between his fingers, “Not really. How
about…” His lips quirk as he thinks, “Inokashira park is nearby, right? We could take a
walk?”
Akechi tilts his head, “It’s rather dark out.”
Amamiya gives a small grin, “I think we’ll be fine if we’re together.”
“Famous last words, Amamiya,” Akechi says with a teasing smile, “But I suppose I agree.
Inokashira sounds nice.”
“Great,” Amamiya nods, looking more cheerful, “Lets go, then.”

As they make their way to the train station, Akechi notes the lack of nasal whining that
usually follows Amamiya around and quips at random intervals. He gestures to Amamiya’s
currently empty side bag, “No cat today?”
Amamiya blinks, “Oh, no. I left him at home.”
Akechi guesses that the other boy wasn’t in any rush to hear the cat complain about his
choice of companion tonight, for which Akechi is somewhat grateful. That doesn’t mean he
can’t be a shit about it, though, “I thought you said he had separation anxiety?”
Amamiya takes it in stride, grinning, “Yeah, but he seems to get over it whenever I give him
some fatty tuna.”
“That must be hell on your wallet.” Akechi comments, tilting his head.
Amamiya sighs wearily, “It sure is.”
Their banter trails off as they step onto the train, only waiting around for a few stops to then
get off at Inokashira park. Amamiya takes point, quickly moving forward in the direction of

taking the lead like Akechi’s never been here before.
Eventually, they reach the footpath that snakes through the park, shadowed oddly by the
combination of dense trees and glowing streetlights.
Akechi falls into step with Amamiya. “Did you have anything that you wanted to speak about
in particular?” He asks off handedly.
Amamiya looks straight ahead, pressing his lips together sheepishly, “Um, not really.” He
laughs awkwardly, “I just… wanted to see you, I guess.”
Akechi hums dispassionately. “Well, here I am.”
“Here you are.” Amamiya agrees.
…This is one big waste of time, isn’t it? Though, Akechi supposes that’s what friends do.
His stomach violently curdles at the idea that he and Amamiya could be considered friends.
He’s resolved to avoid killing him, sure- but Akechi barely considers Sumire and Haru
friends, and they looked him in the eye and said they’re down with murder.
Don’t you enjoy his company? Robin hums smugly, knowing full well what the answer is,
even if Akechi refuses to vocalise it.
But that’s hardly the point, Akechi thinks. Even if he doesn’t want Amamiya dead anymore
(Something whispers that he never wanted him dead), Akechi still has no intention of letting
Amamiya and his merry band of idiots get anywhere near Shido, and he’s more than willing
to do whatever it takes.
YOU DON’T SOUND CONFIDENT.

“How have your summer holidays been?” Akechi says abruptly, both to fill the silence and to
cover how close he is to snapping at the voices in his head.
Amamiya shrugs, “Busy. I’ve been spending a lot of time helping out a friend.” He twirls his
fringe between his fingers, and Akechi doesn’t bother to speculate on what he means, “…
How about you?”
Akechi chuckles, “I’ve been busy as well, I’m afraid.”
Amamiya gives a small smile, “Work? All that Medjed stuff is still going on, right?”
Akechi nods, “Yes. We’ve yet to find a solution, short of the thieves just turning themselves
in.”
Amamiya frowns, like he isn’t the problem, “That sucks. I hope it all turns out.”
“I hope so, as well.” Akechi says.
They walk in silence for a while, before Amamiya cracks, “…Have you been up to anything
else?” He asks awkwardly.
Akechi gestures vaguely, “Not anything of note.” He huffs to himself, “…Though, I’ve begun
to acknowledge how persistent some of my… associates are.”
Amamiya cocks an eyebrow, a teasing grin spreading on his lips, “‘Associates’?”
Akechi doesn’t appreciate the mockery, “Well, that’s what they are.” He says, almost

Amamiya’s grin grows wider, and he looks to be fighting to supress it, “I see.” He furrows his

Akechi blinks. What, was Amamiya stalking him, or something? “How could you tell?”

Amamiya blinks, “Oh. That’s good. That you fixed it, I mean.” He says dumbly.
Akechi nods vaguely, “Yes.”
They fall into silence yet again. Amamiya starts fidgeting after a beat, and Akechi supresses a

Amamiya cracks again, “…The park is kind of pretty, at night.” He mumbles.

Amamiya nods, “Sure. A lot has changed since we last spoke about it properly.”
“Are you questioning whether my own opinions have changed?” Akechi brings a hand to his

Amamiya rolls his eyes, “I can’t get your real feelings on one of those.”
Akechi drops his hand back to his side, “Is that so?” He huffs a laugh, “Well I’m sure you’ll
be disappointed to hear that my opinion hasn’t changed.”
Amamiya raises his eyebrows, “Really? Even after they took down a mob boss?”
If Amamiya thinks he’s being subtle, then Akechi redoubles his disbelief that the thieves
have yet to be identified by the police.
Akechi nods gravely, “Even then.” He laughs lightly, “You’ll forgive me if I’m not entirely
grateful for the power vacuum and gang wars that ensued following Kaneshiro’s arrest.”

Akechi hums, “That’s a fair claim. The police certainly weren’t making much headway on
trying to arrest Kaneshiro themselves.” By design, partially. Between the cops in Shido’s
pocket, and the ones that were just the regular kind of corrupt, it’s a miracle Sae made any
progress at all.

Emboldened by the admission, Amamiya continues, “And even if they did, wouldn’t the

Akechi supresses a grimace. “That’s true.” He concedes. Damn. He straightens his back,

Amamiya presses his lips together, and Akechi’s lips twitch at the clear blow to the other’s

the back of his neck, “Or they just didn’t know how.”
Subtlety, once again, is not Amamiya’s strong suit.
“If that is the case, then my point still stands.” Akechi counters, “Why should we as a society
let a nebulous, clearly fallible, entity make such grand decisions? If the thieves are unable to

“I think they’d learn from their mistakes.” Amamiya says firmly.
Akechi supresses an eye roll. He sincerely doubts they would. Their bleeding hearts would all
bend over backwards the moment someone begged to be saved from their shitty situation,

Amamiya grimaces, his unsubtlety clearly catching up to him, “…No, but so far it’s pretty

“You can’t help everyone.” Akechi says quietly, before he can think better of it.
That seems to catch Amamiya’s attention, “So, what? They should just give up?” He folds his

Akechi shakes his head, “At the very least, the police are a known entity.” Devil you know, or

Amamiya hums, and then gives a small grin, “Three times is a pattern, isn’t it? Even if we
don’t know who they are, they’re still doing good.”
“But what happens if that suddenly changes?” Akechi points out, and doesn’t think about

Amamiya looks down “So you think they should quit while they’re ahead?”
Yes. Fuck yes, absolutely. If Amamiya could take a hint then Akechi’s life would be
infinitely easier.

But he won’t. It’s frankly a fool’s errand to even try to get Amamiya to give it up. The Justice
arcana hums in something that must be agreement.
(If Akechi weren’t so good at lying, especially to himself, he might admit that Amamiya’s

“Preferably after they deal with Medjed.” Akechi says lightly, because it doesn’t matter what
