Amamiya barks a laugh, “It’d be nice if the economy didn’t crash, yeah.”
Akechi almost snorts, “Indeed.”
They keep walking, coming up to the end of the trail, the ever-persistent hum of noise from

Amamiya comes to a stop, and turns, “You haven’t won our debate just yet, by the way.”
Akechi tilts his head, “Oh? You’re not conceding?”
“Nope.” Amamiya says with another dumb grin, popping the ‘p’, “Let’s call it a stalemate for

Of course he listened to all of that and only decided to double down.
Of course someone as self-righteous as Amamiya would be represented by Justice, Akechi
thinks as the offending arcana reaches its fifth rank.
Akechi says none of that, and simply holds his hand out, “…Very well. Stalemate it is.”
Amamiya takes his hand and shakes, his stupid smile growing wider, “It’s a deal.”
God damnit.

Later that night, Ren dreams.
It doesn’t start off with a memory this time, but Ren can remember the events of the Aeon all
the same. With the added knowledge of who Crow is in reality, Ren can retroactively see the
pattern of when these dreams happen. He wonders if he’ll ever notice in the waking word.
Ren looks around, confused, as he sits in a chair in a blank, grey room. There’s a metal table
in front of him, and a heavy door looming further back. He looks to his side, and sees some
empty needles litter the floor.
Ren shifts. This chair is pretty uncomfortable, now that he thinks about it.

He jumps as the door across from him opens with a screech of metal on metal, and smiles as
he sees Crow step through.
“Hey,” Ren says, throwing up a wave.
Crow just hums, folding his arms and looking down at Ren with an unreadable expression.
“So,” Ren starts to fill the silence, “No memory this time?”
Crow barks a laugh, and it puts Ren on edge, “Oh, there could be. Unfortunately, there’s no
point in time where we actually interact in this scenario, so we’ll just have to go with some
old-fashioned speculation.”
That’s… different. “Cool.” Ren says, keeping his voice level, “What the hell is that supposed
to mean?”
“Well,” Crow starts, and the black and blue body suit melts away into Akechi’s school
uniform. He smooths down his hair as the helmet vanishes, and tugs on his gloves absent
mindedly. “You’ll see as it happens,” he says waving an arm.
Ren opens his mouth to ask some more questions, but cuts himself off with a gasp as his own
Metaverse outfit shifts, and Ren’s body suddenly hurts. His wrists are red raw, he’s pretty sure
his ribs are cracked, and his head pounds with his heartbeat, making the room swirl violently
in a haze.
“What…?” He slurs, trying and failing to move his words around his tongue.
Ren blinks, and is met with a gun to his forehead.
“Case closed,” Crow says, all smiles, “This is where your justice ends.”
A bang, a pain, a numbness, and Ren’s vision goes dark.
He blinks, and he’s back in the room again. There’s no blood on the table, and when he
sluggishly reaches up to his forehead, he can’t find any evidence of a bullet hole either.
A bullet hole, because Crow just fucking shot him.
The door creaks open again, and Crow steps through, gun in hand.
“What,” Ren starts, mustering up enough spit to form the words, “The fuck was that for?”
Crow shrugs, “Since you weren’t technically here for this, I thought we’d do some method
acting.”
“Okay,” Ren coughs out, “But why?”
Crow looks contemplative, though Ren thinks it might just be for show, “You’re so adamant
that you want to save my counterpart in reality, so I thought It’s only fair that you see exactly
what it is you’re trying to save.”

Ren chokes on nothing as he tries to come up with something to say to that. He settles on
clenching his fists instead.
“Let’s see…” Crow hums, tapping a finger on his chin, “That was one scenario you dreamed
up, that you’ve forgotten, but there’s a couple others rattling around in here.” He grins

Ren blinks, and finds the gun in his face again.
“You don’t have to do this,” The words form on Ren’s lips of their own accord.
Crow’s face twists into something like melancholy, “I’m sorry,” He whispers, and thenAnother bang,
(Ren can’t be sure, but he thinks he can feel a kiss being pressed gently on his forehead before
the scene resets)
And Ren blinks.
This time, Crow is sitting cross legged in the chair on the other side of the table, inspecting
the gun with manufactured interest.
“Why don’t we make this more interesting?” Crow says with a pretty smile.
Again, Ren’s lips move on their own, “I’m game.”
Crow nods in acknowledgement, and the gun is suddenly a revolver, rather than a pistol.
Crow mechanically empties all of the bullets bar one, and lifts the gun to his head.
A click, a blank. Crow smiles wider, “Your turn.”
Ren accepts the gun, and obediently lifts it to his head.
A click, a blank. He returns the gun.
They go round and round, until Crow lifts the gun to his head, and comes up with another
blank.
Crow laughs lowly, “Just one left. Shall I do the honours?”
Ren smirks, and nods, and,
Another bang,
(Ren can’t be sure, but he thinks he can hear another bang, unrelated to the bullet in his own

And Ren blinks.

Crow is drenched in blood, and Ren can see the crumpled body of some nondescript figure in

Ren doesn’t get the chance to open his mouth, before,
Another bang,
(Ren can be sure this time, he can hear delighted laughter in the time before the scene resets)
And Ren blinks,
Crow enters the room, steals the guard’s gun, and,
“I’m here to rescue you,” Crow says cheerfully,

Another bang, and
“Enough!” Ren snaps, his words his own again.

“Good,” Crow says, inspecting his gloved hands. He still hasn’t returned to his own
Metaverse outfit, instead staying in the tan coat. He carelessly tosses the gun onto the table,

Ren rolls his eyes. He’s starting to understand Crow’s shtick. “By ‘perspective’, you mean

“By ‘perspective’, I mean getting you to see the point.” Crow drawls, lifting his eyes to shoot

“You were like this before, too,” Ren continues, ignoring Crow, “In that memory with the

“Warning me about what?” Ren pushes, “That Akechi is going to try and kill me? That you

“I haven’t tried anything.” Crow says dryly, “I’m a cognition. So anything I say and do is

Something about that rings false, in Ren’s mind. He doesn’t have much ground to stand on
with that claim, admittedly, given that he can’t remember shit, but there’s something off about
the way that Crow says it.
But when he thinks about all the things Crow has said to him…
“Are you…” Ren flicks his tongue over his lips, realising that this is probably a ridiculous
thought to be having, “Are you really a cognition?”
Crow grins sharply, “Well, it’s what I’ve been saying, hasn’t it?”
Ren narrows his eyes, “If you’ve proven anything, it’s that you’re a liar, Akechi.”
Crow grins even wider, “Look at that. You’re learning.” He tugs off a glove, and snaps his
fingers,
And Ren wakes up, immediately feeling the Aeon reach rank six.
He sharply brings a hand to his forehead, as a headache pounds behind his eyes. Morgana
shifts at his side, and Ren forces his body to untense.
Ow, is his first thought. It’s more than just the migraine, too, his whole body aches like he’s
taken a beating.
If this is the aftershocks from the fight with the cognitive Wakaba, then they’re showing up a
bit late.
Ren blinks as, uncharacteristically, bits and pieces of the dream return to him. He winces as
he remembers getting shot, over and over, by some shadowed figure he can’t quite make out.
Well. That’s as clear as any of his Aeon dreams have gotten. The violence kind of makes Ren
think he might be on the right track with thinking that these dreams might be about the black
mask, whoever they may be.
Ren grumbles quietly as he hauls himself out of bed, and quickly jots down everything he can
remember.

A few days after their meeting in Mementos, Sumire blinks at her phone, surprised to see the

Sumire opens her mouth, and then closes it.
She knows that Akechi is trying to wind her up with that comment. It’s what he does best,

A café? Could it be Leblanc?

“Was there anything in particular that needed immediate fixing?” Akechi questions.

“Yeah.” He says quietly.

“Whatever.” Akechi huffs, and Sumire’s smile widens.
“Well,” She starts, “I’ll call Haru to see when she’s free.” She presses her lips together, “I
hope she isn’t too sick of all this supernatural stuff…”
“She’ll live.” Akechi says dryly, “I’ll be there as well.”
“Right,” Sumire nods to herself, “Um, I’ll see you then.”
“See you.” Akechi says, and the line clicks.
(In Akechi’s mind, he feels the Magician grow to rank six. He huffs a laugh to himself. These
bonds are nothing if not persistent.)

actually about.
Sumire, given the chance, might have attempted to take the secret of her time travel all the

It takes until the next day for Akechi to suck it up and go to the Velvet Room. Not because he
didn’t have time the day before, but rather because he didn’t have it in him to deal with them.
He goes to Mementos first, not wanting to take a gamble on how going to the Velvet Room in
the real world looks like, and quietly slips inside the blue courtroom door, giving Buns an
awkward nod as he passes through.
She scoffs, and follows him in, tapping her baton in her hand in a way that Akechi assumes is
supposed to be menacing.
“What brings you here, trickster?” Braids says from behind the prosecutor’s bench, and Buns
goes to join her.
“I have some questions.” Akechi starts with no preamble. He doesn’t expect to gain anything,
so he’s more than happy to get this over with as quickly as possible.
“Our purpose is to aid you,” Igor booms from the judge’s plinth, and Akechi privately calls
bullshit on that one.
“Right,” He says instead, and sighs, “What do you know about the state of reality at the
moment?”
“You need to be more specific, defendant!” Buns snaps, “That could mean anything!”
Akechi rolls his eyes, “I mean, what do you know about-” He cuts himself off, and frowns.
“Trickster?” Igor prompts.
Akechi tries a different angle, “How much of my activities in the real and cognitive world do
you see?”

“We can feel your bonds strengthening,” Braids starts,
“Which you’re not supposed to be doing!” Buns interjects,
Braids continues like her sister didn’t speak, “And we can feel ripples within the other world,
and the hearts you choose to rend asunder.”
So nothing specific. Or, so they say.
“What about you?” Akechi nods curtly at Igor, “How much do you see of my actions?”
“I oversee the game as a whole,” Igor threads his fingers together, “Your actions have
consequences, and I see how they play out.”
An entirely vague response, but definitely an implication that Igor sees far more than the
twins do.
Or so he says.
“In that case,” Akechi starts, “What do you know about how time has folded on itself?”
The twin’s head both snap up, looking alarmed. Igor chuckles.
“Time?” Igor questions, “Fascinating. You say that reality has been disturbed?”
Akechi clenches his fists, and hopes he isn’t making a mistake, “Yes.” He grits out.
“Where did you come to obtain this knowledge?” Igor leans forward.
“Is that relevant to the point?” Akechi asks snidely.
It’s at this point that Akechi would expect a comment from Buns or Braids, complaining
about his demeanour. Surprisingly, he’s met with silence. He eyes them in the corner of his
vision, and cocks an eyebrow at the twins exchanging discomforted and confused looks.
“I only ask to verify the claim’s validity.” Igor says, shifting to tap the desk rhythmically.
“What?” Akechi sneers, “Can’t sense it, or anything?”
That seems to snap Buns out of her stupor, “Don’t be disrespectful!”
“The fabric of reality is a fragile weave,” Igor says in a rumbling voice, “If it has truly folded,
then it is something us residents ought to look into. Trickster, could you inform us of any
more information you may find on this possible distortion?”
Like hell he will. “Sure,” Akechi lies, “If that’s all?” He asks for dismissal instinctively.
“Take your leave.” Igor waves a hand, and Akechi can feel the twins’ eyes on him as he turns
and opens the door back to Mementos.

“You’re a real strange one, defendant.” He hears Buns say behind him. He turns, and sees

“I gathered.” Akechi rolls his eyes, and crosses his arms.

Well. That certainly confirms a lot.
Amamiya has access to the Velvet Room. Though, judging by the epithet ‘inmate’, could his

What a pair they are.

But that’s not the only thing he remembers, as Robin and Loki ping for his attention.
It’s been some time since his personas have retreated into the depths of his mind. He relishes
the lack of static that plagued his head at an alarming rate of increasing frequency, his
personas becoming more stable presences in his mind.
They’re even arguing less. Akechi thought he’d never see the day.
He doesn’t want to attribute a cause to the change.

(He knows, somewhere, that the weave of his bonds have sewn the fragments of his soul

It’s still there, but it’s nice to pretend.)
But there’s one place that still forces his personas somewhere else. Not into buzzing static,

“Caroline. Justine.” Akechi turns back around to address the twins, “Why is it that I can’t feel
my personas’ presence within the Velvet Room?”
The twins exchange a look. Caroline shrugs, “Dunno.” Which is just so helpful.

services provided for the inmate. We help the inmate manage his myriad personas, but we
don’t even have the equipment to try in your room.”
“I see.” Akechi hums.
There was never a time where he trusted Igor. That could be said for a lot of people in
Akechi’s life, but especially for the weird old man who visits his dreams with cryptic portents
of ruin.
The fact that Akechi is apparently treated differently to Amamiya for some elusive reason, as
determined by equally elusive beings, makes him clench his jaw.
Who the hell is anyone to decide how Akechi needs to conduct his life?
(Who the hell is anyone to decide how Amamiya does the same?)
Fuck that. Akechi thinks vehemently. He won’t let Igor’s words sway him.

Of course Futaba Sakura joins the Phantom Thieves. Of course she developed a palace. Of

Medjed has been defeated, and Akechi has yet to be called into Shido’s office.
If he were an idiot, Akechi might have taken that as a hopeful sign that Shido simply doesn’t
have anything to say.
But Shido always has something to say, and he’s sure to have a plethora of words given that
Medjed wasn’t taken down on his terms. Nevermind that Medjed falling was always the plan,
the fact that someone else took them down is sure to twist the stick up Shido’s ass.

Akechi is well aware that the balancing game that he, Haru, and Sumire are setting
themselves up to play is dangerous at best. Trying to steer the thieves away from obvious
danger without arousing suspicion is one thing, but trying to stop Shido from chasing after
them when they don’t take the bait is another.
Akechi would like to avoid getting Haru and Sumire involved in that side of the issue. Better
to let them handle the Phantom Thieves.
(He tells himself it’s because they wouldn’t be able to handle the pressure. They couldn’t
make a change in Shido’s plans on their own- it’s objectively the better choice for Akechi to
shoulder the weight of that.
And nothing else.)
When Akechi considers his plans, he comes up empty.
A new phenomenon, to be sure, and Akechi isn’t sure where it’s even coming from. His
conception of an ‘after’ following his revenge against Shido was always hazy at best, but
now he has two people who expect him to be there in the aftermath.
Akechi knows that he could betray that expectation and trust very easily. Haru and Sumire
have made no further attempts to change his mind about his plans, or question him for
details- he could vanish all the same and they won’t have any way to stop him.
But something twinges when he thinks about doing that.
He tells himself it’s because it isn’t fair to them. He made a deal with them both, and it would
be poor form to take their aid and refuse to return the favour.
So he has to adjust his plans. He needs to stick around long enough to deal with Maruki and
Okumura, at least.
Akechi isn’t sure how to do that, though.
And so, he leans against one of the railings in Shido’s palace, staring down at the huddles of
cognitions milling about.
He really doesn’t know why he thought this would be a good place to think. Just being here
pisses him off.
“So, you’re back again.” A voice observes airily.
Akechi carefully doesn’t startle, and doesn’t turn around to look at the voice.
“I would have thought I made myself clear, last we met,” The voice continues, “And one
could argue that you even being here is a form of treachery.”
Akechi turns his head very slightly, “I’m not making any trouble, aren’t I?”

The cognition smiles back in a facsimile of his TV mask, “I suppose you are far less
aggressive this time around.” It muses.
Akechi scoffs, “Are you just going to stand around and bother me, then?”
“Why are you here?” The cognition asks, ignoring Akechi’s question, “What are you hoping
to achieve by being here?”
Akechi rolls his eyes, “Is that your business?”
“It is my job,” It says, raising an unimpressed eyebrow, “Clearing out trash like you is my
purpose here.” It grins, lips stretching just a bit too wide, “And it’s certainly a task that I
enjoy.”
“You’re pathetic.” Akechi spits.
“Ah, but I’m you.” The cognition gestures, “So, what could that possibly mean?”
“You’re not me.” Akechi grits out, turning away again, “You’re what he thinks of me.”
“But is what the captain thinks of you not oh-so-important?” The cognition mock simpers, “If
you’re so disgusted by the impression that you left on him, you only have yourself to blame.”
It chuckles airily.
Akechi presses his lips together, and clenches his fists.
“Oh, is that it?” The cognition says brightly, “You’re here to see me, aren’t you? To prove
that the captain respects you?” It laughs, the mirth bleeding into mockery, “That just goes to
show that we’re exactly alike, aren’t we? But it doesn’t matter. We’ll do what the captain says
whether he acknowledges us or not.”
Akechi bites his lip to stop himself from saying exactly what he plans to do to this
marionette’s captain.
It’s wrong, he repeats as a mantra in his head, it’s lying, we’re not the same.
He doesn’t care.
“I don’t care.” Akechi says, keeping his voice disinterested.
The cognition’s eyes widen, “Is that so?” it taps a finger to its chin, “Then I suppose you’re
just here to take in the sights? What the captain thinks of you is only a bonus, right.”
Akechi sneers and kicks off the railing, “We’re done here.”
The cognition chuckles, “So soon? Well, come back when you need a reminder of exactly
what you are.”
Akechi doesn’t deign that with a response, and nearly breaks his fist on the wall when the
Tower grows to rank two.

He didn’t come here to see the cognition. He doesn’t care what it says, and he certainly
doesn’t believe its lies.
And yet, the thread of the Tower coils around his organs, making neat little cuts against his
insides.

Sumire doesn’t have a particular reason for heading to Leblanc, but she finds that she’s
wound up there anyway. There are, naturally, pros and cons to this course of action.
The cons include possibly seeing Ren. This, Sumire finds, is rather self-explanatory, given
that she still doesn’t have a handle on her emotions regarding… everything.
The pros also happen to include seeing Ren. A contradiction to be sure, but Sumire has yet to
get anywhere in her plan to discover what could have possibly led to him accepting Maruki’s
deal. Any time spent with him is an opportunity to learn more about him- to discover the
aspects about Ren that she either neglected or wilfully ignored the last time around.
Assuming that she can get her act together. Her track record has been spotty at best.
When Sumire pushes open the door to Leblanc, she isn’t met with the sight of Ren, however.
She isn’t met with the sight of Sojiro, either- rather, she hears something that could be a
squeak of panic, and sees a flash of orange duck into the kitchen.
“Oh, um,” Sumire blinks, still standing in the doorway, “Sorry, are you closed?”
“N-no!” Futaba’s voice yelps.
“Oh.” Sumire opens and closes her mouth, “Okay. Um. Is it alright if I sit…?”
“Sure!” Futaba’s voice calls again, still not coming out of hiding.
Sumire nods slowly, and then grimaces when she realises that Futaba can’t see her. She
shuffles to the bar seats, and takes the one in the middle.
Sumire awkwardly taps her fingers on the bar, swinging her legs back and forth as she waits.
She assumes that either Ren or Sojiro stepped out for a bit, but she isn’t sure what she should
do in the meantime.
“Uh,” Futaba’s voice pipes up again, “D-do you want anything?”
“Oh, yes!” Sumire says cheerfully, “Um, do you have any curry prepared?”
“C-coming right up!” Comes the reply, and Sumire smiles to herself.
She jumps, when a plate is carefully dropped in front of her. Sumire blinks at the giant
bobble-headed mask that sits on Futaba’s head.
“Thank you,” Sumire manages to get out around her shock.

“No problem…” Futaba mumbles, slightly muffled behind the mask.
Futaba doesn’t move from where she’s standing, even as Sumire starts to shovel the curry
into her mouth. She wrings her hands awkwardly, and Sumire resists the urge to fill the
silence, instead giving her full attention to the curry in front of her.
Sumire puts down her spoon, having scraped her plate clean. Futaba looks her up and downor at least, Sumire thinks she looks her up and down. It’s a bit hard to tell.
“You, uh, eat pretty quick.” Futaba stutters.
Sumire flushes, “I have a big appetite…” She says sheepishly.
“Do you want seconds, then?” Futaba stands to attention, her hands hovering over the plate.
Sumire nods dumbly, admitting to herself she is still kind of hungry. Futaba snickers and
cheerfully whips the plate off the bar, humming a tune as she rushes off to go refill the plate.
“Thank you!” Sumire does an approximation of a bow while sitting down as Futaba returns
with the plate. “Um, what’s your name?” She asks, as smoothly as she can, “Um, I know that
Amamiya-senpai works here, so…”
Futaba jumps, “Oh, you know Ren?” Her shoulders seem to relax slightly, “Um, yeah, he’s
supposed to be here, but he went to the store down the road. And my name’s Futaba.” She
tacks on.
“It’s nice to meet you, Futaba-san.” Sumire smiles.
Futaba laughs awkwardly, “Uh, yeah. You too.” She jumps, “Oh! What’s your name?”
“I’m Sumire Yoshizawa,” Sumire says brightly.
“Sumire.” Futaba repeats, “Cool.”
Sumire starts on her second plate of curry, and Futaba quietly slinks off to the kitchen again.
She comes back, the mask now missing from her face.
“Um, sorry.” Futaba pushes her glasses further up her nose, “About that. I just get kinda
nervous around… people.”
Sumire quickly swallows her mouthful of curry, plate already half empty, “No, it’s okay! I get
it.”
Futaba raises her eyebrows, “Really? You seemed like… totally slick when you started
talking to me.”
“That’s because…” Sumire starts, and trails off, grasping for a reason that isn’t ‘I already
know who you are’. “Um, you seemed as nervous as I was, so I think that calmed me down a
bit.” Sumire settles for the closest half-truth she can find.

“Oh, that makes sense.” Futaba mumbles, then smiles nervously, “I wonder if that’s the strat?
I just need to make a bunch of friends who are just as bad at people-ing as I am.”
“Sounds like a plan to me.” Sumire smiles cheerfully, and Futaba snickers.
The door suddenly chimes, and Sumire tries not to jump at the noise.
“You’re back!” Futaba yelps as Ren shuffles into Leblanc, trying to keep the door open with
his foot while his hands are full with shopping bags.
“Yeah,” He says, and his eyes narrow slightly as they catch on Sumire, “Oh. Hey,
Yoshizawa.”
“Um. Hello.” Sumire says, eloquently.
“Everything good, Futaba?” Ren says nodding at the scene before him.
Futaba gives a hearty thumbs up, “Yep! I even managed to serve a customer.”
Ren gives a small smile, “That’s great.” His eyes gain a teasing glint, “And you’ve ditched
the mask, too.”
Futaba folds her arms triumphantly, “I think that’s a level up.”
Sumire giggles behind her hand, “What level are you now?”
Futaba’s eyes flash in delight at Sumire playing along, “At least five.” She says, nodding
gravely, “You?”
“Seven.” Sumire decides arbitrarily.
Futaba makes a noise of pain, “Dang, I’ve gotta catch up.” She quickly turns to Ren in a
whirl of orange, “How ‘bout you? Show me your stats!”
“Me?” Ren points to himself as he hauls the shopping bags into Leblanc’s kitchen, “Level
twenty.”
“What?!” Futaba yelps, “No fair! You’re way overpowered!”
Ren shrugs, “Guess you just need to level grind.”
Sumire’s knowledge of video games ends pretty quickly at the stuff she managed to pick up
from Futaba’s long rambles last timeline, and she’s very rapidly losing grip on the context of
this conversation.
Futaba hmphs, and Ren smirks slightly. Futaba whirls around and points at Sumire, “I guess
that means you and I gotta team up to take this guy down! Care to join me in this quest,
Sumire?”

Sumire, despite feeling slightly lost, nods determinedly, “Of course, Futaba-senpai! I would
be honoured.”
Futaba blinks, “Wow, ‘senpai’, huh?” She snickers, “I think that might be another level, too.”
Sumire laughs in response, and catches Ren watching them with an unreadable look in the
corner of her vision.
Well. No progress to be made yet on that front, then.

Ren doesn’t have an answer for why Yoshizawa showed up at Leblanc the other day- and
frankly, the event only serves to further ignite his suspicions about the girl.
Unfortunately, given how quickly and how well she seemed to get along with Futaba, he’s not
going to be an ass and jeopardise that, nor is he going to complain.
So he’ll just have to prepare himself for Yoshizawa randomly showing up. Which, well- he
had to do that anyway, but at least he can expect it now?
“Hey,” Sojiro says, and Ren turns form where he’s wiping down the bar, “I’m heading out.
Keep an eye on Futaba.”
“I don’t need to be kept an eye on…” Futaba grumbles from where she’s washing the dishes,
turning to flick some suds at Sojiro, earning a disgruntled “Hey!”
“I’ll watch the shop.” Ren agrees, shoving his hands in his pockets.
Sojiro nods, wiping the soap off his apron, and hanging it on the hook, “I’ll be back in a bit.”
The bell above the door tinkles as he leaves, and Futaba turns to give Ren a conspiratorial
look.
“Well, well, well,” She says, in her best impersonation of a gremlin, “What shall we do, now
that we have free reign?”
“Be respectable employees and not incur Sojiro’s wrath.” Ren deadpans.
“Boo.” Futaba returns the deadpan.
Ren smirks, and goes to retort with something snarky before the bell above the door chimes
again.
“Oh,” A familiar voice exclaims, “I didn’t realise you worked here, Amamiya.”
Futaba squeaks and rushes into the kitchen, and Ren gapes at Akechi, who has just taken a
seat at the bar.

“Oh.” Ren responds, then clicks his jaw shut. “Uh. Yeah.” He rubs the back of his neck
sheepishly, “I work here.”
Akechi tilts his head, “What a coincidence. I didn’t expect to run into you here.”
“Huh.” Ren smiles, “Did you just wander in here by accident?”
Akechi chuckles lightly, “I like to think I have better directional sense than that. But no, it
was recommended to me by a friend.”
“Yoshizawa?” Ren asks.
Akechi raises his eyebrows, “She did mention it, yes.”
At the mention of Yoshizawa, Futaba pokes her head out from around the corner.
Akechi’s eyes widen, almost imperceptibly, “Oh.” He starts, something unreadable in his
tone, “You- I mean- I’m sorry, I don’t believe we’ve met before.” He flashes one of his pretty
smiles, and Futaba shifts awkwardly.
“That’s Futaba.” Ren cocks his head toward her, and she shuffles a bit closer, seemingly
using Ren as her impromptu shield, “She’s Boss’ daughter. The guy that owns Leblanc.”
“I see.” Akechi hums, the ‘something’ in his face sufficiently buried.
“Hi.” Futaba mumbles.
“Hello.” Akechi says smoothly in return, weirdly seeming just as uncomfortable as Futaba is.
Now doesn’t seem like the right time to pry, though.
“So,” Ren starts, twisting his fringe between his fingers, “How have you been?”
Akechi’s attention snaps back to Ren, “Things have been fine.” He says, waving a hand
dismissively, “…A lot has happened, lately, but, well, you know how it is.”
“Yeah.” Ren hums in agreement, even though that description definitely doesn’t sound ‘fine’.
Akechi tilts his head, and shoots him a smile, “How about you? Anything interesting?”
Ren stifles a borderline hysterical laugh that he isn’t entirely sure where it’s coming from,
“Uh. Yeah. You could say that.”
Akechi hums lightly, “That bad?”
“No, not really.” Ren says hurriedly, “Just. A lot.” He waves at the shelf behind him, trying to
change the subject, “Anyway, did you want coffee or anything?”
“Well, this is a café.” Akechi says dryly, then tilts his head in a polite smile, “I’ll have
whatever you recommend, I suppose.”

“Coming right up.” Ren nods, and gets to work.
He can feel Akechi’s eyes tracking him as he works, “Do you consider yourself a competent
barista?” He asks, resting his chin on his hand.
“What is this, an interview?” Ren quips lightly, keeping his attention on where he’s preparing
the coffee. He smirks, and lets his eyes flick quickly towards Akechi, “But I think I’m pretty
good.”
“Do you, now?” Akechi smiles brightly, “I think I’ll be the judge of that.”
Ren laughs quietly, finishing the pour-over and placing the coffee down on the bar, “Enjoy.”
Akechi nods, and takes a small sip from the mug. He tilts his head, seemingly considering,
before giving an approving nod.
“It is rather good.” He concedes, and Ren grins triumphantly.
“The best you’ve ever had?” He pushes.
Akechi raises an eyebrow, “I wouldn’t go that far.”
Futaba snickers quietly, still not having moved from her position behind Ren, “I bet Sojiro’s
is better.”
Ren places a hand on his chest, “Betrayal.” He says flatly, and Akechi makes a noise that
sounds suspiciously like a snort.
There’s a beat of silence as Ren goes back to wiping down surfaces that are already clean,
and Akechi takes delicate sips of coffee that must still be piping hot.
“Do you have anything planned for the remainder of the holidays?” Akechi asks over the rim
of the mug.
“Yeah, actually.” Ren says, lifting his head up, “We’re all going to the beach in a couple of
days.”
“Sounds fun.” Akechi says lightly.
Ren shrugs awkwardly, “Yeah.”
Another beat.
“Uh.” Ren starts, and before he even fully registers what he’s about to say he can feel it might
be ill-advised, “Did you want to come with us?”
Ren winces as Futaba kicks him as hard as she can. Which, as it turns out, isn’t that hard.
Akechi blinks at him, “You’re…?”

“I’m asking if you wanted to come to the beach with us.” Ren says, doubling down, despite
the clear out Akechi was granting him by way of confusion.
This might have been a bad idea; Ren finally registers in his mind. Arsène seems delighted, at
least.
“Oh.” Akechi blinks again, then opens and closes his mouth, “I…”
“You don’t have to if you don’t want to.” Ren says quickly. He bites his lip, “Um. Haru and
Yoshizawa can come along too.”
The mention of Yoshizawa seems to deter Futaba from kicking Ren’s leg, and Akechi’s
eyebrows shoot up.
“I see.” The detective hums, looking far too serious for someone contemplating whether they
should go to the beach.
“You can decide later, if you want.” Ren says, trying to keep how much he wants Akechi to
decide now (In the affirmative, preferably) out of his voice.
“I- no. It’s okay.” Akechi shakes his head, seemingly snapping himself out of his thoughts, “I
think I’ll go.”
“What- really?” Ren perks up, forgetting to sound disinterested.
Akechi nods, the hint of a smirk twitching on his lips, “Yes. I’ll ask Haru-san and Sumire if
they wish to join in as well.”
“Great.” Ren says, a smile tugging at the corners of his mouth.
Akechi huffs something that could be a laugh, and takes another sip of coffee, before setting
it back down on the saucer with a clink.
“Well.” Akechi starts, “I suppose I should be leaving. Text me the details?”
“Yep.” Ren nods, throws out a wave as Akechi stands from his seat and leaves Leblanc, the
bell tinkling in the wake of his exit.
“So,” Futaba starts from behind him, and Ren has to stop himself from jumping, “Are all the
randos you know that pretty, or…?”
“’All’?” Ren raises an eyebrow, tearing his gaze from the door.
“Well we’ve got pretty boy over there,” Futaba points where Akechi was just sitting, “And
pretty girl from the other day,” She points to the adjacent seat where Yoshizawa had been
sitting a few days earlier.
Ren shrugs, and bites back his laughter of Futaba’s assessment of his respective friend and
acquaintance.

Futaba smirks, “Don’t think I didn’t notice how bad you have it.”

“Of course I like him, he’s my friend.” Ren says defensively, and then shuffles awkwardly,

“It’s fine,” Futaba waves a hand dismissively, “You said Sumire would be there, right? And

Ren huffs a laugh, “I guess that’s true.” He takes Akechi’s abandoned mug over to the sink,

“Hope so…” Futaba mumbles, kicking absently at the ground. She sighs, “The beach sounds
like so much effort…”
“It’ll be fun.” Ren insists, “And like you said, we’ll all be there.”
“Yeah…” Futaba groans, but she sounds like she’s doing it more performatively than

Ren chuckles lightly, and Futaba shoots him a death glare.
He cleans the dirtied plate and mug absently, thinking about the days ahead.
He had perhaps let a little too much slip in his response to Akechi’s question earlier. Ren is
usually a lot better at hiding when things are… a lot, as he had put it- given that things have
been pretty consistently as such ever since he came to Tokyo.
But, well, the detective had slipped slightly as well, so it’s not like he left on the back foot.
Ren pauses in his washing up, and bites his lip, face flushing slightly in embarrassment.
…Yeah, his invitation wasn’t smooth at all, was it?

Akechi’s prediction that Shido does in fact always have something to say is proven correct,
when he gets the unfortunate call into the fucker’s office.
Akechi has to admit that it feels different meeting Shido, now. There’s a strange tension in his
body that is one step to the left of the tension that he normally feels.
Perhaps, Akechi muses to himself, it’s because of his slight change in plans, now that he has
the aid of Haru and Sumire. He always planned to stab Shido in the back (as well as the front,

and twist the knife as viciously as possible), but now he’s making identifiable progress to
actually achieving that goal.
(The implication there, that Akechi doesn’t care to examine, is that he never would have
attempted to undermine Shido’s bullshit if not for the pull of the Strength and Magician in his
chest.
Akechi doesn’t think about the cognition stalking its way through the cruiser of pride that
sails in Shido’s head.)
But there’s no time to be thinking about treachery when he’s supposed to be putting up a
good act.
Shido taps at his desk rhythmically, leaning back in his chair, “Care to explain how this has
happened, Akechi?” He sneers.
Akechi takes a long, steadying breath, “I’m afraid that I don’t have a specific answer, sir.” He
debates on the level of truth he’ll have to spill to keep Shido satisfied, “But I believe it’s safe
to say that the Phantom Thieves have either recruited or hired a rather skilled hacker.”
Shido scoffs, “That’s all you have to say?” He waves a derisive hand, “It’s been four months
since this whole fiasco started, and you don’t even know who they are?”
Akechi keeps his expression perfectly blank. “…No,” He says, after what is probably too
long of a pause, “I don’t.”
Shido seems to pick up on it, because of course he does. “Is that so?” He drawls.
Akechi smiles brightly, “Their identities are hardly going to be an issue, no?” He hurries to
continue when that doesn’t appear to be a satisfactory answer, “And we’ll find out soon
enough once they start infiltrating Okumura’s palace.”
If all goes well, then the Phantom Thieves will never set foot in the space station palace,
giving Akechi a very reasonable excuse as to why he supposedly is unaware of the thieves’
identities. Of course, he’ll have to deal with the consequences of all that as well.
Shido raises and eyebrow, that might come off as approving if Akechi were a fool, “You’ve
scouted his palace, then? I see you are good for something.”
Akechi smiles politely, and clenches his fists behind his back.
Shido taps the desk again, and leans forward, “Listen here, Akechi.” He begins, in a suddenly
far more threatening tone, “I expect nothing less than your very best for this. You understand
that, don’t you?”
Akechi doesn’t swallow, because that would give him away. There’s only so much of this he
can keep up in his right mind, so he instead lets his throat go dry and lets his consciousness
slip under the surface. “…Of course.”

Shido nods curtly, “Good. Now, I want you to keep an eye on Okumura’s palace, obviously.”
He laces his fingers together, “We’re stopping our media suppression of Okumura’s legally
questionable dealings, so the news should have a field day. That should draw the thieves’
attention.”
Akechi tilts his head, “Do you believe that will be enough?”
“There’s more.” Shido snaps, and Akechi wonders why he even asked, “There’s been a recent
addition of a polling feature on the Phantom Thieves website. I believe fudging the numbers
should be rather effective.”
“I see.” Akechi hums.
The information is hardly new, courtesy of Sumire. But the specifics are nice to have on
hand.
It would be nicer if it actually gave Akechi any new ideas on how to get the thieves to leave
well enough alone, but no such luck.
‘Don’t give the thieves a reason and hope for the best’ is their best plan so far, and even the
most incompetent strategist can see that it’s held together with tissue paper and particularly
worn-out chewing gum.
When Akechi finally gets dismissed from the meeting, he sighs.
(The Devil grows to rank four, and Akechi resolutely ignores it.)
What the hell can he do about this?

Chapter 28
Chapter Summary

Cognitions, beach trips, and deadlines.

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

There are often reasons for why Akechi does things, and he’d like to think that near all of
them are rational.
‘Near all’, being the key phrase here, given that he isn’t quite sure where crippling paranoia
fits on the scale of rationality.
(He isn’t quite sure where a lot of the things he feels fit, either, but he elects to ignore the
thought.
If he isn’t feeling it right now, then it hardly matters.)
Crippling paranoia, as such, is the reason he finds himself back in the opulent halls of Shido’s
cruiser, less than a week since he was here last.
He thinks he acted normally during the last meeting with Shido. He’s sure. Fuck, he hopes so,
because he doesn’t know what he’s supposed to do if Shido has miraculously caught a whiff
of Akechi’s plans, now that he actually has a reason to act on them.
What can he do? Swear loyalty? Beg for forgiveness? Fake his own death?
None are particularly appealing.
And, so as to not jump the gun, he glares up at the shimmering rafters of the foyer, searching
for a glimpse of a tan blazer or the silver flash of a pistol.
He doesn’t blink, when he catches a blur in his peripheral, and instead carefully turns to level
a pointedly disinterested stare at the corner of shadow where the cognition inspects its gloved
hands.
“Back again?” The cognition says with polite surprise, still not looking up, “And so soon, at
that.”
“I suppose I’m curious.” Akechi says, his lips curling in a sneer.

The cognition looks up, and blinks rapidly with big doe eyes, “Oh, but you were so insistent
that you don’t care, last time.” It sighs, and shrugs, “Well, we are practiced liars, I suppose.”
“I don’t care.” Akechi corrects forcefully, “Your entire existence is pathetic.”
“And so you contradict yourself.” The cognition heaves a long-suffering sigh, “I don’t
understand what I’ve done to deserve such venom coming from you. You are me.”
“You aren’t.” Akechi says, and he gets the feeling he’s going to have to keep saying that as
long as the Tower continues to stand, “And you threatened to kill me, the first time we met.”
He tacks on dryly.
“Ah. I suppose I did, didn’t I?” The cognition tilts its head, “But I’ve left you unscathed
since, no?”
“How generous.” Akechi deadpans.
“Of course!” The cognition smiles brightly, “But you should know that I only deal with
things that become problems for the captain. And, well, you’re not a problem, are you?”
“No.” Akechi agrees, ignoring the bitter tang that comes with the word.
He also quietly files away the cognition's words as a note for later, not letting the relief seep
into his bones just yet.
“You always seem so put off by my actions.” The cognition muses, “Which is strange, since
we’re the same person.”
“Are you going to keep fucking saying that shit?” Akechi snarls, whirling around to properly
glare at the cognition.
“Why wouldn’t I?” The cognition blinks, the picture of innocence, “It’s the truth.”
“No it fucking isn’t!” Akechi hisses, “You’re a cognition. Nothing more.”
The smile the cognition gives in response is uncomfortably wide, “But isn’t this how you’ve
chosen to act? What’s the point of your internal thoughts, if your external actions stay the
same?” It gestures to itself, “You don’t think like me, or so you say, but you do act like me.
So are we not the same?”
Akechi scoffs, “Shido doesn’t know me at all, if this is how he thinks I act.”
“Or you’re not very self-aware.” The cognition hums.
“I’m not his goddamn puppet,” Akechi spits, forgetting to reign in the veritable mountain of
vitriol that keeps pushing towards the surface.
“We’ll see.” The cognition smiles, “If the captain thinks of you as his puppet, can you truly
be anything else?”

“We’ll see.” Akechi echoes, and stalks off towards the exit, pushing open the foyer doors
with excessive force.
He can feel the cognition’s eyes linger on his back.
He can also feel the Tower grow to rank three.

Ren rubs the back of his neck. It’s usually more of a nervous tick, but right now Ren feels
like he’s doing it simply for lack of anything else to do.
“Sorry for dragging you along.” He turns to Akechi, who just shakes his head.
“It’s fine.” Akechi reassures, “It would take more than one person to carry all the drinks, and
I don’t mind helping out.”
“Still.” Ren shrugs.
Akechi hums, and his lips twitch up, “I suppose my question would be why you asked me,
specifically.”
Ren tries to avoid letting the question catch him off guard, but his steps falter slightly
anyway. “Well…” He starts, like this is a question of far more weight than it reasonably
should be, “You kind of looked like you wanted to be somewhere else.”
Akechi raises an eyebrow, “Oh?”
“Yeah.” Ren nods, then smiles sheepishly, “You didn’t have to come along if you really
didn’t want to. To the beach, I mean.”

Akechi huffs, amused, “Trying to get rid of me, Amamiya?”
“No, I’m glad you’re here.” Ren admits, surprising himself.
Akechi covers his mouth to cough, but Ren is pretty sure he can see the subtle curve of a
smile around the other’s eyes.
That’s not quite what catches his attention, though.
“I don’t think I’ve ever seen you without gloves.” Ren points out.
Akechi’s eyes widen slightly, before their shape is forced back into neutrality, “Huh.” Akechi
hums, and a TV smile takes over his face, “I suppose I rarely go without them, yes.”
If not for the near-violent speed with which Akechi had shoved his hands back into his
pockets, Ren might’ve been fooled by the act. “Any particular reason?” Ren chooses to push.
“Well, I do work in law enforcement,” Akechi says flatly, “It’s poor form to go around
contaminating evidence.”
A small grin twists on Ren’s face, “All the time, though? Sounds like the actions of someone
doing the crime rather than solving it, detective.”
That gets a laugh out of Akechi, “Who knows? Being a detective would be a rather good
cover in that case.”
Ren nods solemnly, “Smart. It fits.”
A bemused look passes on Akechi’s face, “What, being a criminal?”
Ren tilts his head, “Sure?”
Akechi raises another unimpressed eyebrow, and the two laugh before falling into silence.
“Jokes aside,” Ren starts after a beat, ignoring the slight irony of the statement, “Is there a
reason you usually wear gloves?”
Akechi frowns slightly, “What makes you so curious?”
Ren shrugs, reaching up to twist his fringe between his fingers, “It’s just a pretty strange habit
to have, is all.”
Akechi hums, but doesn’t respond.
Ren assumes that the other has no intention of answering the question, but perks up when
Akechi starts speaking again, “I never gave it much thought, at first.” He starts, looking at the
ground.
Ren makes a small noise to prompt him to continue.

Akechi shoots him another look before obliging, “It wasn’t until it was a fully established
habit that I realised I had become somewhat reliant on them- and, well, it seemed harmless
enough that I didn’t bother to try and break the habit.”
Ren nods slowly, “What are you reliant on them for?”
Akechi tilts his head, looking contemplative, “A defence, perhaps? You know, I never
bothered to examine that particularly closely, either.”
Ren smiles a little, “How come you didn’t wear them today?”
“It would be a bit inconvenient to wear leather gloves at a beach, don’t you think?” Akechi
asks flatly, “I doubt they’d survive the sand and salt water.”
“Yeah, that’d ruin them pretty quick.” Ren concedes.
Akechi laughs slightly, and runs a hand through his hair, “I am a bit uncomfortable, I’ll
admit, but it’s not as bad as I thought it would be.”
“That’s good,” Ren says softly.
Akechi shrugs, and looks away, “How about you, though?”
Ren blinks, “Huh?”
“Well, you’re not wearing your glasses.” Akechi points out, making eye contact again, “And
I happen to recall that I promised to figure out why you wear them.”
Ren vaguely remembers the banter shared at the fireworks festival, and nods dumbly.

I deal in smoke, and you mirrors.”

Akechi pastes on a bland smile, “Did you hear that she threatened Futaba-chan’s guardian
over his custody, as a last-ditch attempt to try and squeeze information out of him?”
Makoto’s face crumples, and she kicks lightly at the sand, “…It was implied, at one point. I
was hoping it was a misunderstanding.”
“No such luck, I’m afraid.” Akechi says flatly.
Makoto sighs, “Yeah… She’s been… distant.” She huffs, “I didn’t realise she was getting
so-”
“Aggressive?” Akechi supplies.
“Yeah.” She presses her lips together, “I’ve always looked up to my sister, so it’s a bit much
to hear that she’s been doing this.”

Akechi hums, “She’s always been intense, as long as I’ve known her.” He folds a towel with
a bit more force than necessary, “But her skirting the line of legality and morality is
something of a recent development.”
Makoto laughs weakly, “I can’t tell if that’s a good thing or not.”
“Who’s to say?” Akechi says lightly. He looks down, “At the very least, I doubt this is an
inherent part of her personality.”
Makoto smiles to herself like she’s in on a joke, “Just a distortion of it, I guess.”
“Hm.” Akechi offers, carefully not reacting to her choice of wording.
Makoto sighs, and continues, “It’s just so… frustrating, how she’s been acting. I remember
that she looked up to dad as much as I do, but now it’s like she’s trying to forget he even
existed.” She scowls, and snaps the sun umbrella shut, “She just gets so mad when I try to
bring up justice or anything related to her or dad’s job. I’ve tried connecting with her, but
she’s always busy, or giving her attention to someone else-” She cuts herself off.
“Right.” Akechi almost laughs, “That is part of the reason we don’t get along, no?”
Among other things.
Makoto shoots him a look, “…Among other things, Akechi-kun.”
Akechi does laugh, this time, “Right, of course.”
There’s a beat of silence, and Makoto speaks up again, “…I don’t know why she’s so
different. But I remember how passionate she used to be about justice and social issues, and I
can’t help but wonder what happened.”
Akechi doesn’t think anything happened, personally. Sure, Sae’s father died, but she’s hardly
special in that regard- people’s parents die all the time. Even if Sae had managed to dodge
that bullet three years ago, it would have happened eventually.
And if not that, doubtless something else would have happened to get the ball rolling.
(Akechi wonders if he would have turned out any different, if his mother had lived a little
longer. He cuts off the train of thought before he settles on an answer.)
“…Who knows?” Akechi eventually settles on saying, “Shall we get moving? I believe
everyone is waiting for us.”
Makoto tilts her head at him before a beat, before collecting herself and nodding.
Akechi almost jumps when the High Priestess grows to rank two.
***

Ren half-walks, half-waddles over to where the other thieves (plus Haru and Yoshizawa) are,
dumping the bags he’s carrying unceremoniously on the ground. He picks up the remaining
cans of drinks, and hands them out to everyone.
“Thanks!” Ann says, cheerfully accepting her can of soda. She pops open the top, and then
frowns, “Where are Makoto and Akechi-kun?”
“Packing up the rest of our things to move over here, I believe.” Yusuke chimes in, placing
his bag down on the ground with far more care than Ren had shown to his own belongings.
“How long are they gonna take?” Ryuji calls from where he’s setting up the volleyball net.
Futaba shrugs, and claims the one chair they have, “Dunno. It took us like ten minutes to set
up, but they’ve gotta take everything down, too.”
“Not too long, then.” Yoshizawa says, tossing the volleyball in her hands up and down
absently. She gives a tentative smile when Ren passes her drink to her.
“Should we start a game without them?” Haru asks, standing up and dusting the sand off her
legs, “It’s a three-on-three game, so someone would have been sitting out anyway.”
“Sounds good.” Ren says with a nod.
Volleyball, as it turns out, is a difficult game to play when you’ve played it a total of once
before. It is especially difficult when you have to play on sand, which is not the most
forgiving surface to stand or jump on.
Everyone else appears to be having similar problems to Ren, which he takes solace in.
A surprising number of people within the group have some measure of obvious or hidden
athletic ability. How each person’s latent ability translates to volleyball is another factor.
Yoshizawa, being a gymnast, can jump far higher than she has any right to. She’s also rather
precise in her movement, making her one of the more formidable opponents to face.
Haru, surprisingly, actually has quite a lot of muscle that wasn’t immediately obvious. When
asked, she cheerily explained that she has a lot of experience with swinging axes, and Ren
stopped asking pretty quickly after that. Her muscle doesn’t actually do her many favours,
aside from thoroughly bruising her unfortunate targets whenever she manages to hit the ball.
Yusuke is not athletic in the slightest. He is pretty tall, but any benefit he could have reaped
from such an advantage is pretty quickly cancelled out by how he barely seems to be paying
attention to the game.
Ann is also somewhat lacking in the athletics department. On the other hand, she has the best
grasp on the rules -no doubt from Shiho- which doesn’t actually translate to being a great
player. At some point, she stops playing games and joins Futaba and Morgana in being
referees.

Ryuji is a former track star, which, much like Haru, doesn’t actually do him many favours in
volleyball. He also starts sitting out after a few games, and waves off any concern when Ren
tries to surreptitiously ask if his leg is acting up.
Makoto and Akechi, when they both finally join the games, are both intensely competitive,
and have the athletic capabilities to back them up. (Ren learned his lesson from when he
asked why Haru was so athletic, and chooses to let these instances slide.) Ren was
unfortunate enough to be on a team opposing Makoto, Yoshizawa, and Akechi for one game.
The game did not last long.
Ren himself can modestly say he’s pretty athletic- some holdovers from when he did dance as
a kid, as well as the muscle he’s been rebuilding for the sake of Phantom Thievery. He can
also say that he gets pretty swept up in the competition of it all, and has earned himself a few
stink eyes from when he went a little too hard in the games that were supposed to be casual.
Ren was lucky enough to be teamed up with Akechi and Yoshizawa for one game. That game
did also not last very long.
Eventually, as the sky begins to dip from blue to orange on the fringes, and the group splits
off and fragments to start gathering their things, Ren sees Futaba squatting right on the shore,
staring out at the rhythmic push and pull of the waves.
He walks over to her, and he doesn’t seem to be the only one, as all the other thieves slowly
gather in a circle, while Akechi, Yoshizawa, and Haru are all elsewhere, packing their
belongings away.
Futaba sighs, and eventually speaks, “Y’know, I’ve been wondering about the fake suicide
note those men in black suits read out.”
Ren winces at the sudden change in tone, but nods slowly, “Yeah?”
“I believed it for so long,” Futaba continues in almost a whisper, “…I know it was faked now,
but… I’m still stuck on the why.”
“Yeah…” Ann suddenly says, her eyes widening, “Do you think there was a specific reason
for it, Futaba-chan?”
“My mom didn’t commit suicide.” Futaba says firmly, “She didn’t jump into the road, it was
more like she just… collapsed.”
“So it could have been an accident, then?” Yusuke asks, folding his arms, “Just a symptom of
overwork?”
Futaba shakes her head, “That could’ve been it, but… I read my mom’s research once. She,
uh, got really mad at me when she caught me,” She laughs sheepishly, “But I remember
seeing one of her theories, that the other self is tied to the real self, and anything done to the
other self will be reflected in some way in the real self’s actions and thought processes.”
“That sounds like she was talking about shadows.” Morgana says gravely, flicking his tail.

“Shit, just how deep was your mom’s research getting?” Ryuji exclaims, running a hand
through his hair.
“It sounds like she could be describing the psychotic breakdowns and mental shutdowns.”
Makoto cuts in, a hard look in her eye, “If we assume that those phenomena are caused by
someone interfering with people’s shadows in the Metaverse.”
Ren frowns, “…But haven’t those things only be happening for the past two years?”
“And my mom died two years ago.” Futaba finishes, “So I don’t think she was researching
those events specifically.”
Makoto hums, and then shakes her head, “That doesn’t mean her research wasn’t about them,
though.”
Futaba nods, “Which is kinda my point. I can’t find my mom’s research anywhere. And I’ve
looked.”
“What are you implying?” Yusuke furrows his brow.
“I think that someone stole and hid my mom’s research.” Futaba clenches her fists, “And I’d
bet a lot that the men who read her suicide note were involved.”
Ren nods slowly, “We kind of theorised about this in your palace.” He admits, “When we saw
some stuff in your memories of everything that seemed kind of off.”
“So…” Ryuji starts, “Do you guys think that someone stole Futaba’s mom’s research, and
then used it to give her a mental shutdown?”
“That’s definitely something I’ve thought of.” Futaba says quietly, giving Ryuji a nod, “If she
was the only one who was looking into this stuff, and the way she died…” She shakes her
head, “The more I think about it, the more I think she was murdered.”
Ren sighs, pressing his lips together, and he can see the other thieves doing much of the same
around them. They had considered this as a possibility, but to have it pretty much confirmed
is another thing.
“We think we might have a lead.” Makoto says, turning to Futaba, “Both Madarame and
Kaneshiro mentioned another Metaverse user.”
“Madarame indicated that they had a black mask.” Yusuke chimes in.
“And Kaneshiro said, or, well, heavily implied that the same guy was the one behind the
mental shutdowns and psychotic breakdowns,” Ann says, tugging at one of her pigtails.
“Damn, really?” Futaba’s eyes widen.
Morgana nods solemnly, “We also think they might be watching us in palaces. Both Ren and
I could sense someone when we were in Kaneshiro’s palace.”

“I don’t think they were watching us when we were going through your palace, though.” Ren
cuts in, “Or they got better at hiding, at least.”
Futaba nods slowly, humming, before she suddenly jumps up, “Oh!”
“What?” Ryuji jumps at her sudden exclamation.
“I just remembered something!” Futaba says hurriedly, “So, my shadow merged to be my
persona, right?”
Everyone gives some variation of a tentative nod.
“So, I didn’t get, like, everything that happened in my palace,” Futaba continues, tripping
over her words as she gets them out as fast as possible, “Just some vibes, really. But I do
remember feeling like there was something else in my palace other than you guys.”
Ren stiffens, and the other thieves all look at each other with varying degrees of alarm.
“Do you think…?” Makoto starts, and there’s about a hundred ways Ren could finish that
sentence.
The black mask, if that’s who it was- could they have been just spying on the thieves? Could
they have been there to hurt Futaba, to tie up the loose end? Or maybe-?
“Uh, calm down.” Futaba cuts into everyone’s panicking, “It’s weird, since it doesn’t really
feel like they were… malicious? Like, at all.”
“So…?” Morgana prompts.
“It’s like…” Futaba huffs, shoving her glasses further up her nose, “The vibe I got from all of
you being there was pretty much just the warm fuzzies, since you were all trying to help me.
And the vibe I got from the other thing is… a step to the left? They weren’t trying to get
through my palace at all, I think. But I feel like they were nice.”
Ren narrows his eyes, and presses his lips together.
He’s still yet to share his suspicions about Yoshizawa.
It’s not like the suspicion has gone away, far from it- but he doesn’t exactly have the evidence
to back it up beyond a hunch, and a lot of suspicious coincidences.
Ren’s original reason for being wary of Yoshizawa is based largely in the few scraps he can
remember from the Aeon dreams, as well as the fact that she acts so weirdly towards Ren
specifically.
Those are the things that are a little harder to explain away, but if Ren opens up the list of
coincidences, he can start painting a bigger picture.
Yoshizawa was at Leblanc on one of the days that the thieves went to Futaba’s palace. Not
really a base for anything, but if she is the black mask, she could have found Futaba’s palace

by following them fairly easily.
She also gets along with Futaba quite well. Definitely a stretch, but now that Futaba herself
has said that the intruder in her palace seemed ‘nice’, it means that Yoshizawa’s and the black
mask’s intentions at least align in this.
She’s also friends with Akechi- and Ren feels really bad for being so suspicious of
Yoshizawa purely based on who she’s nice to, but Akechi is a detective on the case of the
mental shutdowns and psychotic breaks. Ren isn’t sure what that could imply, but it’s another
coincidental connection.
But that’s all Ren has. He knows that his friends are all pretty fond of Yoshizawa, too, so he
doesn’t want to cause a rift on such flimsy evidence.
He’ll have to keep an eye on her in his own time.
Futaba sighs, snapping Ren out of his thoughts.
“I want to find whoever killed my mom.” Futaba says, determination written all over her
face, “And, I know you guys are already looking for them so… um, can I join you guys?”
Ryuji grins, and pats her shoulder, “Are you kiddin’? You’re already one of us.”
Futaba crumples, looking relived, as all the other thieves nod in affirmation of Ryuji’s
declaration.
“Thanks.” She says with a small smile. She tilts her head, “You guys all use codenames,
right?” She grins mischievously, “So! What should mine be?”
***
Sumire shakes out her towel of as much sand as she can, and carefully folds it into a neat
square. She looks out over the near-empty beach, and tries not to let her eyes linger too long
on where the thieves are standing on the shoreline.
“What do you think they’re talking about?” Haru asks quietly.
“Thieves-related business, I assume.” Goro says sharply, “That, or something generally
personal that they simply didn’t want to share with us.”
Sumire hums in agreement, “I think all their personal things kind of link into their Phantom
Thieves stuff, anyway. So it’s probably a bit of both.”
From where the three of them can see, the conversation certainly looks somewhat sombre.
Haru sighs, “Well since we’ve been given the opportunity, any updates on our end?”
“Shido has started his plans to make Okumura the Phantom Thieves’ problem.” Goro says
darkly, “It largely involves using his control over the media to draw attention to the man’s

ethical malpractice, and messing with the thieves’ website to stage the level to which the
public wants to change his heart.”
“I see.” Haru hums.
Sumire shifts, “Do you think that not giving them a personal reason will be enough?”
“Well, you’d be the expert on that, wouldn’t you?” Goro says dryly, raising an eyebrow.
Sumire laughs sheepishly, “Right…” She frowns, “We should definitely keep an eye on them.
I don’t think Kaneshiro was nearly as personal as the rest of them, so it’s not like the thieves
will just ignore this because they don’t have a personal stake.”
Haru nods, “We may have to try and influence them slightly. I can help with that, if it comes
down to it.”
“I can as well.” Goro cuts in, “But I’m not sure how effective my word would be on their
decision making.”
Sumire raises her hand, “I can… try?” She awkwardly adjusts her glasses, “I don’t know how
good I’d be at convincing them, though. It might just be weird for me to start talking about
it.”
Goro nods, “That’s true. We don’t want to raise any suspicions accidentally.”
Haru claps her hands together, “I think I might have a few ideas on how do dissuade them.”
She looks down, “Though, I think I can only start doing them after my father starts getting
some bad press.”
Goro shakes his head, “That’s perfectly fine. It would be odd to steer them away from
Okumura before he’s even a blip on their radar.”
Sumire sighs, “So we just have to wait?”
Haru smiles in commiseration, “Seems like it.”
Goro waves a dismissive hand, “We have time.”
***
“You’re back late.” A voice cuts in as Haru closes the front door behind her.
She flinches at the icy tone. “I’m sorry, father.” She says quietly, walking into the living
room, “I was with someone at all times, so I wasn’t in any danger.” She says, knowing full
well that particular hangup isn’t the cause of her father’s grievances.
Her father hmphs, and waves a hand dismissively. “Don’t do it again.” He says shortly, and
Haru quickly nods and moves to head to her room.

“Oh, Haru.” Her father calls out again, and she turns around, “Have you been getting along
with Sugimura?”
It is with great difficultly that Haru manages to supress the sneer that threatens to cut her
face, “Yes, father.” She lies.
“Good.” He doesn’t turn to face her, “He suggested that you move in with him, soon.”
Haru can feel ice prick at the edges of her nerves, “Oh?” She hums, “When, exactly, did he
suggest?”
“Sometime in October, I believe. Think about it.” Her father says, and judging by the tilt to
his voice, Haru can tell that the conversation is over.
October. So she has two months at best, and just one at worst. Though, if her father is to be
believed, she does have some measure of a choice.
Shit.
Haru, with as much grace and decorum as she can muster, quietly ascends the stairs to her
room, and slowly clicks the door shut behind her.
She resists the urge to break all of the prettily arranged porcelain tea sets placed on various
shelves. As satisfying as it would be, it wouldn’t serve much purpose.
Instead, Haru sits down on her bed, and falls back with a thump to stare at the ceiling.
