Chapter 29
Chapter Summary

Dreams, control, and school trips.

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

That night, Ren dreams.
When the dream fails to start off with a memory again, Ren is a little concerned that this
particular encounter is going to end the same as the last time.
That being, getting shot in the head over and over for no discernible reason other than Crow
being a cryptic piece of shit.
That doesn’t seem to be the case, though, as Ren takes a second to properly observe his
surroundings. He's in Leblanc, standing behind the bar- though he’s still wearing his
Metaverse outfit, making for quite the picture.
The bell above the door tinkles, and Crow walks in and slumps on down on one of the stools.
The same stool that Akechi had sat on the other day, Ren notes absently.
Crow makes no attempt at conversation, and instead makes a show of inspecting his
gauntlets. Ren rolls his eyes, and tugs off his gloves, looking to busy himself with making
coffee.
He can see Crow tilt his head slightly as he starts up the siphons. Crow looks up properly
when Ren places a cup of coffee in front of him, giving him a pointed look.
Crow rolls his eyes with his entire head, and takes off his helmet with a short click. He
continues glaring at Ren as he takes a sip of coffee, his face scrunching like he’s swallowed
an entire lemon.
“What?” Ren makes an effort not to pout, “S’not good?”
“You don’t remember my order.” Crow says snippily.
“It’s what I made for the you in the real world, and he seemed to like it fine.” Ren frowns.
Crow rolls his eyes, “I’m sure he liked it ‘fine’, yes, but it wasn’t the best thing he’s ever
had.”

“What high standards I have to live up to.” Ren deadpans.
“The standards are yourself.” Crow snaps, “This would be a lot easier if the forces of the
universe let you remember.”
Ren throws up his hands, “So you’re just as annoyed as I am!”
Crow scrapes a hand down his face, “Of course I am. I keep telling you that I’m not in
control of this.”
“And you don’t know who is.” Ren states more than asks, and Crow nods in confirmation.
Ren huffs, leaning over the bar and holding his face in his hand.
Ren kicks at the floor, “…So no memory this time?”
“No.” Crow takes another sip of coffee.
“And no weird ‘speculation’ where you find excuses to shoot me a bunch?” Ren asks, raising
an eyebrow.
Crow rolls his eyes, and Ren thinks it’s a wonder they don’t get stuck, “I was just warning
you what you’re getting into.”
“Yep.” Ren says, popping the ‘p’, “And I still don’t want you to die, believe it or not.”
Crow scoffs, “Are you sure that not just because you’re charmed by the real me’s bullshit?
He’s lying to you, you know.”
“Uh huh.” Ren mumbles, moving back over to the siphons.
In the waking world- though it’s kind of hard to tell with his mind as it is now- Ren knows he
isn’t suspicious in the slightest of Akechi. Ren doesn’t know how much he should be, eitherCrow does make a good point in saying that there isn’t a monopoly on the colour black.
…A sentiment that falls somewhat flat, when Crow made such a point of making sure Ren
‘knows what he’s getting into’.
Assuming that Ren’s cognition is accurate, then the Akechi in the real world is, at the very
least, hiding his real personality. It has slipped lately, though, Ren thinks, remembering
Akechi’s scathing remarks about the state of Ren’s trial. A small smile twitches onto his lips
as he thinks about it.
“What are you doing?” Crow asks, with the tone of someone who just saw their cat throw up
on their shoes.
“Trying to guess your order.” Ren says, moving back towards the siphons.
“I meant with your face.” Crow snaps, narrowing his eyes.
Ren blinks, “What, smiling?”

“Yes.” Crow glares, “Cut it out.”
The smile stretches into a grin, “Why?”
“Because I see that despite all my efforts, you have missed the point.” Crow growls.
“You might want to give up, then.” Ren says, pouring another cup, “I’m clearly never going
to get it if I haven’t gotten it by now.”
Crow folds his arms in a huff, “You’re insufferable.”
Ren smirks, and shrugs.
“This is kinda nice.” Ren mumbles as he places the coffee down on the bar, “Talking with
you without all the weird memory stuff.”
“I don’t think there’s a way to separate me from all the ‘weird memory stuff’.” Crow says
dryly, picking up the new cup, “And you can talk to the me in the real world, can’t you?”
“Yeah.” Ren agrees, and he would make a note to spend more time with Akechi if he could
remember this afterwards. He frowns, “Is Akechi forgetting all of this as well, or is he just
fucking with me?”
“He can’t remember, either.” Crow says, in a rare bout of clarity, “No one can.”
Ren’s eyes narrow, “So this is bigger than just us?”
“Your actions don’t exist in a vacuum.” Crow explains, giving Ren a piercing look, “Your
actions have consequences. And they have had consequences, beyond the scope of you and
I.”
Ren’s eyes narrow even further, “What the hell happened for the end result to be all of this?”
“Oh, you know.” Crow says flatly, knowing full well that Ren, in fact, does not know.
Ren sighs and slaps his hands over his face, “Part of me doesn’t even want to try guessing,
because I get the feeling that it’s going to be both so much simpler and so much more insane
than anything I could come up with.”
“Giving up already?” Crow raises an eyebrow.
“Why me?” Ren says, and then winces when it sounds too whiny, “I mean,” He starts again,
“Why are you trying to get just me to remember? What about Akechi? What about anyone
else who got caught up in this.” Ren pauses. “And why are you trying to get me to hate you
while you’re at it?”
Crow scowls, “I don’t have much choice in the matter. You’re a wildcard. You’re supposed to
remember this stuff, and it’s insanely frustrating that you don’t. And I can’t leave your head to
try with anyone else.” He tilts his head, “As for the last, it just seems to be in my nature. You
might want to examine your own cognition, for that one.”

Ren sighs, and files it away for later.
Ren traces random shapes into the countertop, “… No one else remembers?”
Crow hums, and tilts his head, “Well…”
Before Ren can leap onto that train of thought, the dream ends, and he wakes up.
As he rapidly gains lucidity, and feels the chime of the Aeon reaching rank seven, Ren tries
desperately to grasp at any details for the dream. He -quietly- slaps his hands against his face,
huffing, when he fails to grab anything.
Maybe these things are all dying down, Ren thinks, with a hope he doesn’t think is entirely
unfounded. Even though the Aeon is still ranking up, he’s having less of these dreams, and
the visions have all but stopped.
…Ren feels like he might jinx himself if he keeps thinking like that, but he remains hopeful
either way.
***
Sumire carefully tugs out another plant by its roots, placing it gingerly in one of the pots that
Haru has set up.
“I’m going to cut down the garden’s size by about half, now that we’re moving to the roof.”
Haru explains as she surveys the garden, “I’ve picked out the healthiest plants that I want to
keep.”
Sumire looks up from where she’s patting some dirt down onto the freshly buried plant,
“What about all the others?”
Haru sighs solemnly, and frowns, “I’m honestly not sure. I debated moving them to the
garden I keep on my balcony, but I don’t know if they’d all fit.”
Sumire hums, her eyes flicking back down to her work.
They continue in silence for a time, and Sumire jumps violently when the silence is broken.
“Okumura-san.” A voice cuts in, and Sumire looks up to see Kawakami approach the
gardens.
“Y-yes, Ms. Kawakami?” Haru blinks, clearly confused at being singled out by a teacher not
in charge of her class.
“Sorry, can I have a word?” Kawakami asks flatly, sounding bored, “You don’t have to leave,
Yoshizawa-san, it isn’t confidential or anything.”
Sumire nods awkwardly from where she’s squatted on the ground.

Kawakami sighs, “Anyway, the second-years are having their school trip to Hawaii next
week, and some things have come up.”
Haru tilts her head, furrowing her brow, “Oh?”
“The police have started getting antsy about catching the Phantom Thieves, and they want to
question the teachers here over the coming weeks.” Kawakami continues, “Which means that
some of us can’t go. So, we’re looking to get some of the third years in as proxies.”
Haru blinks, “Oh! You want me to go?”
“Yeah.” Kawakami shrugs, “You’re one of the more responsible students, so the staff
collectively decided that you were one of our top choices.”
Haru nods, a smile spreading on her face, “Thank you, Ms. Kawakami. I’d love to go.”
Kawakami slumps in relief, “Great. Thanks, Okumura-san.” She makes an aborted move to
leave, before quickly turning back around, “Oh, and Niijima-san is going as well, so you can
ask her if you have any more questions.”
Kawakami turns and leaves, and Sumire waits until she’s a decent distance away before she
turns to Haru.
“Um, so I’m also going to be in Hawaii that week.” Sumire starts.
She hadn’t forgotten, definitely not- she’s just had other things on her mind. Such as a
government conspiracy.
Haru blinks in surprise, “Really? That’s…”
“Convenient?” Sumire finishes, “It’s a second-year trip, so that means that all of the Phantom
Thieves except for Futaba-senpai and Morgana are going, I think.”
Haru nods slowly, before frowning, “Even Kitagawa-kun?”
“Yeah…” Sumire starts, remembering how she had seen the artist last timeline in the
souvenir shop. She never questioned why he was there, so she supposes that might be up in
the air.
“Well, he was there last time.” Sumire decides on, shrugging.
Haru presses her lips together, “This might be a good opportunity to start subtly influencing
the thieves, if we get the chance.”
Sumire nods quickly, “I think so, too. Well, if things start happening with your dad at that
point.”
Haru hums, tilting her head, “Do you remember when that started happening, last time?
Goro-kun didn’t seem to have an exact ‘start date’ for us to work with.”

Sumire wracks her brain, frowning, “I… think some things started happening by the time I
went to Hawaii? I was so focused on gymnastics at the time, though, so I wasn’t really paying
attention.”
Haru smiles, “That’s okay. It’s not like everything will happen all at once, so we have time to
improvise.”
Sumire nods, and shoots her a relieved smile, “I’m sorry that all my information is kind of
vague. I only started paying more attention after I awakened my persona, last time.”
“When did that happen?” Haru asks.
“Early October.” Sumire replies confidently- this she remembers quite well, “It was sort of an
accident, but once I knew who all the Phantom Thieves were, I wanted to make sure they
were okay, even if I didn’t join them at the time.”
Haru hums, “Well, by the sounds of it, that’s around the time that things started getting a bit
dire, so it’ll be good to have some extra knowledge on the situation.”
Sumire makes a sound of agreement, and turns back to the plants.
***
“How are we even going to get any info on the black mask?” Ryuji asks with no small
amount of annoyance in his voice, leaning back in his chair.
“It does seem an impossible task.” Yusuke chimes in gravely, leaning against Ren’s work
bench.
Ann leans back against the couch, “It’s not like we can just… stake out Mementos, or
anything. We’d be waiting for months.”
“That, and forcing an encounter with an assassin isn’t exactly what I’d call an advised course
of action.” Makoto adds dryly.
Ren frowns, breathing out sharply through his nose. He tries not to let his theories run amok
in his head, knowing that he can’t really back them up.
How to catch the black mask, his team asks? Well, he could discretely try and ‘accidentally’
activate the Nav around Yoshizawa, and see what happens. He could also enlist the help of
Morgana to tail her- or, if she’s been spying on them, see if she trips up with Morgana’s
voice.
Of course, that could also lead to just accidentally dragging a completely uninvolved girl into
the Metaverse with no persona. Or having a cat stalk her. Or having a cat meow at her
nonsensically.
…This is why Ren didn’t want to let his theories get out of hand.

He must look a little too deep in thought, as Morgana shoots him a questioning look. Ren
waves him off, and is saved from further prying by Futaba’s low cackle.
“You’re all thinking too inside the box.” She says, fingers rapidly tapping away at her laptop,
“We’re not the only ones looking for this guy- we’re just the only ones with access to the
Metaverse.”
“Uh… ain’t that the point?” Ryuji asks, furrowing his brow, “Aren’t we the best people to
catch this guy if we’re the only ones who know how he’s doing it?”
“Sure, we’re the best candidates to catch the black mask,” Futaba nods, not looking up from
her screen, “But as for finding their identity, I’d say the police have a much more organised
system.”
Makoto raises an eyebrow, “How do you expect them to have any idea?”
“Spreadsheets.” Futaba says flatly, “We don’t know anything about the black mask, but if
they’re an assassin, then they’re probably working for someone, right?”
There’s a round of nods from everyone.
“So!” Futaba continues, “Someone’s gotta be analysing all the mental shutdowns and
psychotic breaks, right? So if we just get a hold of that, and take a look at who the majority of
these incidents are benefiting, then bam! We have our mastermind, if not the black mask
themselves.”
“Then we can check out their palace.” Ren murmurs, “There’d probably be a whole lot of
stuff about the mental shutdowns in there, if they’re the one orchestrating them.”
“Bingo!” Futaba cheers, finishing her typing with a flourish, “We just need a lead, and then
all the rest should fall like dominoes.”
“But how are we going to get information like that?” Makoto cuts in.
“Uh…” Ann leans forward, “Makoto, didn’t you say your sister was on the mental shutdowns
case?”
Makoto sighs, pressing her lips together, “Yes…”
“And Ren,” Yusuke tilts his head, “Aren’t you and Akechi-san somewhat close? I recall he’s
on that case as well.”
Ren frowns, but nods anyway.
“Hey, that’s like half the problem already solved!” Futaba says, looking between the two of
them, “Now we just find a way to get some information off them.”
Makoto opens and closes her mouth, “I- can’t you just hack the police database, or
something?” She asks weakly, and Ren is inclined to agree.

“Not unless I wanna get arrested, I don’t.” Futaba raises her eyebrows, “I mean, I could, but
it’s kinda risky. There’s a whole lot of firewalls that’ll ping if I try to push past them.”
Makoto presses her lips together, “I mean, I can’t just ask my sister about her case. She
barely talks to me at all.”
“Does she have a laptop, or something?” Futaba asks, tilting her head, “I’d prefer raw
information over just asking your sis for the deets.”
Makoto sighs, “She does bring her laptop home sometimes…”
“Then here!” Futaba whips out a USB, “This’ll copy the hard drive, and bypass the OS
password. All you need to do is plug it in.”
Makoto tentatively reaches out and takes the USB, looking at it with a conflicted expression.
“You don’t have to if you don’t want to!” Ann says quickly, “This is kind of a big ask…”
“Yeah,” Ryuji cuts in, “And Ren can ask Akechi too, right? We’ve got a backup!”
“I don’t want to betray his trust.” Ren says quietly, “I’m definitely not stealing from him. I
don’t even think I could- I’ve never seen him with a laptop or anything.”
The thieves deflate at his declaration, and then turn to Makoto with a hopeful expression.
Makoto worries her lips together, “I…” She sighs, “Fine. If Ren doesn’t want to do
anything…” She mutters, sounding slightly bitter, which Ren elects to ignore, “I’ll try, next
time she comes home.”
There’s a collective -and not very subtle- sigh of relief, and Makoto slumps, “I can’t promise
anything, though!” She says firmly, “And I’ll definitely be in trouble if I get caught.”
“Just don’t get caught then.” Futaba says, ducking back down to stare at her laptop with
intensity.
“Right…” Makoto mumbles, looking resigned. Ren shoots her an apologetic look, and she
frowns deeper in response.
The meeting trails off after that, with the plan in place. Ren drags the table and chairs back
into place after the thieves leave, slumping onto his bed from exhaustion.
Morgana pokes at his shoulder, “You should probably go to bed early, if you’re this tired.”
“Yeah.” Ren mumbles, turning onto his stomach and burying his face in his pillow.
“At least eat dinner first!” Morgana yelps, “And brush your teeth!”
A smile tugs at the corner of Ren’s lips, and he buries his face further into his pillow.

Morgana gives an exasperated sigh, and curls up into a loaf. After a beat, he speaks up, “Hey,
I’ve noticed you always get this weird look when we talk about the black mask.”
Ren freezes, and then slowly peels his face back up to look at Morgana properly, “What do
you mean?”
“Well…” Morgana huffs, “You look really deep in thought. Like you’re considering
something.” He flicks his tail, “Do you… have some suspicions about someone? Or do you
know something?”
Ren opens his mouth, then clicks it shut. He didn’t realise he was being so transparent.
Thinking on it, though, probably only Morgana has enough of a catalogue on his facial
expressions to notice something’s up.
He could tell Morgana. He doesn’t want to worry the thieves, since they’re all pretty fond of
Yoshizawa, but Morgana has no such reservations. But, on the other hand, he doesn’t want to
split the group into parts with what knowledge he grants. The Phantom Thieves only act on
unanimous decision, but that hardly holds if Ren’s allowing them to operate on differing
information.
He’ll keep it to himself, for now.
“Nope.” Ren eventually responds, “I’m just kinda worried, s’all.”
Morgana narrows his eyes into slits, “Really?”
“Yep.” Ren lies with his best poker face, “Who wouldn’t be, in this situation?” He mashes his
face back into the pillow, signalling the end of the conversation.
He can feel Morgana’s eyes on him for a long pause, before Morgana makes a sound
somewhere between a hiss and a growl, and trots out the window.
Ren sighs, and rolls over to look at the ceiling.
Maybe he should speak to Yoshizawa more.

Akechi chooses not to interrupt Haru’s moment of solemnity as she surveys the garden before
them- a third of its planters already emptied and moved elsewhere.
The courtyard is painted in a golden-orange light, as the sun starts to dip behind the cityscape
surrounding Shujin’s main building. Haru had invited him to help out with this particular
task- something he only agreed to do if there were no other students around, thus, the late
hour.
“It’s a bit sad…” Haru murmurs, which Akechi thinks might be an understatement, looking at
her expression, “I put a lot of effort into this garden, and now I have to get rid of most of it.”
Akechi hums, “You haven’t considered moving it elsewhere?”

Haru shakes her head, “I have. I mentioned it to Sumi-chan, but I don’t have anywhere that
all these plants could fit. And it would be a lot of work, too.”
Akechi nods, “I see. Well, how are we disposing of all this?”
“We basically just need to take everything out of the ground and toss it into one big pile,”
Haru says after a beat, clearly collecting her thoughts, “The school set it up for someone to
come and collect it, I believe.”
Akechi scoffs, “They couldn’t have made it so this other person took care of this part of the
process as well?”
The corners of Haru’s mouth twitch up, “Too much effort to organise, I suppose. And
besides, I don’t mind the work, and it’s a good chance to say goodbye.”
Akechi won’t pretend to understand Haru’s sentimentality towards a garden that could be
easily cultivated elsewhere, but he hums in affirmation all the same. He tries not to look too
disgusted by the idea of digging a bunch of roots out of the dirt, and gingerly peels off his
gloves, putting them in his pocket.
Haru must sense his apprehension, as she tosses him a pair of gardening gloves. Akechi
catches them, sending her a grateful nod as he slips them over his hands.
They get to work in silence, scooping up plants by the roots one-by-one, and tossing them
into a slowly growing pile at the edge of the courtyard.
After a while, Haru speaks up, “Do you remember when we first met?”
Akechi raises an eyebrow at the sudden question, “At one of Shido’s functions, yes.”
Haru’s eyes widen, “You know, I never actually thought about that.” She smiles, “I’m
guessing the reason you gave me for why you were there was a lie?”
Akechi smirks, “Indeed it was. Shido wanted me there to get some palace keywords out of
some people he wanted to have insurance on.” He scowls, roughly tugging out some
particularly stubborn roots, “I had long since finished by the time I met you in the gardens,
but I wasn’t exactly in a position to leave early.”
Haru laughs behind her hand, “You didn’t seem particularly enthused.”
“No.” Akechi agrees dryly, “But neither did you.”
“No…” She says quietly, shaking her head. “I did enjoy it a little more once we started
talking, though.”
Akechi hums, “Speaking with you was certainly more entertaining than speaking with the
other rich assholes there.”
Haru giggles properly at that, “We did spend quite a bit of time making fun of their gardening
tastes, didn’t we?”

“Truthfully, Haru-san, I know shit about gardening.” Akechi says flatly.
“Well, our opinions seemed to line up either way.” She says with a cheerful smile, clearly
supressing more laughter. She frowns after a moment, “I was thinking about that
conversation recently, which is why I brought it up.”
Akechi hums, nodding slightly for her to continue.
Haru lets out a small sigh, “Sumi-chan once asked me why I started gardening. I told her that
it was some combination of finding it an interesting hobby, and another bullet point in a
string of failed attempts to connect with my father.”
“…But that’s not the whole truth.” Akechi guesses.
“It seems not.” Haru says, lacing her fingers together clumsily through the gardening gloves,
“I never quite considered the reason why I enjoy gardening so much, but I think part of it may
be the control.”
Akechi tilts his head, regarding her with a serious look.
“It makes sense,” He settles on saying, “Given the way that you have been treated in many
aspects of your life.”
Akechi has certainly scrambled for any semblance of control ever since he first got a small
taste of it. It’s an odd dichotomy that he feels- both the need to be meticulous in every aspect
of his existence, and the desire for complete freedom and chaos. He supposes that Haru’s
garden may actually strike that balance, in her life.
He would take a leaf out of her book if he wasn’t so horrible at keeping things alive.
“I’m just a little surprised that I never noticed it for what it was.” Haru admits, moving to
scoop out another plant from the soil, “It’s rather obvious, in hindsight. I think I spent so long
telling myself that I was okay with how things were that I never realised that so much of what
I do is a way to cope.”
“Does that change anything about it for you?” Akechi asks, then snorts, “Do you view
yourself as a tyrant of the school gardens?”
Haru presses her lips together in a small smile, “Something like that.”
Akechi lets out a small noise of acknowledgement, and turns back to the soil.
“…You’re nothing like your father.” He says after a pause, “Which I believe is one of the
highest compliments I can give to people like us.”
Haru freezes, halfway through raising a mess of dirt and roots out of the ground, before she
gives a bright smile that crinkles the corners of her eyes, “Thank you, Goro-kun.”
Akechi shrugs, uncomfortable with how genuine she seems, and looks back down at the
ground.

Haru laughs slightly, “I think that I feel better now that gardening isn’t the only avenue of
control I can have over my life. The Metaverse and helping you feel like things I can do for
myself.” She winces, “Not to say that I want to help you only for my own benefit.”
Akechi shakes his head, the corner of his lips tugging upwards, “Honestly, Haru-san, the fact
that you’re helping me for yourself doesn’t concern me at all. If anything, it makes me feel a
bit better about all of this.”
Haru sighs wearily, but her smile gives her away. “Anyway, I’m glad that I can finally choose
a path for myself. I know that our scheme is to try and have our cake and eat it too, but I
really think that we’ll be able to do it.”
Akechi pauses, “…What will you do if we can’t?”
Haru looks up, “Hm?”
“What do you intend to do if we don’t manage to avert the Phantom Thieves from falling for
Shido’s trap?” He clarifies, giving her a piercing look.
Haru’s expression falters, and she bites her lip, “…I don’t know if that’s my choice to make.”
“Why not?” Akechi raises an eyebrow, “Your father’s life is at stake.”
“And so is yours.” She points out firmly, “It isn’t fair for me to ask you to sacrifice yourself
in place of my father.”
“You could argue it isn’t fair for me to kill him to save myself, either.” Akechi says blankly,
standing up to toss a plant into the pile.
Haru laughs sadly, “Well, none of it’s fair, is it?”
“No.” Akechi says grimly, “No, it isn’t.”
Haru sighs, and then forces a smile, “Well, that’s why we have to succeed, right?”
“We can only hope.” Akechi says dryly, squatting back down next to the planters.
By the time they finish clearing out all of the planters, leaving only haphazard piles of dirt
and soil strewn about, the sun has nearly entirely gone down.
Haru dusts off her skirt and peels off her gloves as she prepares to leave. Akechi tosses her
the borrowed gloves, and turns towards the exit.
“Oh, Goro-kun,” Haru calls out, and he turns his head, “One last thing.”
“Yes?” He turns to face her fully, raising an eyebrow.
“If we do fail,” She starts, a serious look on her face, “Then you should do what’s best for
you. Don’t let yourself get hurt for my sake.”

Akechi raises an eyebrow, “I wasn’t planning on it.” He runs a hand through his hair,
“Besides- you said it yourself, we’re going to succeed, right?”
She smiles, “Right.”
As Akechi takes his leave, he can feel the Strength grow to rank six.

Sumire hides a yawn behind her hand, and rubs at her eyes underneath her glasses. At her
side, Haru doesn’t seem to be faring much better, as she blinks away sleep in her eyes, and
politely clenches her jaw to supress a yawn of her own.
“Why is the plane so early…?” Sumire mumbles, slumping onto one of the -very
uncomfortable- airport chairs.
“I think they want us to arrive during the day, to make things easier.” Haru returns sleepily,
“And you didn’t have to get a flight this early, Sumi-chan- didn’t you have to arrange your
own transportation?”
“Yeah…” Sumire sighs, very much regretting her decision to book the same flight that the
rest of the Shujin students were taking. She could have just taken a flight at a far more
reasonable hour, but she felt it would be nice to travel with Haru. It became significantly less
nice when she had to wake up at four in the morning for it, though.
“Oh…” A quiet gasp interrupts Sumire’s self-pity.
“Niijima-san,” Haru’s eyebrows shoot up, and she gives a small smile, “It’s good to see you
here.”
“Oh, yes,” Makoto returns the smile, if a bit awkwardly, “I didn’t realise that you were going
on this trip as well, Haru-san. I was just surprised to see you- and you as well, Sumire-chan,”
She narrows her eyes, “Actually, aren’t you a first year?”
Sumire blinks, and flushes, “Um, yes, but I’m going to Hawaii for a gymnastics training
camp.”
Makoto’s eyes widen, “That’s quite the coincidence that it lines up with the location and the
timing for the second-year trip.”
Sumire feels like she’s being interrogated, for some reason. “I apologise…?”
Makoto jumps, “Oh, I didn’t mean to-” She sighs, “That was kind of pushy, huh?”
Haru giggles behind her hand, “A little. But it does seem like you, Niijima-san.”
Makoto’s lips press together in a near-pout, “I can’t tell if that’s a compliment or not. Oh, and
you can call me Makoto, if you’d like. I already call you by your given name, after all.”
Haru nods cheerfully, “Of course, Makoto-san.”

“So, when do we have to start boarding?” Sumire asks, standing up from the chair she was
slumped on to be on level ground with the other two.
“In about forty-five minutes, I believe.” Makoto answers matter-of-factly, then frowns, “It’s a
little worrying that we’re some of the only people here. I would have thought that it would be
a good idea to arrive a little early for something like an international flight.”
“Maybe most of the other students are struggling to wake up this early?” Haru suggests.
“Well, between waking up early and missing the flight altogether…” Sumire counters.
“That’s true,” Makoto nods at Sumire, “If anyone misses the flight, it’s their loss. It’s too late
to be properly refunded for the trip’s expenses- unless something actually happens, and they
can have insurance cover it.”
“Oh thank god I’m not late…” Another loud, bright, voice cuts in. Ann staggers dramatically
over to the group, throwing her arm around Makoto’s shoulder and pouting, “It’s so early, this
sucks.”
Sumire laughs slightly, “We were just talking about that, actually.”
“Oh, really?” Ann straightens up, then sighs, “I wish they picked a better time. Surely there
was a reasonable hour that still would have lined up well with Hawaii’s time zone…”
Haru winces, “I forgot about the time zone difference, actually.” She frowns, and mumbles,
“I hope there isn’t an emergency or anything that happens in the middle of the night in our
time.”
Makoto tilts her head, “Is there anything that you’re worried about, Haru-san?”
Sumire supresses a grimace, and Haru pastes on a reassuring smile, “Not at all, Makoto-san,
nothing out of the ordinary.”
Not for people like them, at least, Sumire thinks- Metaverse issues are becoming constants in
all of their lives, so much so that she’s almost expecting something to go wrong while she
and Haru are out of the country.
…She probably shouldn’t jinx herself like that.
Ann’s head swivels around as she bounces on her toes, “Ugh,” She groans, “Ren and Ryuji
aren’t here yet.” She rolls her eyes, “If they’re late, I’ll kill them.”
“We still have about half an hour until we need to board,” Sumire says placatingly as she
checks the time, hoping to avoid a murder, “Oh, and…”
Speak of the devils and they shall appear. Sumire gives an awkward wave to Ren as he
approaches the group, a shock of blond hair dragging behind him.
“I almost didn’t wake up in time…” Ryuji whines as he joins the circle.

Ann gives him a look, “How did you wake up?”
“My mom hauled my ass outta bed.” He deadpans, rubbing his eyes.
Makoto sighs, “Well, whatever works…”
Sumire tries to ignore the piercing look that Ren is giving her. “What are you doing here,
Yoshizawa?” He asks after a beat.
Ann swivels around, “Oh, yeah!”
“I have a gymnastics training camp,” Sumire explains again, “Since it lines up with your trip,
I thought it would be nice to take the same flight, so…” She gestures vaguely to herself.
Ryuji snorts in commiseration, “Bet you’re regrettin’ that one.”
Sumire’s shoulders slump, “Yep…”
She continues to ignore Ren’s look, and ignores him even harder when his eyes narrow
slightly at her explanation.
She isn’t quite sure what to make of that. She smiles brighter to hide the doubt that starts to
creep over her skin.
Makoto looks around, and purses her lips, “There’s still not nearly as many students here as
there should be.”
“What are you, a teacher?” Ryuji grouses.
“I think she kind of is, for this trip,” Ren cuts in, tugging at his fringe, “The third-years are
teacher proxies, remember?”
“Does that mean you’re here for that too, Haru-san?” Ann asks, leaning on her suitcase.
“Mmhm!” Haru nods.
It looks like a few people are halfway through opening their mouths to say more, before
Ren’s phone buzzes loudly.
Several heads swivel to look at him, and he frowns. He takes out his phone, and his
expression crumples into something distinctly unimpressed.
“I think Futaba bugged my phone.” He offers by way of explanation, and Makoto sighs
wearily.
“That’s…” She starts, then deflates, “I don’t think she’d care about my complaints, actually.”
Ren’s phone buzzes again, “She says you’re right.” He says, clearly trying to supress a grin.
Sumire jumps as yet another voice cuts into their conversation. “Guys!” Mishima jogs up to
the group, “The teachers are saying that we should starts boarding soon, just so you know.”

He jogs off again before anyone gets a chance to respond.
“What?!” Ann whines, “But there’s still like, twenty minutes, right?”
“I suppose they just want us to be early.” Haru sighs, a small frown pulling at her lips, “It’s
certainly better than being late, in this case.”
“Well, I guess that makes sense.” Ann concedes, outrage evaporated.
“Hey, before we go-” Ryuji says hurriedly, “We should take a picture, right?”
“That sounds quite nice, actually,” Makoto nods, smoothing out her skirt.
“I can take it,” Ren volunteers, then frowns and stretches out his arms, “I think I can get us
all in.”
“Ooh, a selfie?” Ann asks cheerfully, wrapping her arms around all three of the other thieves,
“Well, get in, then!” She looks over her shoulder, “You two as well! You’re not getting out of
this.”
Sumire jumps, “Oh! If you’re sure…?”
“Hell yeah, man!” Ryuji gesture excitedly, “Come on!”
Haru laughs, “If you insist!”
Sumire squishes awkwardly between Ryuji and Makoto, while Haru finds room on the edge.
Ren winces slightly as he hyperextends his arm to fit all of them in the shot.
“Say cheese,” He says with a grin, and Sumire smiles brightly as the camera flashes.
Ren pulls his phone back in, and gives the photo an approving nod, turning it around to show
everyone else. As they all take a look, another message pings at the top of the screen.
Taba: you all look like nerds lol
Sumire giggles, “That’s mean, Futaba-senpai.”
Another message pings,
Taba: ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
“Stop spying on me.” Ren chides to his phone without heat.
“…Man, she can really hear everything, huh?” Ryuji says, eyeing the phone suspiciously.
Sumire pulls out her own phone, “Um, actually, can we take another one quickly? I kind of
want to send a photo to Goro.”
Ren turns to look at her, “I can just send this one to him, if you’d like?”

Sumire blinks, “Oh! That works too.” She smiles in a way she hopes is natural.
Ren turns to his phone, tapping away. After a beat he snorts, and shows Sumire the screen.
Ren: [img attached] hey Yoshizawa said she wanted to send this photo to you
Akechi: Amamiya, it’s 5am.
Sumire giggles behind her hand. She stops, awkwardly, around the same time that Ren does,
and they both look away uncomfortably.
This is definitely starting to get out of hand, she thinks.
Sumire’s aware that she kind of started it, but the fact that Ren is now just as uncomfortable
as she is definitely signals something bad.
Before she can get too in her head, the group starts shuffling off towards the boarding area,
and Sumire quickly jogs to keep up.

Chapter 30
Chapter Summary

Hawaii, murder, dreams, and the fabric of reality.

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

Ren knows he’s being paranoid. At this point, he’s willing to consider that being paranoid
might be a permanent personality trait. It certainly wasn’t always this way- Ren would have
actually considered himself fairly trusting, up until somewhat recently. Giving someone the
benefit of the doubt was something of a personal skill.
But Sumire Yoshizawa is stressing him the hell out.
He can’t help but see everything she does as some underhanded way to ingratiate herself with
the thieves- even when Ren has next to no proof that she even has an inkling as to who they
are.

Akechi knocks lightly on the door to Shido’s office.
“Enter.” A grating voice barks from the other side.

‘I’, he says, like he personally has the hacking skills required to enact this plan. Akechi

“I have no doubt that the thieves will fall for this,” Akechi says with a smug smile, “They’ve

push them to target Okumura as planned.”
Conversation is always a game, when you want something. Give a little, and take everything
you can find. Don’t interrogate- such an act is akin to breaking open someone’s ribs and
wrenching out what you need.
No, to win the game, subtlety is required. Misdirection, flattery, slight of hand- dazzle them
with words so they won’t notice the chisel you’ve taken to their skull.
“Get to the point, Akechi.” Shido snaps, finally looking up.

A game that Akechi finds far easier to play when his opponent isn’t an absolute piece of shit

Subtlety can be forgone when you have a good excuse.
Akechi can guess what Shido wants to do with the Phantom Thieves once they’re backed into
a corner. Murder seems to be his favourite solution to every problem, and Sumire already

But as much as Akechi can assume, for all his associates, himself, and the Phantom Thieves

It’s getting harder not to gag when he says shit like that, these days.

In the space between dreams and reality, a god’s ill-fitting skin curls its mouth into a smile.
Tides are turning, and fate becomes ever more obscured, hm? When his chosen trickster
asked about the weave of time, he had become admittedly quite curious.

A factor in the game that even he, the one who set out the board, had overlooked? It seemed
unlikely. His pride alone had dissuaded him from examining the idea further.
But now…
The other trickster seems to be making waves in the weave of reality. Purely by mistake, at
that. He doesn’t know what has spurned this change, but perhaps…?
The god tugs on the thread of the Fool connecting him to his opponent’s pawn. It is by his
own intervention that this trickster has started down the path that the god wishes for him to
follow, and yet he strays anyway.
He formed no such bond with his own trickster. He could see, merely by peering into the
fractured soul of his champion, that he would traverse the path of ruin no matter the sway of
outside forces. He need only watch, and observe as he wins the game without raising a single
finger.
And yet, it seems that has changed.
The god leans back, and ignores the piercing stare of the shattered attendant. He draws a card
out from his stolen deck of tarot, and allows the Magician to fly out and hover in the space in
front of him.
The god may consider his lack of bond with his champion an oversight, especially now that
the Fool has been attributed to another source. He lacks the connection to examine the
Magician’s sway further.
The other trickster lacks a bond with this entity, as well. A shame.
The god slides the Magician back into the deck, and smiles wider at the small chime he feels
when he reaches too far.
A slim, likely accidental, but entirely undeniable connection to the Velvet Room.
My, the god thinks, how desperate were the times to necessitate this?

Sumire sits down on one of the benches littering the beach-side footpath with a slump. She
finally has some free time after several days of intensive gymnastics training, and it’s just
now hitting her how much her body hurts.
Her coach did warn her to take a break, but Sumire has been incredibly neglectful in her
practice as of late, and a meet is coming up in late September. She felt that now was as good
a time as any to start making up for lost time.
…She probably should have taken a break. Her muscles feel like jelly.
Sumire thinks back to what Haru told her the other night, when she managed to catch Sumire
before she headed back to her hotel.
She does remember the principal dying, as she had various interactions with the vice
principal as a proxy after it happened. The thing she forgot, was that it was a mental
shutdown that killed him.
Sumire isn’t actually sure she ever knew it was a mental shutdown- she heard a few things,
from a heart attack, to suicide, to an unfortunate road accident- in hindsight, the unclear cause
of death should have been a red flag.
She’s honestly trying not to think about the principal too much. She isn’t exactly the man’s
biggest fan, but, well, murder…
(Sumire finds that she stops feeling bad rather quickly when she remembers it’s a choice
between the principal’s death or putting Goro in danger. That train of thought makes her feel
a bit bad too, though, so she chooses to ignore it entirely.)
The other thing Haru reminded her of is that her father has started making the news, meaning
they can start talking about him in relation to a change of heart without sounding insanely
suspicious.
Sumire picks at the edges of her nails, and frowns. Maybe that’s why Ren is acting cold
towards her? Does he think that she’s acting suspicious? She did almost get caught in
Kaneshiro’s palace that one time, but surely if Ren saw her he’d have already confronted her

about it. That, and none of the thieves seem to hold the same reservations- Surely Ren would
have said something if he was concerned?
"Sumi-chan!" A cheerful voice cuts through Sumire’s spiral of theories, and she looks up and
smiles.
“Hello, Haru-senpai.” Sumire shuffles over slightly to make room for Haru to sit.
Haru smooths out her skirt and shuffles against the back of the bench, “I feel like I’ve hardly
seen you at all. You’ve just been so busy.”
Sumire laughs sheepishly, “Well, I’m finally taking a break now!”
Haru smiles, “That’s good. I wouldn’t want you to burn out.”
Sumire hums in agreement, and they fall into relatively comfortable silence.
After a beat, Haru tilts her head, a lightly perplexed expression on her face, “Is that…?”
Sumire follows Haru’s line of sight, and, sure enough, sees Ren, Ryuji, and Yusuke
wandering around and talking to locals.
“Huh.” Haru mumbles under her breath, “I guess Kitagawa-kun really is here.”
Sumire nods absently, and gives the three boys a wave when they finish up their conversation
with a tall man who seems to be cheerfully entertaining whatever topic the thieves had
brought up.
Ryuji brightens when he sees Sumire and Haru, and jogs over, Yusuke and Ren trailing
behind.
“Hey guys,” He says with a grin.
“Hello, Ryuji-kun,” Haru says politely, “How has the trip been for you so far?”
“Pretty good, pretty good.” Ryuji rubs at his nose, “It doesn’t feel too different from when we
all went to the beach.”
“I guess beaches are pretty universal.” Sumire says, considering.
“Indeed,” Yusuke chimes in, “Though I must say, this particular beach presents a pristine aura
which I believe I would be hard-pressed to discover in Tokyo.”
Haru giggles behind her hand, “Well, it is a resort location. They like to pretty the place up
for the tourists. But,” Haru tilts her head, “Why are you here, Kitagawa-kun?”
“Hm?” Yusuke turns back from where he was framing the ocean view with his hands, “Ah,
yes. Kosei was set to visit Los Angeles this week, however a storm diverted our path, and we
happened to settle in the same location as Shujin.”

Sumire blinks.
Haru also blinks, “Oh…”
Ren coughs, “It is a lot weirder than I originally gave it credit for, now that I think about it.”
Yusuke turns to Ren, “What are you talking about? I though it a perfectly reasonable
sequence of events.”
Ren pats Yusuke on the shoulder, “Sure.”
“Um, anyway,” Sumire starts, trying to keep the amused smile off her face, “What were you

“Well, since the Phantom Thieves took down Medjed, we were wonderin’ if even folks

Bingo. A perfect segue. Sumire tries not to tense, or seem too eager. At her side, she can feel

Ren frowns, “You don’t sound too happy about it.”
Haru smiles weakly, “Don’t get me wrong, I’m very grateful for all that the thieves have done

“It was lovely speaking to you both.” Yusuke says with a polite bow, and he turns to leave.
“See ya!” Ryuji says brightly with a wave, and jogs off in the same direction.
Ren stays, and tilts his head slightly with an unreadable expression.

“I don’t have any issue with the people themselves, so much,” Haru laughs, “I’ve never met

If turning a shadow insane is like a slow or rapid or maybe nothing at all unravelling of
Akechi’s mind, then killing one is a little more like dousing his heart in liquid nitrogen.
A sharp, all-encompassing, hit of something, until the ice takes hold and Akechi can feel
nothing but pleasantly numb.
Even the ‘pleasantly’ might be a stretch. Such is the nature of being numb, after all- it’s hard
to tell if a limb hurts when it’s functionally dead, for a time.
There was a point, several years ago, when Akechi’s hand would have shaken as he stares
down the whimpering and defeated shadow, blubbering apologies and begging mercy. At that
time, killing someone and turning them insane were both equally unpleasant.
But now, as the thrill of battle fades, Akechi simply gives the shadow of Hiroshi Kobayakawa
a look laced with dispassionate disdain, and pulls the trigger.
There. Done.
…
Doing it doesn’t feel any different from before.
Akechi sighs, lowering the gun, and holstering it at his side. He doesn’t feel bad, but he
doesn’t feel good, either. He would love if his mind could come up with a slightly stronger
reaction.
Akechi rolls his eyes when neither half of his mind decides to comment.
He turns on his heel, pulling back the curtain of distortion. As soon as he steps through the
other side, the portal vanishes like a whirlpool, leaving a flat wall in its wake.
His bonds do not shiver, do not cut at his insides for the deed he has just done. They simply
sit, and make no indication of their opinion.
Huh. He’d assumed that the metaphysical representation of his connections with others
would be a little more morally aggrandising.
Akechi tilts his head, and leans against the newly formed wall, worrying his lips together.
In a bout of curiosity, he pulls on the Star.
After a beat, José’s car comes careening around the corner into the dead end, and screeches to
a halt far closer to Akechi than he would have preferred.
“Hey, mister!” José says cheerfully, bouncing out from the driver’s seat of the car to waddle
over and stand in front of Akechi, “It’s been a bit, huh?”
“It hasn’t been that long.” Akechi says, raising an eyebrow, “Though I’m never sure how
time passes in the Metaverse. It seems to vary.”

“Well, it passes when you’re here!” José answers brightly, and Akechi resists the urge to roll
his eyes. Some relativity bullshit, of course. “Or when any other human is around.”
Akechi shrugs, “Well, it hardly matters. I’m here now, right?”
José laughs, “You sure are, mister. What did you want to talk about?”
Akechi leans back against the wall, and slides to the ground, tucking his legs loosely against
his chest. “You’ve spoken about fate, in the past. How these bonds have the power to change
it, and such.” Akechi begins slowly, “But you’ve never really described to me what fate is.”
There’s a lingering fear in Akechi’s mind, born ever since the concept of fate was discussed.
What if fate is as it’s described in so many religious tales? Immutable, unchangeable, the
great expanse to the lonely speck of dust that is humanity, insignificant against the will of
gods?
No, some thread of logic had protested. If fate was set in stone, then why bother sending
Sumire back in time to alter an event? There has to be something, some factor of uncertainty
that humanity possessed, for whatever it is that caused this to even care. There has to be a
reason for why José, and apparently others like him, are so curious about humanity’s
supposed potential.
The fear remained, of course, swiftly ignored- Akechi despises the idea that his actions are
not his own. It is a fundamental contradiction of his very being, on a far greater level than
any other conflict that uses his soul as a battle ground.
So it is with morbid curiosity that Akechi broaches this question.
“Fate?” José asks, wide eyes blinking as he tilts his head, “Well… there’s a lot to say, I
guess.”
“If there is a way to change it,” Akechi prompts, “Then that implies that there is a way it
should be, yes?”
José frowns, “Well… not exactly?” He flops down onto the ground, sitting cross-legged,
“There isn’t like… a plan, or anything. It’s more like… a lot of things happen, in the past,
and the past informs the present. So, because of the past, some things just want to happen.”
Akechi breathes a sigh of relief. What a roundabout way to say that actions have
consequences.
“But,” José continues, “Sometimes you humans can put that limitless potential to use! So
even if something is ‘doomed’ to happen, a lot of people can come together and change fate!”
He claps his hands together, “Is that what you were asking, mister?”
Akechi nods, “Yes, it was.” He stretches out one leg, and looks at the ceiling of the tunnel,
“What’s the relevance with wildcards and their bonds, then?”
“Oh, well that’s easy!” José laughs, “You wildcards are especially good at changing fate- it’s
why that person is so interested in you! And when you deepen your bonds, you’re…

spreading yourself out? It’s all one big collaboration between you and your bonds to push
events in the direction you want them to go.”
Akechi raises an eyebrow, “So the more I rank up the arcana, the more I get what I want.”
“Uh, pretty much, mister.” José nods, looking a little perplexed at the wording. Akechi snorts.
“Us wildcards seem to be especially good at a lot of things.” Akechi say dryly after a beat.
“Well, yeah!” José exclaims, “You’re wildcards!”
Like that explains anything.
Akechi sighs, and wonders idly about the Tower.
A bond forged with a cognition. It seems like it would be difficult to have any impact on the
fate of something that isn’t even real. It hardly matters to the cognition if it lives or dies- it
isn’t alive to begin with.
Akechi doesn’t care either, so he wonders why the bond continues to grow.
The Star, almost as if it’s demanding attention, grows to rank six.
José smile brightly, “Hey, look at that! Speaking of.” He jumps up to his feet, “Is that all you
needed from me, mister? I have some flowers I need to collect.”
Akechi gives a nod, and slowly draws himself up from where he’s sitting on the -frankly
disgusting- ground.
José hops back into the driver’s seat of his car, and raises his leg to stomp on the pedal. He
freezes, mid-stomp, “Hey mister, did you want to collect flowers with me?”
Akechi narrows his eyes, “What would that entail?”
“Uh, well, mostly leaning out of the car and scooping up as many as you can?” José laughs
sheepishly, “I’m not picky on how you grab them.”
Akechi furrows his brows together with a healthy suspicion, “Sure…?”
“Great!” José bounces up and down, “This’ll be fun!”
It was not, in fact, fun.
Well, Akechi concedes that it may have been fun for José. It was decidedly less fun for
Akechi himself, who has the ill-fortune to be cursed with a human stomach and motion
sickness.
When José finally drifts to a stop against one of the subway platforms, it takes all of Akechi’s
willpower to not spill his rather pitiful lunch onto the tiles. He slowly draws himself back up
to standing and gives José a weak thumbs-up, not trusting himself to speak.

“That was great, mister!” José says with as much cheer as ever, “You were a lot of help- I
hope we can do this again, sometime!”
Akechi will never be doing this ever again. He still doesn’t trust himself to speak, however,
so he gives a vague gesture that José seems to interpret as agreement.
“I’ll see you around, mister!” His voice echoes through the subway tunnels as he peels off
into the darkness.
Akechi slumps against the wall, huffing.
He turns to leave, but pauses when he remembers another pending task. He’s pretty much
ignored the presence of Shiji-Ouki in his soul, the acquired persona’s strength truly pathetic
in comparison to Robin Hood and Loki.
But, he did promise the twins to try and collect a few more personas, no matter their
uselessness.
Akechi kicks off the wall, dropping down onto the train tracks. He cranes his neck to see
what shadows happen to be lumbering about, smirking as he sees one attempting to cower
around a corner.
He unholsters his gun, quickly shooting the shadow right in its mask, its hulking form
exploding with a shriek. It reforms, leaving a dog-headed shadow sitting cross-legged,
holding a scale in one hand.
The shadow growls, and Akechi rips off his mask.
“Loki!” He snaps, and throws out a heavy curse attack.
The shadow laughs as the curse glances off its skin, and Akechi hisses through his teeth as he
narrowly dodges the retaliating Hamaon that gets shot his way. He narrows his eyes, andAh. Immune to both bless and curse. Damn.
Well, nothing to be done. Akechi rolls his eyes and tries his luck with a Laevateinn,
slamming down onto the shadow while it’s laughing.
The shadow screams out as the flaming sword slices into the hand holding the scale, the
balance twisting, causing the shadow to go tumbling to the ground in a heap. Akechi grins,
knife-sharp, andFinds that it’s rather difficult to surround something with only one person.
Oh.
…Seriously?
Akechi scoffs to the empty air, shooting at the shadow several times in quick succession. It
evaporates into smoke with a pitiful whimper, and Akechi turns on his heel to leave.

What a waste of time.
When Akechi finally reaches the top floor of Mementos, he approaches the Velvet Room
door with a scowl. Caroline’s head snaps up as he approaches, and she levels him with a
glare.
“Been busy, defendant?” She says snappily, leaning on her baton. She narrows her visible
eye, “You don’t even have another persona for us to look at!”
“A negative result is still a result,” Akechi says breezily, folding his arms.
Caroline stomps her foot, “What the hell is that supposed to mean?!” She scoffs, and kicks

Justine emerges from the Velvet Room, wearing an unimpressed expression as she looks

“Yeah, yeah.” Akechi flips up his visor to pinch the bridge of his nose, “It isn’t difficult,” A

The twins’ eyes widen, as they both seem to come to the same conclusion that Akechi has

The main benefit of being a wildcard, as far as Akechi can tell, is the useful skill of being

The catch of wildcard abilities seems to be that ‘bonds are power’ isn’t just a cute metaphor.
The only way for Akechi to continue collecting personas is if he enlists Haru and Sumire to
lend him a hand in cornering shadows.
So, Igor’s insistence that Akechi ignore the arcana seems to have a far more precise purpose

“I don’t understand why our master…” Caroline frowns, trailing off.
Justine pulls her clipboard close to her chest, “It seems we have done you a disservice,

Akechi raises an eyebrow.
Justine sighs, “For reasons that I cannot comprehend, our master clearly seeks to supress your

Caroline furrows her brow, “I don’t know why we never…” She huffs, “Well, whatever.

“If there is, I’ve been left unaware.” Akechi says dryly.

“And if the defendant shouldn’t gain so much power, then what of the inmate?” Justine points
out, turning to her sister, “The defendant has proven that he and the inmate have the same
power in every way.”
Caroline groans, “Then what the hell?!” She crosses her arms in a huff, “Why would our
master do that?”
“Are you sure he’s entirely benevolent?” Akechi asks lightly.
“W-well…” Justine stutters, turning her gaze at the ground, suddenly looking much more

Caroline isn’t fairing much better, pressing her lips together, her eye occasionally flicking to

Akechi sighs. Perhaps now is not the time to push, then.
“Defendant.” Caroline eventually says, drawing herself back together, “We don’t know

“As our master has not given his reasoning for this situation, then we are not so much

Akechi thinks that reasoning is held together with rotting wood and tissue paper, but, hey,

“I’ll have a new persona for you to inspect next we meet, then.” Akechi nods sharply, turning

The twins both nod in agreement, and the Temperence reaches rank three.

As soon as Ren and the other thieves get back from Hawaii, Futaba gives him a sharp look

Morgana keeps giving him the side eye. Ren shifts uncomfortably, but otherwise deflects any

Sumire frowns up at the rapidly darkening sky. It’s later than she thought it was, coming back

Normal things, that happen to normal people.

Despite everything, despite the hot and sticky mess that is how she feels about all this, she

friend.

people to perform a hold-up. It kind of allows for a handwave of "if Akechi was a real
wildcard, then why didn't he pick up any personas?" since, well, he had no teammates to
help him out.

ambiguous on purpose. I think that even if Akechi /can/ recruit shadows- by the time of
the third semester, he's specifically not trying to out of spite. He seems to not use Robin
Hood out of spite, too, since we see in the engine room that he CAN swap his personas
without much fanfare and without changing his clothes, since he uses Loki to cast call of
chaos on the Cu Chulainn and Cerberus while still in his prince outfit, and then starts the
first half of the fight immediately after while using only Robin. So I guess Akechi just
wanted to be a dick in the third semester lol. That Samerecarm could've been helpful,

you already know, then why haven’t you arrested us?”
“It’s not like I have solid evidence, for one,” Akechi starts, wondering how this conversation
turned into an interrogation of him rather than the other way around, “And two: I didn’t want
to.”
“You.” Morgana opens and closes his eyes, like that will change what Akechi just said, “You
didn’t want to.”
“I didn’t want to.” Akechi agrees simply.
It’s not a lie. The best deceptions are laced in truth all the way up to the point where people
will stop looking, after all.
“Wait, then,” Morgana splutters, “Why did you say all that stuff about us on TV? And why
were you always kind of threatening us every time we saw you?”
“I don’t necessarily get to choose what I say on TV,” Akechi begins, thinking of the best way
to spin this, “Though a lot of my opinions are still my own- just because I don’t want to arrest
you, doesn’t mean I agree with you.”
“Then why…?” Morgana tilts his overly large head.
Akechi sighs, and finds he doesn’t have to fake the annoyance he feels in voicing this, “I
appear to have developed a modicum of fondness for Amamiya, and so I’d rather he don’t go
to jail. Most of my comments in the presence of your group were trying to get you all to cut it
out, or stop being so obvious.”

And, partially, because it was funny to see them squirm.
Morgana gives him an appraising look. He opens his mouth to say something, before jumping
at the sounds of more shadows approaching from down the hall.
“We should get out of here.” Morgana says hurriedly, “You must be exhausted, and I’m low
on stamina.”
Akechi hauls himself off his knees, making sure to sway on his feet slightly. “Alright. Which
way?”
“Follow me!” Morgana dashes off in the direction of the palace entrance, and Akechi follows
close behind.
“There should be an app on your phone that looks like a red eye,” Morgana explains as they
reach the foyer, “If you tap on that, we should get back to the real world.”
Akechi taps on the app, not wanting to draw out Morgana’s explanations of things he already
knows any longer than necessary. He makes sure to gasp in surprise as the world shifts back
into the plaza outside Okumura Foods HQ. Morgana dashes into the shadowed garden strip
along the side of the path, and Akechi joins him.
“So, now we’re back in the real world, I can get to explaining things properly.” Morgana
says, flicking his tail.
“You can talk.” Akechi says blankly, “Oh.”
“Surprised?” Morgana asks smugly.
Akechi smiles, “A little, I suppose. It does make sense, though. It would be rather
inconvenient if you had no way to communicate in this world.”
“Huh. Well, when you put it that way.” Morgana gives as much of a shrug as a cat can,
“Anyway, as I was saying about the Metaverse-”
“Wait.” Akechi interrupts, “Shouldn’t this wait until we meet with the rest of your group? I
would assume they would have some words for my inclusion in this.”
Morgana looks away, slumping slightly, “I’m… not part of the Phantom Thieves anymore.”
Oh?
Akechi narrows his eyes, “What do you mean? Did you quit?”
“Why is that your first assumption?!” Morgana yowls, and then looks sheepish, “But. Yeah. I
quit.”
Akechi raises an eyebrow and waits for Morgana to elaborate. When he doesn’t, Akechi
sighs, “…Why?”

“I just,” Morgana huffs, “Had a disagreement. And I’m mad at Ren.”
Akechi raises his other eyebrow, “You’re upset with Amamiya? Are you just going to ignore
him when you go back to Leblanc?”
“I’m not going back to Leblanc.” Morgana says simply, turning up his nose.
Akechi frowns, “Then where are you going to stay? Are you going to ingratiate yourself with
the local street cats?”
“Of course not!” Morgana yelps, sounding disgusted, “I’ll be staying with you, naturally.”
What.
“What.”
“I mean, you are a new persona user that I found,” Morgana continues, ignoring Akechi’s
weak protest, “What kind of mentor would I be if I left all your questions unanswered?”
“One that isn’t intruding on my home.” Akechi says dryly.
“Oh, come on!” Morgana whines, “I don’t take up that much space.”
“What if my apartment doesn’t allow pets?” Akechi folds his arms. His apartment does allow
pets, but Morgana doesn’t need to know that, “And what do you even eat? Do I need a
litterbox, or something?”
“I’m not some common housecat!” Morgana snaps, leveling Akechi with a glare, “I’ll eat
anything. And no, I don’t need a litterbox.” He spits the word like it’s an affront to him
personally, “I can use a toilet.”
Akechi tries and fails to not picture a cat using a toilet.
Akechi sighs deeply and pinches the bridge of his nose, “You aren’t going to let this go, are
you?”
“Nope!” Morgana agrees cheerfully.
Akechi can tell he lost this argument before it began. Damn cat.
He presses his lips together in a facsimile of his normal TV smile, “Well then, Morgana, I
suppose you’ll be following me home this evening.”
***
Akechi spends the rest of the train and walk to his apartment with Morgana blathering in his
ear about Metaverse concepts he already understands. He nods and hums at all the right
times, but otherwise tunes the cat out and focuses his energy on keeping Morgana mostly
hidden as he rides on public transport and walks down the now completely dark streets
surrounding his apartment complex.

Akechi smiles blandly at the receptionist, and spouts some rather useless pleasantries as he
signals for Morgana to run towards the stairwell.
After extracting himself from the conversation, Akechi leads Morgana to his apartment door,
quietly unlocking it and slipping inside.
“Welcome, I suppose.” Akechi waves his hand in an arc.
Morgana turns up his nose, padding into the centre of the living space, “It’s kind of empty in

“I don’t have a particular penchant for material possessions.” Akechi says dryly, kicking off

“It’s kinda dusty, too.” Morgana says, entirely ignoring Akechi and batting at a small tangle

“Quite sure.” Akechi can feel his pleasant composure slipping, and it’s from a cat, of all

“You should clean up, or something.” Morgana sniffs, hopping up onto the kitchen counter,

Akechi ignores the sudden urge to polish his apartment to sparkling just to get a one-up on

“I don’t spend a lot of time here.” Akechi says, truthfully, “It serves its purpose, and not

Morgana sighs, “Well, whatever. What’s for dinner!” He flicks his tail in excitement.
Akechi raises an eyebrow, and opens his fridge.
“There’s eggs,” That are probably bad by now, “Milk,” Almost certainly past its best-before,
“…An onion?”
Morgana stares at Akechi as he lists off the options, looking horrified.
“Do.” Morgana starts, “Do you have something in the pantry…?”
Akechi turns to open one of the other cupboards, “There’s instant ramen.”
Morgana jumps up, “You have nothing to eat? How do you live?!”

should.

“Just order some sushi, or something.” Morgana says weakly.
Akechi turns to where Morgana can’t see him and rolls his eyes, taking out his phone. He

Akechi turns the TV onto something generic, and distracts himself by scrolling through his

Morgana sits still for about two minutes before he starts poking at Akechi’s leg.

“If you’re not going to do anything, then we should at least talk or something.” Morgana says

“I suppose we should.” Akechi relents, “How long do you intend on staying here?”
“I just got here, and you’re already trying to kick me out?!” Morgana yelps.

Morgana rolls his eyes -an impressive feat, for a cat- “You’ll live. I just…” He sighs, “Don’t

“Yet?” Akechi tilts his head.
Morgana stares at the couch, “I… feel kinda bad, for getting mad at Ren.”
“Then surely all you need to do is apologise, no?” Akechi leans back, “Amamiya doesn’t

Morgana groans, “It’s not that simple.” He paws at the fraying edge of one of the throw

“So the issue is that you’re still upset.” Akechi brings a hand to his chin, and raises an

“Well…” Morgana starts, “There was a lot of stuff I yelled at him for.” He looks sheepish,
“And I think I’m in the right for some of it, but I also told him off for spending so much time

“Oh.” Akechi says blankly.
“Yeah…” Morgana mumbles, “I thought he was putting the team in danger by getting all
buddy-buddy with you. But I guess I was wrong.”

“You couldn’t have known that.” Akechi says with no particular intonation, because
Amamiya is definitely still an idiot.
“Well, yeah, but Ren did,” Morgana sighs, “So I guess I didn’t trust him either.”
Akechi hums lightly.
Morgana flicks his tail, and gives a toothy grin, “But hey, now I think you’re not so bad. You
don’t want to arrest us, and you have a lot more on common with everyone else than I think

“Oh?” Akechi furrows his brow, curiosity piqued, “In what way?”
“Well you’re a mess, for one.” Morgana starts, and Akechi feels his eye twitch, “Seriously, I
don’t know how you live like this, there’s like, nothing in here-”
As Akechi tunes out Morgana’s list of backhanded insults, he feels the world crackI am thou, thou art I
Thou hast acquired a new bond.
It will lead thee closer to freedom, by traversing the hidden depths of one’s soul.
Through the forging of the Hermit arcana, thou hast gained a glimpse of the power of

Akechi shouldn’t be too surprised, he supposes.
“-And you’re just as bad as Futaba when it comes to eating right. And since everyone likes

Akechi hums quietly.
Though this improvised stunt was a way to get an in with the Phantom Thieves, Akechi has

(He’s thought that before, though, about Haru and Sumire, and look where that led him.)

Akechi stills, and then reaches out to scratch behind Morgana’s ears, “Sure.”
Morgana looks like he’s trying very hard to pretend he isn’t enjoying the pets, and gives

Akechi raises a hand to his chin, “It could be.” He frowns, “Haru, could you check if he’s just

‘Candidate Found’ The app chimes from Haru’s end of the line.
Sumire hums lowly, “A whole palace…”

Haru breathes a sigh of relief, “Thank you, both of you! I’m sorry to ask so much…”
“Not at all!” Sumire insists before Akechi can, “I’m asking you guys to help me take down a

“That, and I’m asking for aid in dismantling a political conspiracy.” Akechi deadpans, “One

Haru laughs, “If you say so. Thank you.” She says again.
“We can figure out the keywords and do some preliminary scouting once I’ve dealt with the

There’s a pause, “Thank you, Goro-kun,” Haru laughs, “I’ve said that so much just now,

Akechi shrugs at nothing, scuffing his feet against the ground, “You don’t have to say it.”
She laughs again, “That just makes me want to say it more, you know.”
Akechi rolls his eyes, “Well, anyway. I’ve believe that’s all we need to discuss?”
There are simultaneous chimes of agreement from both Haru and Sumire, and they both

(The Fool reaches rank four.)

Before Akechi can make it five steps, his phone rings again.
He frowns at the caller ID, and picks up the call.
“Sumire?” He asks with narrowed eyes, “Did you forget something?”

There’s some light shuffling, and a small sigh, “Um, not really. I just wanted to ask you

“Something you couldn’t have asked in front of Haru-san?” Akechi raises an eyebrow, more

Sumire laughs, “I guess I could have, but I didn’t want to tag-team you or anything.” She

Akechi freezes, “…In what context?”
Sumire huffs, “For Shido, I mean. We’re trying so hard to steer them in the right direction,

“Weren’t you the one so hellbent on avoiding the thieves, when you approached me?” Akechi

Sumire doesn’t answer for so long that Akechi thinks the call might have disconnected, “…
It’s… complicated.”

“Only if you and Haru do.” Sumire says immediately, and some of the tension Akechi didn’t

Sumire pauses, and Akechi can almost see her small frown, “…I’ll take that as an ‘I don’t

Inexplicably, Sumire laughs at that, and then seems to sober up, “I just…” She huffs, “We

don’t-” She cuts herself off.
Akechi doesn’t move. He opens his mouth, closes it.
(In his head, he never considered his goal suicide.

The way he sees it, suicide would be giving up. But it isn’t giving up, if he’s already won,
ergo, not suicidal.
But alas.
Like mother like son, something in his head cackles, and, god, can his mind shut up for

After school, Akechi comes back to his apartment to find Morgana pacing a hole into the
floor.
“Is there a problem?” Akechi asks lightly.
Morgana’s head snaps up, “Nope.” He plonks down, licking at his fur, “I was just thinking.”
“About?” Akechi moves over to the couch, leaning his attaché case against the wall.
“How I’m going to go about teaching you, of course!” Morgana puffs out his chest with an
air of smugness.
Akechi pauses, “…Have you not already explained the ins and outs of the Metaverse in great
length?”
“Well, yeah.” Morgana hops up on the kitchen bench to meet Akechi at eye level, “But
there’s a difference between theoretical and practical experience. Your persona isn’t gonna
get stronger if you don’t start fighting some shadows.”
“I suppose that’s true.” Akechi begrudges. “But is there a reason you find that so important?”
“Well,” Morgana falters, “All the other persona users that have awakened have all joined the
thieves, so…”

“Right.”

How kind of him to notice, Robin preens, clearly pleased at his long-standing nickname for

Well.
“That’s the point, no?” Akechi counters with a pleasant smile, “These names are supposed to

Morgana seems to mull it over, “…Huh. Sounds good! Let’s head to Shibuya then, Crow!”

Thinking about it, he should probably downplay his strength a little more. Robin is already

Oh. He gets the idea.

The best value Akechi’s found to having teammates so far might be this, he thinks. No holds

Akechi and Morgana both skid back into place, out of breath and grinning manically as the

Akechi smirks. He’ll have to remember that move for when he needs to crawl through

…That’s it?
“That’s it?” Akechi asks, incredulously.
“Huh?” Morgana looks up, “Oh, yeah. That was a change of heart! Pretty easy, right?”
That’s it?
Akechi folds his hands neatly behind his back to hide how hard he’s clenching them. Could

circumstances? Was he just unlucky? No- Wakaba was a thorough woman, and she never
managed to come up with anything like this. And didn’t Sumire mention a calling card?
“Don’t you need a calling card?” Akechi asks, voice innocent.

“I see.” Akechi hums.
So not the kind of thing someone could just stumble into.
Akechi isn’t quite sure if that’s better or worse.
But it was just so easy-

That’s what those strange mirages of distortion were for? That was the core? How the hell
could he have missed this?
Akechi laughs, a little more bitter than he intends. The leader tilts his head with some
concern, but Akechi ignores him. Of course it was easy for him, of course he gets all the
answers on a silver platter- free from the endless cycle of trial and error and theories and
failure andIts not like this ability would have been useful to Akechi, anyway, so what does it matter?
Or would it? Is there another world, where Akechi had another option? Would he have taken
it?
He clenches his fists, snapping his smile back into place. It doesn’t matter.
-Oh.
Perhaps Akechi had this revelation last time, too.
“Anyway,” Morgana starts, cutting through that, “How are you feeling? All the spells you
have seem kinda draining.”
Akechi pastes on another smile, “I am feeling a little drained, actually,” More from the

continue?”
Morgana hums, considering, “I wouldn’t want to push you, especially since you’re so new.”
He bounds towards the exit of the pocket of distortion, “We’re not in a hurry, so let’s head

Akechi nods, and feels the Hermit reach rank two.

Ren shuffles uncomfortably at his school desk, Morgana’s absence making itself very

batted at his face for calling him a cat.

Joker: Meeting after school. Leblanc attic
He shoves his phone back in his pocket, and gives a small grin when Kawakami raises an

Fuck, I hope he’s not going to arrest me. Ren thinks, ubruptly. That would be kind of

The discussion at Leblanc is a long and tedious one.
Most of it is Akechi pasting on a smile while explaining thing’s he’s already explained to
Morgana. This time, with a significant degree more scepticism, largely from Makoto and
Sakamoto, with the occasional clarifying question from Kitagawa, Takamaki, and Futaba.

Akechi’s mouth.

into the mousetrap Shido has laid at their feet. If Akechi had more sinister intentions, (And he
likely would have, in different circumstances, he thinks) then the Phantom Thieves would
have been tragically easy to destroy.
But those aren’t his intentions.
No, Akechi tells them, he has no intention of turning them into the police.
Why, they ask? It’s far easier to tell Amamiya one-on-one that he is the primary reason for
Akechi’s half-feigned benevolence, and less easy to grit out to an entire group. It’s the only
explanation he has, though, if he doesn’t want to start muttering about political conspiracies
and time travel.

a reminder, he explains- if Akechi could put their identities together, then anyone could.
Why not come clean earlier? Akechi has to scramble for an answer, and he settles on an
adjacent truth: There was no reason to. Akechi couldn’t be sure of the consequences of telling
them all that he knew their identities, so he simply chose to keep quiet.
Why say all those things on TV? A combination of PR for the police department and some of
Akechi’s own opinions. He’s still not on the side of the Phantom Thieves, after all, even if he
doesn’t want them arrested.

Now that he’s on the other side, Ren feels like he may have shot himself in the foot by
keeping all his suspicions to himself.
Getting everything out was… fine. Not nearly as daunting as he hyped it up to be. They
believed him, didn’t smother him with concern, and now he doesn’t have to stew in all his
theories alone.
On the other side of things, Ren isn’t sure how to feel.
‘The best possible outcome’ was what he had declared to himself, when Akechi was revealed
to have a persona and joined the team. Why wouldn’t it be? They basically have a double
agent now, and oh, Ren is impatient as he waits for the moment when he can see how Akechi
fights.

Though, that was all before Ren was hit with the memory of his hopefully-not-prophetic
dream.
If he lets himself think about it too hard, all Ren feels is dread.
For one of his bonds to die; he imagines it would feel like ripping a pulsing vein out from his
chest, and he knows that he’s sewn the Justice close to his heart. He wonders what it would
feel like to try and remove something that’s become so integral.
He barely even remembers it happening. Was it inch by inch? Or was it all at once? It feels a
bit likeWell, he doesn't know.
He wonders why Akechi is different, in that regard.
His contemplation is cut off as Ren slips into sleep.
He’s staring at the walls of Mementos as the memory of the Aeon returns. Ren frowns, slowly
taking a seat on the nearby bench. Convenient- he’d hate to have to sit on the floor of this
place.
Ren’s head shoots up when Crow takes a seat next to him.
“Anything interesting happen lately?” Crow asks lightly, like the asshole he is.
“Fuck you.” Is the first thing Ren thinks to say. He only half regrets it.
Crow gives him an innocently surprised look, “Really? I’m sure I would have remembered
something like that.”
Oh, for- “Not what I meant.” Ren hisses, “I’m starting to remember stuff outside of all this,
too. What the hell was that dream?”
Crow shrugs, “A good sign, hopefully.”
Ren huffs, “Great. Wonderful.”
“I would have thought you’d be grateful for the event.” Crow tilts his head, “You’re so
determined to keep me alive, and yet you were unable to properly fulfill your resolve in
reality since you can’t remember these occurrences.” He leans back, “But now you have a
hint.”
“A hint?” Ren says incredulously, then bites his lip, “I still don’t have all the information
when I’m awake.”
“You don’t have all the information now.” Crow points out dryly. “You’ll have to work with
what you’ve got.”
Ren slaps his hands against his face, “What I’ve got is a whole pile of worry.”

“That’s pretty standard when it comes to you, no?” Crow snarks, clicking off his helmet.
Ren ignores him, and tries running through his head, skimming for anything that could help
him figure this out.
“I’m missing something.” Ren mumbles.
“Your memories, yes.” Crow deadpans, raising an eyebrow.
“No, like,” Ren groans, “Yes, my memories, but I feel like the memories aren’t the point.” He
frowns, “Or, they’re part of the point, but there’s something I’m supposed to be working

Crow hums, “What are your options, then?”
Ren presses his lips together, “Akechi’s going to die. Or in danger. Or, fuck, something, and I
think I need to find a way to help him. You.”
Crow rolls his eyes, “Sure. Do what you want. You’ve made it clear I can’t change your mind.
What else?"
Ren smiles slightly at the other's exasperation, “Yoshizawa.” He frowns, “I don’t think she’s
the black mask. Not really.”
“Who do you think it is, then?” Crow asks dispassionately.
“Kind of obvious that’s it’s you.” Ren says flatly, then frowns, “Hey, do you have two
Metaverse outfits or something?” He pouts, “No fair.”

Crow points to himself, batting his eyes innocently, “Me?”
“You.” Ren nods, leaning forward.
Ren bites at the inside of his mouth, “You’ve been saying this whole time that you’re my
cognition of Akechi. Kind of.” Crow smiles blandly, “But then you agreed with me, when I

Crow scoffs, “A wonderful conclusion.”

The sounds of breaking chains, and the Aeon reaches rank eight.
Crow raises an eyebrow as the sound fades, “Two more ranks. Think you can figure it out by

Ren smiles, “I’m confident.” He isn’t. Crow can probably tell, because he snorts derisively.
