Futaba stretches her arms out over her head, cracking her knuckles. She then slumps forward
in her best impression of a hunchback, and snickers to herself as her fingers start racing
across her keyboard with decisive clacks.
So, she isn’t allowed to hack pretty boy’s phone. Boo.
But, Ren never said anything about digging up every piece of information that Futaba can
find from the breadcrumbs scattered across the net.
Futaba has to admit that finding out that her basically-brother-at-this-point (not that she’d
ever admit to feeling like that) is practically a seer threw her for a loop.
She also has to say that finding out the nice girl that seemed almost eager to be her friend
might have killed her mom kinda stung.
Not to mention the fact that the pretty boy she’s currently ignoring the privacy of might die.
So, a lot. And Futaba isn’t quite sure how to feel about it, so she’s going to settle on just not,
and instead shove all her focus on her excellent stalking abilities.
Even if Ren might object to what Futaba’s doing, he’ll surely thank her if she comes across
something that saves Akechi’s life. Like a deeply buried connection with the yakuza, or
something. Or maybe some tragic medical records. Or some arrest history against a deeply
vengeful criminal.
Or maybe he’s a serial killer. Anything’s possible in the world of celebrities, Futaba thinks.
She taps away, almost cheerful, as she widens and narrows her search parameters, finding
small little leads to tumble down in a frenzy of research.
She takes a quick look at the public records. Pretty standard, nothing too interesting. Dead
parents- join the club! Born to Emiko and Hiroshi Akechi, who both died when he was
around ten,
Boring. Futaba thinks as she types in the names to try and get a little history on them, and-

Oh.
Less boring.
Actually, scratch that, very boring, because there’s nothing there.
Okay. Akechi’s parents don’t exist. The only records of an Emiko and Hiroshi Akechi exist in
relation to their apparent son.
Futaba tentatively notes that down.
She bites at her lip. Either Akechi’s parents’ records were wiped, and that’s why she can’t
find anything on them, or Akechi’s own record was severely altered to make up two new
people.
Neither exactly spell great things.
Futaba tries, on a long shot, to go digging for- hell, she doesn’t know, older versions of the
public records?
She isn’t surprised when she doesn’t find anything of use.
On the contrary, a little voice quips in her head, the fact that she can’t find anything pretty
solidly confirms that it’s Akechi’s records that got scrubbed, rather than his parents.
Or not-parents, Futaba guesses. She throws out the names. Not important.
She snickers. Maybe she should be the detective.
Perhaps a little more cautious of what she might find, Futaba starts digging into any and
everything she can find about Akechi’s past. She can already tell that there’s probably
something shady going on with his parents, but she clearly can’t really find out anything
more.
All his high school records are intact. Perfect grades, no clubs, definitely teacher’s pet- wow
those are some glowing comments- and… pretty much spotless.
Boo.
Moving onto middle school…
Futaba pauses.
Fuck, nothing again?
She groans. This is getting really weird. Who the hell did Akechi pay off to have his entire
history banished from the face of the earth?
She glares at the screen. Alright then, if so much of it is gone, what can she find?

Not a lot. The most she can get is a certificate acknowledging Akechi’s status as an
emancipated minor, which he got a hold of at fifteen, coinciding with his first year of high
school.
Great.
She slides unceremoniously down her chair, until she’s half on the floor and staring at her
ceiling.
Why on earth would someone like Akechi want his past completely inaccessible to anyone
who would think to look?
Actually, stupid question. He’s basically an idol, and those guys need to be spotless to avoid
some kinda scandal where people poke at things that don’t concern them.
The confusing part is why Akechi needed so much of his past erased. A whole lotta
questions, which thanks to pretty boy over there, Futaba can’t find answers to.
She pouts at the ceiling. This is just like when she went looking for her mom’s researchWait.
Actually, it’s exactly like when she went looking for her mom’s research.
Futaba jumps back into her chair with a speed she didn’t think was possible from her twig
body.
Okay, maybe it’s not exactly like how all her mom’s stuff went poof, but the fact that both
chunks of information just evaporated sets off all the alarm bells in her head.
She huffs in frustration. It’s suspicious, sure, but the nature of the thing means that she can’t

Maybe not alone though.

“Well, good luck.”

When Ann returns with the crêpes, Akechi is somewhat relieved to see that his own is topped

“How much do I owe you?” Akechi asks as Ann passes him the crêpe.
Ann blinks, “Huh? Oh, no,” She shakes her head furiously, “I’m the one who dragged you

Akechi raises an eyebrow, but chooses not to push. If she chooses to waive the debt, it’s her

“Why did you drag me out here?” He chooses to ask instead.
Ann nearly chokes on the giant bite of crêpe that she had shoved in her mouth in her haste to

“…Yes?” Akechi says slowly.

Ann smirks, “Sure, but we can’t be friends if we don’t hang out. Plus I bought you a crêpe.

Ah. So this is an ambush. Akechi probably should have noticed around the time Ann started
physically dragging him places.
“Is there something you needed, Ann-san?” Akechi decides to cut to the chase.
The smirk fades from Ann’s face, “…Huh? I- no. I just don’t know you very well, and I

Akechi narrows his eyes. Either he has a propensity for meeting incredibly skilled actors or

He’s seen Ann’s attempts at acting. The latter, then. He isn’t sure if that’s worse.

Akechi raises his other eyebrow, bemused,
And isn’t surprised when the world cracksI am thou, thou art I

“Is it weird to say that all this Metaverse stuff has actually made me better at school?” Ren

“I don’t find it strange, no.” Goro shakes his head, “I’m certainly curious about it all. I’d
certainly be interested in learning more about the origin of everyone’s personas.”
“Yeah.” Ren huffs, “I’ve read a lot of books I’ve found in the library about everyone’s
personas.” He grins, “I’ll have to find one on Robin Hood.”
Goro’s lips twitch, before he tugs on his gloves, ducking his head, “Speaking of, I hope my

Ren quickly nods, “You definitely were. Mona wasn’t kidding when he said you’re a
natural.”
Goro chuckles wryly, “It’s a special kind of ironic that I am apparently so naturally skilled at
something I was so hesitant to involve myself with.”
Ren tilts his head curiously, “Still not a fan of the Phantom Thieves?”
Goro sighs, narrowing his eyes in contemplation, “I can’t say that I particularly approve of
your actions still, no. Though I do acknowledge that being backed into a corner like this can
present little in the way of alternatives.”
Ren taps his fingers against his chin, humming, “Last time we talked about this, you said that
the Phantom Thieves are dangerous because they’re unknown. But, well,” He gestures to
himself.
Goro huffs a laugh, “Another round of debate, then?” Ren nods eagerly, “Alright.” He
straightens up, “My point about vigilante groups has hardly changed. I know and trust your
intentions, sure, but the rest of the public does not. And you are still a group of teenagers
beholden to mistakes.”
Ren nods, “True.” He looks up at the ceiling, mulling it over, “I’m not sure if the public’s
opinion is the point.”
Goro cocks an eyebrow, “Oh?”
Ren tugs at his fringe, “Our goal is… nebulous.” He admits, “’Changing society’ is pretty
vague, so I guess our main motive is doing what we can when we see injustice.”
“And because you operate on a case-by-case basis, things like unanimous vote are enough to
serve as checks and balances for whether your actions are just or not.” Goro concludes. He

hums, “I concede that I am… glad that you’re not so easily swayed by the public. Such an
informant is easily manipulated and biased.”
Ren smiles, “Am I convincing you?”
Goro smirks, “Not yet.”
“What other issues do you have with us, then?” Ren asks, crossing his legs.
“Moving the issues of vigilante justice aside,” Goro starts, “How about the act of changing

Ren frowns, “What about it?”
“It isn’t quite as merciful as people make it out to be, is it?” Goro says, placing his hand to

“Better than killing them isn’t it?” Ren asks dryly.
“Is it?” Goro pushes, “Could the people who’s hearts you’ve changed ever become
functioning members of society again, even excluding the consequences of their crimes?”

“No.” Goro says simply, “I agree that all the people who’s hearts you’ve changed have

Ren hums quietly, considering the point.
“I… don’t think you’re wrong.” Ren starts, surprising himself, “We kind of are killing them,

Goro smirks slightly, “We’re in agreement there.”
“But.” Ren continues, “I still think that changing their hearts is better.”
Goro tilts his head, “And why is that?”
“They confess.” Ren smiles, “We started the Phantom Thieves to help people, and isn’t
changing hearts like having our cake and eating it too? We stop our targets from causing any

Goro hums, “That’s true, I suppose.”
“So we agree, then.” Ren says, smug.
Goro rolls his eyes, “About the bigger picture, it seems.”
“Then what are we even debating?” Ren says, smile growing.

“We’re debating, so that you get off your high horse.” Goro says, lips twitching into an
almost-scowl, “Changing a heart is a punishment- it’s revenge- and you’d do well to
remember that.”
Ren barks a laugh, “Well, when you put it that way.” He leans back, giving Goro a serious
look, “I won’t forget that.”
Goro nods slowly, seemingly satisfied with Ren’s response.
Ren feels his lips twitch up, “…Not a fan of revenge?”
Goro snorts, “On the contrary.”
(As soon as the admission is made, the Justice reaches rank seven.)
Ren feels a rush of curiosity, “Oh?”
Goro waves a hand, “Another time.” He kicks off the workbench, straightening up. “Well, I
believe I may have overstayed my welcome.”
Not at all, Ren wants to say, stay as long as you like. But, he recognises an exit strategy when
he sees one.
Instead, he gives the other a warm smile, “Until next time then, Goro.”

Perhaps it is the oxymoron of the strange sense of calm amidst the ever-present stress that
Akechi feels, that causes him to be caught off-guard by Shido’s demand to meet.
Things have been odd. Nothing and everything is going to plan- ‘falling up’, Akechi believes
is the best descriptor, except the ground is crumbling faster than he can fall, and he wonders
when all the deadlines and necessities will come to knock; knowing his luck, it’ll be all at
once.
The strange stasis of waiting that Akechi finds himself in does him no favours with Shido,
though. Nothing to report and everything to lie about.
When Akechi clicks open the door to Shido’s office, he sees the man swirling a glass of some
alcohol or another, looking surprisingly calm.
A dangerous mood.
Shido regards him cooly when he takes a short bow. “Akechi,” He says, leaning forward,
“You’ve been making regular trips into Okumura’s palace, correct?”

Shido raises an eyebrow, “Well?”

Akechi barely stops himself from rolling his eyes in time. “Unfortunately,” He begins
smoothly, “The Phantom Thieves do not appear to have begun any infiltration attempts on

A very dangerous mood.

have a solution to this predicament?”
Ah. Akechi sees how it is.

attempt at deflecting whatever the fuck Shido wants from him.
“That’s what I’m asking you, Akechi.” Shido snaps, the icy neutrality quickly fading, “Or do
you need me to hold your hand through every step of the way?”
Akechi grits his teeth and clenches his fists behind his back. “No sir.” He says, wracking his
brain for some way to balance the spinning plates.
Stall. That usually works.
“In all likelihood, the thieves are simply being cautious.” Akechi settles on, making sure to
not break eye contact, “I wouldn’t be surprised if they’re doing their own research into

The sneer melts off Shido’s face as quickly as it came, his expression becoming unreadable

“Of course.” Akechi says confidently.
They already have, after all.
Shido nods slowly, seemingly satisfied with Akechi’s bullshitting. “Keep a close eye on the
palace.” He says, “I want you to notify me immediately if they make any movements. Make

“Good.” Shido takes a longer sip of his drink. He pauses, and looks Akechi up and down,
“How are you feeling, by the way?”
What? Akechi almost says, before clenching his jaw and reconsidering.

WHY IS HE ASKING THIS? Loki hisses, indignant.

A test. Robin warns, bristling.
How does he feel about the prospect of killing the leader of the Phantom Thieves? Shido isn’t

When he first met Amamiya- Ren, the thought that Akechi might have to kill him was a

Chapter Summary

Mirrors, confusion, and overthinking.

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

The life of a cognition is a funny thing.
Are any of his thoughts his own? It’s hard to say. It feels like his thoughts are separate from
the captain’s; but is there really a difference when he’s unfailingly loyal? If his thoughts are
his own, he doesn’t think much would change, either way.
Goro stares out at the foyer of the ship, idly swingling his legs back and forth over the edge,
tapping his gun against the ground in some rhythm of a song he’s sure he’s heard before.
There’s a bit of a pattern he’s noticed. After the captain calls the real him in to chat, then his
counterpart will occasionally grace the cruise ship with his irritating presence.
Irritating, but certainly entertaining.
Are his thoughts his own, he thinks again. It’s a rare treat, to compare himself to the person
on which his existence is based. It’s strange- Goro thinks they’re exactly the same, and yet
nothing alike at all.
There’s a spark of fiery hatred that Goro can see in his counterpart’s eyes. A hatred that he
was somewhat unfamiliar with. It isn’t as though the captain missed this aspect about Goro
Akechi, but he deemed it irrelevant, nonetheless. Goro would do anything for the captain
anyway, so does the fact that he hates him even matter?
And yet…
More recently, Goro has felt aspects of himself change. It’s extremely frustrating. He has no
basis for why these things happen- he simply has to accept that this is how he feels now.
Something has been happening with the him in the real world, and Goro is very curious as to
what that is.
Maybe his counterpart is feeling more defiant. Or maybe the captain finally got a clue about
how much Goro hates him, the piece of shit that holds the cross brace tied to the strings
dangling from Goro’s limbs- and oh he can’t wait to pry open the fucker’s ribs one-by-oneAh.

There’s the change. It might just be Goro’s imagination, but he thinks it’s happening more
often.
Goro stops swinging his legs when he sees his counterpart unceremoniously kick open the
doors to the foyer.
He smirks. Time for some fun.
The other him is already eyeing the surrounding area suspiciously. His eyes, partially hidden
by his jagged black mask, rake up the wall, and eventually settle on Goro, who gives a
cheerful wave with the hand holding the gun.
The other him scowls, and folds his arms.
Making Goro do all the work, it seems. He sighs, kicking off the ledge had situated himself
on, neatly folding his hands behind his back as he walks up to the real him.
“Back again, are we?” Goro says with a bright smile.
His counterpart’s lips curl up in a sneer, “You make it sound as though you expected me.”
“Well, there isn’t much else to do around here other than wait.” Goro says truthfully, “And
besides, three times is a pattern, isn’t it?” He gasps performatively, bringing his hand to his
mouth, “Don’t tell me- you visit to see me?”
His counterpart scowls, annoyance written over his face, “And why the fuck would I want to
spend time with you?”
Goro hums, tapping his chin, “Mirrors in the real world are funny things.”
“What the fuck are you-”
“They reflect reality exactly as it is,” Goro continues, as though his counterpart never spoke,
“And yet you still have to perceive their reflections through your own eyes. Really- what’s
the point of a mirror at all?”
“So people can look at themselves, generally.” His counterpart says dryly, sneer unabating.
“Is there any value in perceiving yourself through your own eyes?” Goro asks, more to the
empty air, “You’d have to be remarkably self-aware to get anything out of it at all.”
His counterpart takes a deep, steadying, breath that speaks of repressed violence, “Is there a
point to this tangent?” He snarls, “Or is Shido waxing philosophical in some repressed corner
of his subconscious?”
Goro shrugs, “Who’s to say?” He chuckles, “My point, though, is that spending time with me
would be like looking in a mirror, no?” He smiles brightly as his counterpart slowly bares his
teeth, “Literally, yes -we do look identical- but, ah, what is it? ‘Actualisation of the self
through the perception of others’?”

His counterpart lets out a frustrated growl, abruptly stepping forward to grab Goro by the tie,
spitting in his face, “You’re. Not. Me.”
Oh, to be a broken record. Does he not tire, insisting of truths that do not exist? Goro feels his
lips curl up in a bright smile.
“You’re not a mirror.” His counterpart continues, eyes averting as he starts rambling to
himself more than Goro, “You’re convenient. You’re a walking, talking, little doll filled to the
brim with information, if you’d care to spill it.” He hisses.
Oh, so he wants information on the captain, then? Goro would be happy to oblige- which is
probably indicative that his counterpart is doing something wrong.
“Whatever makes you happy.” Goro says brightly, and his counterpart looks seconds from
abandoning all self-restraint and shooting Goro then and there.
But, well, they both know that cognition is a volatile and dangerous thing. Killing Goro could
have unpredictable effects on the captain, which his counterpart is clearly trying to avoid.
Tragic, then, that father dearest already has him pegged.
“This is a waste of my time.” His counterpart mutters, “It’s always a waste of time, why the
fuck am I even here?”
“You should think about what I said.” Goro hums, shoving the real him away with more force
than strictly necessary, “But you’re leaving now, aren’t you?”
His counterpart shoots him one final glare before stalking off, looking at him like one might a
stain in their carpet. Goro supposes that’s fair- he isn’t truly a person, after all.
(In Akechi’s mind, he seethes.
A waste of time- spent talking to a cognition that proves more insufferable than most.
The Tower grows to rank four, ever unsteady, and Akechi kicks the wall with an infuriated
shout.)

“See you later, Sumire-chan.” Ann says, thankfully not reverting into stilted pleasantries.
Sumire jogs off in the direction of her class, and tries not to overthink.
That was… weird. But what does she know?
She sighs, and sits down at her desk with a thunk.
It’s- not important. No need to spiral over one slightly awkward conversation. And whatever
mood they were in got dashed pretty quickly as they got distracted. Sumire doesn’t even

time to pay more attention to gymnastics.
It’s fine.

judgement, “I recall there being a twist of some sort towards the end, though my memory’s a
bit foggy.”

“Yeah…” Futaba hums, “Osagiri, the scientist, was my favourite character, since she
reminded me of my mom.”
Akechi goes still.
“I thought it was super cool.” Futaba says, eyes flicking down, “The whole… science stuff to
get special powers.”
(Akechi had thought the same, when it first began)
“It made me think of my mom as like…” She smiles, “A superhero, or the good guy’s righthand man. I already wanted to grow up to be just like her, and playing this game made me
want that even more.”
She shifts.
“Do you remember the twist?” She asks, staring ahead at the screen.
Akechi nods slowly, “I remember that Osagiri was not who she appeared to be.”
“Yep.” Futaba presses the buttons on the controller quickly as a fighting segment comes up,
“Something, something, turns out that Osagiri is secretly Alya, some agent from Zylam who
made Grey Pigeon as an experiment for a fighter that’s even stronger than the feathermen.”
She sighs as she finishes the fight segment, another cutscene loading in.
“I really hated that twist.” Futaba says, tucking her knees under her chin, “In my head,
Osagiri was my mom. And my mom could never do something so…” Her face twists,
“Slimy. Evil. Whatever.”
Right.
Akechi hums, keeping his face very still.
Futaba laughs awkwardly, “I mean, I was seven. So, not super good at separating fiction and
reality. And I know from like, an objective standpoint, that that twist was super cool, and a
real departure from the formula that featherman usually follows.” She shrugs, “But, yeah. It
kinda made it so I wasn’t a big fan of the game until way later.”
“What changed your mind?” Akechi asks.
Futaba pauses, “…When my mom died, I remembered playing this game with her.” She rubs
her nose, “At first, that made me want to think about the game even less, but, now…”
“It’s good to have the memories.” Akechi finishes, injecting no particular emotion into his
voice.
Futaba’s face breaks into a bright smile, “Yeah.” She says. “Um,” She fiddles with her
glasses, “You mentioned your mom. What… what was she like?”

Akechi swallows, and looks away. “She was…” He murmurs.
His mother was a lot of things.
“Complicated.” Akechi settles on saying. “But I loved her.”
Futaba gives a small smile, “That’s good.”
It is with a sense of dread, then, that Akechi feels the world crackI am thou, thou art I
Thou hast acquired a new bond.
It will lead thee closer to freedom, by traversing the hidden depths of one’s soul.
Through the forging of the Death arcana, thou hast gained a glimpse of the power of
rebellion, and hast begun to uncover thine own truth.
Futaba will definitely be the death of him at this rate, Akechi thinks humourlessly.
Futaba jumps as her phone buzzes. She quickly snatches it out of her pocket, eyeing the
screen critically. She hits pause on the game, “Everyone’s showing up soon. So, um…” She
smiles shyly, “This was fun.”
Akechi pulls his face into a smile, hoping it doesn’t seem too strained, “I’m glad.”
***
Akechi often feels as though he’s balancing on a tightrope made of razor-sharp wire.
A delicate game of juggling cups and spinning plates- There’s no way around it, really.
Unless, of course, Akechi were to simply stop, and let the porcelain dishware drop to the
ground.
But, well. Then they would shatter.
Akechi has given a lot of thought to Sumire’s suggestion that they join the thieves in the
periphery of his mind. There are myriad pros and cons to keeping them in the dark or
reaching out- and Akechi is frankly amazed that Sumire hasn’t snapped and told him to make
a decision already.
But how can he, when Futaba loved her mother so much? She’ll hate him, no doubt- and the
only way for Akechi to dampen the blow of his crimes would be to tarnish her mother’s
memory, which she’ll probably hate him for even more.
(And he won’t- can’t, tell her.)
As for everyone else? Who’s to say.

For some of the thieves, Akechi thinks they might be just as insane as Sumire and Haru. Ren,
and possibly Ann and Morgana seem like they might help him, even if they knew the truth.
Maybe.
Makoto, Sakamoto, and Kitagawa are all unknowns, though. Akechi leans more towards the
thought that they wouldn’t be particularly happy to know his secondary occupation.
Akechi drags himself out of his thoughts, pressing himself against a wall as Ren ducks into
hiding to avoid a shadow. They actually never made it to a saferoom last time, so they’ve had
to trek through the parts of Okumura’s palace that they’d already explored. Akechi can’t
complain- it buys more time, though it is slightly tedious.
Ren must notice his boredom, as he shoots Akechi a sharp grin, dashing out of hiding to flip
stylishly onto a shadow’s back, slicing ribbons into its face to get at its mask.
Akechi raises an eyebrow at the unnecessary spectacle, falling into formation with Ann and
Kitagawa as Ren does a backflip to skid into place.
Ren’s stunts don’t stop there- the battle is finished rather quickly with an impressive fire spell
from Ann and a Megidola from Ren, cast with more flourish than is strictly necessary.
As the shrieks of the woefully outmatched shadows fade, Ren turns and gives Akechi another
grin, wide and eager. He’s yet to return to his usual hunch, instead standing at his full height
with an air of self-satisfaction.
It’s somewhat charming, that he seems to be performing for Akechi’s sake.
Ridiculous, he corrects with a hiss.
“Still bored?” Ren asks, a smirk tugging at the corner of his mouth.
Akechi makes sure to look distinctly unphased by the dramatics, “I’m afraid I don’t know
what you’re talking about.”
Ren smiles even wider, seeing right through him, “Really?” He winks, “Guess I’ll have to try
harder, then.” He spins his gun, “Can you keep up?”
In spite of whatever front of inexperience Akechi has forced himself to present, he smirks, “I
believe I can. The question really should be if you can keep up with me.”
Ren laughs, “You’re on.”
The fights go even faster after that, in this early part of the palace, as Ren and Akechi both
tear through any shadows that cross their path with increasingly showy attacks, barely
leaving space for anyone else to get a hit in.
It’s more of a collaboration than a competition, but Akechi can tell they’re both keeping score
anyway.

He would help you, if you asked. Robin whispers amid the frenzy, You know this.
But what if he doesn’t? One of the many dissenting voices posits, What if he doesn’t carewhat if he does, and he’s fool enough to let Shido hurt him as some trade or sacrifice?
Akechi lingers on that last thought.
Ren is a fool, isn’t he?
He would do something stupid, if he asked for help- Akechi can see it in every line of the
thief’s body and in every spark in his eye; overeager, sentimental, self-sacrificial, and Akechi
can’tIt pains him to do this. Everything about this pains him, actually- this entire situation is a
massive fucking pain, and apparently it’s Akechi’s problem.
He shouldn’t even be here. He doesn’t remember how he got to this point, and the more he
sees of this grating new reality, the more that itches at the back of his mind. What if, what if,
what ifBut none of that truly matters. He has a deal to pitch and compromises to make, and he can’t
stop thinking about how the other boy’s eyes are wide and brimming with an emotion Akechi
doesn’t care to name, acting like if he blinks Akechi will disappear like he was never there at
allAkechi snaps back, head pounding, barely managing to contain a pained grunt.
Right in the middle of a fight, too. Fucking wonderful.
He barely manages to duck to the side of a shadow’s attack, still dizzy, his lip curling as he
can’t quite get Robin to release the spell he had been holding. He would consider it a point
lost on his side, but he doesn’t hear Ren casting any spell, either. He almost turns and glares
at him for letting Akechi catch up when this is a competition, but stalls as he sees a grimace
painted across Ren’s face, shaking his head slightly like he’s holding back a migraine of his
own.
Well then.
Ann and Kitagawa pick up the slack- the shadows not posing much of a challenge. Ren
shoves his hands in his pockets when the fight ends, face even more still than usual, as
though he’s willing whatever lingering pain Akechi knows he feels from the vision away
through sheer stoicism.
Neither of them comment on their slip up, if Ren noticed it at all. Akechi is more than ready
to move on entirely until he sways slightly, dizziness taking one last hit to his balance.
Immediately, the blankness on Ren’s face melts into concern, “Hey, you alright?”
Akechi pastes on something bright and presentable, “Just fine, Joker. Don’t worry.”

“Are you sure?” Ren asks, stepping a little closer, “We’ve been going kind of all-out.”
“Joker.” Akechi repeats, “I really am fine, I just stumbled a little.”
Ren shakes his head, frown deepening, “You seemed dizzy. You’re drained.” Something else
passes across his face, and whatever snippy reply Akechi had prepared dies on his tongue,
“You should take a break, get some rest. I can get someone else on the front lines for a bit.”
Akechi barely manages to stop the scowl that tugs at his lips, “I assure you, that isn’t
necessary.”
“C’mon, please?” Ren tugs at his fringe, and a stupid, shy little smile tugs at his lips, “For
me? It’d make me feel better.”
Akechi deflates slightly, and fuck- why did that shit work on him?
“Fine.” Akechi almost spits, but manages to turn it into a huff.
Ren smiles, relief evident. He waves at the reserves, “Hey, Skull, you’re up.”
“Hell yeah!” Sakamoto shouts cheerfully, jogging up to join the front as Akechi slips back,
rolling his eyes.
Ren shoots him one last smile, and a grateful thumbs up. Akechi pretends he doesn’t see it.
Akechi falls into step with Makoto and Morgana, folding his arms and clenching at the fabric.
Ren is an idiot. Akechi knows that he’s established himself as ‘new to the Metaverse’, but
Ren seems to be taking that as ‘fragile and weak’- this time and the last, and Akechi can feel
his patience fraying at the edges.
(Akechi wonders if Ren treated the others like this, too. Does he see Akechi as lesser? Surely
Akechi has proved otherwise, many times over. Ren had seemed so delighted to entertain their
stupid competition, all to sate Akechi’s boredom, so why,
Is Akechi more important, somehow? A narcissistic thought, but for what- why? Does Ren
recognise Akechi’s dizzy spell as similar to his own? The timing, circumstance, and symptoms
too suspicious for him to overlook?
Akechi cannot, for the life of him, get a read on this boy.)
At his side, Makoto clears her throat.
Akechi snaps back to reality, turning to raise an eyebrow at her.
“You seem annoyed.” She says flatly, while Morgana is absorbed in his own conversation,
speaking with Futaba via Necronomicon, “Everyone gets some time in reserves eventually.”
Akechi doesn’t glare, but instead smiles brightly, “I’m aware.” He says pleasantly, “I’m
merely a little… put out. I’m not injured, nor am I really that drained, and yet Joker still

insists I take a break.”
“…Maybe he just wanted to give someone else a go on the front lines?” Makoto offers, not
sounding particularly confident, “We like to rotate spots pretty often.”
Akechi raises and eyebrow, “If that were the case, then he could have just said so.”
Makoto frowns, “Point.” She concedes, and sighs, “He’s just worried about you. You are new
to all of this, and you two were really giving it your all. I could see it from back here.”
Akechi supresses an eye roll, “And was Joker this worried about everyone else when they
first joined?”
Makoto pauses, “…I suppose not, from what I’ve seen with myself and Oracle.”
Akechi doesn’t bother stopping the scowl this time, “Wonderful.” He deadpans.
Makoto frowns, “I thought that would make you feel better…”
Akechi blinks, “Queen.” He folds his arms, “Why on earth would the knowledge that Joker
clearly sees me as too weak to handle myself make me feel better?”
Makoto looks bewildered. She opens and closes her mouth a few times, “I-” She starts, her
brow furrowing, “I feel like we’ve read this situation very differently.”
Akechi narrows his eyes, “How did you read it?”
“Don’t worry about it.” She says quickly, looking embarrassed, “But- I’m pretty sure that
Joker doesn’t see you as… weak.”
Akechi shrugs, “Think what you will.”
Makoto rolls her eyes, looking exasperated, “Whatever.” She mutters, then seems to draw
herself back together, “How are you finding the Metaverse?”
“Entirely absurd.” Akechi says honestly, “There’s nothing I can do but accept it at face value,
though that doesn’t exactly dampen the blow of its existence.” Two years has dulled the
shock, but Akechi can remember the panic and confusion he felt when he first found the other
world.
Makoto huffs, looking amused, “You seem to be having fun, though.”
Akechi tilts his head, “I am, I suppose. There’s a thrill to fights in this world that doesn’t hold
quite the same weight in the real one.”
Fighting with a persona is… different, in an almost intimate way. Personas are the soul, or so
everyone seems to insist, and sharpening something so personal into a blade that can deal and
receive pain in turn- well, the feeling is definitely more than a brawl in an alley can offer.

Makoto furrows her brow, “Do you… get into fights in the real world often…?” She asks
sceptically.
Akechi forces a bright smile over his grimace, laughing politely, “Of course not- It’s simply
an assumption I’ve made.”
Makoto doesn’t look particularly convinced, but she nods anyway.
“I’m glad you’ve decided to work with us.” Makoto says after a beat, “I can admit it was
quite stressful when we thought you would arrest us if you found out who we are.”
Akechi huffs a laugh, “Perhaps all this would have been more painless had I come clean
earlier.”
Makoto presses her lips together, “It would’ve been, yes.” She sighs, “But the stress isn’t
really gone, either.”
“Do you not trust me?” Akechi asks lightly.
Makoto falters, “Well, no, it’s not that.” She shakes her head, and Akechi notes that she
didn’t quite answer the question, “It’s more that, even if you’ve made it clear that you don’t
want to arrest us, you didn’t seem happy to join us, either.”
Akechi shrugs, “You did manage to convince me, in the end.” Twisted his arm, more like, but
it hardly matters when the result is the same, “I have no intention of backing out before we
complete our goal.”
Makoto stutters on a nod, “Good.”
Akechi hums, tilting his head, “Why does that concern you, anyway?” He raises an eyebrow,
“Surely you aren’t worried about my comfort.”
Makoto snorts, “Of course not. I just don’t want you holding us back.” She says, almost
teasing.
Akechi smirks, “I doubt that will be a problem.”
Makoto gives an exasperated sigh, “You’re so confident. But I suppose you do have the skill
to back it up.”
“I suppose I do.” Akechi says, disimpassioned.
(It’s a strange rapport Akechi has with Makoto; he thinks, as the High Priestess grows to rank
three.)
***
Further into the infiltration, Ren has yet to let Akechi back on the front lines. It’s quite
grating- Ren has yet to take a break himself, despite having been dizzy as well. Akechi
wishes he had pointed out the other’s hypocrisy while he had the chance.

But alas, he’s stuck making small talk with Makoto after their banter died down. Akechi finds
he much prefers the banter- Makoto keeps trying to talk about the weather.
Eventually, Ren calls to the reserves, “Queen, you’re up. Panther’s out of SP.”
Akechi places all his annoyance into a small sigh rather than the death glare he would have
preferred. Makoto jogs forward with a nod, as Ann walks over with an exaggerated yawn,
looking very ready to collapse.
“Hey Crow.” She drawls out, “Hiya Mona.”
Morgana looks up from where he seemed to be communicating with Futaba, “Hey, Panther!
Did you get sent back?”
“Yup.” Ann stretches her arms out over her head, “I went a little overboard towards the end
there.” She smiles, “Anyways, anything fun been happening back here?”
“Not really.” Akechi informs her.
“Nah.” Morgana confirms, “I’ve been trying to help Oracle out with the navigation a bit. This
palace has been kind of annoying.”
Ann tilts her head, frowning, “What do you mean?”
Morgana sighs, “Well, we still haven’t found a map- and we haven’t even stumbled across a
safe room yet! I think Joker’s going in circles.”
“Mona and I have been doing our best, but we really don’t have a lot to go on.” Futaba’s
voice grumbles from above, “Honestly, we probably should’ve gone home by now, but we
haven’t even been able to save our progress.”
“There really hasn’t been a map yet?” Akechi asks, eyebrow raised. He’s pretty sure he
remembers maps lying around in the times he’s slashed through Okumura’s palace. Even
now, Robin has a record of the palace layout sitting relatively unused in Akechi’s mind.
“There should be!” Futaba exclaims alongside the sound of frustrated keyboard clacks, “But
I think your awakening must have put this place on permanent high alert- what the hell did
you even do to these guys?”
“Nothing so extreme.” Akechi lies. How convenient that his terrorising of Okumura has
become yet another obstacle for the thieves’ progress. He gives himself a mental pat on the
back.
“Well, back to searching, I guess. There’s something really weird about this place.” Morgana
sighs, turning away to continue his discussion with Futaba.
“It must be kinda hard to be a navigator.” Ann muses, combing her hand through her hair,
“I’m no good at that analysis stuff- I just hit things.”
“You do hit them quite well.” Akechi says, “It’s good to specialise.”

“Charmer!” Ann says with a teasing grin, “Thanks, though. Skull, Fox, and I are definitely
damage focused. Though I guess you and Joker are as well…” She hums, “You’re like… allrounders!”
Akechi chuckles politely, “Such high regard.”
Ann bumps his shoulder, “You deserve it! I could hardly keep up with you two earlier. Sorry
Joker took you off the front- he’s just a worrier.”
“So I’ve been told.” Akechi says blankly.
Ann hums, tilting her head, “Well, if you’re annoyed- let’s talk about something else!” She
places her hand on her chin in a familiar pose, and Akechi can’t quite tell if he’s being
mocked, “Oh, I know! How about… what are your hobbies?”
Akechi blinks slowly, “We’re… doing icebreakers?”
“Why not?” Ann shrugs, “I said it before- we don’t know each other too well.”
Akechi feels like it will be a cold day in hell before he manages to keep up with Ann
Takamaki. He shrugs, and concedes, “I suppose… I enjoy cycling. I also go bouldering on
occasion.”
Ann sighs, “You’re just like Skull… that’s all fitness stuff.”
“Not a fan?” Akechi asks, amused.
Ann pouts, “I don’t hate it- and I’m a model, so I definitely need to keep fit, but like…” She
huffs, “Why exercise when I could be doing something else, y’know?”
“Is this the point where I turn the question?” Akechi asks dryly.
Ann nods cheerfully, “Sure is! Hmm… I like… oh!” She gains a small spring in her step, “I
love trying out new places to eat. Even for stuff I’ve had a million times before, each place
has their own spin, for better or worse.”
Akechi hums, “I find I do that a lot as well.”
Ann nods excitedly, before frowning, “…But you don’t enjoy it?”
Akechi shrugs, “It has its purposes- conversation topics, for one. But if I could cut out any
part of my schedule, I’d get rid of preparing for small talk with my coworkers first.”
Ann whistles, “Your schedule really must be crazy. I thought mine was bad, but you’ve got,
what; school, detective work, interviews, thieves’ stuff, whatever the hell else you do?”
That, on top of assassinations, manoeuvring a government conspiracy to its ruler’s whims,
and attempting to dismantle said conspiracy. “Something to that effect, yes.” Akechi nods.
“Though I’ve had less work in TV lately.”

Ann puffs out her cheeks, “I still don’t envy you.” She hums, “What’s next…” She sighs, “I

Akechi derails his train of thought before it can go anywhere near the memory of his meeting

“Met with some very unpleasant people.” Akechi says brightly, “How about you?”

Chapter 38
Chapter Summary

Palace infiltrations, and downtime.

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

Sumire kicks at a vine that’s bleeding sap all over the ground. It’s pretty gross, but she
supposes it’s about the same amount of gross as shadow guts.
They’re in Sugimura’s palace, trying to make some more progress. They’ve stumbled into
something Sumire can only really describe as a maze- not a normal hedge maze like she
would have expected from a garden palace, but rather a series of curtain-like vines, obscuring
their vision and blocking their path in thick, clumped, tendrils, eerily reminiscent of the
cables that littered Maruki’s palace and Mementos during January.
Crow lets out a frustrated growl as he tries to hack at some of the vines with his serrated
sword, not finding it particularly effective. Noir stands to the side, idly tapping her grenade
launcher like she’s waiting for an excuse.
Sumire nudges Noir, giving her a look to convey that she might as well try.
Noir brightens, “Crow!” She calls, and Crow turns around and shoots her a look. She hefts
her grenade launcher onto her shoulder, “You might want to stand back!”
Crow makes a face, but obediently jumps back as Noir fires. There’s a loud explosion that
shakes the foundation of the room, the vines trembling. The smoke clears, however, and
while there is a sizable scorch mark, the vines remain otherwise unaffected.
“Huh.” Sumire mumbles, pressing her lips together.
Noir sighs, and pouts, “I really thought that would work.”
Crow glares at the vines, “Some cognition bullshit, I’d wager.” He folds his arms, “There’s
likely a puzzle or condition we haven’t met to move these- no other way around them.”
“Should we just…” Sumire starts, not very confident in her suggestion, “Try and make our
way through the maze?”
Noir frowns, “We could try…?” She gives the vines a concerned look, “There’s so little space
between each one, I’m worried we’d get stuck.”

Sumire shudders, “Or they’ll come to life or something.”
“Well, we can only hope that this is some puzzle to find the path, rather than an obstacle in
cognition.” Crow says, walking towards the largest gap in the vines, “I don’t want to know
what Sugimura considers ‘conditions for entry’.”
Noir trails behind him, “I would think I’d have already met them, if it was that.” She gives a
hopeful smile, “So probably just a puzzle!”
Crow hums, using his sword to part the vines for a few centimetres of extra room, Noir and
Sumire following behind.
It does seem to be a puzzle, the further in they go. A directional puzzle, by the looks of it.
A directional nightmare, Sumire corrects herself. Space is more than heavily warped- half the
time they’re just guessing which way to go.
No vines come to life to attack them, though, so that’s a plus.
Sometime during their trek through the maze, Sumire speaks up, “How are the thieves going
with Okumura’s palace, Crow?”
“Terribly.” He says, still facing forward, “They’ve yet to find a map, and only just found their
first safe room at the end of yesterday’s infiltration.”
“That’s good.” Noir says, “I was a little worried that they would get through the palace
quickly, and we’d be in trouble.”
“Our deadline for stopping them is nebulous.” Crow says with a nod, “As soon as they’ve
sent the calling card, we’re out of time, and we’ll have to make a lot of big decisions very
quickly.” A dark expression passes over his face.
Sumire frowns, “So do we just… stall?”
“That seems risky.” Noir shakes her head, “The last time we tried for something as vague as
that, it didn’t make a difference.”
“And we’d have to stall long enough to take out Sugimura and Shido.” Crow points out,
“Which could take months.”
Sumire hums, and furrows her brow, “Speaking of Shido, actually,” She shoots Crow a
pointed look, “What’s the plan?”
Crow presses his lips together.
Haru raises an eyebrow, “Crow…?”
Crow sighs, “I’m… not entirely sure.” He admits, and sighs, “I’ve unfortunately had to scrap
the idea of getting to kill him in the real world, given that would not end well for me.”

Sumire gives him a tentative smile and an encouraging nod.

Third. Again.
Sumire looks out from her position on the podium, and forces a smile.
Third is fine! Really. It’s good enough. It’s good that she placed at all.
(Except it isn’t, because she’s had nearly a year to grow and learn, and be better- third wasn’t
good enough last time, and so it won’t be this time; why is everything the same?)
She had performed her new routine at the meet- the one she chose when she initially got
thrown back in time. She performed well enough, no major mistakes, but the same two girls
who managed to rank higher than her last time did the same this time, and Sumire knows it’s
her own fault, but it still stings.
Sumire gathers her things once the meet wraps up, and leaves.
She’s had other things to focus on, is the excuse that she repeats in her mind. Surely, her
dream can be put on hold to make sure the world doesn’t end.
Sumire swallows, and tries not to think about Kasumi’s bright smile when she declared she
wanted to be top of the world.
She feels terrible for neglecting what she had promised. And then she feels bad for feeling
bad- because the whole world could end, I’m sorry Kasumi please understandSumire barely notices that she’s called Haru until she hears the line start to ring.
“Sumi-chan?” Haru’s airy voice comes through the line, “Hello! Did you need something?”
Sumire opens her mouth, and feels like there’s something stuck in her throat. She swallows,
and coughs slightly. “…Um.” She starts, voice not entirely unstuck, “I had a gymnastics meet
today.”
“Really?” Haru says, and Sumire can almost hear her sweet smile, and it calms her down a
bit, “You should have said! How did it go?”

“I… placed third.” Sumire says, unsure what emotion to inject into her voice.
“That’s amazing!” Haru cheers, sounding delighted. “Congratulations!”
“Thanks.” Sumire mumbles, because that’s what you’re supposed to say when people
congratulate you.
There’s a pause. “Are you not happy with it?” Haru asks tentatively.
Sumire lets out a long, heavy breath, “Not really.” She admits quietly.
There’s a soft hum, “Did you think you could have done better?”
“I should have done better.” Sumire blurts, curling in on herself.
Haru sighs slightly, “Well, third is still quite incredible.” She makes a small noise of

“Also third.” Sumire says, feeling mortified at how her voice wobbles, “So I guess I haven’t
improved at all.”
“That’s not true.” Haru insists firmly, “Or, it doesn’t mean that you’re incapable of

“That’s what’s making me feel so bad, though.” Sumire chokes out, as smoothly as she can.
She wanders over to a park bench to slump down on.
Haru hums again, “…It’s not like you only have this year.” She laughs, “We’re making sure
all those bad things don’t happen, right? You have all the time in the world.”
Sumire huffs, “I don’t have time, though.” She says, voice wet, “The retirement age for
gymnastics is so young…” She trails off.
There’s a pause. “…It is young, all things considered.” Haru concedes, “But one year of
minimal progress won’t kill you- especially when that year doesn’t quite count, from an

“But I know I haven’t…” Sumire mumbles, and then winces as she realises how childish that

And then, she thinks about how she really hasn’t had an extra year at all. Can she really
consider anything that she did under Maruki’s spell ‘improvement’, when she was training
for a body that wasn’t hers at all?
The universe granted her a chance to take back the time that was stolen from her, and she still
hasn’t done anything with it“You still have time.” Haru repeats, “And… you’re allowed to have other interests. Or, well,

Sumire sniffs, laughing slightly, “Goro said pretty much the same thing, a while ago.”

Akechi chooses to stay silent.

“I think that the only reason I don’t actively enjoy it is because I know I shouldn’t.” Akechi

Haru swallows her mouthful, and smiles slightly, “Well, you’ve got one up on me.” She

Akechi snorts, despite himself.
Haru’s laugh gains a shade of mirth. She tucks a clump of hair behind her ear, “I always feel

Akechi raises an eyebrow, “Where’s this coming from?”

Haru smiles weakly, “Well, I was just thinking about the Phantom Thieves. When we went to

A beat.

Past the static that threatens to increase in volume, Akechi swallows, throat dry.

Perhaps, Akechi thinks the next day, it is important.
Wandering through Okumura’s palace with the other thieves, Akechi has yet to be placed

Odd.
Sugimura’s palace was the same way.

She had, in fact. Not that the results would be particularly useful here.

Futaba taps away at her screens, not making eye contact. “…You think you’d be interested in

(because he was, at first- the whole thing was so thrilling, so interesting- but it’s a lot less fun

Akechi really needs to stop fucking thinking about this.

(The Death grows to rank two.)
“Right.”
There’s a lull in conversation, until Ren’s voice shouts back from the front lines.
“Hey, Crow!” He calls with an unrestrained grin, “You’re up.”
Akechi smirks.
Fucking finally.

Fear, lies, and dreams

Ren’s decision to invite Goro back to the front lines was not one made lightly.
Ren is, frankly, fucking terrified about what could happen even in the time it takes to blinkbecause the Metaverse is dangerous, and he never thought about it seriously until he started
getting prophetic dreams telling him that Goro is in danger.
So, the solution is simple. Keep Crow off the front lines. He can’t get hurt if he doesn’t
engage, right? He seems annoyed, but Ren prefers him annoyed over dead.
But, the part of Ren that sounds suspiciously like Arsène whispers (Which happens to be
quite a large part of him), fighting alongside Goro was some of the most fun he’s had in a
goddamn while.
Wasn’t it a thrill, his mind taunts, don’t you want to feel like that again?
And Ren relents.
“Hey, Crow!” He shouts back, “You’re up.”
The smirk that slices across Goro’s face immediately dispels any lingering fear Ren has.
“Thank you for the opportunity, Joker.” Goro says, saccharine- and, yeah, he’s definitely still
pissed.
Ren elects to ignore the sarcasm, “Want to pick up where we left off?”
“Our competition?” Goro says, catching on. His expression grows a touch more genuine,
“Who would I be to refuse?”
“A guy who lost the competition.” Ren offers, and Goro snorts.
“I’d argue you forfeited earlier.” Goro mutters under his breath, and Ren can’t tell if he was
supposed to hear that or not.
It’s easy to think that there’s nothing that could ever hurt either of them, when they get into
the swing of battle.

Fighting is such a flow of magic and steps that feel halfway to a dance that Ren isn’t quite
sure if any of this is really a competition, anymore, but it doesn’t stop the pointed glares and
near-fond hisses of kill steal, whenever either of them manages to slice in a finishing blow.
Ren, idly, out of mind, wonders why it’s so easy, to fall into patterns like this.
Ann keeps shooting him looks after each fight wraps up, and he flashes her an innocent look
and moves on.
The flow halts rather abruptly when they stumble headfirst into a shadow that’s far stronger
than anything they’ve encountered.
“It’s immune to bless and curse!” Futaba’s voice echoes, “Uh, scratch that, actually, it drains
them!”
“Great.” Ren grits, leaping out of the way of an explosion of almighty magic.
Goro nearly stumbles into him, having dodged the same blast, “Any weaknesses?” He asks,
in the tone of voice that implies he knows there won’t be any.
“Nope.” Futaba says, and, yeah, Ren was expecting that too, “You might have to brute force
it.”
Goro responds by immediately sending out a megidola, the willowy shadow hissing in pain,
but not looking nearly as injured as Ren would have liked.
Ann and Makoto toss out their own magic, Ann scowling in frustration when her fire glances
off the shadow in whisps.
Ren skids back, tearing his mask from his face, a personas name on the tip of his tongueHe trips over his words and his feet when the shadow beats him to the punch of acting, an
unsettling fog settling over the battlefield as the shadow breathes it out. In the corner of his
eye, he sees both Makoto and Goro stagger; Makoto sinking to her knees, wide-eyed and
muttering, while Goro doubles over and tugs viciously at his hair, body tense and shaking.
“Shit, Crow and Queen got hit with fear!” Futaba shouts with an edge of panic, and RenA sharp pain lances through his skull, and he thinks that this shouldn’t be happening- it’s
wrong, it’s wrong- not now- shouldn’t this be happening later?
Ren shakes his head furiously- he didn’t even get hit with the ailment, he has to get it
togetherThe shadow breathes, and the fog settles once again, and Ren can’t shake it off this time.
He can’t tell where he is anymore- sterile hallways blending with iron, pipes, and smoke- and
Ren is sure that half that iron has to be blood-

There’s something- there’s something there and Ren knows that it’s dangerous, it’ll hurt when
it strikes, and he knows that it knows where to strike hardest.
Throat, lungs, eyes, spine? No, no, Ren can tell that it will go for his heart- not the one
protected by muscle and bone- and he has to do somethingNo, he has to run, something hisses, but that isn’t what Ren sees; instinct fights instinct and
Ren is caught in the middle, wings pinned with bulletsTake his place? Goro glares at him quietly, waiting for him to continue.
Ren laughs weakly, “I don’t think little of you at all. I definitely don’t think you’re weakYou’re pretty amazing, you know that? I mean- I don’t think anyone can keep up with me as
well as you do -in the Metaverse and the real world- and you’re really smart, so-”
“Get to the point.” Goro cuts across, cheeks slightly pink.
Ren clamps his mouth shut to prevent any more of that tumbling from his lips, “I do trust
you. Is my point.”
“You have a funny way of showing it.” Goro says flatly, the pink in his cheeks already faded,
and Ren wonders if it was ever there at all.
“I mean it.” Ren insists, giving a sharp look. He sighs, and finally collapses onto the bed.
Goro narrows his eyes, but eventually wanders over, and slowly sits down in the space next
to Ren.
“You know how I felt, when you joined us?” Ren asks, leaning fully onto his back, looking
up at the ceiling, “It felt fucking amazing, because it meant that I didn’t have to choose.”
Goro tilts his head slightly to indicate he’s listening.

Ren breathes deeply before continuing, “I could have my cake and eat it too, it was great! It
couldn’t have turned out better.” He throws up his arms in a mockery of celebration, before
letting them fall back to the bed with a thump, “But, fuck, I keep thinking there has to be a
catch. Something’s going to go wrong, and I don’t want to lose you.”
A beat.
Goro eventually hums, considering. He raises an eyebrow, “You still haven’t answered my
question, you know.”
Ren frowns, “That being?”
“What,” Goro starts, leaning backwards until he’s level with Ren, “Makes me so different?”
Ren swallows.
There are a lot of things he can say.
It is with a rush of something that Ren realises that ‘A dream foretold your death’ might not
actually be the most accurate answer.
“I don’t know.” Ren says, a half-truth, as a dumb grin slowly spreads across his lips, “You
just are.”
Goro gives him another flat look, but surprisingly doesn’t comment.
They lie there for a while, legs dangling off the edge of the bed, staring up at the ceiling. (Or,
at each other, as Ren steals the occasional glance and pretends not to notice when Goro does
the same.)
“I apologise for my earlier behaviour.” Goro eventually says, cadence returned to being high
and smooth so abruptly that Ren only just notices that his voice had been different at all.
Goro chuckles lightly, “It was rather unbecoming of me.”
Ren gives a crooked smile, “It’s fine. I didn’t mind.” He nudges the other’s side with his
elbow, “I was wondering what was beneath all the smoke and mirrors.”
“And you found a guy who’s pissed at you.” Goro deadpans, voice already slipping back into
something lower, “Truly, you must be thrilled.”
“Surely you’re not pissed at me all the time.” Ren grins wider.
Goro raises an eyebrow, “Oh? Is that a bet you’d like to place, Ren?”
Ren rolls onto his side to look at Goro properly, “Maybe.” He smirks, “I think I’d win.”
“Insufferable.” Goro rolls his eyes, not quite hiding the upward tug to his lips, and Ren
laughs.
Another beat.

Ren swallows, and shuffles a little closer, “I can keep you on the front lines, if you want.” He
smiles, “Unless a shadow cuts off your arm, or something.”
Goro huffs a laugh, “I’d like that. We work well together- it’s only practical to take advantage
of that.” He says, then fixes Ren with a look, “But don’t take hits for me again. It’s insulting.”
Ren snorts, “Noted.”
(In both their minds, the Justice reaches rank eight, and they wonder how much longer their
respective lies will hold.)
***
The part of Ren’s mind that houses the Aeon expects to be called upon that night. However, it
is with some measure of surprise that no such call is made.
Rather, Ren falls into an uneasy sleep, rich with the portent of disaster.
It’s cold. Dark, too, but not in the way that invites fear or loneliness- instead, there’s a buzz of
excitement and triumph that hangs in the air. There are bangs of colourful explosions, close
enough to be beautiful and far enough to feel entirely safe.
It’s perfect. A perfect celebration to end a flawless heist.
Ren can’t shake the feeling that something is wrong.
Another’s voice, light and airy, expresses aloud what Ren doesn’t wish to voice. Everyone
brushes her off- how could anything be wrong? They did everything the same, after all.
Time ticks on, laughs and cheers and revelry distracting from the intuition tugging at Ren’s
nerves. They’ll need to wrap it up, soon- the fruits of their labour coming to fruition in just a
few minutes.
Everyone settles down, once they realise that time is up.
The dream had not been clear, up until this point. But, as colours and voices shift in and out
of clarity, Ren manages to hold onto something clear.
Kunikazu Okumura, though Ren has not seen the man’s face on many occasions, sits before a
press conference- surprisingly composed as he confesses the surface of his sins.
But there’s more- there has to be.
Okumura opens his mouth, Ren leans forwardAnd the man pauses.
Then he chokes.

There’s some tittering behind the cameras. Some assistants, some security, step forward with
words of confused concern, as Okumura sits, slumped, over the table, face obscured.
The part of Ren’s mind that screams something is wrong shouts so loud that he almost
flinches.
When Okumura drags himself back to face the cameras, his face is twisted- eyes bulging,
mouth agape, as blood streams down from every orifice, someone screams, on screen and at
Ren’s side, andAs the cameras cut out, so too does the dream.
Ren doesn’t startle awake, but he does freeze, careful not to wake Morgana as he tenses.
Well.
Shit.
He should probably count himself lucky that he remembers this dream as clearly as he doesbut Ren has to say that he isn’t particularly thrilled to be used yet again as a medium to
foretell someone’s death.
At least it isn’t Goro again, a stray thought hums, and Ren shuts it up.
This is still important.
Okumura might be in danger, then. Take a number and join the line! At least Ren has a little
more context for this one.
He needs to call a meeting.
***
Ren doesn’t call Goro to the meeting. He’s yet to tell him about the visions, and Ren would
like to ease into a conversation like that, if at all possible.
The other thieves sit in solemn silence as Ren explains the possible complication with
Okumura.
Makoto is the first to respond, with a harsh sigh, pressing her lips together, “Well, I suppose
it’s not entirely surprising that Okumura could be in danger. I would expect that it would be
in several people’s best interests to silence him before he can confess.”
“But, isn’t he supposed to be the mastermind?” Morgana asks, eyes narrowed in confusion,
“Shouldn’t he… I dunno.”
“On the contrary,” Yusuke interjects, “Being the mastermind means that he is probably privy
to the most information regarding these crimes- I doubt that others involved wouldn’t hesitate
to deal with him to save their own skins.”

“Like the black mask?” Ann suggests.
Ryuji scrunches his face, “Oh yeah… they prolly know they’d be screwed if their boss’ heart
changes.”
“Speaking of,” Futaba chimes in, nose buried in her laptop, “Did that dream tell you anything
about Sumire, Ren?”
Ren frowns, “No, I don’t think so.” He pauses, and then shakes his head with more
confidence, “If she was there, I didn’t see her. I didn’t see anyone’s face aside from
Okumura’s.”
There’s a collective sigh, weighted with exhaustion and helplessness.
Ann tugs at one of her pigtails, “Should we, like…” She scrunches her face, “Tell Akechikun about all this?”
Ren leans back, considering.
“D’you think he’d believe us?” Ryuji asks with raised eyebrows.
Makoto frowns, “Whether he does or not, we’d be telling him that Ren has,” She sighs,
“Foretold his death, or something. Which, well…”
“That… seems like a lot to tell a person.” Morgana finishes, ears flattening against his head.
“I doubt he’d be inclined to believe us if we tell him our suspicions about Yoshizawa-san, as
well.” Yusuke points out, “They’re friends, no?”
Ren bites at his lip, “True…”
Futaba tilts her head, “I mean… we don’t have to tell him all that stuff, right?” She winces
slightly under everyone’s attention, “Like, he was the one to tell us how much of a bad idea
targeting Okumura could be, so we can just say ‘we’ve taken your concern to heart, senpai!’”
She says in a high voice, parroting mouth movements with her hand.
“And what, just say we’re worried about Okumura’s safety?” Ren clarifies, mulling it over.
“That… could work.” Makoto says slowly.
“But… we don’t tell him about the visions, or about Sumire-chan.” Ann mumbles, equally
slow. She brightens, “Sounds good, right?” She laughs awkwardly, “I mean, I really doubt
he’d believe us if we hit him with all this stuff right out the gate.”
“Prolly give us that judgy look…” Ryuji mutters.
Ren laughs slightly, honestly relieved that he doesn’t have to be on the receiving end of the
aforementioned judgemental look as he stumbles through an explanation of everything, “It’s
decided, then.” He says, taking out his phone, “Should I call him to meet?”

“Before you do,” Morgana cuts in, “Aside from the dreams, have you been getting any more
visions while you’re awake?”
The cat has a knowing look, and Ren thinks he probably couldn’t lie if he tried, “Yeah.” He
admits, “Mostly during palace infiltrations.”
“When?” Yusuke asks, frowning.
“Are you getting them when you run headfirst into enemies?” Futaba asks dryly.
Ren winces, “Yeah… I’m not super aware of my surroundings when they happen.”
Makoto hums lowly, “That could be a problem. Actually, it sounds like it already has been a
problem.”
Morgana has an odd look on his face that Ren can’t quite decipher.
Ren waves Makoto off, “It’s fine. They’re never that serious.” He says, not wanting to slow
down the palace infiltration any more than they already have, “I’ll tell Goro to meet up.”

It is with a modicum of concern and a healthy dosage of suspicion that Akechi makes his way
to Leblanc after a text from Ren, calling an emergency meeting.
Akechi wonders why he didn’t just text the group chat.
His possible theory as to why that may be is quickly confirmed when he ascends the attic
stairs to find all the other thieves already present, all looking varying degrees of grim.
Ren throws up a casual wave, not looking nearly as morose as his teammates, “Hey.”
“Hello.” Akechi says, raising an eyebrow, “I’d go through the spiel of pleasantries, but you
all seem particularly restless today. What is this meeting about?”
“Well,” Ren starts, leaning forward and spinning his phone in his hand, “We have some
updates about the Okumura situation.”
Akechi, in a burst of delusional hope, imagines the thieves calling off the heist for one reason
or another.
“Those updates being…?” Akechi presses, giving his best interview smile to smother his
impatience.
Makoto folds her hands in her lap, “We’re concerned about Okumura’s safety once we
change his heart.”
Akechi’s eyes widen, genuinely surprised. Beyond his bout of wishful thinking, he didn’t
expect the thieves to consider something like this.

“Oh, shit,” Ren sits up abruptly, “Did we ever tell you anything about the other Metaverse
user?”
Actually, they haven’t. Akechi thinks it’s a good thing they’ve decided to loop him in now,
rather than have him accidentally slip with the knowledge at some point down the line.
“The who?” Akechi asks, with performative surprise.
It is with an odd degree of enthusiasm that the Phantom Thieves rush to explain the situation
as it stands.
One: there is another Metaverse user with a black mask who is behind the mental shutdowns
and psychotic breakdowns, as confirmed by both Madarame and Kaneshiro.
When questioned as to whether they have any leads to their identity, half the thieves clammed
up until Ren said that the black mask is likely working for Okumura.
Alright. Weird.
Two: The thieves are concerned that the black mask will retaliate to save their own skin once
Okumura’s heart is changed. Akechi asks some questions about mental shutdowns and
psychotic breaks to keep up appearances, and eventually settles into a contemplative pose.
“I think,” Akechi starts, ready to try his luck, “That you should all reconsider your decision
to target Okumura.”
“Our decision,” Ren corrects, unnecessarily.
“Sure,” Akechi waves a hand dismissively, and Ren seems to be caught between pouting and
looking triumphant, “My point still stands.”
“No way, man,” Sakamoto says, pumping his fist into the air, “If Okumura’s behind all this
shit, then we’ve gotta change his heart!”
“And how, exactly, do you propose we do that?” Akechi sighs, pinching the bridge of his
nose, “If Okumura dies before he confesses, it will not end well for you.”
“Well, we just need to stop a mental shutdown, right?” Morgana points out, “As far as we
know, those can only be done if you kill someone’s shadow.”
“And so far, all our target’s shadows have agreed to return to their real selves after defeating
them,” Kitagawa continues, catching on, “So we simply have to guard Okumura’s shadow
until then.”
“And if the black mask decides to engage?” Akechi points out, exasperated, “We have no
idea how strong they are,” Akechi could definitely fight all the Phantom Thieves at this point
and win, he thinks. Not that he has a reason to. “And that does nothing to protect him from
assassination attempts in the real world.”

“What about Haru?” Ann points out, frowning, “She’s still engaged, right? We can’t just not
help her…”
“I doubt Haru-san will be thrilled if her father is murdered, either.” Akechi says with a tight
smile.
(Though, as Akechi says that, he isn’t sure that Haru would be that torn up by the event,
either.)
“Still!” Ann insists.
“We don’t have any other leads.” Makoto says calmly, “This is our only chance to learn more
about the culprit.”
“C’mooon,” Futaba whines suddenly, pointing at Akechi, “You know you want to! It’ll be
fine!”
“You don’t know that.” Akechi snaps, then takes a deep breath to recompose himself, “I
really think you should reconsider.”
“Do you have an alternative?” Ren says, seeming to be genuinely asking.
“I- No, but-” Akechi cuts himself off with a huff. Sugimura still isn’t an option. These people
are obsessed with the black mask’s activities, of which Sugimura is unfortunately clean.
“What are you going to do,” He starts again, slowly, “If Okumura dies? The blame will be
laid on you, and it’s quite a long fall from the top.”
“It’s a risk,” Ren agrees, “But I’m confident,” He says with a small smile, “And besides,
there are ways to prove our innocence, right?”
“Are there?” Akechi retorts dryly, “And you seem awfully unconcerned at the prospect of
Okumura’s death.”
Ren flushes with embarrassment, “I- well, it’s not like I don’t care, it’s just-”
“We’re all treating this with the weight it requires,” Makoto cuts across.
Liar, Akechi thinks, and tries not to feel too disappointed that he didn’t get to hear Ren’s
thinly veiled opinions about murder.
“I think that you’re all being reckless.” Akechi says darkly, pushing his luck one last time.
“Goro. Trust us.” Ren says. Trust me, is the implication.
There’s no way to turn this in his favour.
Akechi sighs, “I hope you all know what you’re doing.”
“Sure we do!” Morgana declares, the other thieves rushing to agree.

The Judgement reaches rank four, and Akechi bites at his lip.

A roundtable of ignorance, and stalemates.

It isn’t weird per se, that the detective was so pushy about trying to get them to drop
Okumura’s palace, but something tickles at Futaba’s brain anyway.
Number one: She’s still yet to find anything on the guy’s backstory. It’s kind of ridiculous, at
this point- Futaba’s kind of impressed.
Number two: It makes sense, sure, that Akechi isn’t the biggest fan of changing Okumura’s
heart, but he’s still really pushy about it. On edge, almost.
Number three: There’s something Futaba’s noticed, and she isn’t sure if she’s imagining itbut if she’s right… well, she isn’t actually quite sure what it could mean, but it can’t be
anything good.
Probably.

“So!” Futaba starts, crashing into her chair and spinning in a circle, “Any more insights and

Makoto awkwardly smooths out her skirt and sits down on Futaba’s bed. “Not… really?
Nothing useful, at least.”

Makoto straightens up, “Did you find something about his past?” She falters, “Or… anything
