The day after, Ren dreams.
And he’s downright giddy to do it, too. He technically hasn’t been able to think on any of
Crow’s words, since, well, he couldn’t remember them; but he’s sure it’s been simmering in
his subconscious, ripe for revelations to be picked.
He’s in Leblanc again, though he’s in the attic this time. He paces, mulling ideas and theories
over in his head as he waits for Crow to show up.
What, exactly, is Crow? The question is already digging into his brain like a dull spoon,
sinking in with no small amount of resistance. Uncomfortable. He needs to get it out as
quickly as possible.
Ren freezes, as he hears the light scrape of Crow’s metal and clawed boots tapping up the
stairs.
“Hey.” Ren says with a grin.
Crow doesn’t return the enthusiasm, and instead walks over to the bed and collapses on it.
“Well. Let’s hear it.” He says flatly, “What have you come up with.”
He doesn’t really seem to be asking. Ren frowns, “I’ve only had five minutes.”

“With the information you have at your disposal, five minutes will net you the same results as
five hours.” Crow says with a smirk.
“So you think I can’t figure it out?” Ren says with a smirk of his own.
“No.” Crow says flatly, and- ouch.
Ren rolls his eyes, “Sure.” He sighs, “So, I’ve been thinking-”
“Dangerous.”
Ren ignores him, “I’ve been thinking. I doubt you’re my shadow. Because that doesn’t make a
lot of sense for a lot of reasons.”
“Perceptive.” Crow deadpans.
“We’ve already established that you’re not a cognition.” Ren mutters to himself, “…I don’t
think you’re someone else’s shadow- wouldn’t you be in their head, rather than mine?”
Crow tilts his head, “You’re only focusing on what you’ve learned within these dreams.” He
says, “Perhaps I am not just a cognition, but I do seem to reflect your impression of Goro
Akechi regardless. Use that.”
Ren bites at his lip, “I think I had a vision of when he died.” He frowns, “Will die?” Won’t
die.
“And?”
Ren huffs, “I couldn’t really make anything out of it. I just know that I was there, and I was
terrified.”
Crow hums.
Ren scowls, “I don’t understand what I’m forgetting. If these are… visions of the future, or
whatever, then I wouldn’t be ‘forgetting’ anything, would I?” He presses his lips together,
“And these memories that you’ve shown me- none of them have actually happened in the real
world; not a very good prediction of the future, in that case.”
Crow is silent.
Ren throws up his hands, “Can you give me another hint?” He asks weakly.
“Think,” Crow says sharply, “About the words that form your understanding of this
situation. Everything has implications- you simply need to extrapolate.”
Ren nods slowly, still at a loss.
He thinks, and scans, and files through everything about the situation he’s in, andOh.

“Memories.” Ren says, “So this has happened in the past.”
Crow rolls his eyes, “I’m pretty sure I’ve told you this outright at some point.”
“No, but like-” Ren trips over his words as understanding starts to buzz at his nerves, and he
waves a hand, “I thought you were fucking with me, because I didn’t understand what was
going on- but!” Ren grins, “This has happened.”
“Yes.”
“In the past.”
“Uh huh.”
“But the events are different.”
“Get to the point.” Crow hisses.
“I think,” Ren starts, “That this isn’t the first time this year has happened.”
Crow’s expression is unsettlingly neutral for a beat, and Ren almost loses confidence in his
declaration, before Crow starts cackling.
“That!” He gasps in between barking laughs, “Took you so long to figure out!”
“Cut me some slack,” Ren says, finding the mirth infectious as a small grin crawls its way
onto his face, “It’s not exactly a normal assumption to have.”
“No, I suppose it isn’t,” Crow says as his laughter dies down, flipping up his visor and
wiping his eyes, “This whole situation is fucking ridiculous.”
Ren snickers, and then frowns, “I… don’t know how knowing this helps me, actually.”
“Oh, are you fucking serious?” Crow snaps, expression crumpling immediately.
Ren shrugs weakly, “All it really tells me about you is that you’re probably my memory of
Goro from last… what, timeline? Which doesn’t exactly tell me what you are.”
“Think Joker,” Crow growls, “Not a single one of your memories has carried over from the
loop. All you've got to indicate that something is wrong are a bunch of vague visions and
unhelpful dreams from your buried psyche.”
“So you admit you’re unhelpful.” Ren mutters.
“I never claimed to be otherwise,” Crow snaps, “But when taking all of that into
consideration, what is the only thing I could possibly be?”
Ren opens and closes his mouth, words caught in his throat.
He doesn’t know.

But he has to know.
Arsène knew something was up, in the beginning- he just didn’t say anything because he’s a
prick.
Arsène is him, though- if he knows, then Ren knows; Crow sure as hell knows“You’re a persona.” Ren gasps, the dawning understanding hitting him with all the force of
an oncoming train.
Crow smiles.
“You-” Ren starts, gaping, “But- I can’t-”
The Aeon sparks and writhes,
When it settles, it rests on rank nine.
“What,” Crow says lowly, leaning forward, “Is my name?”
“I-” Ren feels his throat tighten, his eyes burning inexplicably, “I don’t know.” He confesses,
weakly.
Crow leans back, disappointment etched into every line of his face.
“Well.” He says with a sigh, “Mull it over.”
Ren wakes up, cheeks wet from a dream he can’t remember.
***
Ren doesn’t know why he woke up crying the other day, but he isn’t in the mood to examine
it.
He has a palace to complete, several people to keep alive, and frankly he’s a little tired of
distractions. If it isn’t immediately relevant, then he’ll think about it later.
They have a deadline (a soft one, but a deadline nonetheless), and they’ve barely made any
progress.
Ren gives a nod to Justine, receiving an eye roll in return, and turns to the Phantom Thieves.
He promised Goro he’d let him on the front lines- a promise he intends to keep- but Ren still
has two other people he needs to choose to join them.
“Mona,” He calls out, “Skull. You guys itching for a fight?”
Ryuji grins, “You know it!”
“Finally…” Morgana sighs. Ren winces, realising he’s been somewhat neglecting the cat’s
vanguard privileges.

“Great.” Ren nods, and turns to smirk at Goro, “Crow?”
“Do you have to ask?”
“Not really.” Ren smiles, “Let’s go.”
Futaba taps at her phone, the Nav bright on her screen, warping them to their furthest safe
room.
Ren shakes off the dizziness associated with quick travel in the Metaverse, and gestures to
the door, walking over to push it open and preparing for any shadows that might be in the
surrounding hallway.
As soon as Ren steps out into the hallway, he pauses, as a dull headache pulses just behind
his eyes.
His decision to ignore it is immediately undermined by the pain blooming like rot and slicing
into every nerve in his head.
“Fuck-” Ren tries to grit out, before, there’s something, he can’t tell what- there’s supposed to
be something here, isn’t there?
“Joker?” Someone’s voice, far, far, away, separated by leagues of water, cries out, “Crow?!”
He’s supposed to be seeing something. There’s flashes, of colour, light, and sound, but there’s
so much pain that all Ren can feel see and think is whitewhitewhiteSomething grasps at his shoulder, and he doesn’t have the energy to pull back- there are other
voices, panicked, that whisper at the edges of his senses.
He’s supposed to remember. He shouldn’t be seeing anything at all, no, he’s already supposed
to know- why can’t he remember? A name, he needs a name, but he doesn’t- he tries sounding
it out, grasping for vowels and syllables that all melt around his tongue into a soup of
nonsense- someone’s angry with him- he can’t handle that- he needs to help, but he still
doesn’t know whatA tug, a whirlpool, shouts of panic, and thenA crumpled heap, as Ren feels himself spill out onto pavement, only just managing to throw
his hands out to soften the blow before his skull cracks on the ground.
“Shit, sorry man!” Someone’s voice- Ryuji, Ren registers- shouts.
Ren can only cough weakly in response, as the lancing pain ebbs into a dull throb.
“Are they both okay?!” Ann’s voice, this time, andBoth?
“Joker…?” Morgana’s voice asks, close to his ear, “Joker, c’mon, we have to move-”

“Yeah,” Ren releases a shuddering breath, slowly pushing himself off the ground. Someone
grabs his shoulder, dragging him upwards.
Ren peels his eyes open, and freezes as they land on Goro, half collapsed against Yusuke’s
shoulder.
“W-what,” Ren swallows, “What happened?”
“You and Akechi collapsed!” Futaba cries, eyes wide and slightly shaking, “You took, like,
one step outside the safe room, and-”
“We had to drag you both back into reality.” Yusuke says, looking grim, “You were
completely unresponsive.”
“Ren.” Makoto speaks up, shooting him a look, “Was this…?”
Another vision? Is the implication. Ren shrugs weakly, blinking rapidly to try and wake
himself up.
“I don’t know,” He says, “It was- something was wrong.”
Whatever something was started as soon as they left a safe space in cognition and ended the
second they wound up back in reality. Ren wouldn't call himself an expert in cognitive
matters, but“Well, we’re not going back into the Metaverse like this.” Morgana mutters, voicing Ren's
conclusion, “We’ll have to delay again.”
Shit.
But, there’s not a lot Ren can argue when he can barely stand.
Across from him, Goro stirs, blinking awake. A scowl immediately pulls at his lips, “…
What-?” He cuts off as he chokes on a cough.
“You and Ren passed out!” Ann says with forced cheer, and the juxtaposition seems to
confuse Goro enough that he wakes up a little more, “So we’re not going to the palace
today!”
Goro opens his mouth, probably to demand several explanations, but eventually jams it shut
and shakes his head.
“Alright, then.” He says, voice oddly flat.
Ren swallows again, trying to combat the dryness in his throat, “To Leblanc?” He asks,
weakly.
(On the way there, still slumped against Yusuke’s shoulder, in Akechi’s mind, the Judgement
grows to rank five.)

***
It is something quite humiliating, to collapse spontaneously.
Akechi had grit his teeth all the way to Leblanc, had smiled tightly at everyone’s concern,
and had nearly snapped when Ren had quietly asked to speak with him even after everyone
else had left.
He’s not in the mood.
But, he supposes, Ren shouldn’t be either, if he also collapsed.
Akechi is dead certain that Ren shared the same vision he did, in that moment. Which is to
say, something entirely useless and unnecessarily painful- so much so that they both fell
something to the left of unconscious.
But, that’s the ticket, isn’t it? Ren isn’t an idiot. Akechi knows that he’s already connected the
paltry dots to realise that Akechi is in the same predicament he is - and who knows what wild
theories his mind will extrapolate upon, following that revelation?
Which, Akechi assumes, is the reasoning behind why he’s being strongarmed into staying at
Leblanc for a while, Morgana having awkwardly skittered off earlier, muttering something
about keeping Futaba company, as he tends do, when escaping uncomfortable situations.
And so.
“What is it that you wanted to talk about, Ren?” Akechi asks brightly, opting for the ‘play
dumb’ approach.
Ren levels him with an unimpressed look, walking around to the other side of the counter to
start busying himself with the coffee siphons. “I wonder what.” He drawls out sarcastically.
Akechi drops the smile, shooting Ren an equally unimpressed glare, “This is hardly the
opportunity to prove yourself right that you think it is. You collapsed as well.”
Ren’s lips tug down in a frown, as he keeps his attention on the cup of coffee he’s making,
“I’m not trying to… berate you, or something. I just think we should talk about it.”
“About what.”
Ren rolls his eyes as he finishes pouring the cup, sliding it over until it rests in front of
Akechi, “Are you being difficult on purpose?”
“Yes.” Akechi deadpans, “I live to inconvenience you.”
Ren sighs, though he looks to be supressing a small smile as he does. “Goro,” He starts, after
he recollects himself, “Do you ever feel like you’re forgetting something?”

Akechi pauses.
“Like,” Ren stumbles over his words, looking caught between wanting to take the words back
and wanting to double down, “Just kind of a feeling in the back of your head- do you get
those kinds of migraines often? Not that badly, obviously, but-”
“Ren.” Akechi cuts across, holding up a hand, “Slow down.”
Ren nods slowly, face flushing.
Akechi flicks his eyes downward, taking a small sip of the coffee in front of him. His lips
quirk up as he gives a short, pleased, hum, “This is different.”
Ren scratches the back of his neck, “I was trying something new.” He says, voice deceptively
neutral, “Is it good different?”
“It is.” Akechi says.
Ren smiles, “Good.”
A beat.
And a stalemate.
A fair one, sure. It’s clear that Ren doesn’t want to actually talk about the incident today any
more than Akechi does- doing so would open up a can of worms for both parties, and neither
are willing to grit their teeth and expose themselves in such a way.
Akechi certainly doesn’t want to admit to ignoring the clearly worsening bouts of pain that
seems to come with the Metaverse as of late, and neither does Ren. That would be an
admittance of defeat in the unspoken game of chicken they've set up for themselves.
So, all that’s left is an uncomfortable silence as Akechi takes another sip of coffee.
“I think everyone wants to take a break from the palace infiltration.” Ren eventually says,
“Give us some time to rest up.”
“Oh?” Akechi raises an eyebrow, “How do you plan on combatting our ever-encroaching
deadline?”
Not that it particularly matters to him if the thieves miss the deadline. It would be beneficial,
even.
(But, another voice chooses to remind him, what if this extends into Sugimura’s palace, too?
Then he’ll have a problem.)
Ren bites at his lip, “I don’t know.” He confesses quietly.
Akechi hums shortly, turning back to his coffee.

Ren audibly swallows, shaking his head, “We’ll think of something.” He laughs weakly,
“Well, now you see why I was worried about you, at least.”
Oh, so they are talking about this. Akechi puts the mug down with a pointed clink, “Evidence
suggests I should be equally worried about you, Amamiya.”
Ren winces, “I- that’s not-” He huffs, “I’m still not trying to tell you off, or anything.”
“Then what are you trying to do?” Akechi says sweetly.
Ren throws up his hands, looking frustrated, “You get annoyed when I try to keep you out of
danger, so I thought it might make you feel better to know why.”
“You’ve given me the same weak reasoning many times.” Akechi hisses, losing grasp of his
mask, “Something about friendship and caring, was it? I’ll have you know that I much prefer
action over sentiment, so I suppose you don’t know me very well at all.”
A low blow, and Ren winces, looking genuinely hurt. He nods silently and ducks his head,
not moving to say anything more.
Akechi quickly tries to reorganise his face into something more neutral, and ignores the
prickling feeling he gets from seeing Ren’s expression crumple.
Suddenly, Ren looks up, a determined glint in his eye, “Let’s go to the jazz club.”
Akechi blinks, “What?”
“The jazz club,” Ren repeats unnecessarily, “We’re getting heated, and the jazz club is
relaxing, so.” He gestures, indicating that his point is finished.
“You remem-” Akechi cuts himself off, clamping his jaw shut. Of course Ren remembers.
He’s Ren.
“Yeah.” Ren says, a small smile pulling at his lips, “So…?”
Akechi resists the urge to roll his eyes and scoff, and instead quietly pushes his chair back to
stand up, gesturing toward the doorway, “Well, if you insist.”
“I do insist.” Ren nods, smile growing a little wider.
Akechi can’t quite stop the eye roll that time.
***
The jazz club does not solve their problems, but it does give them another avenue to ignore
them.
There’s no singer tonight, so Ren and Akechi both avoid eye contact while taking polite sips
of their drinks, listening absently to the record in place of live music.

Ren is the first to crack in the silence.
“Tell me about yourself.” He says, the determined glint in his eye returning.
Akechi raises an eyebrow, thrown by the seemingly random turn, “…That’s a rather vague
question.”
“I know.” Ren tugs at his fringe, “But you’re right. I don’t know as much about you as I
would like. So,” He waves a hand, “Enlighten me.”
“You know plenty about me.” Akechi says dismissively, as unbothered as he can manage, “I
said that to get under your skin. And you don’t talk much about yourself, either.”
Ren tilts his head, considering. “Alright.” He concedes.
“Alright?” Akechi asks, incredulous. He didn’t think it’d be that easy.
“I don’t talk about myself a lot.” Ren says, “So I’ll go first.”
He presses his lips together, seemingly considering what he’s going to say. “So,” He starts, “I
did dance, as a kid- ballet. And some more modern styles.” He adds. He frowns, like he’s
already run out of interesting things to say, “I’m an only child.”
Akechi hums, “I don’t know anything about your family.”
Ren shrugs, “It’s not super exciting. My parents are normal. Aggressively normal.” He ducks
his head, “They weren’t super happy when I got arrested.”
“I assume that’s part of the reason why they shipped you off to Tokyo on your own?” Akechi
asks dryly.
Ren tugs at his fringe again, “Yeah.”
“What loving parents.” Akechi says brightly.
Ren waves a hand, “They try.”
“Do they?”
Ren freezes, like he wasn’t expecting to be challenged about this. “They’re normal people.”
He says, not sounding that confident, “Normal parents… it makes sense that they’d be
upset.”
Akechi leans forward, “Is that really what you think?”
Ren narrows his eyes, “Yes.”
There's a tense pause. Ren ducks his head, while Akechi doesn't move.
“Liar.” Akechi says, conversationally, “You lead a vigilante group. There’s no way you’re not
furious about the way things are. So why are you making excuses for the people who tossed

you away like trash?”
“Of course I’m fucking angry.” Ren finally snaps, his expression twisting into something that
isn’t guarded neutrality, “I tried so goddamn- I did everything I could to keep my head down,
and the one time I decide to do something that’s right, they all but disown me for being a
bother.”
As soon as the words are finished being said, Ren freezes like he’s shocked at what’s just
come tumbling out of his mouth.
Akechi suppresses a smirk.
Well now. There’s something interesting.
“You didn’t answer the question.” Akechi points out, while Ren seems to be grasping for
control over his expression, “Why do you make excuses, when that’s how you truly feel?”
Ren ducks his head, face shuttered, “Sometimes it isn’t worth being pissed all the time.”
Akechi shoots him a flat look, “But you are pissed all the time. You’ve just gotten so
excellent at hiding it that you barely even realise anymore.”
Ren snorts, “I guess.” He pauses, “I think I know why it’s different.”
Akechi gives him a questioning look.
“I mean,” Ren goes to explain, “Why I can be… apathetic about my parents, but not about all
the thieves’ stuff.”
“Go on.”
“Because it isn’t about me.” Ren says with a shrug, “With everyone else, I can see how much
their situations suck, and I want to act on it. But…”
“Self-reflection isn’t your strong suit, then?” Akechi asks, finishing the point.
Ren laughs, “I guess it isn’t, yeah.”
Akechi thinks, distantly, about mirrors.
The Tower prods up his spine, restless.
Akechi ignores it.
“What about you?” Ren says, after a beat, “Your parents, I mean.”
“I’m an orphan.” Akechi says immediately.
Ren winces, “Oh, shit, sorry. I- can’t remember if you told me that before.”

It takes everything within Akechi to not glare at Ren for the pity. “There’s no need to offer
condolences,” Akechi says with his prettiest smile and best interview voice, “It’s not relevant
to you.”
Ren seems slightly put off by the sudden change in demeanour, “You just gave me a pep talk
about my parents.” He points out.
Akechi rolls his eyes, choosing not to dignify that with a response.
“I- technically, calling me an orphan isn’t actually entirely accurate.” Akechi blurts after a
pause, “My father is still alive.” He says to Ren’s confused look.
Ren’s mouth parts in a little ‘o’ as he seems to catch onto the implication.
“My mother raised me on her own.” Akechi says, “For as long as she was able.”
Ren opens his mouth, another apology probably on his tongue, before he seems to think
better of it and clicks his jaw shut. “That sucks.” He says instead, and Akechi laughs slightly.
“It does, doesn’t it?” Akechi agrees, staring down at the table.
Ren frowns, “…How about you? Why aren’t you angrier about this?”
Akechi blinks, and tilts his head, “Where did I give you the impression that I’m not?”
Ren seems to regard him more seriously, “My mistake. You just seem…” He pauses, “Tired.
Sad.” He grins a little, “Morose.”
“Those are all adjectives, yes.” Akechi says flatly.
“Are you angry, though?”
Akechi tilts his head, wondering whether to be truthful.
Something in him doubts Ren would be put off by fury. But, who’s to say? Maybe Akechi’s
ire is too messy, too ugly, to be grouped in with the self-righteous anger of the rest of the
Phantom Thieves.
Maybe they’d hate him, if they all knew how much he’s let rage carve his path.
He tests the waters.
“I am.” Akechi confesses, eyeing Ren’s expression. When it doesn’t change, he continues, “I
hate him. My father. Every time I remember he’s still alive I just get so pissed off, because he
gets to live it up when he left my mother and I to rot without a second thought.”
He cuts himself off with a sharp breath, ducking his head and quickly looking away.
(In part, he had hoped that opening up to Sumire and Haru first would make this easier. It has
not.)

He worries he’s said too much, when Ren doesn’t respond. When he looks back, though, Ren
is regarding him quietly, looking thoughtful.
“Do you know his name?” Ren asks, suddenly.
Akechi narrows his eyes.
“I mean,” Ren shakes his head quickly, “I probably should have asked this first- do you want
to change his heart?”
Well.
All that worrying over whether the thieves would accept his request, and Ren hands him the
offer on a silver platter, without Akechi having to speak a single word of his crimes.
Though, he supposes that was never really the problem, was it?
Akechi keeps his put-upon neutrality as he shrugs, “It’s an option.” He says, because it is.
Ren gives him a look, “You… want to do something else?”
Akechi taps at the table, “I want to give every avenue its due consideration.”
Ren hums, and seems to accept the reasoning. “Alright.”
“What about you?” Akechi shoots back, “Ever thought about changing your parent’s hearts?”
Ren frowns, “I- it seems a little…” His frown deepens, “Extreme.”
“In terms of extreme actions, I think it’s fair to say that they started it.” Akechi points out
dryly.
Ren snorts. “Yeah. Fair.”
They both laugh, and fall back into comfortable silence.
Akechi finishes off the dregs of his drink, “Well. Should we get going?”
Ren bites at his lip, poking at the ice in the bottom of his glass with his straw, “…Can we
stay, for a bit?”
Akechi can’t get a read on his expression. He relents anyway. “Sure.”
Ren smiles, and the Justice grows to rank nine.

With regard to Ren's parents: I don't really actively dislike any interpretation I've come
across- i've read pretty much every option; from them being actively abusive, to them
actually being quite lovely, to what I've chosen to go with here: them being painfully
normal, to the point that it's detrimental. I find that's my favourite way to go about his
parentage, since I think it fits with the themes of p5, where stagnation and fear of change
is what lets horrible people get away with horrible things. Though it isn't super
important in this fic, Ren's parents are pretty standard: They have respectable jobs, they
worried about his grades, told him not to get into trouble, and enacted mild punishments
when he did. They shipped him off to Tokyo so quickly because an assult record on one
family member colours the rest, and setting him off on "rehabilitation" (ha) is their
attempt at damage control- "Look at what a normal family we are! Our son may have
fucked up, but we're setting him straight!" They may not be disowning him, but they
sure aren't standing up for him, either.
It could be worse, yes, but that's half the point. "it could be worse" is such a horrible
mentality to get stuck in and can lead to cycles of abuse and yadda yadda
anyways thematic analysis over LMAO

Chapter 42
Chapter Summary

recursive loops, information gathering, and unfortunate coincedences

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

In hindsight, it was wishful thinking that led Akechi to believe that Sugimura’s palace would
be any different from Okumura’s.
He hadn’t had any visions in Sugimura’s palace previously, so why should they start now?
Akechi suspected that they were largely related to Ren, or anything to do with the previous
timeline, of which Sugimura seemed irrelevant.
That thought was quickly dashed when he doubled over with pain as soon as he entered the
Metaverse, as though something were slowly prying his veins from his skin.
This very quickly led to Akechi being manhandled back into reality by Haru and Sumire,
which brings him to now, where he’s slumped against the brick wall of the alley they use to
enter Sugimura’s palace.
"What,” Haru starts, voice deceptively sweet, “Was that?”
“Ah.” Akechi laughs pleasantly in response, “Did I neglect to inform you?”
Haru’s smile widens, and her eyes crinkle at the corners, “It seems you did, yes!”
Sumire looks like she’s watching a car crash.
“Uh,” She starts, eyes flicking rapidly between the two of them with no small amount of fear,
“So! Goro! Was that a vision…?”
“A what?” Haru tilts her head, the picture of polite curiosity, smile fixed in place.
Akechi lets Sumire hurriedly catch Haru up to speed as he leans a little heavier against the
alley wall, trying to regain his bearings over the muted pulse that pulls at the base of his
skull.
Haru hums softly, looking a little less like she’s about to commit murder, “Alright, then…”
She turns to Akechi, “Are they always that painful?”

“No.” He grits out, rubbing at his temples, “It’s usually just a headache, and I can actually see
something. The only other times it was this bad was yesterday in Okumura’s palace and…”
months ago, when he was fighting off the call of chaos he had cast upon some unfortunate
target.
Sumire grimaces, “This happened in Okumura’s palace, too?”
Akechi nods, “Ren and I both got caught unawares. We’ve had to put off the palace
infiltration until further notice.”
Haru bites at her lip, “Well, if it’s affecting you in all parts of the Metaverse, then we may
have to do the same.”
Akechi’s lips tug downward in a tight frown. Shido hasn’t given him any orders, lately, but
that could change at any time- then he’d really be in trouble.
That, and the deadline for Sugimura is one he’s significantly more concerned about in
comparison to Okumura.
Sumire, as if reading his mind, taps her chin, “Can Haru-senpai and I make progress on our
own…? Just until we figure out a way to fix,” She gestures up and down Akechi’s entire

Akechi rolls his eyes at the jab, before regarding her question more seriously, “That would be
helpful, but neither of you are navigators. That wouldn’t necessarily be a problem in most
palaces, but with the trouble Sugimura’s is giving us, I’d exercise more caution.”
Haru nods, considering, “What about Mementos, though? We were supposed to take a look
down there at some point, yes?”
Sumire brightens, “Oh, right!” She turns to Akechi, “We can take care of that while you rest
up! And if it’s a problem for Ren-senpai too, then maybe the thieves will be able to come up

Akechi sincerely doubts that the thieves will be able to combat metaphysical fuckery, but it’s
a nice thought.
“I suppose that works.” Akechi concedes, “Mementos can be dangerous without navigation,
though.” He pauses, “Actually, here.” He empties his pockets of all the Metaverse supplies he

these- don’t use these, actually. They’re useless.”
Sumire nods attentively as he points to each item, while Haru scans them sharply.
“We’ll be careful.” Haru promises, “We’ll make sure not to split up, and we won’t get into
any fights unnecessarily.”
“Right!” Sumire nods determinedly, “Oh, and we won’t linger on any one floor too long,
either.”

“If the reaper kills you, I’ll never let you live it down. And I’ll never forgive you.” Akechi
tacks on as an afterthought.
Haru giggles, “We’ll be extra sure to stay alive, then.” She tilts her head, “I wonder if Joséchan could give us a lift?”
Sumire looks thoughtful, “If we run in to him, we can ask.”
“Don’t count on it.” Akechi warns, “There’s no guarantee you’ll encounter him.”
Haru shrugs delicately, “Well, if we’re lucky.”
Akechi huffs, “Indeed.” He taps his shoe against the ground, “When do you think you’ll go?”
Sumire presses her lips together, “Not today. Sometime this week?”
Haru nods, “That sounds good.”
Akechi ignores the annoyance at being sidelined in both teams he’s a part of. He can tear his
way through minds and crack and shatter and make sure it stays broken, and yet now he can’t
even take one step in the cognitive world without collapsing.
Wonderful. His only consolation is that Ren has the same problem. He isn’t sure if it’s
pettiness or sympathy that spawns the emotion.
Akechi sighs, “Well. Stay out of trouble.”

Futaba would like to say she didn’t waste time in calling Makoto for an emergency meeting,
but she sort of did, and she doesn’t like to make a habit of lying (unless it’s by omission), so.
She’s spent the day or so between now and their last palace infiltration stewing in the
revelations that were brought about by their brief foray into Okumura’s palace, trying to piece
it into something coherent.
She could tell by the uneasy look in the other thieves’ eyes that everyone understands the
implications of what happened.
But, no one is talking about it. No one wants to be the one to demand a meeting and press
Akechi for what he knows, no one wants to be the one to force Ren to spill the myriad secrets
he’s probably been holding just behind his lips, and no one wants to ask what the two of them
saw in the vision that looked like it was more painful than the slice fire knives ice that follows
a persona awakening.
So, Futaba can only assume that everyone else is doing what she’s taken to do doing. That
being, wallowing in self-pity and helplessness at the situation and hoping that someone else
can come up with a way to proceed. Ren sure as hell hasn’t- he hasn’t even texted the group
chat since the incident.

But no longer! Futaba’s getting a little bored, and she abruptly remembered a few minutes

“Yup.” She responds, popping the ‘p’, “Well, we know for sure now that Akechi’s definitely
getting those visions, right?”
“Right.” Makoto agrees with a sigh. She huffs, “I don’t know what to do about it- No one

Makoto shakes her head, “I guess that’s true. But in our case, we do have something to hide.
Do we want to tell Akechi-kun that Ren foretold his death? It seems…”
“He might already know.” Futaba says, bringing her knees up to her chest, “And there’s no
way Ren would let us just tell him. We’d have to go behind his back to do it, and I… don’t

Makoto sighs, worrying her lips together, “That’s… fair.” She slumps, “I guess we’ll…
remain at a stalemate until someone cracks.”
“That’s stupid.” Futaba mutters.
Makoto’s lips twitch upward, “It sure is.” She intones dryly. She frowns, “Honestly, I think
someone might actually crack sooner rather than later.” Futaba thinks she might crack, at this

“Shit, I forgot about that.” Futaba jumps, “But, that’s good, right? The sooner someone
decides that the palace is more important than whatever the hell’s going on here, then the
sooner we can figure out how to stop their heads from exploding!”
Makoto presses her lips together, “…What if we can’t, though? This isn’t something we have
any idea how to fix- are we going to be down our leader and a member forever?”
Futaba picks at the skin around her nails, “No way it’s forever, right…?”
Makoto sighs, “We don’t know. There’s no way we can know- we only know that these
visions have been escalating lately, to the point where Ren and Akechi-kun can’t be in the

Futaba pauses, “…Do you think it’s hurting them?”
Makoto shoots her a look, “It did look pretty painful, yes.”
“No, I mean,” Futaba shakes her head, trying to get her thoughts out coherently, “Do you
think it could be a little more… permanent? Like, do you think if we aren’t careful it could
kill them?”
Makoto’s eyes widen with understanding, then narrow sharply, “…You think… this could be
what's supposed to kill Akechi-kun?”
Futaba jumps, and quickly waves her hands, “Well, it’s a theory! I mean, he’s not gonna just
drop dead walking in the street, right? So this is super avoidable! We just have to…” She

After a beat, Makoto sighs, “We’ll make sure him and Ren don’t go into the Metaverse. No
one’s going to die,” She says it with such confidence that Futaba almost believes her, “We
just have to figure this out.”
A pause.
“I feel like we say ‘we’ll figure this out’ a lot and then don’t make a lot of progress.” Futaba

Makoto grimaces, “Well, we will.”
“Sure.” Futaba shrugs. Another pause. “How…?”
Makoto tilts her head, “Well, we already know everything about Ren’s side of the visions.”
“Akechi might die, Okumura might die, Sumire might be the black mask?” Futaba

should we… try and get some more information on Akechi-kun?”
“Weren’t we trying to do that already?” Futaba points out.

“Stay the course, then.” Makoto says wryly.
Futaba slumps further against her chair, wracking her brain for something she hasn’t already

Makoto nods, “That’s a good idea. And even if it doesn’t lead to anything about Akechi-kun,

“Yup!” Futaba brightens, then tilts her head, “What about you? Any sources you can poke

Makoto’s face twists like she’s swallowed a lemon, “I… could ask my sis…?”
“You… don’t sound super confident?” Futaba mimics Makoto’s tone.
Makoto huffs, “That’s because I’m not. Akechi-kun said that he and my sis haven’t spoken in

“Well, just try your best!” Futaba says cheerfully, giving a thumbs-up, “Just back off if the

Futaba has no idea if Makoto’s side of the quest is turning out to be a walk in the park, but on
Futaba’s side of things, she’s kind of regretting her declaration that this would be easy.
Realistically, she should have asked Sojiro about all this stuff years ago. But, there was the
time when she didn’t see him for months while all her aunts and uncles were playing hot
potato with her custody, and then she could barely bring herself to leave her room, let alone
speak, for years.
So, there’s that.
And then there’s that lingering whisper of her mom’s voice, snapping at her for taking a peek
at her research. Her mom told her that she didn’t want Futaba to know, so shouldn’t she
respect her wishes? Should she really go looking, out of some misplaced sense of owing her
mom for this?
Futaba knows that excuse is dumb, because she’s already gone looking for her mom’s
research, several times. She knows she’s just scared.
Because what if Sojiro gets mad, too? What if he doesn’t know anything, what if he knows
everything, what if, what if, what ifBut that’s stupid too, and she’s pretty sure Necronomicon agrees, so she just has to get over
it.

“H-hey, Sojiro?” She squeaks, not at all the picture of cool calm and collected she wanted.

Hoo boy. The intensely ‘dad’ vibe that Sojiro is currently emanating is decidedly not helping

“Um.” Futaba stutters, “I wanted to ask about mom.”

Okay. Deep breaths. This is easy.

“It’s just- you worked in the government and stuff right? I think I remember her making fun

The last comment seems to startle a chuckle out of Sojiro, and Futaba cuts herself off.
“It wasn’t anything glamourous.” Sojiro says dryly, waving a hand as he puts down the

Sojiro looks alarmed by several parts of that statement, but looks like he knows how to pick

Futaba quickly scurries over to the couch opposite from where Sojiro’s sitting and plonks

Futaba deflates, “So don’t know anything…?”

Sojiro waves a hand, “I know a few things- she’d gush about her theories occasionally, but if

True. Futaba also has the added advantage of actually being able to travel to the cognitive

“Test subjects?” Futaba perks up, caught between alarm and curiosity.
Sojiro nods, a frown twisting the corner of his mouth, “Yeah. I remember she cycled through

Futaba’s eyes widen and she stiffens, “…A kid?” She clarifies.
A kid. Her mom was experimenting on a kid. That’s fine, right? You have to sign a bunch of
stuff to do that, so totally legal and ethical! ButA kid. It could be no one. This kid could be completely unrelated to everything. She’s pretty
sure Sojiro would still call someone 'kid' well into their twenties, butIt could be the black mask. Or it could be Akechi.
Surely, Akechi would have said something if he knew her mom, right? She even told him that

(Unless, he has a reason to hide it.)
And then the black mask. Sumire, maybe. If her mom was doing Metaverse experiments,

‘incompatible’- maybe the black mask was the first to tear their face off.
(But then, Sumire is Futaba’s age. That, and all its implications, has never registered to her

And yet, something still sits, restless, at the thought of her mom doing experiments on

“Yeah.” Sojiro almost scowls, conveying pretty clearly what his opinion of her mom’s choice
of test subjects is, “I only saw him once or twice. Scrawny. I don’t even remember what he

He.

So. Not Sumire, then.
That still leaves Akechi. Or someone unrelated.
Or, maybe Sumire isn’t the black mask at all.
Futaba pauses.
That’s… a good point, actually.

If Futaba’s so put off by someone her age being experimented on, then why did she not clock

Well- that’s hardly a defence, now that she thinks about it. There isn’t a ‘you have to be this

Right.

Futaba isn’t the best at telling when people are lying, but her bullshit sensors are definitely

It’s too bad that she thinks she might actually agree with Sojiro when he says she shouldn’t

You promised you would not look away from the truths as they fall before you.
Necronomicon whispers in her high, childish, voice.
Well. Not tonight.

The fading sound of a sigh behind her tells her that Sojiro sees right through her, but that’s

Makoto is a lot of things, she’s sure, but a coward isn’t one of them.
She hopes. She hopes a lot, actually; because if she repeats it enough in her head, then maybe
the thought of talking to her sister won’t cause her to clam up, pale and sweaty.
She wonders when her sister stopped really being her sister.
But, now isn’t the time. There are lives on the line, and if sucking it up and talking to her
sister is what keeps her from sliding back into the resigned apathy that had her in a chokehold
as early as a few months ago, then she’ll gladly spit in her hands and do the work.
Metaphorically, of course. Makoto’s lip curls at the thought of actually spitting in her hands.
She can’t imagine her sister would be too pleased, either.
Her somewhat unproductive train of thought is cut off by the sound of the front door opening.
“I’m home.” Sae’s voice shouts from the front, sounding somewhat less tired than normal. A

“Welcome back!” Makoto shouts back, scrambling to get dinner ready.
Sae strides into the living room with about half her usual intensity, her bag and coat already
deposited in her room. “What’s for dinner?”
“Curry.” Makoto says simply, spooning rice into equal piles on two plates. She’s been getting

Sae hums absently, and Makoto stops herself from fidgeting as she quickly carries the two

Sae nods as Makoto sets down the food, whispering a quick thanks for the meal. Makoto

The first time in weeks that her sister is home for dinner, and Makoto has to waste it asking

Some vindictive, petty, part of herself hisses that she doesn’t have to ask. She’s spent more

She promised she wouldn’t run, she promised she wouldn’t be complacent; so she quietly sets

“Hey, sis?” She starts, tentatively, “Have you… spent any time with Akechi-kun lately?”
Sae pauses, looking both caught off-guard and slightly annoyed at the question, “Akechikun?” She says, sounding confused, “Why do you ask?”
How much truth to tell?
“Well, it’s just that I don’t know him very well,” Makoto says, hoping to anything that she’s

Sae’s eyebrows pinch together in something that could be alarm, “Worried? What do you

Sae frowns, “I was unaware you were spending time with him.”
What, am I not good enough? The petty and jealous part of Makoto hisses, and she shoves it

haven’t spoken in a while. You probably know more about him than I do, being closer to his
age.”
Makoto presses her lips together, “Well, you spent so much time with him.”
Sae waves a hand, “In a purely professional sense.”
“And having dinner with him all the time is part of that.” Makoto says, snippily, before she

Sae, thankfully, doesn’t rise to the bait, “If I didn’t give him food, I was afraid he’d keel over.
You should’ve seen him when I first met him. He looked like he hadn’t eaten in months- and

Makoto takes a second to once again stomp on the part of herself that rallies to sabotage this

“Scrawny.” Sae says bluntly, pushing the curry around on her plate, “No one really took him

camaraderie, from that. Neither of us are willing to give anyone the satisfaction of our

‘Purely professional’, Makoto mocks in her head.
Something passes over Sae’s face after a beat, “You said you were worried about him?”
“Yes,” Makoto nods, wondering what angle will get Sae to talk, “He’s the type to hide his
problems, so…”
Sae presses her lips together, “Do you have any idea what could be bothering him?”
Makoto huffs a laugh, “That’s what I was going to ask you. Do you know if he could be in

Sae snorts, picking up on the implication, “If Akechi-kun is in trouble with the yakuza, then I

Makoto tries not to slump, “It’s fine. Maybe I’ll just press him for answers at some point.”
It’s the only option left, unless Futaba manages to unearth a miracle.
Sae huffs, “That might be difficult. He’s not exactly forthcoming about his personal life.”
Makoto almost scowls at the idea that Sae might be more interested in Akechi’s life than
hers. She doesn’t, because that’s hardly the point. “Well, I’ll try.”
They slip back into a stilted silence, as they are wont to do at dinner most days. Makoto

“Oh, Makoto?” Sae speaks up as Makoto moves to put her plate in the sink, “Keep an eye on
him, would you?”

Do it yourself if it’s so important to you, Makoto thinks. “Of course,” She says.

The next day, Sumire scowls at the ground as she leaves the guidance office.
She got the same speech as last time from the acting principal about how she needs to
improve her results. Word for word.
And Maruki was there, giving her a look filled with such gracious pity that she wanted to
claw off her skin.
She wonders if this acted as some affirmation for Maruki’s ideals, if he thought that if only
Sumire were Kasumi, then maybe she wouldn’t be in this situation.
Well, jokes on him, Sumire knows for sure that it doesn’t make a difference. She can’t seem
to get a good result whether she thinks she’s her twin or not.
Sumire doesn’t think she’s a naturally violent person, but right now she really wants to hit
something.
Actually, now that she thinks about it, today is the day she awakened her persona last time.
Not that the event really means anything substantial in this timeline.

Haru gives a small smile, “Well, I certainly understand the feeling.”

“Of course, Joker.” Makoto nods firmly.
As the rest of the thieves rush out of the attic without so much as a ‘goodbye’, Ren and Goro

Ren bites at his lip.
Well. What to do?

What to do?
Honestly, Akechi is surprised that the thieves decided to go off on their own. He thought they
would never dare do something without their precious leader, judging from what he’s seen of
their actions so far.
Ren doesn’t seem thrilled either.
More than anything, Akechi is surprised that the thieves didn’t sit them both down and

happening to them clearly isn’t normal by any standard.
Perhaps that’s why they’ve left Ren and Akechi to kill time in the real world. Force them to
‘talk it out’, or something.
“I feel like I’ve been benched.” Ren mutters to himself in the silence of the attic.
“Doesn’t feel so good, hm?” Akechi snipes before he can reign himself in. “This could be
karma.”
Ren scowls, “Well. I had a reason for that.”
A shitty one. “And so does your team.” Akechi raises an eyebrow.
Ren’s scowl softens into an annoyed frown, “Touché.”
And that’s that.
Akechi sighs, “Are we just going to stand around your attic while we wait for them to come

Akechi gives a dazzling smile, “Oh? If I’m not needed then I suppose I will leave.”

Ren chokes on a laugh, “Wait! Wait,” He manages to snatch Akechi’s arm before he can

Ren smirks, “Of course, how else am I supposed to keep you entertained?”
Akechi thinks that there are a lot of ways to read that statement, and frankly he doesn’t care

Akechi narrows his eyes, “A what.”
Ren laughs slightly, “No, like, we could make it so that we don’t really know where we’re
going.”

That sounds idiotic. Akechi kind of wants to do it.
He makes a show of looking exasperated, “Fine. We’ll do your stupid game.” Ren lights up

Ren tilts his head, “Flip a coin?”
“Sure.” Akechi fishes a coin out of his wallet, “Call it in the air.”

He flicks it up, Ren says “Heads,” As the arc reaches its peak.

on his face. “I guess you start, then.”

It’s… kind of pointless, what with Mementos changing every visit. But at least she can write
down where all the safe floors are, since the distance between those never changes.
She leans back in the empty space of her persona, and thinks that they’ve done a pretty damn
good job.
Back down on the ground, Futaba sees Makoto huff lightly, face contorted in a poor attempt
to hide her relieved pride at her temporary stint as leader.
“Alright, then,” Makoto calls out to the group, voice just shy of commanding the ‘Joker’
gravitas, “Shall we head back?”
“Do we have to?” Ann asks, “I mean, that barely took any time at all!”
“I’ve still got some steam!” Ryuji chimes in, tapping his metal pipe against his palm.
“Did you guys wanna see how much further down we can go?” Futaba asks, finally allowing
Necronomicon to lower her to the ground, “I dunno exactly how much further we can go, but
we should at least make it to the next door we can’t pass, right?”
“Or simply the next rest area,” Yusuke suggests, suddenly one for moderation. Boo.
Makoto tilts her head, considering, “I suppose we can see how far our remaining stamina
takes us.” She smiles, “It’ll make our next Mementos trip easier if we make extra headway
now.”

“Right.” Morgana bounces, and jumps into the air, transforming into a car with a bang at the
peak of the arc. His voice crackles through the radio inside the car, “Let’s get going, then!”
The thieves all pile into the car, and Futaba finds herself kind of relieved that Ren and Akechi
aren’t here- the Monabus was already getting cramped with her addition, so throwing Crow
into the mix would have really started to test the limits of space.
She bets he would have commandeered shotgun like a jerk, too. She bets Ren wouldn’t stop
him, either.
But, for now, Futaba commits the sacred act of hypocrisy, and hops cheerfully into shotgun,
as Makoto climbs into the driver’s seat.
She hits the gas, and they rush out of the pocket of distortion, which swirls and vanishes
behind them as soon as they make their exit.
“We’ve made some pretty good progress into this path,” Futaba starts explaining to the rest of
the car, “I can guess that we have at least three more floors?”
“Do you think we’ll be able to push through into the next area too?” Makoto asks, keeping
her eyes on the road, already proving herself a more responsible driver than Ren.
Futaba shrugs, “I dunno. Mona?”
Morgana’s voice crackles through the radio, “Well, we got access to this area after we dealt
with Kaneshiro- so I think that Medjed’s defeat should give us the next area?”
“You don’t sound so sure.” Ryuji grumbles, leaning forward from the back seat.
“Well, it’s less work for us if it doesn’t,” Ann points out, “We’ll have to explore a whole new
area if that thing opens!”
Actually, that does sound annoying. Futaba scowls, and sinks into her chair.
“We’d just have to do it next time if we don’t do it now.” Makoto reiterates, and sighs, “So…
settle in?”
Oh boy.

Haru narrows her eyes, face deceptively impassive, “Then why is it that we failed to stop

Her thoughts hit a loop, and she’s back at square one.
Sumire slumps.
She remembers, vaguely, through the hiss of her thoughts, how Ren had broken down during

Sumire half smiles to herself. Ren really does care about Goro, huh? She’d almost think thatShe freezes, as the half-formed idea lances ice against her spine.
That- that can’t-

But, no, no, that can’t be right. Goro was very much alive and well for all of January- and no

fighting by their side; if he had died, surely someone would have noticed the ghost among
their ranks, would have realisedBut truth and phantoms mean nothing in a reality designed to keep the world in ignorant
peace- Sumire has been burned by her assumptions before, and she knows that even seeing
something with her own eyes means nothing.
But- Goro couldn’t have been dead, could he? It doesn’t make sense. And Ren and Goro were
never affected by the reality, either; if Goro wasn’t real, then why would Maruki let him
opposeAnother counterpoint. Ren and Goro are both wildcards- and that seems to mean nothing and
everything all at once. She can’t dictate what knowledge their power can and can’t impart.
But it can’t be true.
Can it?
The little flare of hope, the knowledge that Goro made it out of the conspiracy’s grasp in the
last timeline flickers, as Sumire feels her hands shake.
It’s the only thing she can think of. The only stipulation, the only ultimatum Maruki could
have presented that would have worked, that Goro wouldn’t have been able to counter, the

world.
Shit.
“Violet…?” Haru’s voice cuts through, tentative.
Sumire tries to laugh to diffuse the whirlpool of panic and dread swirling in her mind, and

Haru’s eyes widen, flashing in curiosity and concern.
“I think Goro might have been one of the people Maruki brought back.” Sumire says in a
half-mumble, trying to push the words around the lump in her throat.
Haru’s face falls, “Oh.”
Sumire tries to laugh again, and clicks her jaw shut when it sounds more like a sob.
Fate, she thinks, is a cruel joke.
Now, now, there’s no safety net. There’s no assumption that Shido isn’t as big of a threat as
he could have been, now there’s the knowledge that this can’t be, never was, as simple as
moving some threads and spinning some plates with all the grace of a performer- Now, there’s
the ever-looming spectre of death hanging by a spider’s thread, a sword of Damocles

dangling like a decorative set piece above someone she had fooled herself into believing
would be easy to save.
Has she made things worse? Better? Has she stumbled into the solution purely by her biases
and luck? Has she sealed Goro’s death warrant herself? She doesn’t know, because she knows
what went wrong and yet has no knowledge on how to solve it.
There has to be a way.
SheWhat the hell is she going to do?

Chapter Summary

Betrayal, discovery, and shattered glass

The road down the tunnels of Mementos is a bumpy one. Mostly made as such by the shadow
corpses that litter the trail.
Shadows being turned into roadkill isn’t exactly a new phenomenon, Futaba is aware; Ren
likes to make a game out of seeing if shadows can outrun a car (they can’t). But, the thing is,
Makoto hasn’t been doing the same thing. In fact, their temporary leader has been actively
avoiding any and all fights to preserve energy.
So, what the hell is up with all these shadow corpses?
“Uh, guys?” Futaba starts, “Did one of you wander off at some point and set off a bomb or
something?”
Yusuke looks up from his sketchbook and tilts his head as though he’s genuinely trying to
recall if he actually did such a thing.
“Uh, is that a serious question?” Ryuji mutters.
“Obviously not.” Futaba waves a hand, “But, follow up question, why are all the shadows on
these floors dead?”
“Yeah, that is kinda weird…” Ann mumbles, looking out the window nervously.
Makoto presses her lips together, “Mona, is there anything that could have caused this?”
“Yeah, like a gas leak or somethin’?” Ryuji chimes in.
Futaba can almost hear Morgana’s eye roll, “No, Skull, there aren’t any gas leaks in
Mementos.”
“You sure?” Futaba asks, just to be a shit.
Morgana sighs wearily, “Pretty sure.” He pauses. “I think. But anyway, I don’t know why this
has happened.”
Makoto frowns, “Well… everyone stay on your guard.”

Futaba leans back in her seat, idly swinging her legs back and forth. In the back, chatter
erupts back at a normal pace. Futaba cranes her head around to try and catch a glimpse of
whatever the hell Yusuke is drawing.

panic. She taps rapidly to bring up the bare-bones map for Mementos, and stiffens at the
signal that Necronomicon manages to get a hold of.
"Um.” Futaba squeaks, “Guys?”

“Feel what?” Yusuke narrows his eyes.
“So,” Futaba starts, “There’s, uh, two signals I’m getting.”
Makoto slams on the breaks, to the shrieks and disgruntled protests of the people in the back
seat, “What?” She says, eyes wide with alarm.
“Yup.” Futaba laughs nervously, “Two… humans, I guess.”
“Is it Crow and Joker?” Ann asks, which is very optimistic of her.
“How on earth would they have been able to make it down this far without collapsing?”
Morgana nips that optimism in the bud.
“So, then,” Ryuji starts, “Is it… the black mask?”
There’s a nervous pause.
“But.” Makoto protests weakly, “There’s two signals.”
“Did we ever get confirmation that there is only one black mask?” Yusuke points out.
“Yes,” Makoto insists, “Kaneshiro definitely implied someone in the singular.”

only one of them is the black mask. Or neither of them is the black mask and we’re dealing

Futaba tries not to think about the test subjects that her mom supposedly worked with.

“I think they’d be dead if they weren’t.” Morgana answers, “This area might not be so bad for

“Plus, it’s probably those guys that made all this mess.” Ryuji gestures to the piles of black

“Should we… turn back?” Futaba posits.
There’s another pause.

If he’s so impatient, he could just start talking, Ren thinks with a pang of annoyance. Though,

He wonders if Goro’s dreams have done the same. He doesn’t know if that will make

“So.” Goro raises an eyebrow.
Fuck it. “You’ve been getting weird visions too, right?” Ren blurts out.

Weird dreams, as well. They started happening for me around April.”

Oh.
That’s…

…Maybe correlation doesn’t equal causation, then.

He’s been dodgy about this. He can’t seem to decide what he should and shouldn’t say.

Would it help or harm? Would Goro having this knowledge be the key to saving him? Or,

But, Ren’s tried the ‘keeping things to himself’ thing for the past few weeks, and it never

Ren pauses, opening and closing his mouth.

Beginning Navigation.
There is a split second of clarity that Ren manages to grasp before the world shifts, and most
of it is spent in panic.
This isn’t the first time that the Nav has activated without proper input. Getting drawn into a
palace against his will isn’t something that would ordinarily warrant a sinking dread.
But, well, circumstances aren’t exactly favourable, here.

Ren doesn’t know whose palace this is. He doesn’t know what shape it will take, hell- he
barely knows where it will be situated.
And, he doesn’t think that he and Goro will be able to get out in the state that they’ll likely
find themselves in.
The short gasp at his side as the world spins tells him that Goro has probably come to the
same conclusion.
And yet,
The sharp lance of a blinding migraine doesn’t come. Instead, there is an odd quiet in its
wake, leaving Ren’s mind in a state of tense calm. He slowly peels his eyes open from where
he had squeezed them shut, and takes in the sight.
“Shit.” Goro hisses at his side, though he doesn’t seem to be afflicted with a split head, either.
“We can’t stay here.” Goro continues, quickly, “We have no idea how long we’ll be
unaffected in the Metaverse.”
‘Here’ is really something else.
Where the half-built stadium once stood, is a monolith of twisting steel, spiralling up, up,
until a globe sits at its peak. Lenses jut out at haphazard points, all twisting and angling to get
a better look at the two interlopers that have just arrived.
It’s beautiful, in a way. Ren thinks he hates it.
“Joker.” Goro hisses, and Ren blinks out of it and quickly takes out his phone. Goro’s right,
they’re lucky they can still think, but who knows how long that will be the case?
--?-__’s Palace, the Nav reads.
“Uh,” Ren starts, “Crow?”
“What?” The other snaps, tearing his gaze away from the towering structure before them.
“The Nav can’t tell whose palace this is.” Ren says, flat, keeping his voice as calm as
possible.
Goro narrows his eyes, “Alright.” He intones slowly, “That shouldn’t stop us from being able
to leave, no?”
Ren stutters on a nod, and taps at the Nav to deactivate it.
Nothing happens.
Conditions have not been met, the Nav helpfully supplies, and Ren swears there’s a shimmer
in the corner of his vision.

Ren pauses.
“Try yours.” Ren says.
Goro furrows his brow, “What-?”
“Just do it.” Ren cuts across.
Goro frowns, and takes out his phone, tapping on the Nav enveloping the screen.
Again, nothing happens, and Ren can hear the singsong of a similar rejection from the other’s
phone.
“Fuck.” Goro presses his lips together, almost in a sneer.
Ren chuckles uncomfortably, “Why,” He swallows, nerves starting to prick, “Why can’t we
leave.”
Goro gives him a look saying, ‘how the hell am I supposed to know?’, “A property of this
palace?” He muses anyway, “Or, perhaps our affliction,” He spits out the word, “Now
extends to our navigation app.”
Ren shrugs, shoulders tense, “Maybe.” He mumbles, “What are we supposed to do?”
Goro gives him another look, “Aren’t you the leader?”
Ren shrugs again- it feels like the only thing he can do, “Just looking for ideas.”

Ren looks up again at the tangle of steel.

Right.

“Apparently so.” Goro responds dryly.

It’s Goro’s turn for incredulity, “Are you insane?” He asks, wide-eyed, “We have no idea how
long we have before we drop. Do you want that to happen while we’re surrounded by
shadows?”

“We can’t leave, either.” Ren points out, “We either sit here and hope our friends find us, or

Goro scowls, looking more than ready to argue. Clearly, neither option appeals to him, as he

this is when the pain and visions will hit- but the silence persists.

Ren bites at his lip when he sees the Velvet Room missing from what can pretty solidly be

searching for the familiar prison door. He shoots Ren a look, pretty clearly telling him to

And, somewhere else, a fractured mirror sighs.
He had been hoping that Ren would figure this shit out earlier, but he supposes that’s too
much to ask of a traitor.
Ironic- and perhaps deserved. Though, the whole situation feels less funny when it’s the end
of the world, and when Ren only pulled this stunt out of some misguided saviour complex.
The mirror also supposes that he only feels this way because that’s what Ren thinks he would
feel, which is irritating in a whole other way. Technically, the mirror enacted no such
betrayal, and did not suffer Ren’s counter in turn. The mirror thinks that apathy is the only
emotion he really has any right to.
Ah, but was he not betrayed? The sanctity of his being, reversed, cracked, and buried beneath
the weight of a forgotten year, supressed under layers of sediment and grief, until he was
forged into the uncomfortable presence of something that reality dictates should not exist.
He looks, idly, at the glass that litters the floor, and wonders if Ren is even capable of piecing
it back together.

His is not the only existence that was forgotten. But, it is the only one that can manifest
himself as such. Somewhere, at his side, or nowhere at all, the Mother Angel weeps in
treachery that she did not think possible, unable to cry her grievances to the one who slipped
a knife between her ribs.
The others sit in silence- some blissfully unaware that their saviour doomed the world (for
love? What a joke), others stunned into disbelief.
And one, delighted by Ren’s choice, confused by the rubble it is buried beneath.
The mirror hopes that one stays buried.
Myriad complaints aside, it is only the mirror that can whisper in Ren’s ear. He remembers
his own name, somewhere deep down. But, he can’t say it. Any attempt to summon himself
into being is met with a chain around his throat and a reminder that what he represents is not
what exists. It would certainly be a lot easier, if he could just introduce himself.
But, alas, the rules of cognition bind his wings. He had been half-convinced that that was all
he was, for a time. It was what Ren believed, so he believed it too.
And then, the doubt.
Warranted, of course. What kind of cognition knows more than the mind from which it
spawned? Not much more, mind, but enough to feel strange.
A persona. The conclusion that Ren had stumbled upon, and the only one that felt right. I am
thou, thou art I, and round and round and round.
But a wildcard’s heart is strange and malleable, and ‘I am thou’ is only true so long as the
wildcard lets it be so. Right now, the mirror isn’t much of anything. He thinks ‘I am thou’
might apply more to the face he wears, should he ever meet him, but even then- not quite.
The two Fools aren’t even back where they started. And yet, simultaneously, they are leagues
ahead. Something has changed, and the mirror assumes it is for the better.
Maybe it would be detrimental, if Ren were to remember his name. But the mirror is selfish,
hungry, and ravenous, and he wants more than his fill.
He wishes, more than anything, to be remembered. It is the promise on which he was forged,
after all, and he has no qualms of taking and taking until Ren looks and understands exactly
what it is he has shattered, carelessly, across the ground.
The mirror tugs idly at the bond he spawned, in some uncomfortable warping of the sea of
souls. The Aeon, arbiter of memory and dreams, reflection of the Judgement, and absolutely
useless if Ren can’t get it together.
The Mother continues to weep, and the mirror wonders if retribution will come for her, too.
She remains neglected, in this time, but perhaps she can be reforged under the same hammer
the mirror has done to himself.

Or perhaps, that bond lies too fragmented to be saved, its edges ground to dust from misuse,
the only option remaining to start again.
The Mother held so much Faith that she choked on it. Will she swallow it, or will she spit it
back out?
The mirror doesn’t know.
“Ah, Joker,” The mirror whispers, attempting to project feeble waves of comfort to the strings
and glass he makes his home in, “How long will you make me wait?”

Somewhere even further, beyond dreams, and yet so firmly rooted in reality, a man feels as
though something is wrong.
It’s not a particularly urgent feeling. Just the quiet nag of maybe he forgot his keys? No,
they’re still there… his wallet? Nope, that’s there too.
Ah, right- the voice is not quite so trivial. The feeling is more the reverent whispers ofThe time is nigh.
Right. Like that.
A bit ominous, but who is the man to deny the voices in his head?

His excited spiral is cut off again by the feeling that something isn’t quite right.

this point.
But no, no. That isn’t it. He’ll be going in circles at this rate. He feels like his brain itches.
A shame. A disappointment. Heresy.
What?
What is yours lies out of grasp.
Oh. That is a shame. The man isn’t sure what is his that he doesn’t have, but it is a little
disappointing that he can’t have it. Heresy seems like a bit much, though.
There’s a shimmer.

What is he thinking about, again?
Fools, he thinks, and then gets even more confused.
“Get it together, Takuto,” The man mutters to himself, and goes about his business.

He thinks he hates snow, by now.

piles. Enough to look beautiful, not enough to ever be an inconvenience, never melting into
off-white sludge, never layering high enough to hide ice underneath.
But, that should be over soon, and then he’ll have to deal with regular weather patterns like
people in the real world do.
One last calling card, a final swan song for the dramatics that accompany thievery like an
old friend, and then reality will be as it should be.
It’s hard not to feel melancholic, really. Which is odd, because Ren knows that he had no
patience for everyone’s false realities. He didn’t care for what their wishes were, because he
knows he wasn’t part of them.
He knows it was selfish. To take what could have been a perfect happy ending from all of
them. But Ren so rarely gets to be selfish, and if the thieves were so wrapped up in their
delusions that they forgot what Ren means, then what would be left of him?
The thieves didn’t seem upset, at least. They thanked him, even, apologised for their
transgressions, and Ren spent the month assuaging their guilt and trying again and again
and again to crack the façade of the one person he really wants.
Bitter work. But, he thinks he made progress. The new face of Goro Akechi tells no lies, but
he never tells the truth, either. His face was all calm waters, caustic to the touch, and Ren

had to wait and watch for when small flickers of the other’s thoughts would bubble up for air
on his expression.
Ren was happy to wait.
He knows it was selfish; but again, he took the rarity afforded to him without a second
thought.
He didn’t say what he felt out loud, because he knows Akechi would have run. He didn’t put a
name to it within the safety of his own mind, either, because he thinks he might have run, too.
But it’s okay. They’ll have time after this final task is done, the whole world to run and chase
as they please.
So Ren waits. And Maruki arrives. He half listens to the counsellor’s monologue, and snaps
to attention when something doesn’t align with the script Ren had been building in his head.
No.
No, it has to be some sick joke, some manipulation, something, anything, but the truth cannot
beHe had never thought too hard, that he didn’t get a wish. Akechi didn’t get one either; so it
must have been some wildcard thing, some divine intervention that shrouded their dreams in
fog, safe from a madman’s probing.
Except, dead men don’t get wishes, and Ren isn’t special.
And now, he has a choice to make.
He doesn’t listen to Maruki’s half-baked sympathy. He flicks the calling card at him in an act
of spite, even though he knows deep down that it will never go to use, and doesn’t look Akechi
in the eye as the other makes his point.
There’s no choice here, he says, and Ren agrees.
Because Ren so rarely gets to be selfish, and can’t he have something, just this once? Can’t
he please have the one thing he wants more than the world- he doesn’t care that it will be a
cage, he doesn’t care that it’s a betrayal, he doesn’t give a shit, because this is the only thing
that he’s ever let matter to him like thisHe’s begging, but he doesn’t have to. The choice is his to make, after all.
And the Justice reverses.
“Do you understand, yet?”
And Ren does, as the room doesn’t yet reform, his body suspended in waiting. He nods,
shakingly.

“Good, then” Ren can hear the smile in the voice, the relief. And he finally turns, and falls"Will you recall?" The thing that was once Crow whispers, "What I am to you, in full? Every
inch, every turn, will you remember the bond we shared, that you have forsaken?"
"I-" Ren chokes, "Yes," He whispers, throat raw.
The being's face smiles, gentler than Ren has ever seen Akechi capable of, this time or last, as
his memory shifts and fragments again and again,
"Good," It whispers again, metal rippling down its arms and up its face, black and blue being
doused in silver and gold, "I am thou, thou art I, will you remember my name?"
"Metatron." Ren whispers,
And memory returns, in all its entirety, cutting through the blinding fog dousing all the sharp
and jagged crevices of Ren's mind, a hindrance and a blessing in equal measure, in the way it
had hidden the wretched wounds left by the reality that once was.
Ah, but no more.
"Oh." Ren swallows, mouth parted.
The Justice snaps back into place, forged in iron and blood, and yet bent at an angle. Not
quite upright, not quite reversed.
The Aeon, too, solidifies. The thread dissolving into blood and becoming whole.
Ren’s knees buckle, and he slams down against the while tile floors of Maruki’s palace, as he
tries to balance the weight of everything he had forgotten.

A cascade of things already dreamed, shifting and transient, all fold in layers to build a
foundation of memory.
A foundation is not needed, perhaps, when the knowledge in its entirety could simply be
dropped all at once, like a sack of bricks, uncaring of the mind it burdens and the surface it
cracks. But, there is a kindness afforded. By whom, and for who’s benefit? It’s hard to say.
But, ultimately, it doesn’t matter.
It doesn’t matter, because the final thing that clicks into place is a herald of futility all the
same.
He had already dreamed of February- Akechi remembers this, now. Of the anger, the
treachery, and the persistent whispers of why that existed in erratic jabs.
He did not, however, dream of the resigned calm that followed. The methodical way he had
marched towards Odaiba, one foot after the other, tap, tap, tap, all the way until he was faced
with the twisting and towering wreath of steel.
He didn’t bother tearing through the palace. There was no victory to flaunt- he simply
allowed the Nav to take him directly to his destination. The stairs that appeared around the
great tree at the centre of Eden were accompanied only by a soft sigh.

Akechi hadn’t bothered with words. Maruki hadn’t, either, he had simply given Akechi a
mournful look, dripping with pity, and the fight had ended quickly.
The fight was quick. The end of Akechi’s life was not. Perhaps Maruki was too much of a
coward to finish the job, peace-loving as he is, or perhaps he had some delusion that
anything that happened to Akechi from then on didn’t matter, since he would just be dragged
back to the realm of the living on strings come the fourth anyway.
But, until then, he had been left to draw rasping breaths, wet with blood, vision swirling and
dimming, velvet blue at the edges; whether from the blood loss or the fracturing of reality he
couldn’t say.
But the finality of that last memory doesn’t matter.
The Justice, as soon as it twists in knots to form a blood oath, tilts on its side.
And Akechi is left in an empty room, a door shimmering into place where there was none
before, grappling with a sudden clarity, two instances of the Justice bound and braided into
one.
There’s nothing he can do but tilt his head back and laugh.
What a cosmic joke, to become the punchline of.

Sumire feels her knees scrape painfully against the top floor of Mementos, the speed at which
the teleportation occurs not allowing for the time to catch herself. No one else fares any
better- landing at odd angles and on sharp protrusions that Sumire winces at in sympathy.
But despite the rough landing, they’re here. And, very much still alive.
Sumire puffs out her cheeks and blows out a long, relieved, breath.
She nearly jumps as Noir pats her shoulder, smile looking almost giddy.
“That was exciting!” Noir says with a giggle, “I was so worried for a minute, there.”
“Me too.” Sumire confesses, breathless, “That was… a lot.”
The thieves around them clamber to their feet, rubbing at aching sides and necks. There’s a
tense silence that blankets the group now that the imminent danger has passed- and yet,
Sumire realises with some relief, it doesn’t seem actively hostile.
Queen straightens up, her shoulders stiff and her fists clenching and unclenching. She looks
to be unsure how to proceed, and Sumire is thankful at least that she isn’t immediately launch
back into a fight. Oracle stands a ways back, and looks to be just avoiding eye contact, rather
than egging on the potential fight.
So, an improvement.

“Your plan worked wonderfully, Niijima-san.” Noir says with a tentative smile, and Sumire
hastens to nod eagerly, “I think we made it out because of you.”

times, before she untenses slightly. “You can call me Queen. While we’re in the Metaverse.”

each other codenames too, yeah?”
“Oh, yes!” Sumire brightens, “I’m Violet, and Haru-senpai goes by Noir.”
“I… take that you already know all our codenames?” Queen asks, and some of the tension
returns.
Skull groans, “Are we just gonna talk in circles again?”

into another fight...”
“We really don’t want to fight you guys!” Sumire quickly adds, even though she’s fairly
certain that she’s tried to make that point at least three times.
Queen sighs slightly, “I… agree. I acted…” She trails off, looking embarrassed, “Oracle?
What do you think?”
Oracle still avoids looking at anyone directly, and she shrugs, “Whatever. I don’t care.” She
mumbles.

make our way to Leblanc.”
Skull makes a face, “Are you sayin’ we could’ve avoided all that-”
Panther thwacks him on the arm, “Not now.” She mutters.
And that seems to be the end of that. No one makes any complaints as everyone moves to
huddle in together as Queen takes out her phone and activates the Nav. The red hues of
Mementos melt away into the bright and overexposed lights of the Shibuya subway station.
Thankfully, no one looks their way as a crowd of teenagers stumble to regain their balance.
Immediately, half the thieves’ eyes lock onto Sumire and Haru, more curious than aggressive,
and Sumire wonders if they’re surprised that they haven’t tried to run.
Sumire smiles sheepishly to try and assuage what she assumes are their fears, and jumps
slightly as Makoto lets out a frustrated huff.
“That’s odd.” She says, glaring at her phone, “I… can’t get through to Ren or Akechi-kun.”

“Huh?” Ann exclaims, looking alarmed.

she sees a slew of missed calls and a message in the group chat warning her and Haru to
avoid Mementos today.
Well. A bit late.
She presses her lips together and starts the call.
The number you are trying to reach is…
Sumire frowns, “I… can’t reach them either.”

Around the loaf of cat in her arms, Futaba starts rapidly typing at her phone, “I don’t think

The train ride is- well, the train ride is mostly fine. Sumire thinks it might be because there’s

Ren would like some time.
He’d like all the time in the world- a precious resource which he doesn’t have. He’d like
time, to process the two years in his head, twisting and overlapping so much that he can’t tell
what happened when. Conflicting thoughts and emotions all bubble and react, spitting fire
when they touch, and RenHe’s in Maruki’s palace. He knows he’s in Maruki’s palace, because it’s October third, and
October third has always meant this discovery.
This reflection ought to be saved for later. Arsène advises, and sets off another tangent- shit,
Arsène knew, didn’t he? This whole time and not a single wordTo say I knew would not be entirely accurate, comes the protest, You knew, deep down, that
something was wrong, and yet neither of us could say what it was.
Ah, but now.
Now.
Now, Ren needs toHe needs to find Kasumi- No, he needs to find Akechi- Goro?
“It’s October third.” Ren says aloud, to the empty air, hauling himself to his feet and
staggering as he tries to move, “The thieves went into Mementos. We got here because the
Nav picked up our conversation. K-Akechi is in here somewhere and I need to find him.”
He continues muttering what he hopes is true to himself like a mantra, as he braces himself
against the wall and begins dragging his feet.
The Justice shudders, and Ren grasps it like a lifeline. It’s caught somewhere Ren can’t place,
but it’s the only bond that doesn’t give him a headache to think about.

With the Justice as a tether, Ren starts pushing forward.
Steady, Metatron’s voice chimes, and oh, wonderful, he’s here too, You aren’t far.

Black and blue, stripes, belts, and red, and- Ren already knew this, this isn’t a surprise; it

Deflect. “Goro- Goro, we can do this later-”

Try again. “Akechi- We have to go-”

With a shriek, and a display of strength Ren isn’t prepared for or capable of countering,
Akechi lunges, and bashes Ren in the solar plexus, immediately knocking all the air from his
lungs.
Ren stumbles back, choking on a breath, and Akechi leaps forward and pins Ren to the
ground with his entire weight, eyes blown wide and furious. He moves faster than Ren can
think of something, anything, to say, and he can’t breathe as Akechi presses his serrated
sword against Ren’s throat with a low sound, something between a growl and a chuckle, and
Ren knows he’s lostBut then Akechi hesitates.
Ren doesn’t move to struggle, the edge of the sword tapping against his throat as he breathes
heavily. Akechi’s body is all sharp lines and hard angles, drawn tense like a spring, and it
would be so easy for him to slit Ren’s throat in one fluid movement, and yetAkechi’s eyes are still a pulsing red, swimming in the artificial psychosis, and Ren doesn’t
think he’s all there, butVery slowly, he reaches for the hand that Akechi’s using to grip at his sword, fist clenched so
tightly that Ren thinks it might break. He tentatively, lightly, brushes his fingers over
Akechi’s, and grimaces, when the words he tries to say come out as an unintelligible rasp.
I’m sorry, he wants to say, I can fix this, I can fix this, I’m sorry, IBut choking on blood and air doesn’t equate to meaning, and Ren doesn’t say a thing.
Goro’s glare doesn’t abate, nor does the red in his eyes, but something passes over his
expression, and Ren tries to give a small smile.
Too fast to react to, Goro lets out a scream of frustration, removing the blade from Ren’s neck
and slamming it into the ground, cracking the tile, wrenching it away faster than Ren can
gasp, and then he’s gone.
And Ren is left, alone, in the heavenly, clinical, white of Maruki’s palace, now marred with
blood and fury, still struggling to breathe.

Ren is having a bad day.
An understatement, really. But, what he’s feeling ultimately boils down to that.
He thought a good night’s rest would help. It has not.
Morgana took one look at him in the morning and decided to room in Ann’s desk instead,

Ren feels as though there was a seal placed over some part of his brain, that kept all his

Now,

Time, as it turns out, does not heal all wounds.
Or, at the very least, a single day does not heal all wounds.

What time has done, is allow for Robin Hood and Loki to breach the surface of the

He’s not going to school, either; it would provide as much of a distraction as it would irritate
him, and he isn’t willing to roll the dice. He’s called in sick from work, too – they hardly
need him there right now, and frankly the precinct contains more reminders than potential to
stop thinking.
But Akechi has to do something, otherwise he’s going to break his own arm.
He’s in Mementos before he can even fully comprehend where he’s headed.
Well then. Violence is certainly a distraction.
Akechi strides down the station steps, fully intending on wreaking as much havoc as he
feasibly can before he collapses, before a glint in the corner of his eye pulls at his attention.
The cool blue glow of the courtroom door is shaded by two figures, rather than just one.
Akechi frowns.
