Chapter Summary

Seeking advice, seeking information, and calling cards.

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

After throwing on the first clothes he can find, begging Morgana to spend time with Futaba,
and calling Ann to meet him in Shibuya, Ren steels himself.
“Hey!” Ann sings, as she waves with her entire shoulder when she spots Ren. She’s already
standing in line for the crêpe store on Central street, and Ren grimaces a half-hearted apology
to the person behind her as he cuts in line at her side.
“Hey.” He huffs in response.
“Soooo,” She drawls, and lowers her voice, “What’s up? We’re going to the palace today,
yeah?”
“Yeah.” Ren confirms, “Hopefully we can secure the route today. Morgana thinks we can.”
Ann puffs out her cheeks, “Jeez, I hope so. Every second we’re not in the palace, I get this
really guilty feeling like we should be making progress at all times.” She idly scans the menu,
like she hasn’t got it memorised, “Like procrastinating for a school assignment, y’know?”
Ren snorts, “Sure.” He rubs the back of his neck, “But, uh, that wasn’t what I wanted to talk
about.”
Ann raises her eyebrows, “Oh?” She says, in her spill the tea voice.
“I wanted to ask about-” Ren coughs around the sudden lump in his throat, “I- have you
ever-?”
Ann raises an eyebrow, “Have I ever what?”
Ren wonders if he should have asked someone else for help. “I need your advice.” He settles
on.
Ann’s eyes widen with curious excitement, “Ooooh, what about?”
“Akechi.” Ren bites at his lip.
Ann blinks, “Oh… oh!” She shakes Ren’s shoulder.

“What?” He splutters.
Ann laughs, “God, I am so glad you came to me. Watching you two was torture.”
“Does this mean you have a perfect solution at the ready for me?” Ren asks, perhaps a little
too hopeful.
Ann tugs at her hair, “Um… Maybe?”
Ren feels that fleeting hope shrivel and die with a pathetic little puff, “…What do you have?”
Ann laughs awkwardly, ducking her head down, “Ren, I’m gonna be honest, I’ve never dated
anyone before.”
Ren blinks. “Neither have I.”
“Wait, what?” Ann whirls around to give him a look, “But- I thought- Akechi?”
Ren tugs on his fringe, kind of wishing the floor would swallow him, “We weren’t dating, we
were just…” something. Like he knows.
Ann blinks away some of her blatant bewilderment, opening her mouth to respond before
flinching as the server calls for her to order. She quickly mumbles out an order, Ren doing the
same, and they shuffle to the side to wait.
“You seriously weren’t dating?” Ann eventually finds her words again.
“Nope.” Ren says with a pop, rocking on his heels, “I honestly don’t know where you got
that idea from.”
“Well- I thought-! Even before all the time travel stuff, I thought there was something going
on with you guys!” Ann stumbles over her words in a rush.
“Oh.” Ren says, intelligently.
“And then after we figured out- everything,” She continues, waving a hand, “Like- Ren, you
ended the world for him.”
“Yeah.”
“That’s intense.”
“Yeah.” Ren agrees.
“And the way the two of you act- I dunno, Ren!” Ann groans, “Can you blame me?”
Ren, despite his embarrassment, feels a grin pulling at his lips, “I think you figured it out
before I did, Ann.”
Ann snorts, “Wow, you’re really bad at this.” She tilts her head, “…Like are you sure you
weren’t in, like, some weird undefined thing where you didn’t call it dating but you kind of

were?”
Ren opens his mouth, closes it. “…Maybe?”
Ann’s eyes glimmer with interest, “Did you kiss?”
Ren wishes. “No.”
Ann blows a raspberry, “Well, shows what I know.” She sighs, “What do you need my help
for, anyway?”
Ren shrugs, “You’re good with people.”
Ann looks mildly taken aback, “Oh.” She looks down, and bites at her lip, a hint of a smile at
the edges, “Thanks.”
Ren rubs the back of his neck, feeling the embarrassment creeping back in, “No problem.”
Ann perks back up, “Well, in that case! Let’s talk it out! What are you trying to do?”
Perform a miracle. “…Try and patch things up with me and Akechi, mostly.” Ren admits, and
laughs weakly, “I- I know I messed up, I just don’t know how to…”
Ann nods brightly, looking entirely too cheerful against Ren’s worsening mood, “Okay…
have you tried talking to him at all?”
“Once.” Ren counts. He tilts his head, “Three times, if you count when I took him aside in
Okumura’s palace. And if you count when he nearly killed me.”
“Okay…” Ann says, the word sounding far more exasperated this time, “…Have you thought
about… I dunno, trying to be a little more proactive…?”
A huffed laugh escapes Ren’s lips, “I’m asking you for help, aren’t I? And yes,” He quickly
adds, at Ann’s unimpressed look, “I do want to talk to him. I am going to talk to him. I just- I
don’t know why I had it in my head that you were some master of- romance?”
Ann snickers, “You sound so unsure that that’s the word you’re looking for.” She teases.
“Well…” Ren grimaces, “It’s not- stuff like that wasn’t really… us, I guess. It didn’t have to
be. Not explicitly, at least.”
Ann’s grin softens into a smaller smile, “…That’s kind of sweet, you know?”
“Thanks?”
“I mean it.” She elbows him, “I can tell how much you care.”
Ren shrugs, “Yeah.” He swallows, “I just don’t know how to…”
“Make it so Akechi knows it?” Ann guesses.

Ren shakes his head, directing his stare at the ground, “No. I don’t know how to promise to
him that how much I care isn’t going to turn him into another puppet.”
Ann’s lips part in a little ‘o’, “…Right.” She looks away, and frowns, “…I don’t really know,
Ren.”
Ren laughs a little, “That’s fine. It makes two of us.”
Ann looks towards the counter, shuffling her feet as she continues to wait. She nudges him,
“Just talk to him.”
Ren huffs a laugh. “I will.”
***
Even despite his new resolve, Ren knows that Rome wasn’t built in a day.
It also doesn’t help when Rome in this context is actively fighting against his attempts at
construction (which Ren supposes is fair- he is the one who burnt Rome down in the first
place), and is making life all around more difficult for everyone involved.
This to say, that Ren knows his best smile isn’t going to sway Akechi to play along now that
they’ll be entering a part of the palace where they have to work together.
However, his smile has historically worked on people who aren’t Akechi, so he’ll try his luck
elsewhere.
It takes two rings for Sumire to pick up, as Ren calls her not long after he finishes his crêpe
with Ann.
“Ren-senpai?” Sumire’s voice crackles through the speaker, “Is something the matter? We’re
still meeting up at the palace later, right?”
“Yeah, no, that’s all fine.” Ren instinctually shakes his head. “I… had a favour to ask?”
There’s a pause, and Sumire giggles slightly, “Aren’t you the one who’s supposed to owe
me?”
Ren wonders if Sumire is going to hold that over him for far longer than he initially assumed,
“Can I start a tab?”
There’s a proper laugh at that, “Sure, Senpai. Um, what did you need?”
“So…” Ren takes a breath, “I was thinking- you know how we can’t really split up,
anymore?”
“In the palace?”
“Yeah.” Ren confirms, “So, we’re all going to have to work together, and- I’m wondering
how to phrase this.” He admits.

Sumire hums, “I… assume you’re asking if I can try and get Goro to be less of a loose
cannon?” She asks with a fair amount of humour.
Ren huffs a laugh, “Yeah, pretty much. Think it’s possible?”
A sigh, “Maybe…? I mean- I can’t control him.”
“I wouldn’t want you to.” Ren reassures her.
“I know. it’s- he’s not being difficult on purpose.” She pauses. “Well. He is, but-”
“It’s because of me.” Ren finishes, keeping his voice blank, “I get it.”
Sumire sighs softly, “I think it’s more… being near you stresses him out?”
It’s not a good thing to hear. Especially not from Sumire, when Ren knows Akechi never
would have phrased it that way himself. “…Should I hide in the shadows?” Ren suggests,
only half-joking.
Sumire laughs, “I think he’d be able to sense you. But, no, I think Haru-senpai and I can…
step in, I guess, if people start fighting.” Another pause, “Um… sorry, by the way, for not
really helping during our first infiltration. …And I didn’t really follow your orders either.”
“No, no, it’s okay.” Ren shakes his head to the empty air, “I know that you and Haru probably
see Akechi as more of a leader than me, so…”
There’s a laugh, “I honestly didn’t even realise that’s what was happening- Goro was our
navigator, but the only time he ever gave out orders was mostly when Haru-senpai was still
learning the ropes.”
“Huh…” Ren tilts his head in contemplation. Oh, to be a fly on the wall. “Anyway, um,
thanks for agreeing to help out. Hopefully this won’t be for too long. …I’m planning on…
trying to fix things, soon.”
“Really?” Sumire blurts, “That’s great! Uh- good luck?”
Ren laughs self-deprecatingly, “You sound so confident.”
“Well, you know.” Sumire says sheepishly.
Ren does know, unfortunately.
***
To what Ren would like to credit as his good leadership, nothing breaks immediately.
Would like to, being the operative part of that thought- Ren doesn’t bother splitting up the
team into ‘frontlines and backup’ for this part of the infiltration, the corridors are too linear to
warrant it. The presence of Sumire and Haru directly at his side seems to do wonders for
Akechi’s instinct to act out. Ren decides not to poke the bear by commenting on it.

“I really think we’re getting close…” Futaba hums from above, “But I think we’re coming up
on something funky, too.”
“Like what?” Makoto looks in the general direction of Necronomicon.
“Like… just a big room, I guess?” Futaba says, not sounding entirely confident, “But not
really. It’s pretty narrow.”
“We’ve had weird-ass museums, falling-apart factories, boring hallways…” Ryuji lists, “Any
guesses?”
Haru frowns, and tilts her head in contemplation, “I suppose it’s hard to tell… I don’t exactly
have much of a frame of reference, but this palace seems like it’s been in disarray.”
“You’d be right.” Akechi speaks up. “In comparison to before, even more so. I’d wager that
Okumura’s sense of grandeur is much more fragile than he lets on- trying to rebuild it in his
head after it’s been shaken must be an ordeal.”
“Right…” Ren hums to himself.
He’d love if exploring this palace didn’t feel like a ticking time bomb. He’d take the actual
time bomb they were greeted with last time over the one walking among their ranks.
His resolve from his dream the night before, coupled with looks from Ann he catches in the
corner of his eye, has not faded. This is his problem, his mistake, he will fix this,
But, now? In the middle of a palace infiltration? While they’re walking around? Not the best
place to start an argument, Ren thinks.
Where is the best place?
Infuriatingly, opinionated as he tends to be, Metatron seems to hold no answer. Maybe he just
likes watching Ren squirm.
“Oh!” Futaba’s exclamation interrupts Ren’s self-pity, “Brace yourselves, guys!”
Ren holds out an arm to signal the group to stop, pressing himself against the shadow of the
wall, peeking his head around the corner. The room really isn’t that different in size and
shape than the hallway that precedes it. There’s a window along one wall that overlooks the
stacked factory ports within the larger space station, and Ren thinks he catches a glimpse of
the museum, tucked away in a distant corner, surrounded by shards of debris and haphazard
scaffolding.
But, the most pressing difference in this room isShadow Okumura whirls around with a furious glare, “What are you doing here?!” He barks,
“Guards, how could you let this happen? Do you forget the task you’ve been given?”
Two shadows melt into existence at his side, but say nothing.

Ren tilts his head.
Behind him, Yusuke hums, and whispers, “Does he seem nervous, to you?”
“Yes.” Haru responds immediately. She grips her axe tightly, “What should we do? This is
the only path forward.”
Ren considers his options.
From memory, Okumura himself -his shadow, that is- is a pushover. If they engage, he’d
likely flee, and they’d only be faced with the problem of taking down his guards. But, Ren
isn’t sure he wants to know the consequences if they provoke him too much. Usually, all of
the thieves’ early encounters with palace rulers are punctuated by an awakening to scare them
off before they can really fight.
They’re so close to securing the route. Ren doesn’t want to push it back another day.
The best place to start an argument isNot now, obviously, butBuild the first layer, Ren thinks.
“Hey, Crow.” Ren says, unplastering himself from the shadow of the wall, “You’re up.”
Akechi tilts his head, “Hm?” He hums, not sounding like he’s really questioning anything at
all. He stalks forward, and sings, “Oh, Okumura-san.”
Okumura’s shadow, who had at this point been narrowing his eyes suspiciously down the
partly shaded hall, narrows his eyes in anger, “You?! Black Mask- how did you get here?”
“It wasn’t particularly difficult, you know.” Akechi drawls flatly. Behind his back, he makes
a gesture that Ren interprets as get over here.
Ren signals for the rest of the group to move forward, and stops them a pace behind Akechi.
The shadow shrinks back as they rest of them come into full view.
“Phantom Thieves…” The shadow seethes.
“Oh, you can tell?” Ryuji perks up with a mocking grin.
“Who else would be scurrying around in my domain like rats?” Okumura’s shadow spits.
“Useless! Every last person in this damn station.”
Haru sighs quietly, and steps forward to stand at Akechi’s side, “You should stand down,
father.” She advises, “Let us through, please.”
The shadow’s face twists, “Haru? You’re back again…” He scoffs, “But no, I should hardly
be surprised. I should have realised you were against me the moment you set foot in here with
these thieves.”

Haru huffs quietly, looking to be steeling her resolve, “That’s not… Father, we are here to
take your treasure, but-”
“You admit it!” Okumura’s shadow declares with grim triumph, “To think my enemies could
buy even you- I thought I taught you loyalty better than this?” He narrows his eyes at Akechi,
“Or perhaps you were offered something. Was Sugimura not to your liking?”
Both Haru and Akechi’s lips curl with disgust at the implication presented. At Ren’s side, he
sees Sumire take a step forward, ready to intervene, the rest of the thieves tensing or scoffing
behind him.
“I believe that’s enough insinuations.” Akechi spits, “Would you like to bring this to a fight
so soon? Your options are rather limited.”
The shadow sniffs, “Hardly. Why would I let you pass, when I could cut you down here?”
“You?” Akechi asks, “Or your pitiful guards?”
“Ren.” Makoto whispers, as the exchange goes around, “I’m all for getting this over with, but
shouldn’t we use this opportunity?”
“What do you mean?” Sumire cuts in, turning her head slightly.
“The museum implied Okumura has… some interest in cognitive psience.” Makoto explains,
“Shouldn't we determine the extent of that?”
Ren turns to refocus on the back on forth in front of him. Haru hasn’t spoken up again, but
Akechi has taken to lightly goading Okumura by rebutting all his words- not to the point of
violence, just stalling.
Whenever you’re ready, Is the underlying taunt Ren hears, and he gives Makoto a nod. “Take
a shot.”
“Okumura-san.” Makoto takes a step forward, voice just a bit too snide to truly be respectful.
Thankfully though, shadows, and especially Okumura’s, are uniquely terrible at picking up
on sarcasm, “I apologise for my companions. There seems to have been a misunderstanding.”
Okumura’s shadow looks her up and down derisively, “What misunderstanding? My
treacherous daughter is running around with assassins and has just admitted to targeting my
greatest possession.”
Makoto falters for a beat, before regaining some of her composure, “That… is exactly where
the misunderstanding lies. We meant theft in a more… metaphorical sense.”
“Dude, is this gonna work?” Ryuji mutters behind them.
Ren barely tilts his head, “Even if it doesn’t,” He whispers, “We were probably going to have
to fight anyway.”
Ryuji shrugs to concede, and all eyes are back on Makoto.

“Metaphorical, you say?” The shadow drawls, clearly not believing her one bit.
“Y-yes.” Makoto says quickly, “We wish to… admire the majesty of your empire. In fact, we
passed through the museum on our way here. You outlined your goals for the future.” She
smiles as she regains more of her rhythm, “Would you care to elaborate on that?”
“Ah,” Okumura’s shadow grins, distracted enough by the praise to miss the leap in logic,
“You’ve seen the history of my legacy? Where my daughter,” He shoots Haru another look,
“Should be working.”
“Yes.” Makoto grimaces, as Haru’s expression hardens, “Of course. That place.”
“I don’t expect you to understand my goals for the future.” Okumura continues, “My enemy
may consider himself the one true expert of the subject, but anyone as educated as those
among our number can grasp the topic.”
Ren hears Futaba scoff lightly from above. He narrows his eyes as he sees Akechi pointedly
directing his gaze down at the floor.
“Please, tell me if you can.” Makoto pushes, “Um- I’m sure your daughter would be
interested too-?”
“I can hardly reveal my plans, little girl, to my enemies.” The shadow cuts her off, “Do you
forget who is among your number?” Akechi looks up with a grimace, “No. This has been
pointless.” He waves a hand, “Guards, deal with them how you please. The rest of you ought
to scurry away like the rats you are, if you know what’s good for you.”
Okumura strides away, further down the hall and past the door. The shadows’ forms bubble
as he leaves, splitting into a veritable menagerie- spinning stars and demons and golden-clad
bipedal elephants, and Ren sighs.
Nothing gained, then.
“It was going to happen eventually.” Ren reassures the negotiators that took a crack, spinning
his dagger.
“Yeah…” Morgana sighs as he gets into formation with the rest of the thieves, “Look alive
guys! This should be easy. I don’t know why Okumura thought this would stop us.”
“The price of arrogance.” Haru hums quietly, hauling her axe over her shoulder.
***
The fight is, in fact, quite easy. The only issue Ren encounters is not being able to give orders
to eight people at once, and in a rather narrow hallway at that. This turns out to not be much
of a problem, really, as each of them has more than enough battle instinct to sustain
themselves- though there is the occasional bit of friendly fire in the limited space.
“Well…” Futaba sighs from above, Necronomicon also looking cramped, “Too bad you
didn’t get anything outta that, I guess.”

“You tried, though!” Ann offers, “And we can just try again later, right? We’ll see him after
we send the calling card.”
Makoto sighs, “That’s true. And it’s not like he’ll be able to do much about anything
nefarious he might be planning after we change his heart, anyway.”
“Having the information would be good, though.” Haru points out, “The… ambiguity of this
place is putting me on edge.”
“Me too.” Futaba agrees, “Plus, even if Okumura knows jack shit, there could be other stuff
he’s got.”
Akechi tilts his head, and Ren assumes he has an eyebrow raised, “Like what?”
“My mom’s research.” Futaba says, a bit curt, “I wanna find it.”
“Ah.” Akechi blinks slowly, “I see.”
“…Uhh, anyways…” Ryuji drawls out, clearly picking up on some of the awkward mood
seeping in, “So, Mona, Oracle, the treasure as close as we thought?”
“Oh, yeah.” Morgana nods, “I can smell it- it’s really close.”
“I can’t sense Okumura’s shadow, though.” Futaba interjects, “He must’ve cut and run pretty
quick.”
“Hopefully that will be indicative of the strength of his final stand, as well.” Yusuke hums,
“It would be nice for our post-calling card infiltration to run smoothly, for once.”
Ren barks a sudden laugh, remembering waves upon waves of cognitive workers at
Okumura’s disposal, “I wouldn’t get your hopes up.”
Sumire gives a small smile, “Well, there’s ten of us, so hopefully it won’t be so bad.”
Ren certainly hopes so, too. He shrugs noncommittally in response, and signals for the rest of
the group to follow him as he walks forward.
The treasure room is far grander than it had been, even last time.
Its edges are incongruent, blending from an auditorium to another production line to falling
apart entirely, not even a pane of glass that separates them from the expanse of space.
Sumire gapes in awe, “I guess…” She swallows audibly, “I guess we didn’t have to worry
about oxygen? Or… physics.”
“Ugh!” Futaba complains, “Would’ve been great to know earlier!”
“No kidding…” Morgana mumbles, “We were tiptoeing around the palace like it would
break, earlier.”

“Look.” Akechi interrupts them, “I believe we can consider our route secured.”
He gestures to the shimmering light suspended in the centre of the room, shifting and
unformed.
“When are we sending the calling card?” Sumire asks.
Ren bites at his lip as he considers it, “…I want to do it as soon as possible. Fox, is it possible
to make something quickly right now?”
“That should be possible.” Yusuke frowns, “But, it will hardly be to the standard I-”
“That’s fine.” Ren quickly waves a dismissive hand, “Noir, do you think you could hand it to
him tonight?"
Haru blinks, “You’d like to get it all done tomorrow?”
“Yes.” Ren nods firmly, “The sooner the better, and if we can get it done sooner, then we
should.”
“I suppose that’s true.” Haru nods, “I’m sure I can get it done. If I say that I found it in the
mailbox, then it won’t matter that my fingerprints are on it, no?”
“My own can hardly be transferred through these,” Yusuke gestures to his gloved hands,
“Assuming I complete this project within a nearby safe room?”
“Of course.” Ren nods. He takes a deep breath. Shit, he hasn’t completed a palace infiltration
in months. “Let’s get it done.”
***
Haru steels herself before entering her apartment.
She had made a whole show of finding something in the mailbox for whatever cameras may
have been stationed around. She isn’t entirely confident in her sleight of hand, but it should
be good enough.
“Father,” She says as she enters the living room, trying to twist the nervousness in her voice
to something that could read as worry. There are servants milling about cleaning- good. More
eyewitnesses. "Father- I’ve found something, you have to see this.”
“Can’t you see I’m busy, Haru?” Her father snaps, not looking particularly busy at all.
“I found this in our mailbox.” She continues, and drops the calling card onto the coffee table,
“It’s- it’s addressed to you.”
In the corner of her eye, she sees the servants immediately break out into quiet gossip, the red
and black distinct of a Phantom Thieves’ calling card clearly visible even from several paces
away.

Her father’s eyes widen in shock and anger as he snatches the card from the table. “Sir
Kunikazu Okumura, profiteering sinner of greed…” He mutters. He stands abruptly with a
low growl, “This is outrageous! How dare-?” He cuts himself off with a scoff.
Haru decides to push her luck, and put on a show, “Father, I saw- it’s from the Phantom
Thieves, isn’t it?”
The whispering in the corner of the room gets louder as Haru loudly confirms their
suspicions. Her father narrows his eyes.
“Apparently so.” He spits. “I have to- No, the police are in his pocket…” He grits his teeth,
“Damnit!”
“Father-?” Haru starts as he starts pacing.
“It’s fine, Haru!” Her father shouts, “I’m going to fix this. This is probably his- Nothing is
going to happen to me, I-” He glares at the servants gossiping in the corner, “What are you
doing? Do something, would you!”
As her father’s ire is directed at anything that breathes, Haru takes this as her cue to leave.
She quietly pads up the stairs, closing her door with a small click and collapsing back on her
bed.
She frowns, and sits back up as she hears scratching at the sliding door to her balcony.
“Haru!” Morgana’s voice filters through the glass, “Hey, can you let me in?”
Haru blinks.
“It’s cold!” Morgana adds.
That spurs Haru into action, as she quickly stands and jogs over to the sliding door,
unlatching it and pulling it open. Morgana pads inside with an overdramatic relieved sigh,
stretching out his back and dragging his claws against the carpet.
“Oh, sorry.” He quickly sits with a bit more decorum as Haru’s concern for her carpet must
show on her face.
“What are you doing here, Morgana?” She asks softly, as she scoops the cat up in her arms
and walks back over to the bed to give them both a seat.
Morgana goes along with the manhandling with minimal protest, gratefully stretching out as
he jumps from her arms onto the bed.
“Ren sent me.” He explains, “He wanted me to make sure you were doing okay.”
Haru smiles, “Oh, well that’s very sweet.” She shakes her head, “But I’m alright, don’t
worry.”

Morgana flicks his tail, “…Are you sure?”
Haru sighs, “I was a little stressed before, I think.” She admits, “But it’s over with now, so
I’m okay.”
“That’s good.” Morgana says with a bit of triumph, “Are you ready for the fight, tomorrow?”
Haru nods firmly, “As I’ll ever be.” She deflates a little, “I must admit, it feels awfully…
anticlimactic.”
Morgana frowns, “Oh?”
“Yes.” Haru laughs slightly, “I suppose I got a lot of my- everything out of my system when
we changed Sugimura’s heart. And now…”
And now,
Perhaps she’s lying, a bit, when she says it doesn’t feel climactic. It certainly doesn’t feel the
way it did when she faced Sugimura along with Goro and Sumire, with Milady at her back
rather than Astarte.
Maybe that’s the difference, then. The change in resolve. Though, that doesn’t feel quite right
as she thinks it, either. The circumstances are just too different. The way she feels about her
father is markedly different from the way she feels about her ex-fiancé, one wreathed only in
disdain and the other soaked through with old sentiments and dying hopes of what could have
been.
Sometimes, she wishes she could just hate her father and move on. Part of her still feels like
she owes him not to, though; a thought that Goro would probably raise his eyebrow at, she
thinks with a bit of humour.
“I suppose it’s just… going through the motions.” Haru concludes with a small sigh and a
weary smile, “We’re changing his heart because we have to, but we probably would have
anyway. I think I would have wanted to, anyway.”
“I guess I know what you mean.” Morgana agrees, “All of this is just so…” He huffs,
“Weird.”
Haru laughs, “It is, yes. You’ve had less time to adjust to it than me, though.”
“What, with the time travel stuff? That’s true.” Morgana concedes. “It feels wrong having a
change of heart just be… a stepping stone.” He sighs, “But, no choice, so.”
“Right…” Haru frowns, “We’ll get used to it.”
“We have to.” Morgana agrees, “But I don’t think we should get too cocky, either. I don’t
know if it’s just the fact that we have a plan, but I get this nagging feeling that things aren’t
going to happen the way we want.”

Haru breathes another laugh, “No, I feel it too. But there really isn’t much we can do, other
than this.”
Paranoia, she hopes.
Morgana groans, “Yeah, yeah.” His ears perk up, “Speaking of, though, I forgot to ask, did
everything go fine with the calling card?”
Haru quickly nods, “It did. My father saw it, and I don’t think he suspected me of anything. I
made sure to give it to him while some of the servants were in the room, too. I suspect there
will be a lot of paparazzi propositioning our workers, once the news breaks.”
“Oh ho!” Morgana’s chops peel back in a grin, “Clever, Miss Haru!”
Haru giggles, “Well thank you, Mona-chan.”
“Mona-chan, huh?”
Haru quickly waves her hands, “Oh, I’m sorry! Do you not like the nickname?”
Morgana shakes his head, “No, it’s- you call your friends names like that, right?”
Haru nods, “I do it with Sumi-chan, at least.”
“Then I like it.” Morgana declares, “I know we kind of got off on the wrong foot thanks toeverything. But, I’d like to be your friend, Haru.”
Haru’s smile widens, “I’d like that too, Mona-chan.” She giggles slightly, “Shall we shake on
it?”
Morgana immediately offers his paw, which Haru takes in a small shake. She tries to tamp
down her smile at shaking hands with a cat; a rather magical experience, in her opinion.
Morgana puffs out his chest as he retracts his paw, and then curls up into a loaf on her bed,
“Well, I’m staying here tonight. Ren will live. And it’s too cold to go back.”
Haru covers her laughter behind her hand, “That sounds good, then.”
***
As Akechi settles down for the evening, he catches himself staring expectantly at his phone,
waiting for it to ring.
It doesn’t.
Last time, Shido was the one to inform him that Okumura had reported a calling card
addressed to him, with the accompanying message of deal with it quickly. That had been fine
by Akechi- he had been keeping an eye on the thieves’ infiltrations, of course, but he couldn’t
have known exactly when the thieves would send the calling card after they secured the
route.

But, a thread of logic warns, Okumura has paranoia twisting his logic far enough around that
he may have ended up with some common sense. This time, he has no good reason to report a
calling card, when he suspects enemies in every shadow.
Akechi supposes that means he’ll have to break the news.
Shido picks up on the third ring.
“Yes?” He demands, curt as ever.
Akechi catches his sigh before it escapes his lips, “Some good news, sir.”
“Oh?” Shido asks, interest apparent, “And what might that be?”
“Okumura’s thief problem seems to have reached its end.” Akechi explains, as vague as he
dares over the phone, “It should come to a head tomorrow, I’d wager.”
“Why hasn’t he come to me about this?” Shido questions, as though Akechi would
reasonably have the answer to that.
Conveniently, he does have the answer. “Perhaps he doesn’t trust in your services.” Akechi
suggests blandly, “Either way, I’m certain in my timeline. Our, ah, pests, are quite loud with
their intentions.”
Shido chuckles, sounding pleased, “If you say so. If they really are so loud, I’m surprised you
didn’t find them sooner.”
Akechi grits his teeth, “Loud, only in places where they expect to be alone.” He lies.
“If you say so.” Shido drawls out, “Anyway, I’m sure you know what to do?”
“Of course.” Akechi agrees easily, “No changes in plan?”
“None.”
“Good to hear.” Akechi hums. He swallows, “I won’t let you down.”
“You’d better not.”
The line goes dead.
Well, Akechi thinks, time to put on a show.

Chapter 62
Chapter Summary

Desperate times and desperate measures.

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

It’s been quite some time since Ren has been in a palace in this state.
The oppressive red, the distant blaring alarms, the shadows in panic and disarray. It’s almost
nostalgic, he thinks; though that may be a bit much. It’s only been a few months, after all,
since they sent the calling card for Futaba.
The treasure room itself, however, holds no such feelings. Ren almost grimaces at how

There are myriad reasons why Akechi doesn’t want to be here.
He’s not entirely put back together, he thinks. Still scattered about in cracks and debris,
clawing himself forward and trying to see if the jagged edges still fit.
The buzzing static and complete inability to think hasn’t persisted for very long, this time. A
blessing and a curse, Akechi supposes, as it turns out that Robin and Loki are never truly
silent during these episodes, he just can’t hear them.
Akechi pinches the bridge of his nose, and takes a deep breath.
This is your fault.
MINE? WOULD YOU RATHER WE BE A COLLECTION OF LIMBS IN THE
VACCUM OF SPACE?
Hardly! But it is your incessant effects on his mind thatI AM THOU AND THOU ART I! HIS MIND IS HIS OWN! THERE’S NOTHING
WRONG WITHDriving himself mad?
“I’m right here, you know.” Akechi grits quietly, feeling the sentiment ought to be expressed
aloud on the off chance it will make his personas shut up.
On his worst days, he has been inclined to blame them for all his misfortune. On his- best is
pushing it, but on the days he doesn’t entirely hate existing, he would be inclined to consider
them far more favourably.
He always remembers what they are. I am thou, thou art I. His choices and actions are his
alone, and having two halves of his head arguing about it is doing wonders about driving him
more permanently insane.
He doesn’t want to go to the school festival. Haru said she wants to talk, however, and, well.

He wonders, if the Haru of last timeline had attempted to strongarm him into a conversation
about her various grievances, if he would have complied. The uncertainty almost makes him
laugh, for how he is entirely unable to say no to her now.
The journey to Shujin takes longer than it feels it should. He wasn’t lying about his headache,
while on the phone to Sumire and Haru; mustering up the poise to smile and wave at the
students that point and whisper is taking a toll on what energy he has left.
He didn’t get a lot of sleep, last night.
He spots a flash of bright red, and an even brighter ribbon, along with blue, bleach blonde,
regular blonde, orange- the whole cohort.
HeDoesn’t want to talk to all of them.
Finding a relatively empty hall to duck into isn’t too difficult, and he sends a quick text to
Sumire and Haru announcing his presence. It’s Haru who finds him first- or perhaps she
called first dibs on talking to him.
“Goro-kun.” She says, as she walks up to him, a half-smile pulling at the edges of her lips.
“Haru-san.” Akechi responds in kind.
Haru’s smile widens slightly, “I’m glad you agreed to show up.”
“Hm.” Akechi hums shortly, “Well. You insisted.”
“That I did…” Haru trails off, a little awkward.
Akechi hates this. It feels strange, to reflect on his friendship with Haru in this way- their past
conversations suddenly seem far easier, in comparison to whatever the hell this is supposed
to be.
He never could quite read what she was thinking, last time- his freshest collateral victim.
There had almost been a businesslike politeness to her, throughout January. It had been
grating, at the time, just as it is now, though for far different reasons.
“You do that a lot.” Akechi comments.
Haru blinks, “…Insist on things?”
Akechi shakes his head, “No. Force yourself to act amicably.”
Haru looks almost hurt, “…I’m not forcing myself to act any particular way at the moment,
Goro-kun.”
Akechi looks her up and down, appraising. “…Right.”

“Why did you assume I was?” Haru pushes.
Akechi clenches his jaw, lowering his voice, “Haru-san, need I remind you what I just did to
your father?”
A short laugh bubbles from Haru’s lips, before she clamps a hand over her mouth, looking
mortified, “I-I’m sorry!” She stammers, like the apparent humour she finds in the situation
matters to Akechi at all, “It’s just- ha.”
She presses her lips together in a wobbly line, and Akechi stiffens. He knows how to deal
with her anger, wherever it may be directed- appreciates it, even. He doesn’t know how to
deal with her tears. He fears he’d be even less help than last time.
“I’m not upset.” Haru insists, and Akechi can only give her a flat stare at the blatant lie. “I’m
not, it’s just-”
Akechi presses his lips together.
Haru laughs delicately, “I honestly did just want to talk. I didn’t mean to-” She gestures to her
face, and it twists a little further, “…I honestly don’t know why I’m so upset.” She admits,
voice a bit wet. She laughs weakly, “But I feel like I’m not upset enough, either.”
Akechi doesn’t care to repeat what he said to Sumire the day prior. And any empty platitudes
would be frankly insulting.
So he stays quiet.
“…I feel like we’ve had this conversation before.” Haru observes, quickly swiping at her
eyes.
“We have.” Akechi confirms. “You can say it again though, if you’d like.” He offers, for how
little he’d like to retread the ground that always leads him a little too close to thinking about
Shido.
Haru, thankfully, shakes her head, “No, no it’s alright.” She rolls out her shoulders, and
straightens up, “I told you, once, that if you were put in a difficult position, not to sacrifice
yourself for my sake.”
“I told you I never intended to.” Akechi points out.
“And you haven’t.” A ghost of a smile plays on Haru’s lips, “I think I’m glad.” She huffs
shortly, “We were all going to die.”
“Right.” Akechi murmurs, thinking of alarms and machinery and a wash of stars. The list of
imagery that has been solidly ruined for him is on the rise, it seems.
Haru takes a shaky breath, “Quite the close call, no?”
“Quite.” Akechi agrees, “Closer than last time, too.”

Haru laughs humourlessly, “Let’s hope this isn’t a pattern.”
“I’d make a guess, based on our plan, but that’s all in the trash, isn’t it?” Akechi sighs, “I hate
this waiting.”
“I hate it too.” Haru agrees, “It seems like it’s all we do lately, isn’t it?” She sighs, an ironic
grimace pasted on her face, “Let’s hope we don’t have to wait for long.”
“No, I expect that we won’t.” Akechi mutters.
Haru’s gaze flicks to the floor, “Do you think- that is to say-” She pauses to retake her breath,
“Do you think my previous… preparations, will still be necessary?”
Akechi tilts his head, considering. It’s a valid question, steeped in just as much uncertainty as
the rest of this nightmare.
“I would say no.” Akechi eventually decides, “Don’t dismiss them entirely, in case there is a
follow-up attempt on your father’s life; but, I think the chances of that occurring are
unlikely.”
Haru nods slowly, “I understand.” She pauses, “I wonder-” And cuts herself off.
Akechi cocks his head in question, but Haru just smiles slightly and shakes her head.
“Nevermind.” She says, “Now, shall we join the others?”

Futaba doesn’t know how to feel about the past few days.
It’s weird to think that she hasn’t actually been a Phantom Thief for very long. Okumura’s
palace, excluding her own, was going to be the first time she actually participated in a full
heist and stole someone’s heart.
She supposes they technically still succeeded. She also knows that the response to do you
guys accidentally cause psychotic breakdowns often is a solid ‘No’.
She guesses there’s a first time for everything. It’s nice to be included.
…She thinks she would have preferred not being included in this, actually. She feels weird.
The purest essence of the word, in fact. She feels guilty, too, which she thinks might be a bit
stupid, because what else was she supposed to do? Navigate harder?
As that thought crosses her mind, she think that it might have actually been beneficial if she
did. Her whole job is to make sure a fight goes smoothly, and that fight did not go smoothly.
She feels weird about being saved, technically, by Akechi as well. She feels worse that the
result is this.
At least Haru seems to be taking it alright. Or she’s a great liar- what does Futaba know?

It’s a mess, but at least it has a short fuse. Futaba isn’t sure she could handle stewing in this
for weeks- the projected few days is more than enough already. Pretending everything is fine
is pretty easy while she’s running around a school festival, anyway.
She sees Haru rejoin them, with Akechi at her side. Huh. She thought he wasn’t going to
show up, honestly. She wonders if he feels bad.
That thought is a sure-fire way for Futaba to trip into other thoughts that she very much does
not wish to have, so sheWell.
Hm.
Akechi’s standing off to the side, not talking to anyone, aside from Sumire or Haru
occasionally turning and saying something, plus some weird non-verbal eye fight with Ren
(ew)- though, as she looks a little closer, that seems to be mostly Ren making a fool of
himself while Akechi ignores him, what else is new?
There’s an opportunity here.
It’s the afternoon, and there’s only an hour or so before the festival starts wrapping up for day
one anyway, so,
Fuck it.
“Hey, nerd.” Futaba blurts, as she sidles up to Akechi.
Akechi gives her the flattest look she’s ever seen. She valiantly doesn’t shrink back from it.
“Futaba-chan.” Akechi says, “To what do I owe the pleasure.” It doesn’t sound much like a
question. Futaba thinks it actually sounds an awful lot like go away please, which she
guesses is about as polite as Akechi gets when he’s not doing his weird idol routine.
“I want to talk.” She manages to get out.
Akechi gives her an incredulous stare, and looks pointedly around at the festival, “Now?”
“No, in three years.” Futaba sticks her tongue out, “Yes now.”
Akechi gives a quick side eye to the rest of the thieves milling about the student body, and
tightly folds his arms with a roll of his eyes, “Fine. Where to?”
Futaba matches the eyeroll, asshole, “Around the side somewhere, I guess. Away from
people.”
“I figured.” Akechi lets his arms fall to his side, “Lead the way.”
Futaba stuffs her hands in her pockets, and attempts to do just that. It’s a little awkward,
trying to find her way through a campus that she’s never actually been to before. She’s not

sure if Akechi notices, since he shouldn’t have spent that much time here either, but she still
feels thoroughly judged.
Not a great start.
Eventually, she manages to find an alley around the side of the school, far from the general
clamour of the school festival. They, miraculously, only managed to draw a few weird looks
on their way there- surely they recognised Akechi, but no one was brave enough to walk up
to him, it seems.
She spins on the balls of her feet to face him, pressing her lips together in a little huff. “So.”
Akechi looks almost resigned, which Futaba almost finds funny, “So. I believe I know what
this is about.”
“Do you.” Futaba states more than asks, shifting on her feet, “Did you think I dragged you
out here to be like ‘you killed my mom, prepare to die?’”
“Something to that effect.” Akechi raises an eyebrow, “Though, perhaps not, if you’re so
blasé.”
Futaba snorts, and looks at the ground, “Yeah, sure. I think- I don’t know what I think.
Maybe I’d like to do that.” She takes a deep breath, “But there’s something I want to ask
first.”
Akechi inclines his head slightly, “Go ahead.”
Futaba puffs out her cheeks. Great, she really has no idea where to start with this- her nerves
are starting to catch up to her.
From the beginning, then, “So, before we figured out all your time travel bullshit, Makoto
and I were trying to figure out your deal.”
Akechi’s other eyebrow shoots up to meet the first, “Oh? Even considering your respective
skillsets, I can’t imagine you found much.”
Futaba will think about that response later. “Not really.” She admits, “Not at first. All your
records are wiped clean,” Which is suspicious in and of itself, “And Makoto’s sis knows jack
shit about you.”
“I don’t tend to tell the gritty details of my sordid past to my coworkers, no.” Akechi says
dryly.
Futaba makes a token effort not to laugh, and ends up with a half-choked scoff, “Good tragic
backstory practice. Keep it mysterious. So, we couldn’t find anything, and I was kinda
weirded out because usually I can find anything, and-” She’s getting sidetracked, “But,
basically, I started thinking about the other big time where I couldn’t find any information
about something.”
Akechi tilts his head, “That being?”

Futaba chews on her lip, “My mom’s research. I spent a long time looking for it, and just like
all your stuff, I couldn’t find even a bit of it.”
Akechi freezes.
“So, I started thinking it might be connected,” Futaba continues, spurred on by the response,
“And I asked the only other person who might know something about my mom’s stuff.”
Akechi can’t quite meet her eyes. “Sakura-san, I presume?”
Okay, okay, now she’s getting somewhere, “Yep. And he said that my mom was-” She
swallows, “-Experimenting. On people. He said he met some ‘scrawny kid’.”
Akechi’s nose wrinkles at the descriptor. Futaba doesn’t know if she should laugh or cry.
“So?” Futaba pushes, “It was you, right?”
Now, Akechi’s eyes shoot up to glare at her. “What makes you think that?”
Oh, this is how they’re doing this, huh? “Well.” Futaba starts, and tries to find her thin thread
of logic, “I guess my first thought was- for a kid to be useful in a cognitive psience study-” It
feels wrong, speaking about it so detachedly; her mom, a name on a research paper, probablyAkechi, an unnamed participant, “-They’d probably have something to do with, y’know,
cognitive psience. Like a persona user, maybe. So I got to thinking that maybe it was the
black mask, since we didn’t know who it was at the time. And, well,” She gestures to the
aforementioned black mask.
“Well?” Akechi echoes, “So what? What are you trying to get out of this? It’s not like I have
access to her research- Shido keeps that under lock and key.”
That’s as good as a confirmation- even more than all the other little ticks that have littered the
conversation. Futaba presses her lips together- she has no idea where to go from here.
“That was one thing I wanted.” She admits. She sucks in a breath, a bit shaky- shit, “But…
you knew her.” She accuses.
Akechi’s eyes narrow at the ground, “I did.”
“And you killed her.” Futaba says, properly accusatory now.
“That’s been established.” Akechi intones, clipped.
“You-” Futaba clenches her jaw, a righteous anger bubbling in her chest, “You don’t just get
to-!”
Her eyes sting, throat tightening, and she thinks: this, this is why she didn’t think about it. To
think, that someone who knew her mom, worked with her, had entire conversations with her,
to think that person killed the mom she loved so, so much, and Futaba had to watch-

“I don’t just get to what?” Akechi says lowly, a hiss creeping into his voice. “I don’t want to
talk about this.”
“Well I do.” Futaba spits, “You knew her, you knew her and you still killed her. Did you even
care? Did you know about me?”
“I did.” It almost sounds like a confession.
Futaba clenches her fists, “Why?” She asks- begs, voice wrecked.
Akechi clicks his tongue, shoulders tense, “What do you want to hear? That knowing her
made it so hard? That I cared about what would happen after? Even if it were true, it clearly
doesn’t matter. She’s dead all the same.”
“So you did care?” Futaba chokes out, furiously rubbing at her eyes so that they stop“No. I didn’t.” Akechi sneers, “I didn’t give a single shit. Hell- I felt relieved when I got the
order.”
Stop, stop, her mom was amazing, and wonderful, and how could anyone that knew her be
glad she’s gone, “Shut up.”
“Don’t ask things you don’t want answers to.” Akechi grits.
(What about the-) How dare he- why the hell does he get to be here when her mom isn’t?
Why does- (She hasn’t asked about the research, that’s the missing-) No, no, shut up, it
wasn’t bad, her mom would never- (How does she know? How could she-)
“Just- just leave me alone!” Futaba shouts, tears properly streaming down her face, “Just go
away!”
She spins on her heel so fast that she stumbles, sprinting out of the alley, ignoring the way
people turn and look at her, and people are staring, don’t look, why can’t they just leaveShe staggers to a stop outside the school, pressing herself against a brick wall and sinking to
the ground, legs tucked against her chest and face streamed with snot and tears pressed
forcefully into her knees.
(The Death grows to rank four, and Akechi ignores its thrum.)

Ren tries not to feel worried when both Akechi and Futaba suddenly vanish from the group,
an hour or so before the festival ends for the first day.
He had actually been looking for the right moment to pull Akechi away himself- but it seems
like Futaba beat him to it. Which is- new. He thinks he should be worried, but it seems worse
to look for them to try and, what, intervene?
He can’t be the mediator for everything, and certainly not something like this.

Still, the urge to make sure nothing goes too awry remains.
The festival activities come to a close for the day, and he still hasn’t seen Futaba or Akechi.
The other thieves slowly start to disperse, expressions tense- likely from a combination of the
Sword of Damocles resting over their necks and their obvious absentees.
Ren shoots Futaba a quick where are you? text.
Three ellipses appear and disappear for a moment, before eventually a response comes in.
Futaba: outside the school
Ren: front or back?
Ren: or all the way at the station?
Futaba: front
Ren takes that as enough invitation. He steps through the gates, scanning the street up and
down, until he sees Futaba, half tucked away in a gap between the buildings.
He squats in front of her, “Hey.”
Futaba slowly drags her face out of her knees. Her cheeks are wet, and her eyes are puffy,
“Hey.” She mumbles.
Ren thinks that maybe he should have played mediator. Though, maybe that would have
made it worse. “What’s up?”
“Mm.” She swallows, “I think I messed up.”
“Yeah?”
She nods, chin tapping against her legs, “I didn’t mean to…”
Ren tries not to fill in the blank with whatever worst-case scenario his brain is insistent on
cooking, “You were with Akechi, right?”
She nods again, “I wanted to ask him something. But then I just got so mad, and…”
Ren tries for a light-hearted smirk, “He’s still alive, right?”
“Oh, he’s just fine.” Futaba mutters, steeped in bitterness.
Ren drops the expression, “Alright. …Why do you think you messed up, then?”
“I wanted to ask him about mom.” Futaba says quietly, and Ren is starting to get a better
picture for why this went horribly.
“About her research?” Ren asks, wondering if that’s something Akechi would even have
access to.

“Yep.” Futaba says with an unceremonious pop. She tucks her knees even closer to her chest,
“I needed to know if he was the guy mom did experiments or whatever on, and he didn’t say
it, but it’s definitely him.”
Ren loses the thread.
What?
“Your mom…?” Experimented on people. Cognitive psience, so Ren guesses that makes
sense, but experimented on Akechi“Mmhm.” Futaba hums flatly, “I don’t know anything about it, because I didn’t ask.” She
says, brows furrowing in frustration, “And I dunno if he’ll talk to me again.”
Ren smiles weakly, trying to bring himself back to the conversation, “I’m sure he will.” He
says, and he’s fairly certain he’s telling the truth, “He can’t be more upset with you than me,
right? If he’s mad at you at all.”
Futaba snorts, “Sounding pretty confident there.”
“Well, you know.” Ren shifts out of his squat to sit properly on the ground.
“I don’t.” Futaba grits out, “I don’t know. I have no idea what to do.”
Ren hums, “What do you want to do?”
“I don’t want to apologise.” Futaba grips at her knees, “He was a dick.”
“Maybe you can both apologise, then…?” Ren suggests tentatively, “If you hurt each other?”
He doesn’t know where the middle ground is, for something like this.
“Maybe.” Futaba mumbles, not sounding convinced. She abruptly stands, “I want to go
home.”
Ren stands as well, “Then let’s go.”
Futaba nods, and stares at the ground as she walks.

Chapter 64
Chapter Summary

Musings, festivals, and talks that none want to have.

Chapter Notes

CW: small reference to suicide and suicidal ideation

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Akechi doesn’t like thinking about Wakaba Isshiki.
Some days are better than others, as is commonplace. Some days, even the thought of her
name will send him spiralling into rivers and lakes in his mind, pushing his head underwater
to drown his voice and lungs. Some days, he can regard her memory with a calm detachment
more befitting of someone far removed.
That all happened to someone else, you see, of course! There was no laboratory, there was no
temple, there was no gun, and there was no child that the researcher would always love more.
Akechi never particularly liked thinking about Futaba Sakura, either, until circumstances
have forced him to start thinking about her quite a bit.
How Futaba managed to unearth the dots that all string together in a neat little row with
words like experiments and Black Mask and ethical malpractice is beyond him. He only met
the elder Sakura once, during his time at the lab, before Wakaba had quickly ushered him out
with cheerful deflections and vague allusions to NDA’s. Perhaps Sakura just has a good
memory.
Perhaps, Akechi owes Futaba something like answers. He disagrees. In his opinion, Wakaba
owes Futaba answers, Wakaba owes him answers too- but, well,
If there’s no one left alive to provide what Futaba is looking for, that’s fine by Akechi. He can
play a role in her head just fine. So long as she doesn’t forget the larger villain while she’s at
it.
It’s curious, though- this didn’t happen last time. This argument, these questions. The most
obvious difference Akechi can think of that Futaba alluded to is that she went properly
digging, as opposed to having the go-ahead to pick through his phone and find all his secrets.

But it still doesn’t add up. Futaba was borderline friendly to him, during January, and Akechi
has never been able to understand why. He certainly can’t now, when this Futaba is reacting in
the way that he can only expect her to.
He did taunt her, though. He didn’t do that last time. Is that really enough for such a drastic
difference? Maybe she was able to stomach talking to him by silently plotting his revenge,
unaware of the fact that Akechi already had a death sentence ticking down in both past and
future.
The worst reason he can think of is that witnessing his death made her pity him. Akechi
doesn’t like that one, so he disregards it.
But none of that matters, really.
The facts are as follows: Akechi is not going to discuss Wakaba Isshiki, not with Futaba, not
with anyone. He isn’t going to think about her either- he’s had more than enough of that
between Futaba’s little mission and Sae’s probing questions, and that brief conversation with
Sumire months ago,
He didn’t particularly enjoy learning that Futaba had a palace.
(It felt, weirdly, absurdly, like a betrayal to Wakaba. Like Futaba stewing in her own misery
was some fate that Akechi had promised to circumvent.
He promised no such thing. He and Wakaba didn’t have promises- not ones that held any
weight, not worth the paper they were written on.
He idly wonders if Wakaba ever read contracts she signed. He thinks (fondly, absurdly,
absurd, it’s all so ridiculous) that she may have been too scatterbrained to ever bother.
She was far more precise in practice-)
He isn’t thinking about her, he isn’t.
If he tries to avoid the school festival again tomorrow, no doubt Sumire or Haru will pester
him until he folds. Maybe if he’s snappy enough they’ll leave him be. He doubts it.
No choice, then, as ever.
You’re stagnating.
AREN’T YOU BORED?
Is he?

Ren is determined.

It’s the second day of the festival, and while he would have honestly preferred to do it
yesterday, now seems like as good a time as any (far superior to, say, a week from now, when
Ren will surely lose his nerve and sink beneath a lake of apathy) to find Akechi and demand
they talk. Properly. No holds barred.
It’s something of a surprise that Akechi is here at all, considering what Ren can only interpret
as a disastrous conversation with Futaba yesterday, but he won’t look a gift horse in the
mouth.
The group is still tense, scattered about in twos and threes without being entirely separatedAkechi is standing off to the side, avoiding even Haru and Sumire, it seems.
Ren takes a breath and takes his chances.
“Hey.” He says, marching up to Akechi’s side, “Can we go somewhere? I want to talk.”
The look Akechi gives him is eerily blank, like he’s deciding how violently to react. Ren
hopes he can convince him to just come along before he lands on an answer.
“Somewhere more quiet.” Ren continues. Abruptly, he realises that Akechi might have some
assumptions about what this is, “I’m- this isn’t about Futaba. Or Okumura. I wanted to talk
about- uh, us?”
He curses himself for the stutter, and for phrasing it like a question. Fuck, where the hell is
Joker’s conviction when he needs it?
Left somewhere behind in the false reality, probably.
Well, it’s not like it was that reliable to begin with.
Akechi’s eyes narrow, flicking up and down.
“Please?” Ren adds quietly, “It’ll be quick.” Probably a lie, knowing them.
Akechi scoffs, seeming more tired than affronted. Ren can work with that.
“Where to, then?” Akechi asks snippily, “You’re the one who knows your way around.”
Ren bites at his lip as he considers it, “The old PE faculty office, I guess? It’s empty.” He

You are. Metatron interrupts, and Ren deflates.
