Futaba feels like her eyes have been wrung out like a dish rag. Turns out, staring at screens
for hours on end, barely blinking, has some shitty side effects. Who’d have thought!
She swears she used to have better stamina than this. She must be going outside too much.
Ugh.
On the desk, Morgana yawns, “Are you done yet?”
“You don’t even know what I’m doing.” Futaba mumbles in response.
“Because you won’t tell me!” Morgana yowls, “And that just makes sitting here even more
boring!”
Futaba sticks out her tongue, and gets back to work, thankful that her lines of code are
incomprehensible to those not in the know.
She doesn’t have to be doing this, technically. In fact, she’s pretty sure that it’s nothing more
than a time sink, having already hit every dead end feasible at least a year ago. And she’s
already got a deal with Akechi to start cracking on this exact problem.
But kicking Shido’s ass could be months away. Just one or two, most likely, but still. Being
reminded that her mom’s research is out there somewhere makes it unbearable to just sit
around, twiddling her thumbs.

Not like she’s found anything, though.
She’s even tried poking at a new avenue that’s relatively unexplored. That is, immediately
betraying the trust of her tentative ally to poke through his records again and see if there’s
any connections to her mom. She didn’t find anything before, but, hey! She only looked once.
…Predictably, she’s come up with nothing. It’s like being time gated, or plot blocked.
Annoying is what it really is. She’d complain to Mona, but there’s a fine line between doing
sneaky hacker things on the down low and loudly yapping to all her friends about her and
Akechi’s plans.
Not that there’s much of a plan to begin with. She doesn’t even think Akechi would care all
that much if everyone knew the two of them intend to go research-hunting, but Futaba figures
that spilling all the implications that come with their deal wouldn’t win her any gold stars.
This would be so much easier if Akechi just sucked it up and told her stuff“What did the screen do to you?” Morgana questions suspiciously, “You look like you want
to smack it.”
“I wanna smack something.” Futaba grumbles. Alas, noodle arms.
Morgana groans, “Can’t you tell me anything?”
Futaba waves a hand, “I’m doing cool stuff.”
“Didn’t know you had it in you.” Morgana mutters.
“Hey!” Futaba yelps, “Bad kitty! That sounded like an Akechi insult! You’ve been spending
too much time with him.”
Morgana’s fur fluffs up, “I barely talk to him! He doesn’t own sass!”
“Eh, fair enough.” Futaba concedes, “I guess Ren probably got to you first with that,
anyway.”
Morgana snorts and curls up into a loaf, before suddenly jumping back up, “Don’t try to
distract me! Answer my question!”
Futaba groans, “It’s super boring, trust me!” Only kind of a lie, “I’m just doing some
research. For a personal project,” She quickly adds, “Not related to the thieves at all. Super
unhelpful.”
Morgana gives her a look.
“Don’t worry about it!” Futaba insists. She’s sure she’s not that bad at lying. She’s better than
Ann at least. She hopes.

Morgana rolls his eyes, and finally gives it up. Futaba takes that as her cue to spend some
more time letting her eyes shrivel into raisins thanks to the light from her monitors. Maybe
she should get better ones, actually.
She slaps her cheeks. Now isn’t the time to get distracted. Morgana gives her a look that she
steadfastly ignores.
Trying to poke through Akechi’s records again is looking to be a bust. Even now that she
half-knows the gaps she’s supposed to be filling, doesn’t mean she can find what’s there. It’s
filling a hole with plaster and expecting it to look like brick.
Cross referencing what she has with everything else she’s patched together in a timeline of
events gets her nowhere, either. It’s not like all her mom’s research is gone, just the stuff
that’s important, all leading to a cut-off point of four years ago.
(Interestingly, Futaba notes, that’s around the time that the development of the lab in Odaiba
was cancelled, changing tracks to become a stadium. She had looked it up after finding out
what Maruki’s deal was, and she’s not one to ignore a coincidence like that.
But the coincidence also doesn’t tell her anything, beyond what vague speculation she can
muster. Shido has a chokehold on cognitive psience research- gee, who could have guessed!)
The parts of her mom’s research that are still around are, interesting, sure, but not particularly
in-depth. Or accurate.
The stuff that Futaba knew about the Metaverse prior to actually going there is the kind of
thing that she sneakily read off her mom’s computer before the documents got tossed into the
void. The papers she can find online and in archives are all highly theoretical. All speculation
and, frankly, nonsense, that her mom must have dreamed up in her frantic search for the way
cognition shapes reality.
She can make some guesses as to how her mom’s ideas started getting decidedly more
accurate.
Futaba glares at the screen a little harder.
If there’s nothing here, she’ll just have to wait.
She scowls. She’s never really been known for her patience.

Makoto will always be the first to admit that she finds Akechi infuriating.
She does, however, find him marginally less infuriating than the version of him that her
sister’s mind has cooked up. The real Akechi, to his credit, is far less inclined to speak in

The truth and all its consequences are spread on the table for all to see. Makoto is grateful,
somewhat, even if it mostly means that riddles become blunt demands and backhanded
insults turn into regular insults.
Thinking on it, she isn’t quite sure if it’s really a set of truths as it is a simple change in
perspective. But she supposes that from where she’s standing, there really isn’t that much of a
difference.
A sentiment that makes the task of somehow shifting her sister’s perception of Akechi all the
more daunting. At the very least, Sae is actually home for once.

Akechi allows himself to be moderately impressed when Makoto calls for another meeting

everything between is just as liable to have changed than it is to have stayed the same.

admit -far, far away from the ship- that he has a degree of curiosity in understanding how it is
he is perceived. He puts so much effort into tailoring such a thing, after all.
In theory, he should know the inner workings of these cognitions inside and out. It’s a little
disheartening to find that this is not the case.

your identity is malleable. So long as you declare yourself as another person entirely when
the time comes, you should be able to get away with it.”
Ann hums with understanding, an eager smile playing on her lips. Well, at least one of them
is enjoying this mess.
“How will you be fixing the slots?” Makoto asks the cognition as they walk out of the lunge
housing the dice games.
“You speak so crassly.” The cognition teases.
“Yes, yes,” Akechi rolls his eyes, “But really, how will you be getting around them? Are you
going to assume the form of a machine, this time?”
Ann tilts her head, as if imagining it, as the cognition laughs, “Of course not.”
“Then what- ” Makoto starts, before coming to an abrupt stop as they enter the slots hall.
The enormous slot machine still stands at the opposite end, bright neon flashing Win! Fifty
Thousand! The cognition ignores the sight entirely, taking a hard right to open a door marked
employees only.
“Wh- hey!” Ann calls.
“Sorry!” The cognition chirps, and winks, “Employees only.” And the door slams shut.
Akechi grits his teeth, “Sneaky little…”
Makoto snorts. “Sorry,” She says, when Akechi gives her a look, “It’s just- that’s exactly
what Sis said.”
Akechi rolls his eyes, “Hilarious, truly.”
“It kinda is.” Ann says, unhelpfully, as she tries to open the door the cognition just
disappeared through. “Won’t budge…” She mutters.
“I imagine that the sign is meant to be taken literally.” Makoto grouses, “We might need a
disguise after all.”
“Wonderful.” Akechi mutters, thoroughly done with this. He scans the hall, scowling when
he sees some uniformed shadows carrying trays of champagne flutes to cognitions chatting
and laughing around the slots.
Makoto follows his gaze, “Do you think we can take out three?”

“We don’t have to.” Akechi points out.
Ann blinks, “What, you want one of us to go in alone?”
Akechi shrugs, “It’ll be faster. And I doubt shadows will attack anyone they perceive as an

“I suppose that’s true.” Makoto agrees warily, “…Who’s going to do it?”
“I’m the only one of the three of us that can act.” Akechi points out blandly, loathe as he is to

“I’m not bad at acting.” Makoto mumbles, petulant.
“Uh, Queen?” Ann smiles, amused, “Remember when you were stalking us, and you’d

“Alright, I get it!” Makoto quickly interrupts her, “Just- get it done quickly, Crow.”
Akechi rolls his eyes, and doesn’t bother responding as he stalks off to sneak behind one of

It’s quick work, stabbing one of them through the neck before it can transform. The

shatters across the floor.
Akechi picks up the uniform left behind, letting black and blue melt into white and red,
before ducking behind one of the slots to quickly change. He rolls out his shoulders, and
heads towards the door, glaring at Ann as she giggles at his new attire.
The door opens easily, and he slips inside.
***
The halls are familiar. The structure and atmosphere are all the same, Akechi thinks, and yet
the exact twists and turns are slightly off. Despite that, it’s hardly a maze, and it isn’t long
before he spies a mirror.
“What’s your problem?” Akechi hisses, as he strides stiffly to match pace with his
doppelgänger.
“Whatever could you mean?” It asks airily, apparently unfazed by Akechi’s reappearance.
Akechi hates this thing, “You can’t seem to make up your mind.” He spits, “You didn’t lend
us your card, even though we have the same goal. You did help us with the dice, which
turned out to be entirely pointless now that you’ve left us on our own with the slots.”
“Ah, right.” The cognition hums, as though it had forgotten, “The dice… call it a favour.”

“A favour for what? ”
“ Repaying a favour, that is.” The cognition corrects, “Something changed. It was your doing,
right?” It smiles, “Everything is so much more involved. It’s far more interesting, don’t you
think?”
The day cognitions wearing his face stop spouting cryptic nonsense will be a wondrous day
indeed, “You tell me.” Akechi grits out.
The cognition laughs again, as it opens the door to what looks like a server room, with one
main terminal sitting at a desk, “I actually have things to do now, you know? And the
manager has no idea! Or, she does, but there’s nothing she can do about it.” It strides forward,
tapping at the terminal to wake it up, quickly tapping in some commands, “Much more
interesting, like I said.”
Is Sae really so bitter? Has she come to the conclusion that Akechi was stringing her along
this whole time, content to play his games while she floundered?
Well, Akechi reconsiders, he really has no right to be offended, when she’s not so far off the
mark.
He does reserve the right to be offended that her deductions have manifested as the thing
before him. As enigmatic as Akechi is sure he comes off to Sae, he was hardly in it for kicks.
Does she think Akechi hates her?
Maybe she does, a thought whispers, and Akechi decides that now isn’t the time for this.
The cognition finishes its business at the terminal with a flourish, “Well. That’s me.” It says,
“I’ll be off. I suspect I’ll see your friends back outside.”
Akechi just sneers, and marches over to try and take a crack at whatever this terminal is
supposed to do. The cognition just laughs at his hostility, and leaves without any further
comment.
Akechi frowns as he takes in the screen. It’s familiar- he recalls Futaba doing whatever it is
she does to manipulate the odds of the slots at one of these. Several, actually; the probability
here is a little tighter than that of the dice.
But, the cognition seemed to deem its work done after just working at this one. Perhaps
there’s a trick to it that Futaba missed?
Or, Akechi frowns, Futaba had more roadblocks to work around. She had been coming at it
from the perspective of an invasive force, trying to barge her way in. But, coming at it from
the perspective of an employee, simply adjusting the odds as is their job…
Perhaps they were all a little too reliant on Oracle’s skill set, Akechi thinks, as he types in
adjust probability > Makoto Niijima > 777 > 1.0
Command accepted, the terminal chimes. The power of cognition, Akechi snorts to himself.
Perhaps it’s for the best that neither he nor Sae have any real grasp over whatever hacking

entails.
He leaves the server room briskly, flashing a cheerful smile to a shadow he passes, who pays
him no mind. Arriving back in the main hall, he quickly lets his black mask and
accompanying bodysuit burn back over the stolen uniform.
Ann catches his eye, and waves, “Hey! Your, uh, double came through just before.”
“Did you run into any trouble?” Makoto asks.
“None at all.” Akechi dismisses, “Your card should find some success in the slots now,
though. That one, in particular.” He points towards the giant slot machine.
Makoto nods, and startles as there’s a cheer and a smattering of applause from the other end
of the room. The giant slot machine flashes 777 as coins spill onto the ground. Akechi stands
on his toes, and sees the cognition dusting off its hands as a show of accomplishment. It
turns, and flashes the three of them a grin, walking in their direction.
“May the three of you have similar luck.” It says slyly.
“Thank you.” Makoto fires back, marching over to shove her card into the machine, hopping
a bit as she tries to manoeuvre over the piles of coins.
Card accepted, 5000 coins deducted, the machine chimes, and the slots start spinning again,
predictably landing on triple sevens.
Makoto has to jump back, as yet another batch of fifty-thousand coins spills from the
machine. She quickly reclaims her card, and walks stiffly back towards the group.
“Alright!” Ann cheers, as the cognition politely claps, asshole, “We can go to the next floor
now, yeah?”
“You can.” The cognition replies before Akechi can, turning on its heel with a small wave,
“I’ll see you there. I think you’ll like what’s up next.”
“Will you? ” Makoto asks.
The cognition’s smile becomes a shade more genuine, “I suspect I will. I hear there’s a
coliseum there. I’d certainly like to try my hand.”
Ann tilts her head, “You’ve never been to the next floor before?”
The cognition frowns, “How could I? I didn’t have enough coins.” It laughs, “Well, don’t
take too long.”
Akechi furrows his brow as the cognition walks off, “…That receptionist shadow said the
card under my name has been registered for three years.”
Makoto hums, Akechi’s own confusion reflected on her face, “Maybe Sis didn’t see you as
above everything until recently?”

“Possibly…” Akechi mutters, though something still rings false.
Ann shrugs, “Weird.” She says, eloquent as ever, “Anyway, should we go?”
***
They arrive on the next floor, fifty thousand coins deducted from the card under Makoto’s
name, the Yuko Suzui card safely tucked away, the shadow that lets them pass none the wiser

Akechi walks forward, passing the shadow that greets them-as Ann and Makoto are quickly stopped.

“What was the point of getting all the coins, then?!” Ann complains.
Ah, right. Akechi remembers this.
“The courtroom.” He starts, and hastens to continue when Makoto glares at him, “This entire

immensely unfair, but there is room for… unexpected developments, I suppose.”
“Sooo, Niijima-san needs to see us as allowed to be in a courtroom?” Ann summarises,
tugging at her hair thoughtfully.
“But there’s no limit on who’s allowed to witness a trial.” Makoto points out, “Do we need to
be lawyers, or something?”
Akechi waves a hand, “It’s more of a presence of mind thing. Sae-san just needs to see you in
the audience of one of her trials. That’s what worked last time.”
“When’s her next trial, though?” Ann frowns.
“…I think she’s booked out all week, actually.” Makoto says, “We could probably go as soon

“You should.” Akechi nods, grateful that it is presumably his role within the justice system
that allows him to avoid any awkward scenarios, such as waltzing into a courtroom while

“Then we will.” Makoto decides with a firm nod.

Makoto does her best not to shy away from the strange looks she gets from security as she
and Ann shuffle their way into the sparsely populated courtroom.
They probably recognise her. She and Sae do look quite alike.
Sae is sitting behind the prosecutor’s bench, flipping through a folder. An intensity that
Makoto has been seeing more and more often burns in her eyes, brows furrowed in a scowl.
From what Makoto knows, this trial is barely anything special- already won before it’s begun.
She isn’t sure if she should be amused at how seriously Sae is taking it.
At her side, Ann shifts and fidgets in the quiet. “How long do these take, usually?” She
whispers.
Makoto laughs under her breath, “They haven’t even started yet.” She teases, “But, it should
only be a few hours today.”
Ann looks like she’s trying very hard not to pout, “That’s… I can wait. Yeah.”
Makoto suppresses her snickers. Her eyes flick back to the prosecutor’s bench, and she nearly
bites her tongue as she makes eye-contact with her sister, wide-eyed and looking bewildered.
Makoto gives a stiff wave. Ann notices, and joins in, far brighter. Sae narrows her eyes in
response.
The trial is actually shorter than Makoto expects it to be. They hit a snag a few hours in that
initially forces a recess, and then a push to a later date. Makoto hears Ann’s sigh of relief as
the judge dismisses the court.
She isn’t all that surprised when they bump into Sae as soon as they leave.
“I didn’t know that you planned on watching a trial, Makoto.” Is Sae’s greeting, laced with
accusation.
“…It was a last-minute decision.” Makoto elects to say.
“How come?” Sae pushes.
Makoto fights not to shrug, “I’m curious about your work. And since I’m heading off to
university soon, I thought I’d… do some research.”
Sae hums, and inclines her head towards Ann, “…And you’re interested in law as well?”
“Um,” Ann starts, “Hi- uh, sort of?” She laughs, loud and grating, and Makoto prepares
herself for the Takamaki acting special, “I mean, I’m a second year, so I’m just… checking
out my options.”
“I see.” Sae tucks some hair behind her ear, not revealing at all whether she believes the
display or not. “I take you two are friends?”

Ann smiles, “Yep! I’m Ann. Ann Takamaki.”
“I mentioned I was coming here, and she asked to tag along.” Makoto tacks on.
Sae seems mollified by this, as her expression softens slightly, “Well, I’m glad to hear you’re
both interested in the field. It’s good to start thinking about these things early.” She huffs a
laugh, “I’m glad that you’re taking initiative with this, Makoto, but I’m also glad you didn’t
bring a whole crowd. A courtroom isn’t a playground.”
It is, however, host to a coliseum of all things. Makoto keeps this to herself. “Of course. Most
of my other friends wouldn’t be particularly interested in a trial, anyway.”
“Ren might.” Ann interjects. “But you’d have to drag Ryuji there kicking and screaming.”
“And I’m not sure Ren would actually be that thrilled by a courtroom.” Makoto points out.
Ren is interested -or can feign interest; she’s never quite sure- in a great many things, but she
thinks that spending any amount of time in the defendant’s chair would probably colour one’s
perception of the whole thing.
“Ren?” Sae questions.
Makoto really hopes this conversation isn’t a gateway to awkwardly listing out all her
friends. “You might have met him, Sis. He works at Leblanc?”
“Oh, right,” Sae blinks, seemingly surprised by the coincidence, “The part-timer. Small
world.” She huffs.
“Right.” Makoto says in vague agreement. She coughs, “Well, I’m sure you’re busy…?”
Sae’s expression shutters back to her usual pinched frown, “Of course. I’ll see you at home.”
“It was nice meeting you!” Ann calls after her, waving goodbye.
Makoto bites her lip, “Well,” She says, “That should be enough, shouldn’t it?”
Ann blows a raspberry, “Hope so. It would kinda suck if I’m still not allowed in because she
doesn’t believe I’m actually interested.”
Makoto laughs, and figures that probably isn’t the case considering that presumably all the
Phantom Thieves would have had to sit in on a trial, last time. She doubts they would have
collectively been able to convince Sae that they’re all interested in law.
“We’re going back in tomorrow?” Ann asks.
Makoto nods. “Tomorrow.”
It’s high time they upped the ante, she thinks.

Cognition works in interesting ways.
Ha! A statement as bland and broad as they come. Cognition is the human mind! Of course
it’s entirely nonsensical, and so damn fascinating .
It becomes especially fascinating, though, when an entire person (or several!) is thrown into
the mix. A person inside a mind! A mind inside a mind- it’s lucky that the two don’t clash and
collapse in on each other.
Except they do, somewhat. It took some trial and error to prove this, but in the absence of an
impression inside a manifestation (or a palace, as he’s taken to calling them. I can’t decide if
it sounds cool or stupid. Futaba would probabl- ) can allow for an invasive presence to make
one in its stead. Entirely out of their control, of course- it takes some serious force of will to
truly withhold the brain from taking the path of least resistance.
The kid subject does have some pretty strong will, though. All that Persona nonsense, most
likely. Some more trial and error later, it’s become clear that in the complete absence of any
impression, a gap in the link between whatever metaphor a Shadow has strung together, it
will either make one up, or collapse altogether (whoops!).
Some minds are a bit more stubborn, though; their inner workings obfuscated by layers of
hurdles and riddles- it’s all very irritating. The work-around for that seems to be going to the

source; needling a real person is both easier and harder than needling a shadow, and in this
case it swings in our favour.
It’s a balance. A delicate one, at that. A gun becomes real in the other world, because the
host mind (or, the shadows attracted to it,) can’t tell it’s fake. The gun’s effectiveness,
meanwhile, increases based on the perception of the invasive mind, since it’s the only one
with access to that knowledge. (That might be a test for later, actually- see if a host can be
tricked into believing a gun or other object is more effective than it really is.)
A clever little system! And, as stated: Annoying. Really annoying. A right pain in the ass. At
least we’ve finally found something of a formula of steps to take for when we hit these
roadblocks, so we’re not taking shots in the dark anymore.
I’m still unclear on whether it’s better or worse for the host mind to know the invader
personally, when it comes to ease of progression. The subject can progress rather easily
through my own manifestation, but it’s likely that’s because I want him to progress. And, even
then, there are some doors he can’t seem to open. ( I’m not sure if- I’ve been- Maybe it’s fine
if they stay locked-)
It’s all a matter of circumstance, probably. And besides, if an unknown invader reaches an
impassable wall in a manifestation, then they’d have to make themselves known in some
capacity to force a change in cognition that lets them pass.
I have to say, though, those Persona things are useful for more than just kicking ass. The
masks they come with remove any of the negative effects from spending too long in the
cognitive world, and they act as a barrier against one’s true identity being perceived by the
Ruler Shadow in a manifestation. Mostly. It looks like a certain degree of familiarity between
a host and invader will remove this benefit.
Every claim I make, I get the urge to test it until it breaks. So does the subject, by the looks of
it. A researcher in the making, that one! ( Futaba also- I wonder if he and Futaba would get
al- Sometimes I- ) Or a detective, maybe.
There’s always more to be done.
The notes end there, dated the first of March, 2014.
A sharp eye cuts across them, searching, and finds nothing of import.
Onto the next, then.
“You ought to be grateful,” Shido says to the next stack notes, handwritten in Isshiki’s messy
scrawl, “That you are useful to me in death. Most do not have the luxury of a legacy.”
No, obscurity is the fate that awaits most.
Not him.

Gambles and losses.

Makoto does feel a bit bad, calling an infiltration into her sister’s palace only hours after the
thieves’ meeting wrapped up.
She can’t say she’s entirely convinced of their success, as it stands. But what else can they
do?
There is one thing they can do, she thinks. It would only be fair, really. Surely, the best way
for justice to be served is if Akechi simply confessed his crimes once all is said and done.
Makoto thinks it’s likely that she’s the only one who thinks like this.
(Except, there’s a little thought that tickles at the back of her mind: that Akechi taking the fall
isn’t truly the best outcome.

swoop?

asks as they arrive, “You may pass.”

deal with in the real world, she hopes.
At her side, Ann lets out a sigh of relief as the three of them march onward, “Oh, thank god.

Akechi can’t really be bothered to organise the events of today into neat little folders. Instead,

From Ren’s persistence, to whatever Makoto’s problem is, to the thing that wears his own

It makes sense, in hindsight. The fact that the card under his name has been registered for

If Takahashi were even marginally capable of getting results, Shido considers, then maybe he
wouldn’t be in this position.
It’s his own fault, he supposes. Wakaba really was an excellent researcher.
Combing through her journals is an arduous task. It’s the kind of thing he’d be tempted to
foist off on Akechi, if the kid didn’t look halfway to being ill every time Wakaba’s name is
mentioned. He would hardly be able to compile a thorough report like that.
And, Akechi has been having something of a rebellious streak lately.
Irritating, this close to the election. But uncertainties cannot be suffered this late in the game.
I hate to admit it, Wakaba had begun, in one of her later journals, but I think the subject might
have been right about it being impossible to cross the veil to the cognitive world without that
Nav app.
Even the Nav itself is fallible. Sometimes, people aren’t dragged in even when they’re
standing right next to where it’s activated. Physical contact with whoever is activating it
seems to be a surefire way to 100% drag another person in, but even then, one guy couldn’t
get it to work no matter how hard he tried.
I, myself, have a respectable 56% entry rate into the cognitive world! The subject,
predictably, has a 100% success rate. I’d test if it’s a persona thing (it definitely is, but I
wouldn’t be a very good psientist if I assumed stuff like that), but considering we have a
whopping sample size of one, I can’t do anything too crazy.
All this messing around with cognitive world entry has led to a pretty interesting discovery,
though. As it turns out, that veil that separates the two worlds is something that can be
weakened. Repeated and consistent entry to the same pocket of cognition leaves a signature
that we can record.
It doesn’t work as well on weaker manifestations, or on ones that are too broad,
unfortunately. Even when the subject shifted in and out of Mementos repeatedly for hours, the

change in reading was so minuscule that it could only really be discounted as normal
variability.
Strong manifestations, though- now that lights up like a beacon!
The journal devolves into Wakaba’s excited ramblings about the exact method behind this
particular method of interacting with the Metaverse, and, ah , Shido thinks:
Here’s something worthwhile.
It’s unfortunate, that Wakaba never discovered a way to pierce that veil without Akechi’s
particular brand of nonsense, but this will do just nicely.
Takahashi is useless at discovery, but at least he’s competent enough at replicating results.
Shido makes a call. Sitting through the psientist’s useless blubbering is a chore, but he’ll
endures it.
“W-we could actually do that right now, sir.” Takahashi stutters, after Shido recites his
request, “We have all the equipment-”
“You have the capacity to take initiative.” Shido says mildly.
It almost sounds like Takahashi chokes at that, “Of course, sir. I-it will take -um- and hour,
perhaps?”
“Call me back when it’s done.” Shido orders, “Don’t keep me waiting.”
“I’d never dream of it-”
Shido hangs up before Takahashi can spew another stream of nothing.
He makes another call.
“Shido-san.” The SIU director’s voice filters through the receiver. “To what do I owe the
pleasure?”
The director sounds almost smug, to receive this call. He always was such an incurable suck
up. If Akechi weren’t being a stubborn brat, this man would likely be dead by now.
It’s really too bad. He’ll have to commission the cleaner, later.
“I have a favour to ask of you.” Shido begins, crisp. “I’d like you to be prepared to mobilise
some of your officers.”
“O-of course!” The director gets out, unable to erase the surprise in his voice, “Where and
when?”
“Just stay on alert.” Shido snaps, “I’ll contact you.”
“Right you are, sir.” The director says briskly, “I’ll be waiting.”

their combined cards. Makoto wastes no time marching towards the stairs leading to the
bridge of judgement, Akechi and Ann left to trail behind her.
Makoto forcefully shoves the card under her name into the machine.
One-hundred thousand coins are required to activate the bridge of judgement, The machine
announces, Pay?
“Yes.” Makoto says aloud, “Please.” She tacks on.
A beat.
“Well done.” Sae’s voice mocks through the machine. “I’m surprised to see you’ve made it
this far.”
Makoto’s fists are clenched tight, “Well.” She says haltingly, “We did.”
The shadow hums, “I can see that.” She laughs, “Unfortunately, the price-”
“Is now one million coins?” Akechi interrupts. It was a lot more fun letting all this play out
when he was taking everyone by surprise, but now he just wants to get this over with. “I think

Akechi adds the Yuko Suzui card to the machine, and allows himself to indulge in Sae’s

Sae chuckles lowly, “I should have expected something like this.” There’s a chime from the

play.”

Ann puffs out her cheeks, “Don’t like the sound of that…” She mumbles, as the scale bridge

The layout of the floor is different.
It’s hard to miss. The plinth where the unformed treasure used to sit is gone entirely, replaced

At the table’s head, Sae’s shadow waits, leaning back in her chair with a mocking smirk.
Great.

Akechi concedes to this, stiffly sitting down as Ann and Makoto hover at his sides.

“The bet is simple.” Sae’s shadow says, smile curving like a knife, “If you win, you get to

She deals out the next round, and shoots Akechi a meaningful look as she passes him his set

Akechi is careful not to show any reaction, suddenly grateful for his helmet-like mask as he

Playing the long game, is she? Clever.

A two of spades, a five of hearts, a queen of hearts, two sevens, spades and diamonds, and…

Funny.
Akechi lets the joker card drop into his tattered sleeve.

“Four of a kind.” Sae calls, placing four sixes and a five down.
Akechi would be very hard-pressed to beat that even under normal circumstances. “Onepair.” He says, revealing his measly double sevens and other assorted nonsense with a
flourish.

Seven, this time. He must commend Makoto’s sleight of hand. Though, he hopes she isn’t
playing it too risky to speed things up.
Two twos, diamonds and hearts, two kings, spades and diamonds, a seven of diamonds, a
jack of spades, and an ace of spades.
Options, then.
Choose wisely. Robin warns.
Going by pure card value, it would make sense to pocket the ace and a king, or perhaps the
pair of kings.
But in order to beat Sae, he needs a perfect hand. Or, as near perfect as he can feasibly get.
The joker swimming in the fabric of his sleeve is already a major hurdle cleared, but…
He can only assume that Sae’s cognition means he will always be dealt a hand that is of lesser
value than hers.

He lets the twos drop into his sleeve, alongside the joker.
“Full house again.” Sae says with some amusement, placing down her three queens and two
kings.
“One pair. Again.” Akechi says flatly, placing down his remaining cards.
“Hey, so how long is this gonna go on for?” Ann hisses in his ear.
“We are infinitely lucky that Sae-san has more patience than you.” Akechi hisses back.
“Hey!”
Akechi sees Makoto’s lips twitch up at their back and forth, as she starts dealing out the fifth

“Hold on.”
Makoto freezes.
“You dealt two cards at once, there.” Sae accuses, eyes narrowed.
Makoto opens and closes her mouth, “…My mistake.” She eventually says. “Shall I

“No.” Sae interrupts, “They don’t.” She clicks her fingers, “I think we’ll be going back to

Makoto stumbles back as a shadow bursts into existence at her feet. She glares, and shuffles

The shadow dealer reshuffles the cards, and begins setting them out.
Akechi picks up his hand.
“Are we set?” Makoto whispers a question, having no way of knowing which cards she had
actually sent Akechi’s way.
Akechi grins in response.

“Five of a kind.” Akechi announces, spreading four twos and a joker onto the table.

Shit, shit, those words are familiar; they need to calm her down now unless they want this to
break out into a brawlThe dealer shadow bursts into nonexistence, and Sae’s hat flutters to the ground as she
staggers back, “You think you can play games, here? You think this is all so funny, one big

Akechi feels his lip curl, so much for deescalating, “You-”
“And what do you think you are, sis?” Makoto shouts.
The shadow’s eyes flick to her sister, “Stay out of this, Makoto.”
“No!” Makoto slams her knuckles down against the table, “No, I’ve been here this whole
time, and you haven’t even cared! And now you’re telling me to stay out?”
“You’re acting,” Sae says, clipped, “Like a child.”
“Really?!” Makoto sputters, face flushing red, “You’re the one sitting here and cheating at

“You want to play holier-than-thou?” The shadow scoffs, “Don’t act like you’re some

“This isn’t the real world!” Makoto’s jaw audibly grinds, “Do you think dad would have-”

“What do I care?!” Sae shouts, “He’s dead, all because he seemed to think upholding justice

The red and black dissipates all at once, the shadow dropping to her knees, barely visible

Makoto doesn’t immediately fire anything back. She takes a shaky breath, clenching and

“The cognition of me.” Akechi clarifies, “He could get away with anything, until he couldn’t.

Akechi stares, waiting.

Sae glares at him, “Then what were you wasting everyone’s time for?”

The Moon grows to rank eight.
Sae stares him down, “Get out.”
Akechi scoffs, and turns around to walk back to Ann and Makoto.
Makoto shuffles on her feet.

“How about you say all that shit to her in reality and find out?”
Makoto laughs, brighter, but only just, and the High Priestess grows to its seventh rank.
“Let’s get out of here.” She announces, brushing past Ann and Akechi.

Ann chews on her lip, looking more than a bit out of her depth, “Think it’s fine if we leave

“I’m with Niijima on this one.” Akechi continues, “Let’s get the hell out of here.”
***
The sea of souls holds endless depths.
It shouldn’t. There are a finite number of humans, and there always will be, even as time
marches on and the sea is less an ocean and more a rushing river. By logic, there should
always be a quantifiable amount of information trapped within the depths of the collective
human unconscious.
And yet, it is infinite.
There isn’t much point to dwelling on it.
The fact that it is infinite is rather helpful, in fact. It’s almost amusing, that it is humanity’s
own repressed thoughts that continue to nearly bring about their destruction- some in more
permanent ways than others.
Some of these beings are more powerful than others, too.
The god tests the stretch of its face in a wide grin. It never quite gets old, knowing that he definitively, categorically, quantifiably- holds more power than the old fool that could do
nothing but spout nonsense about bonds right up until his sanctuary was entirely usurped.
He oughtn’t be overconfident. He can’t help but indulge himself, sometimes.
It is something of a miracle, that the unfathomable depths of humanity also spawned a being
that can fold time at its whim. The god admits that he thought time to be absolute, immutable,
like death; but apparently his opponents in this game are sore losers.
All it grants him is a second chance to win. To have come so close, only to be beaten by his
opponent’s champion that crumbled not a month later almost stings.
Not this time.
It is irritating, though, the god thinks, that his own champion is being such a bother. And that
shared link the wildcards both have- the Faith, or the Magician. The god finally got a closer
look, once the trickster remembered his bond with her, but- nothing. Nothing out of place at
all. By all accounts, an entirely normal human girl, aside from the ability to wield a persona.
No matter. She’s not relevant to his game.

The game half feels like a farce, by now. The rules have been entirely discarded. If chess
pieces realise they’re on a board, then is there any point to continue playing?
Of course there is. Just because all participants in this wager are being difficult, doesn’t mean
that the god isn’t in a position to get things back on track.
But how to go about doing so?
The border between Mementos and reality is malleable by design. It was quite the task, to
create something that would only shatter when the god willed it.
Or, more accurately, something that would only shatter when the time was right.
Unfortunate, now that the god needs to do some intervention.
The Velvet Room rumbles as he tugs on another thread.
There’s a knock at the door -a courtroom, for now- and the voice of the shattered attendant
filters through, “Everything okay in there?” high and concerned.
“Just fine, girls.” The god replies, dropping the thread.
Strength and Temperance. Not nearly as obedient as they ought to be.
But, as they are, they can do nothing.
Another thread, another rumble.
There’s another frantic knock, “Are you sure?”
The god doesn’t bother with a response.
Perhaps the next thread will be the one.

Something doesn’t feel right.
Not that anything ever quite does, in the Metaverse. But especially now, Akechi feels Robin
sound an alarm every which way at nothing at all.
He spots the twins at the entrance to the Velvet Room. Justine is furiously rifling through her
clipboard. Caroline is chewing on her lip, visible even from the other end of the entrance.
Akechi turns away.
“Are we ready?” Ann asks, looking exhausted.
“Yes.” Makoto says, just as tired, “I think I could collapse.”
“Try and hold out.” Akechi says, mild. “We’ve got to trek through Mementos yet.”

“You can’t drive.” Makoto points out.

Incapable of Navigation. The Nav chimes.
Akechi blinks.

Ann looks nervously at her phone, “Uhm?”

Incapable of Navigation. The Nav repeats.
Akechi opens his mouth to make a suggestion of his own-Before experiencing a very uncomfortable sensation.
When exiting the Metaverse, or shifting between two distortions, one is often braced for it.
Even if they aren’t, it’s still something that fades in its intensity the more it is experienced.
It’s familiar, like a sailor laughing off the rock and sway of waves.
This is not that.
A violent displacement, like being grabbed by the throat and pulled, back, far, out- left?
Down. Up.
Akechi’s knees slam to the floor as the world rights itself, digging into dirt and prickling

“Who’s there?” A sharp voice rings out.

“What if we drag someone in with us?” Makoto hisses back.

“Turn it on silent.” Makoto reminds her.

Ann nods, tapping at the side buttons, and types out Mementos rather than saying it. She

What little she knows, is this:
One, there is allegedly another world that can be accessed through and app on certain

Two, Akechi is adamant that he is the true culprit behind the mental shutdowns and psychotic

Three, he has alarmingly little to say on the matter of the Phantom Thieves.

he went wrong.
Of course Sae wouldn’t take kindly to the possibility that someone had tried to change her
heart. Akechi would have reacted the same way, in her position. Why should she help
someone who potentially deemed her in need of a personality rewrite?
Leaving him to rot is entirely reasonable.
Akechi supposes that unless the Phantom Thieves have some grand plan to spirit him away as

Chapter 78
Chapter Summary

sweeping the mess.

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

The drive to Leblanc is tense.
Six people must spread out across five seats, for one. Ren decides to focus on the discomfort
for lack of space rather than the unconscious boy laid out delicately over the three in the back
seats, rather than the sharp eye that glances at them through the rearview mirror, rather than
the dial tone as Ann finally decides that the rest of the Phantom Thieves are no longer in need
of live updates.
Takemi is not happy to see them. Ren supposes it’s for the best that she’s already clued into
all their thieving exploits by now, or the need for explanations would have taken longer than
he could stand.
“Isn’t he supposed to be dead?” Is her snappish commentary, even as she rushes to check
Goro’s breathing, deliberating as to whether a blood test is worth it.
Ren can’t remember if Takemi gave him a blood test, when Sae had dragged him to the
clinic’s door. He chooses to not give any advice. He doubts it would have been seriously
considered in the first place.
“He was able to remain conscious for nearly three hours after he was drugged.” Sae informs
Takemi, as Ren and the other thieves hover uncomfortably in the corner of the exam room.
Ren also can’t remember how long he was able to stay conscious after he was drugged. He
thinks it was longer than three hours. Though, he also thinks he may have passed out a few
times intermittently, so maybe it doesn’t count.
He tries to muster some dull satisfaction at the thought he may have managed to beat Goro
out on this fact. He doesn’t succeed.
“I’m guessing it’s wishful thinking to hope that you know exactly what they gave him?”
Takemi turns her head towards Sae slightly.
“I haven’t the foggiest.” Is the grim reply.
Takemi clicks her tongue, and gets back to work.

“…They would have called it ‘Truth Serum’.” Ren speaks up.
“I hate to break it to you, Amamiya, but that’s pretty much meaningless.” Takemi tells him
without turning around, “You can call anything truth serum if it makes the recipient barely
lucid enough to remember to hold their tongue.”
“Akechi kept a pretty good grip on his.” Sae offers.
Takemi shrugs, “Maybe he’s got a high tolerance.” She scribbles something down, “Maybe
their drug is shit. Maybe he’s just got an especially good hold on what he wants to say, even
when he’s barely conscious. Who knows?”
Not Ren, certainly.
“…Is he going to be okay?” Sumire asks quietly.
Takemi’s frustration softens slightly, “Good news and bad news. Good, is that I think I can
pretty safely say he’ll be fine. His breathing and heart-rate are normal, and his
unconsciousness seems to be caused by exhaustion more than anything else, since he can still
be roused and reacts to external stimuli. He doesn’t have any broken bones, either.”
Ren feels something in his chest unclench. Of course Goro will be fine. Ren was.
“Bad news,” Takemi continues, “Is that this is going to have to resolve on its own. Nothing’s
broken, but a hell of a lot is still cracked and bruised. I can’t counter the drug, since I don’t
know what it is, and I can’t prescribe him painkillers for the time being since I’d rather not
make a cocktail of his bloodstream.”
“Oh.” Ann is the only one to respond.
Makoto eventually takes a breath, “Can he be relocated?”
“Is it also wishful thinking to suggest a hospital? ” Takemi mutters.
“A hospital is out of the question.” Sae says sharply, “And I hope we’ve made it clear that
this encounter is to stay strictly between us. I’ll pay you, if need be.”
Takemi throws up her hands, “I don’t need to be bribed. Forget about payment. Consider it as
my continued return favour for the guinea pig over there.” She nods towards Ren, and levels
with a glare that clearly expresses don’t make this a habit.
I wouldn’t dream of it. Ren attempts to inject into his raised eyebrows.
“Where should we take him?” Sumire asks.
“He can stay in the clinic overnight, if you need.” Takemi offers, before glancing at the clock
on the wall, “Or the morning, rather. If you do move him, I’d suggest somewhere close by,
just in case something goes south and I have to be there quickly.”
“Is Leblanc compromised?” Ren turns to Sae.

Sae shakes her head, “Not… immediately. I had it and the Sakura residence on my list of
places to raid, but only because I was searching for any remnants of Wakaba Isshiki’s
research that I suspected Sakura-san might be hiding.”
“He isn’t.” Sumire says.
Sae gives her an odd look, and Sumire shrinks back, “…I was beginning to suspect as much,
but I was desperate.”
Ren doesn’t think this is a conversation for a crowded clinic.
“Let’s go to Leblanc.” He says, and no one protests.
***
Leblanc is worse, Ren decides.
He didn’t expect Sojiro to still be here in the early hours of the morning.
“Where the hell have you been-” Sojiro starts, halfway to livid before he spots the entourage
trailing behind Ren.
“Sorry, boss.” Takemi shoves her way to the front of the crowd, Sae closing the door behind
her with Goro’s arm slung over her shoulder. “Do you have anywhere I can lie this kid
down?”
“The attic.” Ren says immediately, and Takemi nods, gesturing for Sae to follow her.
“Wh- hey! ” Sojiro protests, eyes snapping into a glare as he sees Sae.
“Apologies for the intrusion.” Sae says briskly, striding towards the stairs, Goro in tow, “But
this is urgent.”
Sojiro finally seems to register the unconscious teenager in their midst, and splutters, turning
to Ren and the other thieves present for an explanation.
“I’m here!” Leblanc’s door bursts open with a flash of orange, as Futaba gasps for air,
Morgana securely in her arms, “M’ here- what’s happening? Is everything fine?”
“Is Akechi okay?” Morgana asks, hopping to the floor.
“He’s fine.” Makoto says. “As fine as he can be, at least.”
“What the hell happened? ” Sojiro demands. “Why is that prosecutor here?”
“She’s helping.” Ren quickly says.
“Someone’s going to have to keep an eye on Mr Detective.” Takemi announces, coming back
down the stairs. “Treat it like you’re taking care of someone who’s drunk to the point of

unconsciousness. No painkillers, plenty of water once he’s awake, I wouldn’t risk solids,
make sure he doesn’t choke on his own vomit.” She gives Sojiro a stern look, “Got all that?”
“I-” He stammers, “ Yes, but, god, is anyone going to tell me what’s going on?”
“The police have unsavoury interrogation practices.” Sae explains as she also returns from
the attic. Ren snorts.
Sojiro glares at her, “That something you did?”
“I wasn’t the one who left him like that if that’s what you’re asking.”
“Sojiro!” Futaba quickly interjects, “It’s fine! She’s on our side!”
Sae blinks, taken aback by the sudden vote of confidence. “…And you’re…?”
“Uh.” Futaba wilts slightly, “Oracle.”
“I figured.” Sae nods. “Now, if you don’t mind, I’d like an explanation as well. A full one,
that is. Akechi has a habit of painting a very... specific picture.”
Ren glances at the other thieves, “…Should we call everyone else?”
Morgana’s tail lashes with agitation. “Should so many people be coming here at once?”
“Do they even know Akechi’s missing yet?” Makoto points out, “But, using public transport
at this time of the morning might be suspicious…”
“Noir.” Ren says immediately, “She can probably drive everyone.”
“I’ll call her.” Ann says, taking her phone out of her pocket.
“You do that.” Takemi says dispassionately, “I don’t want any part in this. Call me if you
need me. I’ll be awake.”
She wastes no time pushing past the blockade at the door, the bell tinkling with her exit.
Sojiro sighs, weary, pushing up his glasses to rub at the bridge of his nose, “…Someone
should head upstairs.”
“…I will, if it’s going to be some time before the rest of your… friends show up.” Sae offers,
giving a short bow before she turns on her heel.
Ren nods, and swallows, throat dry.
“Won’t be long!” Ann announces.
Any time at all is far too long.
***

It is in stiff silence that the current occupants of Leblanc wait.
Sumire has taken to quietly swinging her legs back and forth on what she remembers is
Goro’s preferred chair at the bar. The others are each scattered between the ground floor and
the attic, wandering aimlessly and shuffling about as the clock ticks on.
The gaze of the Sayuri on the wall seems especially piercing today, Sumire thinks. She looks
away.
She startles, as Ren marches down the attic stairs.
“I’m going for a walk.” He announces, in the midst of pulling a jacket over his shoulders.
Sojiro looks up from where he’d been wiping down the counter for the fifth time this hour,
“…That’s dangerous.”
“Not far.” Ren says, not particularly reassuring, “Bye.”
The bell is jostled violently as he slams the door shut.
Ann, nestled into one of the booths with Morgana, frowns, “Everyone should be here soon.”
“I don’t think he should be walking around right now.” Sojiro mutters, belated in his protests.
Sumire stands abruptly, surprising herself, “I’ll go after him.” She says. I need to go for a
walk too, she doesn’t say.
Sojiro sighs, not bothering to tell her off as she leaves.
Sumire almost starts on a walk around the block as she gently closes the door behind her,
before a shadow in the laundromat catches her eye.
She carefully knocks on the door frame as she approaches, and yet Ren still jumps a metre
high, curled into the corner, backed against the dryers.
“Hello.” Sumire says, awkward as she’s ever been.
Ren breathes out slowly, “Hey.”
He doesn’t say anything more. Sumire shuffles over to the washing machines, and pulls
herself up to sit on top of one. She hesitates, before pulling her feet up to sit cross-legged.
“How are you feeling?” She asks, feeling that speaking any louder than a whisper will be far
too loud in the quiet of the early morning.
“How do you think?” Ren snaps.
Today, or yesterday, Sumire thinks, is entirely beyond the realm of what she cares to handle.
She didn’t enjoy sitting through a forced and overly charged conversation with Doctor
Maruki. She didn’t enjoy hearing that Goro was in mortal danger and there was nothing she

could do. She, at present, doesn’t enjoy having to face the brunt of Ren’s ire, wherever it is
being directed.
“Bad.” Is the only answer Sumire can offer. She’s feeling it quite potently, herself.
Ren doesn’t respond, beyond a derisive snort. Sumire presses her lips together.
She flinches when Ren slams his fist against the dryers with enough force to rattle the whole
wall.
“ God. ” He hisses, “Just, fuck. ”
Sumire makes an effort to stop gripping the edge of the washing machines so tightly.
Ren sniffs, furiously wiping at his eyes, “Why the fuck did you go to Maruki’s palace?”
“Futaba asked.” Sumire says simply, “And I wanted to.”
“Why didn’t you tell anyone. ”
Why indeed? “I think Futaba wanted to be discreet.” Sumire explains slowly, “And I didn’t
want to bother anyone.”
And, she also wanted to be discreet.
Ren glares at the floor, lips pressed in a sneer. Sumire can only be grateful it isn’t directed at
her. “What happened in there?”
“Nothing interesting.” Sumire lies, “I ran into Doctor Maruki’s shadow, but he was just-”
Hm. “-Normal.”
Ren stares at her flatly. Sumire refuses to crack.
“…Are you going to come back inside?” Sumire hazards.
“No.” Ren snips.
Alright.
Sumire can wait.
She sees Ren open his mouth, before grinding his teeth together. She waits a little more.
“Do you think we can do anything?” He asks, voice small.
“What do you mean?”
“I mean this. ” Ren hisses, “It’s all happening the same. Okumura isn’t dead, but he might as
well be. We have to play by Shido and Yaldabaoth’s rules. This bullshit still happened, but it
was Goro instead of me.”

Oh.
Sumire had tried to stop thinking about this very thing shortly after she realised that
Mementos was set along rails in more ways than one.
Her hands tighten on the edge of the washing machines again.
“And it’s smaller stuff too.” Ren continues, words spilling in a wave, “Mona still ran off.
Some of us still ran around in Niijima’s palace without changing her heart. And didn’t
everything go to hell on the same day you awakened your persona last time?”
It did.
“Haru-senpai awakened her persona earlier, didn’t she?” Sumire says.
“And what good did that do?” Ren snarls, pushing off the dryers, “Is that all this shit is?
Moving grains of sand from a pile and calling it a change?”
“If you move enough…” Sumire trails off.
“Yaldabaoth won’t let us! ” Ren shouts, “ He’s the one who cut off our access to the
Metaverse, even if he can’t do it right. What, are people going to be diving around corners to
take a shot if Goro manages to live past December? What if has to be an equivalent exchange
to get what we want? What if someone else-”
He cuts himself off, and takes a shuddering breath.
(Something in Sumire recognises this conversation as very dangerous.
This, she thinks, is the kind of thinking, the kind of despair, that led Ren to considering
Maruki’s reality a worthy trade to get what he wants. To disregard everything else that
matters.
Tunnel vision, she muses with a dull sense of fear, will get them all killed.
Sumire believes she harboured a fundamental misunderstanding of Ren, in their initial
friendship. Maybe she only saw what she wanted to see. Maybe she only say what Ren
wanted her to see.
She is quite sick of falling for masks. Of not being trusted with what lies beneath. Kasumi,
Doctor Maruki, Ren, hell, even Goro, she never gets it until it’s too late. A second chance
means nothing when half her problems are already too far gone.
How dare he, Sumire seethes, he has a second chance too, and it’s like he’s not even trying.
Why does everyone keep giving up before the finish?)
“That’s bullshit.” Sumire blurts.
Ren is appropriately startled.

Sumire jumps off her perch. “What if you’re right?” She demands.
Ren blinks, “Huh?”
“ What if you’re right? ” She pushes, “What if we can’t change anything? What are you
going to do about it?”
Ren stares.
“Take Maruki’s deal again?” She accuses, distantly surprised at the words tumbling from her
mouth.
Ren gapes at her, swallows, “No.”
“Then what are you saying? ” She begs.
Ren clicks his jaw together, and has no answer.
“…You’re right.” He finally says, very quietly.
About what? Sumire wants to ask, but she has the sense that Ren isn’t quite sure either.
“I just needed to get out.” He adds, “…I used to like it, when I could get him to crack. To
show me something he didn’t mean to.”
Sumire can hazard a fair guess for who ‘he’ is.
“I still like it.” Ren admits, “But it usually only happens now when he’s upset with me.”
“…Is that different from before?” Sumire asks, without the usual humour she would be able
to muster.
Ren snorts anyway. “Sometimes. I like getting a rise out of him. When it’s intentional. I like
it when he trusts me, too.”
He trails off, looking somewhere into the middle distance.
“I hate seeing him like this.” He murmurs, “I hate that someone else did it.”
You wanted to be trusted with this. Sumire reminds herself.
She gathers the fragments that Ren has gifted her into her heart, and vows to guard them
closely.
She smiles, and says: “Let’s go back inside.”
Ren nods dully, and quietly trails behind her.
***

Sae nearly jumps out of her skin when she’s met with rusty eyes, bleary and glazed but
decidedly open.
“You’re awake.” She comments, brisk.
“G’morning to you to.” Akechi mutters.
“You’re technically correct.” Sae tells him, “It’s three in the morning.”
Akechi looks like he has half a mind to go right back to sleep.
“How are you feeling?” Sae ventures, and adds, tentatively, “…Do you need more rest?”
“I feel,” Akechi pauses to swallow, “Like shit. I don’t suppose you know where we are?”
Sae is surprised he doesn’t recognise the place. A bit concerning, but it is quite dark, she
supposes. “Leblanc. The attic.”
Akechi scowls viciously.
“Where’s…” He frowns, like he can’t decide where he’s going, “People.” He eventually
settles on.
“Downstairs.” Makoto had been up here, earlier, but she skittered off to discuss something
with her friends. Sae finds she prefers the solitude (unconscious teenager notwithstanding)
over Sakura’s cold glares, or an uncomfortable staring contest with a cat she has been
informed is entirely sapient.
“Why Leblanc?” Akechi pushes, cutting so bluntly to the core of the problem in a way that
Sae doesn’t recall him ever doing. The riddles and smoke and mirrors were part and parcel
with the act, she gathers.
“It was closest to Joker’s…” Sae concedes that the clinic looked official enough, but the
practitioner herself would not be out of place in a line of doctors she’s questioned about their
dealings in organised crime, “Medical professional.”
Akechi stares flatly. “It’s annoying he gets a back-alley doctor.”
Sae raises an eyebrow at the show of petulance. He usually only whips that out when he’s
demanding free dinner. “As opposed to?”
“Sewing myself up.” Akechi grumbles, and Sae very suddenly wishes she hadn’t asked.
She coughs, “…The rest of the Phantom Thieves will be arriving soon, I hear.”
“Joy.” Akechi bites out, sounding like he’s feeling anything but.
“It would be good if you could stay awake, while they explain everything.” Sae ignores him,
“I assume you’ll want to interject.”

She takes Akechi’s glare to mean she’s correct.
Neither of them have anything more to say. Sae recognises with grim inevitability that this
will likely change very quickly once she is granted the full story.
She can’t deny she’s curious for the identities of the Phantom Thieves that have eluded her
for months, that are painfully obvious as Akechi put it.
She supposes she will find out very quickly, she thinks, as the bell to Leblanc chimes loudly
as the door swings open, demanding voices wafting up the stairs.
***
They discuss everything in the attic, given that Akechi is hardly in any state to tolerate being
sat at a booth for any extended period of time.
Sae is surprised at some of the remaining thieves’ identities. Some, less so. Ryuji Sakamoto,
whom she recognises as a person of interest from her investigation into Shujin, and Yusuke
Kitagawa are hardly shocking. Haru Okumura throws her for more of a loop.
The others introduce themselves by name, though Sae had managed to place most of them
already.
And, so, with everyone present, they explain.
***
Apparently, time travel is something that exists.
It’s hardly consolation that Sakura isn’t taking the news any better.
Sae had already suspended her disbelief enough to accept that the Metaverse exists. She had
already been halfway to doing so months ago, when she went prying for Isshiki’s research,
but empirical evidence tipped the scale the rest of the way.
She sits through long-winded explanations of other worlds, of assassinations, of tyrannical
politicians, of thieves, of a god,
She really isn’t quite sure why she feels the need to draw the line at time travel, but a line
does need to be drawn somewhere. Maybe the second god should have been the line. Sakura
looks like he wanted to draw the line back at the assassinations.
Understandable, given the uncomfortable revelation of Wakaba Isshiki’s fate.
Akechi regards the conversation coolly, seeming almost bored. Sae almost manages to feel
impressed at how detached he’s being.
She wonders how either of the Sakuras can stand to have him under their roof, at present. She
wonders how Amamiya and Okumura can stand to seem so close to him. Not to mention the
others, who should surely have their own grievances by proxy.

Sae isn’t quite sure where she stands.
“When I asked for a better explanation,” Sakura mutters, “I hadn’t been looking for… that. ”
“Tough.” Amamiya fires back, having grown increasingly more clipped as the conversation
had continued.
The cat meows, and the younger Sakura mumbles something in return.
“Mona-chan is right.” Okumura says thinly, “We ought to discuss where to go from here.”
“Has the plan really changed?” Akechi speaks up for the first time in a while.
Ah, their plan.
Sae can’t say she approves. Of anything, really, but what can she do?
“…Let’s figure that out, shall we?” Makoto says primly, and Sae readies herself for another
conversation she can barely follow.
***
Haru isn’t entirely sure where she stands.
With most revelatory events in her life, she has been granted the grace of at least a few hours
to decompress, to process. No such luck, this time.
She hasn’t bothered making heads or tails of how she feels. Ann’s timely request to organise
a way for the scattered thieves to converge at Leblanc without wandering the streets in the
early hours of the morning was a welcome one, if only to give her something to do.
And now, she’s surrounded by a smattering of people who got hurt while going behind her
back.
Maybe she’ll settle on irritated, now that she’s measured it out in her head.
“I don’t see what has to change.” Goro says, half propped up on Ren’s frankly terrible
bedding, “The situation is hardly any different.”
“Won’t Shido be looking for you?” Yusuke asks with a frown.
“He was doing that already.” Goro points out, “And given that I sincerely doubt they’re going
to broadcast my involvement with this little jailbreak, my position with the general public
remains much the same, as well.”
“Infamy wise, we’re about to make some waves.” Ren mutters, “So everything is still on
track with Mementos.”
“Will they even broadcast this, though?” Haru asks, “Surely Shido and the police won’t want
to inform the public of their failure.”

“Couldn’t they just, I dunno, say they won?” Ryuji leans back in his chair.
“Can they even do that? Without proof?” Ann asks, twisting her hair around a finger.
“Shido could.” Sakura speaks up, “If that little plan of yours worked last time, it’s not like
they’ll need to present the media with a corpse. And it’s definitely something he’d do.”
“But that seems like a recipe for trouble.” Niijima interjects, “ He knows you all haven’t been
defeated, so claiming a premature victory is practically asking for you to undermine him.”
“But what else can he do?” Makoto furrows her brow, “The public is already riled up that we
haven’t been caught, and Shido’s rise to becoming prime minister relies on his popularity.
Saying that he’s responsible for our leader’s capture is a sure-fire way to achieve that.”
“Is he just going to try and hunt us down extra hard?” Futaba frowns, “I mean, he managed to
track you three down while you were in a palace, somehow.”
“How did he do that, by the way?” Morgana jumps out of Futaba’s lap to narrow his eyes
suspiciously in Goro’s direction.
“Not a clue.” Goro deadpans in response, “Luck, perhaps? But we shouldn’t talk in circles as
to something we can’t begin to guess. Shido will do something in response, clearly, but what
are we going to do?”
“We can still do our plan with Shido’s inner circle, right?” Sumire wrings her hands together.
“ We can still do that plan.” Ren says pointedly, and turns to Goro, “You’re sitting out.”
“Excuse me?” Goro says, very calmly.
“You’re injured.”
“I’ll heal.”
Ren rolls his eyes, “In a few weeks, maybe. But we need to get started now.”
“Injuries are less debilitating in the Metaverse.” Goro snaps with a scowl.
Niijima frowns, “Didn’t you say that real world injuries can’t be healed there, either?”
“They can’t.” Ren confirms.
“I am not sitting out for Shido’s palace.” Goro snarls.
“You don’t have to.” Haru speaks up abruptly, not caring to see this argument continue, “We
have a month and a half, yes? …Even if that isn’t enough time for you to recover entirely, it’s
enough for you to settle.”
“Are you saying we should waste that much time?” Makoto says, half-accusatory.

Haru quickly shakes her head, “Of course not. But, we could begin working on the less…
emotionally charged palaces while Goro-kun is out of commission, and leave Shido’s palace
for later. It was already implied that were doing so initially, wasn’t it?”
“I… suppose.” Makoto concedes.
“’Kechi’s one of our heavy hitters, though.” Futaba frowns, tucking her knees to her chest,
“Do we really want to risk running into unknown palaces one man down?”
“I’ve been to one of them before.” Goro interrupts, still looking indignant, “You’d have a far
easier time with my help.”
“Sure.” Ren says dismissively, “But we can also just scout the palaces like we always do.
We’ve still got two navigators in the game.”
“That aside,” Yusuke tilts his head, “Might I remind everyone that we only have a month and
a half to complete three -potentially four, depending on our developments with the Cleanerpalaces? Even if all of us were in fighting shape, do we think this is enough?”
Sumire bites at her lip, “We said we’d try…”
Yusuke waves a hand, “I’m not saying we shouldn’t. But I think we should think of potential
ways to… cut corners.” He turns to Goro, “Operating even with one member down is a part
of that.”
Goro looks like he has half a mind to pick a fight, so Haru quickly cuts in, “What if we take
that further?”
Ann’s brow furrows, “Work with… even less people?”
Haru huffs a laugh, “In a sense. I mean: split the load. If we conduct multiple palace
explorations at once, we might shave off some time.”
There’s a round of contemplative looks.
“…That sounds unnecessarily dangerous.” Sakura comments gruffly.
“Oh, not really!” Sumire waves her hands placatingly, “Haru-senpai, Goro, and I completed a
full palace, and defeated its ruler, all on our own.”
Niijima blinks, alarmed, “Who?”
“My fiancé.” Haru tells her, stiff, “Ex-fiancé. The calling card we sent him wasn’t addressed
from the Phantom Thieves, and his family likely stopped him from rushing to the media, so
his change of heart wasn’t publicised as such.”
“…It is a bit dangerous.” Ren corrects after a pause.
“Maybe so.” Haru admits, “But our main struggles in palaces have nearly always been thanks
to our encounters with the ruler shadows, once they’re responding to the threat of their

treasure being taken. I’m certainly not suggesting we take on those fights while divided.”
“We were going to do those after we dealt with Shido anyway, yeah?” Ryuji points out,
“Sounds like a pretty good plan to me.”
“Didn’t half of us just get yelled at for running off in palaces on our own?” Futaba mutters to
her knees.
“You did what?” Sakura glares.
“Nothing!” Futaba lies blatantly, “It was fine!”
“…It was a bit stupid.” Sumire admits quietly. Makoto, and Ann pointedly say nothing.
Goro’s brow furrows with some blend of annoyance and confusion. Haru supposes no one
filled him in on Sumire and Futaba’s exploits.
“It was stupid, ” Ren bites out, “Because you didn’t tell anyone. Among other reasons. But
this…” He trails off, rolling his lips together in thought.
“I think it’s a good plan!” Ann declares.
“Me too!” Morgana quickly adds his own agreement, “If we have three palaces we know
about, and we’ve agreed that we’re doing Shido’s all together, then we have two navigators
still in commission to split the team in half.”
“We could, what was it you said Renren?” Ryuji pokes Ren’s arm, “Scout ‘em both, then
figure out who’s good for which palace?”
“I guess…” Ren mumbles, still looking a bit hesitant.

Beginning Navigation. The Nav dutifully responds.
The shift is…
A step to the left of what Haru is so familiar with, by now. She’s knocked off balance, the

Everyone bar Ren and Goro sit in the stained-red version of the attic.

“Oh!” Morgana exclaims, very suddenly a bobble-headed mascot, “It worked!” Haru sees

What, truly, are the consequences for this endeavour?

Weigh the situation, Astarte advises in her mind, And assess.
Goro, obviously; though that’s always been the case.

They decide to wait until November tenth to make a move.
Niijima needs to analyse her standing at work, she explains. There’s no reason to disappear

A moment being two days, of course. She isn’t so optimistic to believe that Goro’s injuries

“It’s Boss.” He corrects, “And I hope you’re right.”

Dragging things into place, and a lesson in patience

Were Akechi in higher spirits, he might find the fact that the rest of the thieves (including,
tentatively, Makoto) have to head off to school in the morning to be a source of amusement.
Given that he is not, he barely manages to muster apathy to start.
The Niijimas along with, naturally, the Sakuras stayed in Leblanc even past when Haru called
drivers to ferry off the others. Being stuck in a building with a series of people who aren’t
directly expressing their grievances is unpleasant at the best of times, but at least they’re all
leaving him alone.
Including, surprisingly, Ren. If there was ever any hovering during the night, Akechi must
have missed it. The thing that might be disappointment doesn’t get the chance to spark before
it fizzles and dies.
He hears Ren and Makoto shuffle out of the cafe in a flurry, and resigns himself to counting
the scuffs on the rafters.
Sae crests the top of the stairs, “Are you awake?”
Akechi would prefer if he wasn’t. “Yes.” He says.
He can’t quite see Sae’s expression from here, but he thinks he sees it twist.
“I can get you some water.” She eventually says.
His throat is quite dry, now that she mentions it. “Please.”
It only takes a minute before Sae is carefully climbing the stairs with a glass in hand. She
places it on Ren’s shelves, avoiding knocking over the pile of trinkets cluttering the surface.

Akechi didn’t ask. “Hm.”

A fair assumption. Akechi had hardly batted an eye when he tripped into the cognitive world.
Of course, he had thought. This was the reward for years of suffering. A chance to win, all for
him and him alone.
Not quite so.
“Do you regret helping yet?” Akechi asks after another sip of water.
“The Phantom Thieves? No.” Is Sae’s surprisingly decisive response.
“Me, then?”
Akechi can hear Sae’s teeth grind.

They had brushed over the fact that they were gunning to take out Shido’s inner circle to

the two of them would be more than happy to let him take the fall.
It’s too bad, then, that he doesn’t want to.
What could he have, if he were freed from the conspiracy? From the whims of gods? Could

It all seemed so out of reach. Something he could never have, doomed by the world and then

Sumire and her hope is awfully tenacious, though.

Being left in the dark is, apparently, something Sae ought to be used to.
She wasn’t aware of it, of course. From Akechi to the SIU Director to any unknown number
of her coworkers, Sae has been surrounded by traitors and self-interested gamblers from the
start.
Now that she’s in the know, doing something as simple as going to work suddenly seems far
more daunting.
She is here, at the behest of the Phantom Thieves, for reconnaissance. They all have to know:
has Sae’s change of allegiance been noticed? Do Shido and his underlings plan to do
anything about it?
It’s mid morning. She’s not going to be abducted or killed in the middle of the office. All she
has to do is find out if they plan to do as such later, and whether she needs to haul herself and
Makoto to share a supposedly inconspicuous living space with Takamaki and Akechi.
