Lying will only look more suspicious. “I did.” Sae confirms.
“Did you forget something?” Sasaki asks with some humour.
“Yes, actually.” Sae pulls out of her ass, “His phone. I forgot to ask him to unlock it, so I
went back to give it a try.”
“Oh, right.” Sasaki clicks his tongue like he just remembered, “How’d that go?”
“He was uncooperative.”
“Unsurprising.” Sasaki says, commiserating, “Can I have that back, by the way? I’ve got to
pass it off to our IT guys to see if they can take a crack at it.”
“Ah,” Sae stutters despite herself, “I handed it off to-” She can’t remember the names of
anyone in this place, “-Sato as I was leaving last night. I’m not sure what he’s done with it
since.”
Sasaki’s eyes are piercing, “Is that so? He must’ve forgotten to mention it. I’ll have to chase
him down.”
Sae hums shortly.
“Oh, while we’re on the subject, actually,” Sasaki barrels on, “Aside from being
uncooperative, did anything about the thief seem off?”
“Off?” Sae echoes, entirely incredulous, “You drugged him. Of course he was off. ”
Sae immediately wishes she could bite the words back, but Sasaki just laughs. “Well, I
suppose that’s true.”
Well, if they aren’t beating around the bush. “You went too far.”
“Come on, Niijima-san,” Sasaki grins, unrepentant, like they’re talking about a mild change
in the weather, “I get that you and the kid were… friendly, but this is a mass murderer we’re
talking about. We needed to get something out of him, even if that turned out to be a dead
end.”
“There’s no definitive proof that the Phantom Thieves are behind the mental shutdowns.” Sae
counters weakly, even if Sasaki is entirely right.
Sasaki raises his eyebrows, “But people have died from the psychotic breakdowns, haven’t
they? And aren’t you the one who made the connection in the first place?”

“It’s a bad idea to jump the gun as a prosecutor before you have all the facts.” Sae recites, and
adds, pointedly, “And as a police officer, too.”
Sasaki shrugs, “Right you are.” He shoots her a look, “I hope you weren’t caught too off
guard when you went to question him. No one told you his identity ahead of time, right?”
Sae bets Sasaki was laughing it up when they ran into each other, knowing the shock she was
about to receive. “No. His familiarity with me wasn’t any help, anyway. I’m as clueless as the
rest of you.”
A bit heavy handed, perhaps, but Sasaki accepts it with a nod. “True enough. Good talking
with you, Niijima-san. I have to get back to work. I have to figure out how the hell we’re
breaking all this to the press.”
Sae raises an eyebrow, “You’re letting them know?”
Sasaki sighs, “I’d love to keep all this under wraps, but it’s going to leak one way or another.
I’m in agreement with all the higher-ups that it’s better we have control over how the story is
presented than not at all.”
Shido is a shrewd man, Sae thinks. At least she’s managed to gain that piece of information
out of this conversation. She wonders how this will be spun.
“I assume you’ll be keeping his identity secret?” Sae pushes.
Sasaki snorts, “Of course. It’d just be downright confusing if we told everyone the truth-”
Sae almost laughs at the choice of words, “-about that. Not even everyone at the precinct
knows. Only you and the folks who arrested him.”
“I suppose it’s in our best interest to keep it that way.” Sae nods stiffly, “Thank you for your
time, Sasaki-san. I’ll let you get back to work.”
“You too, Niijima-san.” Sasaki says with another unreadable smile.
Sae spends the rest of the day pretending to do any substantial work, tucking herself in a
corner and not having to force her expression much at all to make it fiercely unapproachable.
Her conversation with Sasaki only really proved what she already knew. Her actions last
night haven’t gone unnoticed, and she needs to act quickly.
Can she even still go to work, after this? Likely not, she decides; she’s already told Sasaki a
blatant lie about Akechi’s phone, and retreating to an unknown location via the Metaverse
every day will only take her so far. She’ll have to find some excuse to take Makoto out of
school as well, and hopefully find a way to ensure it doesn’t effect her studies.
Sasaki passes by her desk, giving a cheerful wave as he does.
Sae clicks her laptop shut, and prepares to head home for the last time in a long while.
***

There’s news about the escaped Phantom Thief by noon.
A bold play, Akechi thinks. Shido must be awfully confident in the public blaming the
current government, rather than targeting his own lofty speeches. Akechi supposes that is in
line with what the man has been doing thus far.
He stays in Leblanc the whole day. Sakura very awkwardly brings him a plate of curry
around lunch time, with the charming advice of “If you feel like throwing up: don’t.”
It’s a little after when Akechi assumes school has been let out that Ann suddenly materialises
in Leblanc’s attic, apropos nothing.
“Hey!” She says brightly. “Mementos is looking pretty good. It didn’t even feel weird getting
in!”
Akechi hums.
Ann wilts slightly, “…You’re really out of it, huh?”
The drugs wore off quite some time ago, Akechi is quite sure. Or, at least, their primary
effects. He still feels a bit sluggish. “I’m just tired.”
“Yeah, I bet.” Ann bites at her lip. “Well, uh, d’you think you’re all good to come home?”
“Right away?” Akechi raises an eyebrow, ignoring the epithet she chose for her apartment.
Some of Ann’s cheer returns, “Well, duh. We already said my place was still good for hiding
out, and you can’t stay here too long. That bed looks terrible.”
“It is.”
“And where would Ren sleep?”
“The floor.” Akechi deadpans, and adds, belatedly: “Downstairs.”
Ann snickers, “I think he’d probably just take the couch.”
The couch really doesn’t look much better than the floor. “That aside.” Akechi tilts his head,
“I’m not sure I could walk all the way to your apartment in this state.”
Ann frowns, “Why would you have to walk?”
“We’d be taking Mementos, wouldn’t we?” Akechi gives her a look, “Any other way poses
an unnecessary risk, especially when leaving from Leblanc.”
“Ooh, right,” Ann drawls out, “Well, I was actually gonna ask Morgana for help. He can turn
into a car, so…”
Well, that solves that problem. Even as annoying as it sounds.

“Can you enter the Metaverse normally, by the way?” Ann continues, “I guess either me or
Morgana could keep a hand on you or something while we’re inside if you can’t, but it’ll be
easier if we don’t have to.”
“Well, you’re the one with the capacity to test that.” Akechi waves a hand.
Ann makes a face, and quickly takes out her phone, muttering Mementos into the receiver.
The world, to its credit, does warp. Not correctly, though.
The attic flickers red, and Akechi feels an intense pressure suddenly build behind his eyes.
He presses his lips together, and brings a hand up to his head.
“How’s that?” Ann’s voice sounds distant, like separated by several layers of glass.
“Bad.” Akechi grunts out.
The feeling evaporates, and the red drains away.
“You were there.” Ann informs him, “But you looked kinda sick.”
“I think I only made it halfway.” Akechi frowns, “Being in the Metaverse actually made me
feel better, when Sae-san pulled me in. But I doubt that would be the case if I were caught
somewhere in between.”
“Maybe we should still pull you in, then…” Ann hums, “But maybe that’s all? If you’re
halfway to getting there on your own, then I don’t think we’ll have to find a way to keep you
there.”
That’s something. And good news for Joker, too.
There’s the sound of Leblanc’s bell tinkling downstairs, accompanied by Sakura’s grunt of
greeting and some distant chatter. Think of the devil and he shall appear, Akechi supposes.
Ann perks up, “Oh!” She grins, “I’ll go ask Morgana now. Better that we move fast, right?”
Akechi sighs, and nods.
***
The trip back to Ann’s apartment isn’t nearly as painful as Akechi expected it to be.
Ann’s prediction that entering the Metaverse might not be as painful in the event that he’s
dragged in by another party turns out to be correct, as well. It isn’t nearly as tumultuous a
presence as when Sae pulled him in, either.
It’s almost pleasant. Like it used to be. Almost.
Morgana, predictably, grumbles at Akechi the entire way, and immediately shuts up the
minute Ann interrupts with all the grace of a freight train. The analogy, Akechi finds, is also

rather apt when describing her driving skills. He decides not to voice this in case she decides
it’s a good idea to take her hands off the wheel as she goes to protest.
But, eventually, they arrive. Morgana waves them off, and Akechi manages to drag himself
up the stairs.
It turns out exiting the Metaverse is still an ordeal.
“Whoa!” Ann yelps as Akechi immediately staggers, rushing to catch him by the arms, “Umoh, shit, okay, are you okay?”
“No.” Akechi grits.
“Sorry.” Ann babbles nonsensically, and tentatively tugs him over to the couch, “Sorry,
maybe I should have dragged you back through as well- um- do you need water?”
Is that all these people know how to offer? In saying that: maybe. He does have a headache.
But that’s been true all day. “Sure.”
Ann quickly pats his shoulder, and jumps when he flinches, “Um- yes, I’ll get that. Yes.”
She dashes off, and Akechi lets himself sink into the couch pillows. He feels significantly
less dizzy when he doesn’t have to rely on his own body to remain upright.
He hates this. Everything aches. He can’t even walk on his own, bar being in the Metaverse,
but they’re not going to let him in.
Ann comes back with a glass, and hovers uncomfortably, “Do you need…?”
“I can drink water on my own, Takamaki.” Akechi snaps.
Ann rolls her eyes, “Okay, jeez. You just fell over, so I’m sorry for worrying. ”
Akechi makes a point to glare as he snatches the water from her hands, taking a pointed gulp.
No one thus far has truly been treating him like glass, following all this. He has no intention
of letting anyone set a precedent, no matter what state of indisposed he might find himself in.
Ann sighs, and shuffles away to who knows where, leaving Akechi with some peace.
She returns rather quickly, a few plastic bags looped over her arms. She dumps them on the
oft-unused coffee table, and sits herself next to Akechi, leaning forward to rummage through
them.
Akechi shoots her a dubious look.
Ann huffs, “I thought we could do something nice, since you’re back.”
Akechi feels a small twinge of regret for snapping at her. He ignores it. “It’s only been one
night.”

Ann rolls her eyes, but she almost looks amused, “Well, yeah, but it was a long night. ”
Akechi can’t refute that.
“I don’t know how much you feel up to eating.” She continues, “But I bought a bunch of
snacks. And I rented some movies. Plus you seemed like you had fun with Ryuji and I when
we played a bunch of games the other day, so we could do that too, and-”
“Ann.”
She grins sheepishly. “Yeah?”
Thank you gets caught in his throat. “What food did you buy?”
Ann rummages through the bag, “Oh, just some chips, mostly. Plus some ice-cream. That
would go down a bit smoother, wouldn’t it?”
Akechi hums noncommittally.
“I probably shouldn’t get food delivered…” Ann mutters, “Just to be safe, if they see inside
or something. But I could run out and buy something for dinner?”
“That wouldn’t be particularly safe, either. Not in the evening.” Akechi points out, slowly
placing his glass down on the coffee table.
“Mmm, true.” Ann sighs, and taps her finger against her chin, “I guess we’re eating junk
tonight.”
“What a shame.”
Ann snickers, “Good thing no one has to know but us. Oh!” She fishes something else out of
the bag, “I was wondering if we could do this too?” She waves a bottle of nail polish around,
“Just for fun.”
Akechi scowls, “You’re not painting my nails.”
Ann sighs, put-upon, “Well, you can help paint mine. I always mess up my right hand.”
Akechi just waves her off.
Ann turns on the TV, flicking to a random channel and turning the volume way down, “We
haven’t really been taking advantage of this whole roommates business, have we?”
Akechi tilts his head, “If that’s what you’re going to call it. But what is there to take
advantage of?”
Ann groans, “I don’t know! Just, stuff! We’ve had dinner together, sure, but that’s about it!
You’d always run off at night at first, and then we were both running around Niijima’s palace.
Where’s the fun in that?”

Akechi eyes the mess on the coffee table, “…And this is your alternate proposition?”
Ann smiles, “Yeah! It’s not like we have to do it all the time, but Makoto and her sister are
probably gonna be living with us soon, so…”
Akechi makes a face at the reminder.
“Well, I guess we could get the two of them in on this too…” Ann remarks, “Makoto could
have fun with this. And Niijima-san looks like she needs a break.”
Probably. “Sae-san will be on something of an extended break against her will for the
foreseeable future, I think.” Akechi points out.
“All the more reason for her to relax!” Ann punctuates her point by ripping open a bag of
chips. After a moment, she casts a sideways glance towards Akechi, “Are you going to be
okay with them living here?”
“It’s a bit late to ask, don’t you think?” Akechi says drily.
Ann sighs, put-upon, “Yes, yes, I’m terrible. Better late than never though, right? I know you
don’t always get along with Makoto-”
“An understatement.”
“-And I’m not sure if you and Niijima-san are… good or not.” Ann finishes.
Are they? Akechi isn’t sure. Sae seemed at least somewhat hesitant at the thought of dragging
him to the precinct this morning. But that doesn’t really mean much. She seemed more than
happy to leave him for dead, and turned heel on that rather quickly.
“It’s not like they can go anywhere else.” Akechi says diplomatically, “Aside from Haru-san,
your place is the least at risk from all factors, and Haru-san’s place may still be crawling with
police for who knows how long.”
Ann gives him a long look, before shrugging. “Well, good enough for me. Try not to kill each
other.”
“I expect we won’t have to worry about any murder attempts between the four of us.” Akechi
says, bland, “I’d look out for the other thieves, though.”
Ann winces, “Hm. Yeah. I tried forgetting that they were mad at us, honestly.”
“When did they find out?” Akechi asks.
“Around the time I called Ren panicking and saying you’d been arrested.” Ann explains
sheepishly, “No one was happy, but we just kind of… put it off, since everything was going
to hell. You heard that Futaba and Sumire were off on their own palace run, didn’t you?”
“They were what. ”

“Yup.” Ann says with a pop, “The Doc’s palace, too.”
That explains some of what flew over his head during their explanation to Sakura and Sae.
Akechi cannot believe this.
“Don’t get too mad!” Ann quickly waves her hands, “They’re fine, obviously.”
“That’s not the point.” Akechi hisses.
“We were doing the same thing…” Ann mumbles.
“ I remembered what Sae-san’s palace was like. ” Akechi snaps.
“Wouldn’t Sumire remember what Maruki’s palace was like too?” Ann tilts her head.
“Why are you defending them?”
“I don’t want to be a hypocrite!” Ann protests, “Besides, united front of mutineers? Or
something? We outnumber the others if Sumire and Futaba are on our side!”
“We don’t.” Akechi points out, “That just splits the team in half.”
“Oh.” Ann frowns, “Well, Ren can’t yell at all of us.”
“He can.”
“We don’t have to listen to him!”
“That’s true.” Akechi concedes. He had no intention of doing so to begin with.
Ann crosses her arms, presumably in a show of defiance, and frowns, “Has Ren spoken with
you?”
“Since this morning?” Akechi clarifies, “No.”
Ann hums, “Well, good luck when you talk to him.”
Akechi gives her a deadpan look, “Why are you so certain that he’s going to talk to me, and
not all of us?”
“Of course he’ll talk to you!” Ann huffs, “Or Makoto.”
“And not you?” Akechi raises an eyebrow, “Confident, are we?”
“A girl can dream…” Ann mutters, and snatches a chip from the bag.
“Down with the ship.” Akechi says, and steals a chip of his own.
Ann sighs, overly dramatic, and blows some strands of hair out of her face, “Down together,
then.”

Akechi snorts, and the Sun grows to its eighth rank.

School on Tuesday had invited Makoto’s most paranoid sensibilities. She jumped every time
a teacher called on her, or every time a student asked her for help, as though any one of them
could suddenly be a member of Shido’s conspiracy out to get her.
She was almost relieved to come home and find Sae shovelling everything but the kitchen
sink into suitcases.
“They’re onto me.” Sae informs her without preamble, “Or, they will be, in the very near
future. I’m not sure you should go to school tomorrow.”
Makoto considers it. As much as she doesn’t like it… “Won’t it be more suspicious if we
both vanish at the same time?”
“We live together.” Sae points out. “But…” She presses her lips together, “I suppose you
drawing their attention might be a bad idea. There’s no reason to alert them that you’re in on
it.”
“…I’ll go tomorrow.” Makoto decides, “And then we can discuss it with the others.”
Sae nods, and that’s that.
The following afternoon after school, Makoto takes a roundabout route back home, slipping
into Mementos once she’s inside, dragging her travelling case with her.
“Makoto.” Sae blinks at her, apparently having done exactly the same thing barely a moment
prior.
“Oh- good timing, I guess.” Makoto eyes the three cases Sae has surrounded herself with,
“Do you need any help?”
“Yes, please.” Sae huffs. “I don’t think it’s over-packing, since we’re practically moving in,
but it is quite a lot.”
Makoto dutifully takes one of her sister’s cases, and the two of them shuffle towards the door
and down the stairs. The inside of their apartment building in Mementos is quite barren- the
apartment itself almost a complete void. It holds its shape well enough to leave, though, and
the two of them make their way to the street.
“We’re going to have to walk.” Sae mutters, and turns to Makoto, “Do you know the way?”
“Mostly.” Makoto admits, “…From Shibuya, at least.”
“I know the way there. ” Sae says, and starts off, “I guess you wouldn’t, taking the train
every morning.”
Makoto hums in agreement. “…I’ve been hoping to get my driver’s permit soon, actually.”

“Oh?” Sae turns her head slightly, “After all this, I suppose.” She dismisses.
It’s too much to hope for a normal conversation, Makoto thinks. “Yes. After.”
“…It’s been a while since we’ve lived with anyone more than just the two of us.” Sae
eventually says.
What a unique way of putting it. And, frankly, it’s been a while since Makoto has lived with
anyone aside from herself. “I suppose so.”
“I hope there’s no stepping on toes.” Sae continues.
This facade of a regular conversation is starting to become stifling. “Ann is lovely. I’m sure
everything will be fine.”
“No words spared for Akechi?” Sae chuckles.
Makoto grimaces. Holding a conversation with Akechi is already a headache. She’s been
putting off thinking about how that will translate to sharing living space. “I’m sure everything
will be fine.” She repeats.
“I’m sure.” Sae remarks drily.
Makoto bites at her lip.
“What do you think about him?”
Makoto turns to stare at Sae, “What?”
“Akechi.” Sae clarifies, “I spoke with him yesterday, but you’ve known him like this far
longer than I have.”
“Only a few months.” Makoto mumbles.
“Still.”
Makoto sighs, “Well, we’ve never really gotten along.”
Sae has the audacity to look surprised, “Really?”
“You didn’t notice?” Makoto gives her sister an exasperated look. That certainly explains
some things.
Sae readjusts her grip on her two cases, “…No, I suppose I didn’t.”
Makoto presses her lips together.
“I didn’t notice a lot of things.” Sae mutters quietly.
She really didn’t.

***
Ann is delighted, if a bit startled, to see them materialise in her living room.
“So soon?” She asks with such a bright smile that it couldn’t possibly be interpreted as an
accusation.
“Yes.” Sae clicks her tongue, “Sorry to impose, but I have no idea if our apartment is safe.”
“I invited you.” Ann waves her off.
“Will you still be going to work?” Akechi’s voice drifts from the couch.
“No.” Sae explains, clipped, “Sasaki’s on to me.”
“Ah. Him.” Akechi remarks drily.
Makoto raises an eyebrow, “Anyone important?”
“Not anymore.” Is all Akechi offers in response.
Sae narrows her eyes, “He won’t be a problem?”
“Only if you get arrested.” Akechi shrugs.
“Let’s not do that, then.” Ann declares, and swipes Makoto’s suitcases right out of her hands,
“So, I have one extra spare room- I guess you can have that, Niijima-san. Are you cool with
sharing with me, Makoto?”
Better than sharing with Akechi. Or her sister. “Sounds good.”
“Great!” Ann tears off in a whirlwind, presumably towards the guest rooms.
Akechi raises a bemused eyebrow in her direction, before shaking his head and turning to
Makoto, “If you still intend to go to school, you’ll have to stagger your arrival with Ann’s.”
“You think I can still go to school?” Makoto asks.
Akechi casts a look towards Sae, “I don’t know. Can you?”
“I think it’s too risky.” Sae folds her arms, “It’s all well and good that the rest of your friends
can go, but Makoto already has ties to me. If I disappear, they’ll go to Makoto first for
answers.”
Akechi nods slowly, “That’s true.”
“…Can any of us even leave the apartment now?” Makoto mumbles.
“I can’t.” Akechi says.
“I already stand out. I won’t be risking it.” Sae affirms.

Makoto sighs, not bothering to mask her displeasure.
It’s funny. Just a few months ago, Makoto probably would have killed to spend more time
with her sister. Even through such a roundabout and forced way as this. Now, it just sounds
like an argument waiting to happen. And Akechi is here too, so that’s sure to grate on
Makoto’s nerves.
“…I’ll go help Ann with our things.” Makoto announces.
It takes a few tries to open the right door, but Makoto eventually finds Ann in what must be
her own room, just based on the decor.
Ann is sprawled out on her bed, kicking her legs and tapping away at something on her
phone. She looks up, “Oh, hi Mako.”
“Hey.” Makoto awkwardly sits herself down on the corner of the mattress.
Ann shuffles a bit closer, “Everything good out there?”
“It’s fine.” Makoto quickly reassures her. “Sorry. I know you invited us, but it’s still a lot for
you to suddenly take on.”
Ann waves a hand, “It’s whatever. You and Akechi-kun can handle not being at each other’s
throats for at least a few weeks, right?”
Makoto makes a face before she can reign it in.
Ann laughs, “You’ll get away from him when we go palace diving, at least.”
“I suppose so.” Makoto concedes, “I don’t want to avoid him. It’s just…”
She still feelsIt’s not like it was her fault, that this all happened.
She didn’t even want him there. Or maybe she did. She can’t tell. Can Akechi? Can Ann?
She doesn’t know how she’s going to face the others when the veneer of business fades.
Ann pokes her arm, startling her out of her thoughts, “Maybe living with him will make you
better friends.”
Makoto sincerely doubts that. “Maybe.”
Ann carelessly tosses her phone back on the bed, “Well, enough about him.” She grins, “This
is our room now. A home away from home. A hideout away from hideout.”
Makoto feels her lips twitch up, “It does sound fun.”
Ann playfully flicks her shoulder, “It better! Oh, and, I hope you don’t mind Ryuji barging in
every now and again.”

“That’s fine.” Makoto tucks some of her flyaway hair behind her ear, “It’s your house.”
“Mm. True.” Ann says, and flops backwards onto the bed.
Makoto raises an eyebrow, “Is something wrong…?”
Ann groans, “I’m just thinking. Is your sister gonna make us do our homework? Or study,
and stuff?”
“You should be doing that anyway.” Makoto points out reflexively.
“I know. ” Ann whines, “But, no offence, she seems like a hardass for that kinda stuff.”
She is. “I am, too.” Makoto reminds her.
Ann sighs, “I’m trapped on all sides. I swear Akechi-kun was judging me too.”
Makoto can’t help but laugh at that.
“What are you gonna do about schoolwork, by the way?” Ann props herself up on her
elbows, “…It’d suck if you had to repeat a year because of all this.”
Makoto had been trying to push the thought from her mind. “I suppose I’ll have to ask Harusan for her notes and any work we get.” She begrudgingly adds, the words a chore: “I’ll share
it with Akechi as well.”
“He might not thank you.” Ann warns. “Or maybe he will. He’s been really bored.”
Makoto is hard pressed to imagine any scenario where Akechi might thank her. She’ll live
without. “We have studied together once or twice at cram school before. So that’s something
proven that we won’t kill each other over.”
Ann tilts her head, “…At least you’ll have your sister to mediate, now?”
“That makes us sound like unruly children.” Makoto scowls, refusing to entertain the
comparison any further, “But that won’t be much of a help, really. We’ll just be gunning to
kill each other while Sis isn’t looking.”
Ann snickers, “I’m not cleaning blood out of my floorboards.” She jumps up off the bed, and
shuffles back over to the suitcases, “Y’know… I never thought I’d see the day when the
student council prez would be skipping school.”
“Me neither.” Makoto confesses, and abruptly feels very bad for the duties she’s abandoning,
“…All in on delinquency, I suppose?”
Ann grins, “All in.”

Motives, arcades, and cermonies

Ren can appreciate that things have started slowly, tentatively, to get back on track.
The Niijimas didn’t take long to declare their situation as unsafe. Makoto had texted Ren the
night before to let him know that they were taking Ann up on her offer.
“I’m a little concerned about the safety of Ann-chan’s place…” Haru had brought up during
school break. “Maybe I should have offered to buy a safe house of some kind…”
“The police still have their eye on you.” Ren reminded her, “Aren’t they still investigating
your dad, too?”
“We don’t know where Shido’s eyes are, either.” Morgana had piped up, “Making a large
unexplained expenditure might raise some questions.”
“You forget that Ann-chan may still have eyes on her, too.” Haru pointed out, “She’s been
involved in this since the beginning.”
“In that case, to any outside perspective, she’s still acting entirely normally.” Ren dismissed,
“But I’ll go check how they’re doing, at least.”
He had been wanting to chat with all those present, anyway.
Which leaves Ren here, on his way to the Takamaki residence, Morgana in tow.
He used Mementos for travel, of course. No sense in letting anyone track his movements.
Entering the Metaverse now, three days removed from the incident that forced them out, feels
almost entirely normal. In fact, if Ren weren’t hyper vigilant in searching for a difference in
the experience, he’s not sure he’d have noticed anything amiss at all.
But, now,
Ann yelps as Ren appears out of thin air. Sae, from the couch in front of the TV, looks quite
startled too.
“Uh.” Ann gapes, “Hi. Weren’t we meeting in an hour?”

“We are.” Ren confirms. It’s high time they started getting their plans properly underway, “I
wanted to talk to you first, though.”
Ann abruptly looks like she’s committed every crime in existence, grinning nervously, “Me?”
“All three of you.” Ren says flatly.
“Does that mean I don’t have to be there?” Morgana mutters, poking his head out of the bag.
“If you don’t want to be.” Ren offers. Morgana remains as one of the few people who hasn’t
run off to do something irrecoverably stupid. Ren trusts him more than he does himself at this
point.
Morgana sighs, as Ann’s already strained smile twists into a proper grimace, “Cool. Um, we
can do that.”
“I mostly want to talk to Goro.” Ren throws her a bone.
Her shoulders relax slightly, “Mm. Figures, I guess.”
Ren shifts, ignoring Sae’s piercing stare. He never could get a read on her. “…So?”
“Oh.” Ann jumps, “He’s in his room. Second on the left.” She points down the hall.
Ren would have preferred to talk to all three of them at once, but perhaps speaking to Goro
alone is wise. Or not. Whether or not an idea is a genius solution or fatally stupid is becoming
harder to parse.
Ren squares his shoulders, and hands Ann his bag, at which Morgana makes a pleased mrrp
sound that Ren is sure he will never be able to replicate or force the cat to admit to having
made. “Okay. Thanks.”
Ann seems well and truly out of her depth, as she gives him a dubious look. Sae’s meanwhile,
turns almost pitying.
Ren starts off down the hall, knocking on Goro’s door and not bothering to wait for a
response before letting himself in.
The bruise on Goro’s cheek has bloomed a sickly green and yellow. He looks up sharply as
the door opens, closing the book he was reading with a pointed thump and shooting Ren with
a cutting glare. “Pray tell, have the past few days caused all semblance of manners to
evacuate themselves from your brain?”
Ren snorts, forgetting he’s supposed to be mad for a second. “I wanted to talk with you.” He
says after he regains some composure.
“Talk, he says.” Goro mocks, “What, do you think I was the mastermind behind our sojourn
into Sae-san’s palace? To spite you specifically?”
Ren had, admittedly, entertained the possibility. “Well? Were you?”

“No.” Goro says, clicking his tongue, “You’ll have a bone to pick with Makoto, if that’s what
you’re looking for.”
“Makoto isn’t spiteful.” Ren counters, walking forward.
“Yes she is.” Goro scowls, so indignant that Ren can only accept the words as fact. She’s
probably only petty when Goro’s involved.
“That aside.” Ren takes a seat on the edge of the bed, a metre or so away, “Sae’s palace isn’t
what I wanted to talk to you about.”
Goro raises an eyebrow, “Oh?”
“Yeah.” Ren flexes his fingers against the covers, “According to Ann, you got caught on
purpose.”
Goro gives him a look that’s entirely unimpressed. “Really?”
“What do you mean, really?” Ren snaps.
“That’s what you’re up in arms about?” Goro drawls, sounding genuinely taken aback.
“You could’ve been killed.”
“It was a calculated risk.” Goro waves a hand, “I didn’t want to do it, but I didn’t want all of
us to be caught, either.” His glare turns venomous, “And you are the last person to be
lecturing me about this.”
Ren should’ve known this would be his counterargument. “I had a plan.” He spits.
Goro hums, “One with more holes than Swiss cheese.”
“It worked, didn’t it?” Ren scoffs, and then abruptly realises that Goro can use the same
logic, “And you don’t get to talk either. You were the reason we needed a plan to start.”
Goro laughs, “Well, look at that? All it took for you to complain about getting a gun to your
head was for me to try much the same.”
This argument is meaningless, a voice that sounds an awful lot like Arsène warns. Full of
circular reasoning and pitfalls and far too many landmines he and Goro had long ago come to
a silent agreement to leave buried. Ren ignores the warning.
“Well, go on, then.” Goro turns away, disinterested, “Air your grievances. It’s about time.”
Don’t act above it all, Ren seethes. “I,” He starts, leaning forward, “Have been trying very
hard to keep things from going to hell.”
“Do you want a medal?” Goro sneers.

Ren ignores him. “You talk big, that I act like we have a safety net, but then what the hell are
you doing?”
“Need I remind you,” Goro says, voice like ice, “That we are in this mess because of you?”
“I know!” Ren shouts, and then jolts, remembering they aren’t entirely alone, “I know, but it’s
like you’re trying to get yourself killed to test me.”
Goro’s face twists in a snarl, “Is that so?”
Back down, that same voice warns again. Ren will most certainly not. He leans forward even
closer, “Is it?”
“Fuck you.” Goro spits, “Take your assumptions somewhere else. Be angry all you like, but
don’t delude yourself into thinking this is about you.”
“Then what is this about?” Ren demands.
“Exactly what it looks like!” Goro’s fists clench so tightly the knuckles turn white, “We were
cornered, and I made a choice. Did you want Ann or Makoto in that fucking room instead? If
you want someone to blame, blame that fucking god of yours, or Shido, or Maruki, but don’t
pretend like I asked for this.”
Ren presses his lips together, “If you hadn’t been running around without the rest of us, then
maybe you wouldn’t have been cornered.”
“And now we’re back where we started.” Goro scoffs, folding his arms, “If you have
something you really want to say, then say it."
Ren has wanted to say a lot of things. From when they first met a year and a lifetime ago, to
everything that was November, to the sudden collapse that was December, to when Ren
thought he had all the time in the world to untangle their mess in January, toWell, he said everything he intended to say in February. Bar one thing, of course.
All of this just seems like one more thing for the pile. Ren will take one step forward, and the
rug will pull him five steps back.
“Is it too much to ask for you to stop trying to get yourself killed?” Is all Ren can choke out.
Goro’s scowl returns in full force, “I’m not trying anything.”
Ren’s memories of all that occurred in Maruki’s reality, and then some, would beg to differ.
“Then try harder to keep yourself alive.” He hisses.
Goro’s glare wavers, and his eyes flick down. “I am trying.”
It sure doesn’t look like it, from where Ren’s standing.
“Try harder.” Ren pulls away.

Whatever spell of hesitance Goro had been under shatters. “I’m still alive, aren’t I?”
“Yeah.” Ren contemplates leaning forward again. “You are.”
Goro smiles, sardonic, “Then is that all?”
Yes. No. He can never form the words he wants to.
Goro picks his book back up, “You should go. You have a palace to scout, don’t you?”
“I still have to talk to Ann and Makoto.” Ren mutters distantly.
“Then do that.” Goro says, pointedly opening to what must be a random page, “I think we’re
done here.”
No, we’re not. “I’ll be back later.”
Goro snorts, “And have something else self-aggrandising to say? Save it.”
Ren can’t even muster a glare. With all the fight drained, he just feels tired.
He stands, feeling his shoulders curl in. “See you.”
“You know where the door is.” Goro hums under his breath.
Ren wants to stay. But, he can only turn on his heel to leave, clicking the door shut quietly
behind him.
(And, despite it all, a smile twitches at the corner of his lips as a plan starts to form.
Maybe he’s been going about this all wrong.)

Futaba is not the person that Akechi wanted to see bursting out of thin air in the living room

Think broadly. Robin advises.

Futaba’s nose wrinkles, “You don’t remember if she ever worked on anything like that?”
“No.” Akechi snips coldly. “That’s not the kind of thing I would have had to have been
intimately involved in. So I don’t know.”
If Wakaba ever babbled about it as she regaled him of her projects, he doesn’t recall either.
Though Akechi suspects that can be attributed to something far more concrete.
Futaba looks unsatisfied. Was it that same feeling, Akechi wonders, that urged her to go
diving into Maruki’s palace?
“It is unsettling.” Akechi eventually breaks the silence, “That he knew.”
“Is there any other explanation?” Futaba worries her bottom lip between her teeth.
Akechi shrugs, “A lucky guess?”
Futaba scoffs.
Akechi truly has no idea. Anything he could come up with would be wild speculation.
“…Is that all?” He eventually asks.
A small frown crosses Futaba’s lips, and she doesn’t respond.
Akechi raises an eyebrow.
Futaba puffs out her cheeks indignantly.
“It’s a yes or no question.” Akechi deadpans, patience wearing ever thinner.

Futaba’s glare is rather lukewarm. She only takes a second to deflate. “…How long do you
think it’ll take before you can come with us into palaces again?”
Akechi narrows his eyes. He would have thought Futaba of all people would be happy to get
away from him. “That depends entirely on the rest of the thieves’ uninformed medical
opinions.”
Futaba snorts.
“I personally believe that I’m more than able to join you all at the moment.” Akechi adds.
“Do you, really?” Futaba presses quietly.
Well, everything hurts less in the Metaverse.
It hadn’t taken all that long to overcome the worst of it. The effects of whatever they drugged
him with had faded over twelve hours at most. He’s been on his feet without any assistance
since the day after Ann brought him back here.
He’s experienced far worse. Far worse. He’s died, for crying out loud, and yet he’s still
confined here to stew.
(And so why, why, do the aches still drive him mad, phantom pricks of ice clamping around
his neck, arms, wrists,
He's not thinking about it.
He needs something to do. )
“Yes.” Akechi answers.
Futaba gives him a dubious look.
“Why?” Akechi asks, “Has Sato’s palace already proven too challenging?”
“You’ve been there haven’t you?” Futaba deadpans, “You know it hasn’t.”
Point.
“It’s just…” Futaba trails off, not meeting his eyes, “Um. Get better. Soon.”
“Is that a demand?” Akechi levels her with a flat stare.
Futaba crosses her arms defiantly, “Yes.”
Akechi snorts, “Well, that’s what I’ve been trying to do.”
“Good.” Futaba mumbles.
(The Death grows to its sixth rank.)

Futaba shuffles on her feet a bit, “Uh, that’s it.”
“You know the way out.” Akechi tells her.
Futaba sticks out her tongue, “Ever heard of hospitality?” She turns to leave anyway, before
skidding to a stop with far more drama than her walking speed should have allowed, “Oh! I

Akechi takes it, eyeing it like he’ll be able to figure out its contents if he just stares hard

“Oh?” Akechi looks up.

All good points.
Working with Sae on a case sounds painfully awkward.
You never hated it before. A treacherous little voice tells him. He ignores it.
Akechi slips the USB into his own pocket. “Thank you.” He says to her, “I suppose we’ll do

Futaba rolls her eyes, “As opposed to what, exactly?”
Akechi has recently unearthed a whole stack of literature that Ann had apparently banished to

Futaba levels him with yet another dubious look. “Sure you do.” She takes out her phone,
“Anyway.” Her hand awkwardly hovers over the MetaNav, “Uh. Bye.”

Akechi sighs.
He walks out to the living room, “Sae-san,” He calls, “I believe I have a project for us.”

Candidate Found. The Nav affirms, Beginning Navigation.
Noir feels her mask and feathered hat settle on her head, and lets her hands drift to her axe.
She didn’t get much of a chance to truly fight, yesterday. She’s been feeling rather deprived
of combat as of late.
Her distant musings are cut short as she takes in the sight if the palace.
Where there stood a relatively nondescript office tower is now a sprawling theatre complex.
Another nighttime scene, now with ever-flashing sparks from cameras and set lighting.
Cognitive crowds surround a sectioned-off red carpet that rolls all the way into the street, and

“I don’t suppose,” Joker says mildly, “That following that red carpet will lead us to Ooe?”

the entrance, I wouldn’t be surprised if the shadow Ooe in here had some servants to lay
down an extra metre of carpet for every step he takes.”
“…Speaking of the entrance,” Noir pipes up, brow furrowing as she tries to survey the area,
“How can we get in?”
The carpet leads straight to the doors; the only doors, as far as Noir can see. And she gets the

Fox tilts his head, and inches towards the carpet with a curious look on his face, before

happen.”

hoped with a response like that, “All we’ve encountered so far has been… invisible walls and

Noir refrains from pointing out that Crow has ‘snuffed it’ in the past. Twice, if her memory
serves.

Joker gives the carpet a searching look, and delicately pokes his toe at the fibres.

Noir tenses her grip around her axe,
And smoothly hefts it over her shoulder as Joker leaps forward to rip the mask from the

“You can wait!” Joker laughs, and begins directing them back to where the others are

Haru wonders why the thought of working with Sumire pulls at her frayed nerves.
Sumire is one of her dearest friends. Her first friend, as a point of fact, and Haru has always

(Perhaps the secrets still rankle.
With Sumire and Goro both, really. Haru hasn’t found the time to take them aside and air her

Though, she suspects her true grievances, when she cares to examine them, lie somewhere in

Not being thought about at all hurts as much as the possibility that all this was done with
targeted malice. Haru isn’t sure if either is true, but as long as she ignores it all, she doesn’t
know.)
Sumire has been avoiding her eyes all day.
Perhaps she ought to pay a visit to the both of them, sometime soon.

Akechi, Sae decides, remains an enigma.

She eyes the next name. “Sasaki?”

aggressive, hidden so thoroughly with a sheen of starry-eyed idealist that she wondered if she
entirely imagined the slights tossed her way. The second: unapologetically crass, each barb

seems childish as he concentrates, perhaps the compartmentalisation will only do more

Irritating.

She, tentatively, leans towards the former. She ought not to inflate her pride any further; but

Something normal, maybe.

Akechi gives her a look, like he’s about to call Sae out for staring again.

Haru still has her gun in her hands.
Her father strides forward, still adjusting his tie. His face can’t seem to settle on one
expression, like Ooe is puzzling out how the man should react in real time.
He was shouting about gods in here, too. Ooe must pay attention to the downfalls of his
competitors.
“Haru.” Her father says, “I’m surprised you offered your assistance.”

Her grips shifts on her gun, “…Why so?”
“You’ve taken my position from me.” Her father sneers, and puffs out his chest, “I clawed my
way up from the bottom, and you ride on my coattails after the Phantom Thieves attempt to
discredit me? I’m surprised you made it inside this ceremony at all.”
Not an unsurprising stance from Ooe, she supposes. Haru wonders if he even registers the
myriad coattails he himself is likely gripping to. Shido’s, if no one else.
“I simply explained my achievements to the doorman.” She stretches the truth, her voice dull
even to her own ears, “I can’t say I care for the atmosphere, though.”
Her father’s lip curls even further, “Truly? Why bother forcing the more deserving to endure
your presence, in that case?”
This is silly, Haru thinks.
The thing before her is Ooe wearing a form-fitting mask. If the mask were gone, she’d hardly
be affected at all. Somewhat insulted, perhaps; but when is she not, when faced with people
like him?
Haru raises her grenade launcher again and blows the cognition’s face off.
The remains of it drop to the ground as dust, unceremonious.
It’s only now that Noir tunes back into the chaos that had followed her rather violent
outburst. A few metres behind her, Joker, Violet, and Mona stand to the side.
They must have wandered over during the commotion. Noir dearly hopes that they didn’t see
all of that.
Mona trots over, “Are you alright, Noir?”
She blinks, “…Just fine.” She dusts off her waistcoat. It’s a bit dusty. “I destroyed them
before any of the shadows could transform.”
“That’s good.” Violet says quietly. Noir appreciates that the smile she receives promises not
to push any further.
Joker’s eyes linger on the cognitions still running and stumbling in clumps to try and get
away from them. “…We might have to leave.” He decides, “How’s the security level looking,
Mona?”
“Bad.” Mona replies simply, and Noir abruptly feels terrible for her outburst.
“I’m sorry.” She says quickly, “I-”
Joker waves a hand, “It’s fine. I was gonna call it soon anyway.” Haru can’t tell if that’s a lie
or not. “I found a safe room on this floor, too, so we’re good to head back quickly.”

Noir nods slowly in acknowledgement. “I see.” She clears her throat, “Lead the way, then.”
Joker flashes her a small smile, quite similar to the one Sumire had granted her, and does just
that.
***
If there was ever anything Sojiro used to be good at, it was politicking.
Used to, being the operative phrase. He had to be, being a government envoy that had to deal
with the frustrating likes of Masayoshi Shido and the infinitely more charming but still
irritatingly scatter-brained Wakaba.
He had quit not too long before Wakaba died. Opening Leblanc was something of an old
dream, that quickly turned into nothing better to do when turning a blind eye to whatever
mess Shido and Wakaba were cooking together became all too much of a hassle for Sojiro to
tolerate.
Not nearly enough of a hassle for Wakaba herself. Quitting was never in her vocabulary.
Sojiro had admired it, once; but two years removed and with more hindsight than he ever
cared to have bestowed, that particular quirk of hers lodges itself in Sojiro’s mind as her
worst.
Taking Futaba in once he finally found where her relatives had tossed her was a no-brainer.
As ill-equipped as he found himself, it was the only thing he could have done.
Taking Ren in, (Back then: Amamiya, and even before that: the delinquent kid) required a bit
more thought. He’d curse his bleeding heart, but that heart didn’t have it in itself to do much
more than give the kid a roof and the occasional breakfast in the mornings at first. Certainly
not a door.
He’s grateful, if nothing else, for the fact that he learnt about his kids’ exploits after his heart
got the well-earned beating into shape that it needed from months of teaching Ren how to
make coffee and watching as Futaba started enjoying her mother’s curry again. He likes to
think he wouldn’t have turfed Ren out on the street if he found out too soon, but what does he
know? He’s liked to think a lot of things in the past.
He sure as hell didn’t sign up for all this. Being all but forced to take a back seat doesn’t
really help matters.
He’s sure the Niijima lady is in a similar position. But then again, he never expected to find
common ground with her, either.
The past few months, Sojiro decides as he stirs the pot of curry in Leblanc’s kitchen, have
been the universe testing the limits of how much it can throw him for a loop.
One such loop is having the aforementioned Niijima lady as a contact saved on his phone.
Another such loop is that he’s actually considering ringing her up.
Both the kids are out. The shop is empty, as ever. He has nothing better to do.

He clicks his tongue, and presses the dial button.
“Boss.” Niijima’s crisp voice quickly addresses, “To what do I owe the pleasure?”
Part of Sojiro is glad that he doesn’t have to give her the call me Boss talk. Another part of
him is miffed that she considered herself worthy of skipping past the formalities after the shit
she tried to pull with Futaba.
Water under the bridge he breathes out with his sigh, “Nothin’ much.” He admits, tapping his
stirring spoon on the edge of the pot, “How are you finding the new place?”
There’s a pause. “It isn’t terrible. I do feel like I’m permanently babysitting, though.”
Having to herd three teenagers without any escape doesn’t seem particularly pleasant, no.
“Getting any work done?”
“A bit.” Niijima hums, “Your daughter brought over some material for Akechi and I to parse
through. It’s not helpful for the task at hand, per se, but it’ll be a boon for me once all this is
over.”
He had been avoiding thinking about that detective kid. He resolves to ignore him some
more. “Are you still going to have a job once all this is over?” Sojiro raises an eyebrow at the
now-lidded pot.
A sigh. “Officially, I submitted a request for holiday leave. I disappeared before it was
officially granted, but it’s something.”
Sojiro hums, shuffling over to the coffee filters. “Hopefully they’ll be too distracted to
remember to fire you once the kids do their jobs.”
Niijima snorts. “I can only hope. Assuming I don’t lose my mind first.”
“Bored?”
“Yes…” She sighs, “It’s only been a few days, but I haven’t felt this restless in a long while.
Takamaki is the only one of us that can leave freely, technically, but at least Makoto gets to
run off with the thieves to stretch her legs. At this rate I’m going to have to tie Akechi to his
bed to stop him from straining himself.”
Ignorance fails him once again. He should have learned by now. “How’s he doing?” Sojiro
asks against his better judgement.
Niijima’s sigh this time sounds significantly more long-suffering. “I wish I could tell you. I
can’t tell is the thing. He’s insistent on getting back in the ring, so to speak, but I don’t think
anyone is even considering humouring him.”
“Does he still seem like he’s strained in movement, or suffering from headaches?” Sojiro has
never been quite as roughed up as the kid looked when they dragged him into Leblanc, but
he’s recovered from his fair share of scrapes.

“I can’t tell.” Niijima repeats, “It makes me wonder how many injuries he’s managed to hide
while we’ve been working together these past years. They’ve all made it sound like they get
run through with swords on a regular basis.”
Yet another thing Sojiro was trying to purge from his mind. Both the bloody image and the
reminder of the detective’s extracurriculars. “Might want to tie him to his bed, just to be
safe.”
Niijima laughs. “I’ll try.”
There’s a small beat of silence.
And, well, now that he’s started thinking, he can’t stop.
The Okumura girl had given him the politest talking-to Sojiro thinks he’s ever received when
he tried to pry for opinions about Akechi. She had turned out to be a thoroughly biased
source in the opposite direction to what Sojiro had expected.
He still hasn’t asked Futaba about it. Her announcement a day or so prior that she was
running off to go speak with Akechi had certainly painted a confusing picture.
Maybe Sojiro is the only one that’s confused.
(If there was ever something he was good at, aside from politicking, it was letting cobwebs
accumulate.
Oh, sure, he tried to be wilfully ignorant. Tried not to let Shido’s eyes pierce too far into his
skull. Tried not to let Wakaba’s mood swings and cagey demeanour set off any alarms.
But he was never a fool. Eventually the long-gone spiders’ work would leave tapestries, and
it would only take Sojiro glancing its way to get the whole picture.
He never looked. He almost did, when Wakaba died. But by then he had Futaba to take care
of, and the girl was already too much of a mess for her to ever deserve having a caretaker
entrenched in paranoid conspiracy theories.
Now Futaba herself, and all her friends, have very forcibly taken Sojiro by the jaw and forced
him to look, whether he likes it or not. The tapestry is practically useless when he’s been
handed an essay, aside from the self-defeating task of comparing notes, to see how far off the
mark he was.
And then there’s the extras. The threads he doesn’t want to touch. That kid he can’t remember
the face or name or voice of beyond how he looked like a stiff breeze would knock him over.
Futaba’s probing questions about the things her mother got up to at work. The things Wakaba
wouldn’t let Sojiro know she got up to at work. That detective, two years or more neck-deep
in a conspiracy with his shitty father -of course Shido has a few bastards wandering around,
Sojiro doesn’t know why he’s surprised- at its head.
He doesn’t need to knit the threads together to know what they mean. He isn’t sure if he
cares.

No- of course he cares. The consequences are far too broad for that. His own inaction far too
damning. He just isn’t sure in exactly what way he cares.)
He finishes brewing a mug of coffee, and sets it on the bench. He doesn’t even particularly
want a cup, but it’s there now, so he may as well drink it.
“I’ll let you get back to it.” He says to the phone pressed between his shoulder and ear.
“To what?” Niijima laments, “To my spreadsheets?”
“To whatever. I’ve got a customer coming in.” Sojiro lies.
“I’ll speak with you later, then.”
Sojiro supposes they will. The thought isn’t nearly as unappealing as it was just a few days
ago, but he still feels unsettled. “See you.”
The line clicks off.

Chapter 83
Chapter Summary

tag, chess, and unsettling discoveries

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

It is immediately apparent to Makoto, the minute she steps out of the safe room on the second
floor of Sato’s palace and takes her first good look at the new surroundings, that they’re in
luck.
Well, she isn’t quite sure if she wants to say that definitively yet. But what she can say is that
the next obstacle, whatever it may be, spans what looks like three floors rather than just the
one. There are large openings in the ceiling -twice up- that create oddly shaped lofts and
balconies; interconnecting tunnels leading this way and that, all for a purpose Makoto hopes
won’t be tedious.
The whole place is sparsely illuminated, much like the floor below; but it seems intentional
this time. Makoto doesn’t have much hope in her untedious theory.
“Oracle.” She calls, and the girl in question startles, “What are we looking at?”
“Another game.” Ryuji answers before she can, a grin slowly spreading across his face,
“Look, there’s a booth to sign up ‘n everything.”
“You needn’t look so excited.” Yusuke sighs.
“C’mon, dude.” Ryuji elbows him, “This is, like, the most fun we’re ever gonna have in a
palace.”
“I guess you’re right…” Ann chimes in, “It feels nice to be in a palace where no one has any
emotional baggage about it.”
Makoto tries not to feel targeted. Or jinxed. “We should stay on guard nonetheless.” She
reminds them.
“Yeah, yeah.” Ryuji dismisses, “Let’s check out what we’re workin’ with.”
Makoto sighs, and doesn’t throw a pity party, as the others all bound off the to the booth
without her input. She trails behind, designating herself as the only person keeping an eye out
for shadows- except for Oracle, perhaps. Though she seems quite taken with the idea of a
new game, as well.

“Yo.” Is Ryuji’s greeting to the shadow working behind the desk, “What’s bonkin’?”
Ann very suddenly has to clap her hand over her mouth to contain her snickers. Makoto feels
another sigh pressing against her throat.
The shadow is unfazed. “Would you like to register?”
“What it is that we’d be registering for?” Yusuke asks with a tilt of his head.
“Laser tag.” The shadow announces, and there’s a loud groan from Futaba, “Teams of five,
against four other teams.”
“Sweet.” Ryuji grins.
“Oh, is that all?” Futaba grumbles.
“Hold on.” Makoto quickly pulls them all back. She turns to Futaba, “What’s wrong with
laser tag?”
“Have you ever played? ” Futaba complains, “This isn’t a video game! It’s athletic!”
Ann has an amused smile playing at her lips, “Is it really, though?”
“I imagine it requires some dexterity.” Yusuke muses.
Makoto has set foot in an arcade exactly once. She did not play laser tag, but she knows the
gist. “…So is there anything actually wrong?”
Futaba sighs, “I guess not. I just might not be super helpful.”
“With shooting, maybe.” Ann agrees, “But, uh, navigator? Half of laser tag is trying to find
the people you’re trying to shoot.”
Makoto expects that the game taking place in a cognitive world -and with such a convoluted
stage- will present more challenges than that. But, when Ann lays it out so simply, she can’t
help but feel emboldened.
“Huh. I guess.” Futaba agrees tentatively, drawing herself up a bit.
“Then lets sign up, shall we?” Makoto says, breaking the circle and walking back to the
booth.
“Good thing we’ve got a team of five…” Ryuji mutters as Makoto quickly gives their name
to the shadow ( PHNTM THVS, as Futaba had set a precedent.), and she certainly agrees.
***
They’re sent to a waiting room.
Makoto, Yusuke, and Futaba all take a seat, biding their time. Ryuji stands at some point to
stretch his legs, and Ann similarly gets bored and starts pacing.

“I wonder if they’re gonna give us guns.” Ann muses, “Like, the fun ones.”
Thus far, they haven’t been given any additional equipment. Nothing of the sort has even
been mentioned. Makoto frowns, “And, if they don’t?”
“Guess we’re gonna have to use real ones then.” Ryuji grunts out as he stretches to touch his
toes.
Yusuke hums mildly. “A bit excessive.”
“Not if our opponents are a bunch of shadows.” Futaba counters, nose buried in her
holographic screens.
“On that,” Makoto starts, “Can you sense what our opponents might be from here?”
“Shadows or cognitions?” Futaba clarifies, and Makoto nods. “Let me see… Hm. I can’t
super tell from here, but I can’t sense any shadows in the vicinity at all. So, my money’s on
cognitions.”
“That isn’t exactly an indicator for difficulty.” Yusuke points out.
“This place does remind me of Okumura’s palace sometimes…” Ann sighs.
Futaba makes a loud shushing noise, “Don’t jinx it! With any luck, these guys’ll fold like
paper.”
Makoto doesn’t think they’ve ever been particularly lucky. She keeps this to herself. “What
are the rules, anyway?”
“Uh…” Ryuji looks up, “…Laser tag.”
Makoto rolls her eyes, “I know how laser tag works,” Mostly, “I’m just wondering- since we
haven’t been given equipment usually used in this game, is this a free for all were we have to
kill our competition? Or are we disqualified after being hit once?”
“…Perhaps we should hope for the former.” Yusuke says, looking faintly unsettled.
“We can hope all we like.” Futaba counters, “Let’s just play it like we’re screwed if we even
stub our toes.”
“No pressure, or anything.” Ann mumbles.
“We’ll be fine.” Futaba says unconvincingly, “Also, I don’t have a gun.”
“Are you gonna shoot it even if you do have one?” Ryuji raises an eyebrow.
“Guess not.”
“That’s settled, then.” Makoto says, standing up. “Oracle, perform your navigation as normal.
Stay inside your persona when you can.”

Futaba gives her a salute, “Will do, Queen.”
There’s a chime, and they all stiffen.
“Team four,” An announcement rings, “Please proceed through the door. The match is about
to begin.”
The door inside their waiting room swings open with a small creak. Makoto exchanges a
discomforted look with the others, and takes point.
They exit into a nondescript hallway- dark, with a black floor, walls, and ceiling; lined with
LEDs of a rotating colour, at least. Makoto remembers the house of darkness in her sister’s
palace with a pained grimace.
The hallway opens into a multi-tiered room, with myriad branching paths, pillars, stairs, and
tunnels. Makoto can’t see anyone that could be opponents, nor is the room anywhere near
large enough to span the entire length of the palace, even when taking the front booth into
account. She supposes this is just their starting area.
And, with little fanfare, announcement chimes: Start!
Makoto presses her lips together as nothing explodes immediately.
Well then.
She didn’t expect anything to. It’s just- she thinks she might have preferred if this game
required them to be more reactionary rather than take initiative. Going on the offensive can
be risky.
“So…” Ann drawls as Makoto doesn’t signal for them to move. “I guess we’ve just gotta find
people?”
“ Definitely cognitions.” Futaba chimes in, “I can sense them now. I think they only started
existing once the game began.”
Makoto hums, assessing their options.
There’s only one, really.
“Let’s track them down.” She says, and starts forward.
***
The first team they run into they dispatch tragically quickly.
The cognitions are faceless- a team of five much like themselves. They don’t get the chance
to find out the exact stakes of getting hit, because one flash of steel later and all the
cognitions crumble to dust.
“…Nice work, Fox.” Makoto says, a bit taken aback.

Yusuke tilts his head, “Well, we do want this done quickly, yes?”
Makoto supposes that’s true.
They do run into some trouble with the second team.
Makoto had been leading the thieves with their backs to the wall, trying to avoid being taken
by surprise- something concerningly probable in this environment. It might not be pitch
black, but it certainly isn’t well lit.
She had forgotten about how there are multiple floors. Their second encounter starts with a
panicked screech from Futaba as something drops down on her from above, shouts of pain
and confusion quickly following from the rest as much the same happens to them.
They still dispatch their attackers fairly quickly. The experience conveniently tells them that:
no, they won’t be immediately disqualified from one hit.
“Sorry.” Makoto quickly apologises once the dust has settled, “I didn’t realise the ceiling
opened up here.”
“It’s fine!” Futaba squeaks, clearly still a bit shaken, “Uh, I didn’t notice either, so…”
“…Maybe stay in Necronomicon?” Ann suggests, looking a bit concerned.
“It’s fine.” Futaba repeats, “I’ll just keep a better eye out. Besides, there’s only one team left,
right?”
Quite true.
It turns out that final team is a pain to find.
“Y’know,” Ryuji starts to complain, “I get these guys are probably good at hiding or
whatever, but it ain’t like they’re winning like this either.”
“It does seem to be an inefficient strategy.” Yusuke muses.
“Any luck pinpointing them, Oracle?” Makoto turns her head slightly, still keeping an eye out
ahead.
Futaba shrugs, “Eh. I can kinda sense ‘em, but…” She puffs out her cheeks, “Well, I think
we’re in the right area. They’re around here somewhere . ”
“So, just keep looking?” Ann finishes.
Makoto sighs, “I suppose so, yes. Stay alert. I don’t want to get ambushed again.”
They eventually creep their way into a room that stretches two floors up. Large pillars are
evenly dotted about, standing floor to ceiling. Makoto narrows her eyes suspiciously. She
can’t see anyone here, but-

Her thoughts are quickly interrupted by the sound of Futaba hurriedly pulling herself into her
persona, “They’re here, guys!”
The warning doesn’t serve much purpose, as there’s a sudden bang, and another, and another,
as a wave of gunfire bursts in their direction.
“Shit!” Ryuji yelps, diving behind one of the pillars.
The rest of them quickly follow suit. Makoto grimaces as a bullet clips her shoulder, sending

of the shoulder, not finding cover quite quick enough.
Thank goodness, she thinks distantly, that cognitive bullets aren’t nearly as cumbersome as
real ones. “Mediarama!” She tears her mask away, not willing to let the injuries sit.
“My thanks!” Yusuke calls from a pillar away.
“No problem.” Makoto murmurs back under her breath, more focused on the task at hand.
The bullets pause, and she chances ducking her head out to see what they’re working with.
“Oh.” Futaba comments, “That’s different.”
So it is.
Four of the five members of this team are the same faceless cognitions that they had faced
prior, but one of them stands out quite distinctly.
He has a distinct likeness, for one. And he looks like a middle schooler.
“Oh, shit!” Ryuji exclaims, poking his head out from his own pillar, “I know this kid!”
Makoto blinks, wincing as she has to duck behind another pillar to avoid the next barrage of

“He’s a legend!” Futaba’s voice echoes, “The King. Of Gun About, at least. Otherwise he’s
just a regular kid. I think Joker knows him.”
Makoto supposes that answers what he’s doing here.
“Come on out!” The cognition shouts, “I’m gonna kick your ass anyway, so let’s not waste
time about it!”
“Overconfident, isn’t he?” Yusuke comments.
Ryuji snorts, “You’re tellin’ me.”
Makoto takes a sharp breath, and bolts out from behind her cover, her gun braced in both

She stumbles, but the cognition still cries out. Red bursts from his shoulder, one bullet hitting

“Oh, come on!” The cognition complains, clamping a hand over the wound. “Alright, enough

“Huh?” Futaba mutters, “Hang on, what’s-”
The cognition bursts, leaving a spattering of red blood that quickly curdles black. Slick oil

“What?!” Ann gapes, popping her head out from behind her cover, “A shadow? But, I

“Yeah.” Futaba says darkly. "I did."
“Better watch it!” The cognition-turned-shadow grins, and there’s a fizz of purple in the air.
Makoto realises what’s happening a split second too late, as a shot of psychokinetic energy

“Hecate!” Ann shouts, “ Blazing Hell! ”
Makoto trips back as the floor glows a brilliant orange, the solid surface dissolving into

“Finish him off!” Makoto calls as the dust clears, signalling for the others to follow suit.
She feels muscle and bone give way to that slick oil again, and as she and the others skid to a

“Lame…” He complains, before he turns to dust.
The lights lining the walls glow brighter, and an outcropping in the ceiling flashes: Team 4
win!

“Ugh.” Ann makes a discomforted sound, “I kinda feel bad, since he looked like a kid.”

“I don’t recall ever encountering a shadow masquerading as a cognition…” Yusuke frowns,

“Assuming that’s still how we proceed.” Yusuke adds unhelpfully.
“Yeah, it will be.” Ryuji smacks Yusuke’s shoulder, “These places are the same all the way

Once they leave, they get a dispassionate congratulations from the shadow at the front booth.
They’re ranked in the top twenty-five, now.
As Makoto leads them to the first safe room on the fifth floor to mark their progress, she
wonders what else they’ll find in here. She’s not so optimistic as to think answers, but it

leaves her on edge nonetheless.
***
When Ren gives the other thieves a break on Monday, it is of no consequence to Akechi. He
does get to hear Makoto complain about it, though, given that running through Sato’s palace

Futaba is honestly a bit glad that Ren’s given everyone the day off.
That mostly meant everyone grumbling off to school with no hope of distraction come the
afternoon, but for Futaba it meant she had the whole day to get her side projects done.
The first, being the annoyingly pressing task that Akechi had suggested to her yesterday.
Some part of her -pride, probably- refuses to consider the possibility that Shido has access to
the Metaverse. It’s simply not his turf in her head; it’s her mom’s, and Futaba’s, and the
thieves’ in general. He can’t know about it’s inner workings, not withoutWhich leads to her second side project.
Side quest! Avoid thinking about how Sato definitely snooped on her mom’s research while
he was destroying it. Or, hiding it very thoroughly.
She can begrudgingly admit that it would be a smart move. If she had a super shady boss that
was telling her to destroy all this fancy research, she’d take a peek too. And if that research
had something -for lack of a better word- concerning? She’d be putting some of that stuff to
use sharpish.
But, then again, she doesn’t know what was on that research. Because someone won’t tell her.
And apparently, that same someone wasn’t even privy to all of it.
The logic to her anger breaks down unfortunately quickly when she lingers too long. How
dare dare Sato and Shido covet knowledge of the Metaverse when they wouldn’t know jack
shit without her mom- but, then, her mom wouldn’t know shit without a particularly vengeful
teenager being in the wrong place at the right time, and she suddenly starts feeling nauseous.
She’s failed the side quest of don’t think about it a couple times, but at least she can always
restart.
So: Task One.
Checking CCTV footage is… boring.
It’s tedious, for one. She has to give her search a fair expanse of hours where it would be
reasonable for Shido’s goons to be loitering while the thieves are running around in the other
world. So the time of their entrance, their exit, the whole time they’re inside, give or take

like, an hour on either side to accommodate for whatever is going through the
aforementioned goons’ heads.
Then she has to do that twice, for both the SatoTech tower and the TV studio. And multiply
that a couple extra times, because there could be any number of places where they would
think to wait for the thieves to exit the Metaverse.
She is… reasonably confident, that even if Shido can track their palace-diving, that he can’t
tell where they’re coming in and out of Mementos. For one, they’d have been caught three
times over by now. Ann’s apartment is a Metaverse entrance hot spot at the moment. Not to
mention the rest of the thieves’ abodes.
And yet, they haven’t been caught. Futaba isn’t entirely convinced of Ann’s apartment’s
safety, but it seems to be proving a valuable stronghold for now.
The final piece to the puzzle that she has to pin down is what Shido’s goons actually look
like.
If they were doing some men-in-black-or-whatever-else cliché, with suits, sunglasses, and all,
then Futaba would probably have a very easy time spotting them. They, unfortunately, do not
appear to be doing this. Bummer. It would have made her life easier.
Her solution is simple, but requires a fair bit more tedium than she would have preferred. She
had sent that list of all the Tokyo PD headquarters employees for Niijima’s benefit, mostly,
but Futaba can still get some use out of the new and improved “these are the guys high
enough on the ladder for Akechi to know that they’re working for Shido” list that’s been
thrown together. Pending further revision, but what’s there should serve her purposes.
And so, she gets to work. She fails her side quest once or twice, and then fails some more
when thinking about failing reminds her of why she failed to start, but she forges on
nonetheless.
It’s around seven when Futaba starts picking up on something promising.
As much as she internally bitched and moaned about all the hours of footage she had to comb
through, they’ve only poked around in each respective location three times now. Perhaps
enough to establish a pattern, but that doesn’t mean much if a group of suspicious people
don’t show up all three times.
But, they do show up two times.
Futaba manages to pinpoint several of the people in Akechi and Niijima’s list as scattered
about the two locations. Not in any obvious formation, but their vague presence alone is
enough to ring alarm bells, especially since they don’t appear to be there for any specific
purpose.
She even catches one or two guys that didn’t make it to the more refined list. She makes a
note to tell Akechi and Niijima about that.

Her triumph in catching Shido and his cronies with their hands in the cookie jar is short-lived
as she considers the implications.
Implications that ought to be pondered with an expert, she supposes.
Ugh.
She calls Akechi.
Or, more accurately, she calls Niijima.
“Fu-” A pause, “Oracle?”
“Uh, it doesn’t really matter which.” Better than being called ‘Sakura’. “I need to talk to
Crow.”
“You mean Akechi?”
“Sure do.” Futaba drawls out, spinning uncomfortably in her chair.

There’s a pause, and some shuffling, and some mumbling, before there’s a very distinct click
of the tongue that Futaba would probably recognise anywhere at this point.
“To what do I owe the pleasure?” Akechi deadpans, like the asshole he is.
“Yeah, yeah,” Futaba rolls her eyes, “Listen, I looked into that stuff you asked me to.”
That catches his attention. “Oh? So soon?”
“Well, we had the day off.”
“I noticed.” Akechi grouses.
Judging by that response, Futaba figures someone probably spent their day off bothering him.

“What do you mean what of it? ” Futaba snaps, indignant.
Akechi clicks his tongue again, “How is it relevant to our problem?”
“Well.” Futaba scrounges for a reason. “Maybe he’s helping Shido find us.”
“Unlikely. Takahashi is probably the one behind that, if that’s what’s happening. But if he is,

The rebuttal is irritating for a multitude of reasons.
Akechi doesn’t want to talk. Sure. Fine. Whatever. She can deal with that (She can’t, she

Morgana shakes his head, “I don’t think so. This feels like… the middle of the palace,
maybe? Not just this floor of the tower, I mean that there’s more building past the tower.”
“Huh.” Ren considers this, as two shadows skid around a corner. “Up and around, then?”
Sumire quickly scoops Morgana back onto her shoulders, “Up and around.”
And off they go again. They stop bothering with entering every single window as they creep
their way around the circumference in bursts. Sumire calls out an acknowledgement of more
of the same! as she peers into the windows each time she makes a landing.
(That feeling of wrong, wrong, wrong, comes in bursts and waves. Ren learns to balance the
ebb and flow with as much grace as he can muster, but he still holds tighter to Haru than
strictly necessary, just in case.)
Ren sees the tail of Sumire’s coat disappear high up above, a flash of red trailing behind. He
hooks onto a ledge, not even a window, he thinks, the momentum sending him careening up,
up, curved,
And onto the roof.
“It almost looks pretty like this.” Sumire observes, her heels digging into the shingles of the
spire tower roof.
She’s not wrong. For as gaudy and irritatingly reminiscent of Madarame’s palace Ooe’s
pocket of delusion seems to be, this high up the lights glitter from the eternal self
congratulation, flickering against the night in pinprick gemstones.
“Look.” Haru inclines her head, “That’s the rest of it, then?”
Past the tower they’ve just scaled, is a mirror of the palace before. A skylight with
chandeliers and clumped cognitions that look barely any more defined than ants from this
high up.
The primary difference is that the red carpet is smack bang in the middle of the room.
That, and Ren can see the treasure from here.
Go figure.

“Is- is that just it?” Sumire asks, seemingly spotting the same thing.
Morgana hums a negative. “No… not quite.”
“It’s right there, isn’t it?” Haru asks.
“Sure, but we won’t be able to tell if we can actually access it until we get up close.”
Morgana explains, “Or if there’s a fast one that the ruler shadow is waiting to pull.”
“Right.” Ren agrees, and shoves his hands in his pockets as he looks over the edge. “Which
means we’ve gotta get down.”
Sumire adjusts her new grappling hook around her wrist. “…Should we abseil?
Morgana gives a long-suffering, and mildly terrified, sigh.
Ren grins. “Nah.” He signals for Haru to grab on, “I can think of a faster way.”
Morgana’s expression turns from nervous to despairing, “Joker, please don’t-”
Ren laughs, and pulls both himself and Haru into a flying leap off the edge. He twists midair,
firing back at the roof ledge- grinning and letting out a private sigh of relief as he strikes true.
He carefully slows their descent like a trapeze artist in cloth, hoping the comparisons end at
his self-proclaimed grace before he ends up a tangled mess in metal wires. Above, he can
hear a yowl and the pitter-patter of heels on ceramics, before there’s a sudden absence, a
whoosh , a shhh, and a crack, and Ren doesn’t bother looking up to see that Sumire has
followed suit.
Ren feels the wire run short, and jerks his wrist to detach himself from the tether just before
he and Haru go crashing through their second skylight of the day.
“Zorro!”
A burst of gale-force winds, and their descent is pillowed one last time. They all hit the floor
with the only amount of grace anyone throwing themselves off a notably tall tower can.
Which is to say: not particularly graceful.
Morgana lets out a pitiful mew as all his fur stands on end, “Let’s never do that again.”
Ren privately agrees that maybe that was a bit much, even for him. Aloud, he has a reputation
to maintain. “I don’t know. It was better than shmoozing our way through the palace.”
“That might still be the final hurdle.” Haru says, and points towards the treasure.
It is shimmering, indistinct, as all treasures are. At its side, Ooe’s shadow sips at a
champagne flute and chatters with cognitions that toe the line of the red carpet.
“…We might be starting a fight if we get close enough to check if we can access the
treasure.” Sumire points out.

Ren thinks that’s an ordeal for another day. Everyone looks tired. Morgana looks vaguely
sick.
Ren owes his poor cat a lot of sushi, he thinks.
“There’s should be a safe room nearby.” Ren declares, “Let’s save our progress.”

On the way out, Ren returns to his mental note.
“What do you want, inmate?” Caroline scoffs as Ren approaches.
Ren shrugs, “Thanks for the information the other day. And for fixing up… everything.”
“It was our duty as wardens.” Justine says simply. “…But you did not make conversation just

Caroline scowls, “What’re you implying, inmate!?”
Ren shuffles out of baton range, “It’s just- I felt something.”
“Something.” Justine echoes, in a tone that might be sardonic.
“Like the palace wanted us out of here.” Ren elaborates.

Ren raises an eyebrow, “…The Nav stopped working.” He summarises, “The Velvet Room

bit more leeway, but not for me.”
“That sums up the symptoms. ” Justine nods, “But the exact cause was a little more
involved.”

bit. The barrier that exists to let people like you in got pulled out of shape.”
“A thread came loose.” Justine continues, “The fact that it could come loose at all is the
structural flaw of the Metaverse that we attempted to warn the defendant about.”

Right. “I thought you said that reality would fix itself, though?”

you do?”
Ren has never knitted anything before. “…Knit it back in?” He guesses.
“Yes.” Justine nods, “But think: how would you do that without undoing the entire blanket to
start knitting from where the weave came loose?”
“With great tedium.” Ren says.
Caroline rolls her eyes, “You got that right.”

forces that keep reality together, had to settle for a second-rate fix.”
Great. “So something like that could happen again?” Ren pushes.

for the possibility.”

granted great influence on space, wants you to leave…”

“I think I get it.” Ren mumbles.
“Well, good.” Caroline huffs, and crosses her arms, “We did all we could!”
“I know.” Ren says quickly. “Thank you.”
“You’re welcome.” Caroline sniffs.
“So you’re definitely sure this won’t be a problem?” Ren hazards one last time.
The twins exchange yet another look.
“We’re sure.” Justine eventually says.

Ren hopes, for everyone’s sake, that their confidence in the matter is well founded.

Robin and Loki shrivel back, denying any access to being called. Akechi almost rolls his

“You got it, Mister!” José smiles, and-

If Akechi remembered how violent this process was the first time, he might have hesitated
going for round two.
The jagged oasis that houses his personas is forcefully pried open, heedless of the sharp

God, they’ve barely even startedAkechi sees José raise his hammer-it’s Mementos that twists, this time. The walls fold, the tracks lift and split in jagged chunks.
That heartbeat that pulses through the veins of the cognitive world ticks faster, faster, bones

The presence in his chest as the mask settles is not nearly as intrusive as others before her.
You have been here before. Eurydice comments.
Akechi swallows. I have, he thinks back.
Will the tale remain the same?
Perhaps, the tale need not start. He hasn’t been bitten yet.

Was it? Robin grouses.

“Nothing’s happened yet…”

“All the thieves and then some, I assume?” Haru guesses, and Akechi nods, “You described

“It makes plenty of sense!” José says, the closest to looking affronted that Akechi has ever

The image of Joker running around, picking up fleshy subway flowers and weird stamps is
