Morgana fumes silently.
“Rich, coming from you,” he eventually spits.
It’s irritating, that Akechi can’t argue. “I am attempting to reach acceptance presently.”

“How’s that working out for you?”
“Poorly.”
“See!” Morgana huffs.
“Have I not proven time and time again that people should strive to not be me?” Akechi
clicks his tongue.
Morgana snorts. “Well, yeah.”
“Then there, I’ve said something.”
Morgana kicks him in the ankle. “Jerk! Don’t act like you’re above it!”
(A common mechanism. He will rage and curse and bleed and scoff when he sees it
elsewhere.
He knows well: this is not conducive to success. He knows well: that there is little one can do
but rage and curse when so thoroughly trodden upon by misfortune. He knows well,
Wasn’t it cathartic, to scream blood and murder?)
“Do you really want to hear how I’m feeling?” Akechi sneers.
“Sure.” Morgana scowls. “Yes. Lay it on me!”
“I think,” Akechi begins, “That this is all a pile of hot, flaming, bullshit. And if I had it my
way, Shido would have been paste in his carpet months ago.”
Morgana groans. “We all already know that.”
“And everyone is painfully aware at how desperate you are to be human, and you’re still
sulking.” Akechi snarls.
“Well at least you still get to do something! I’m just,” Morgana gestures furiously to himself.
“Stuck like this!”
“Do you want me to do something?” Akechi’s lip curls. “Maybe I will kill him, since you’re
so insistent. Perhaps I should finish the job with Ren while I’m at it.”
Morgana scoffs. “You don’t mean that.”
“I thought your point was that we were on the same page,” Akechi snaps. “I’m agreeing with
you. None of this is fair. But what recourse do any of us have? Ask Maruki for a solution?”
That shuts Morgana up, as much as it ever has for someone who wasn’t there to witness
January in the flesh. Akechi hands flex and tighten, his gloves straining.
Morgana’s ears flatten against his head as he finally speaks up again. “Was my wish…? Well.
What was I like?”

“Extremely unsettling.”
“Oh.”
(In that moment, the Hermit grows to its eighth rank. Akechi has long since stopped trying to
discern any logic from such things; but still, he wonders)
Morgana kicks at the ground again.
“So I’m really not human?” he asks, voice small.
“I’m trying not to break anything.”
“I’m not fragile.”
“I meant the timeline,” Akechi clarifies.
Morgana sniffs. “Sure.” His eyes are fixed on the ground. “…Do you know what I am?”
“Whatever revelations you may have had, you had them while I was busy being dead,”
Akechi says. “I have no idea.”
Morgana squeaks out a laugh, coughing like he didn’t expect it. “Asking you was a bad idea.”
Akechi snorts, walking ahead. “Now this is a revelation you should have had a long time
ago.”

“Where were you?” Makoto doesn’t mean to snap when Akechi appears back in Haru’s
apartment.
Akechi glares at her, shoving his phone back in his pocket and folding his arms. “Where do
you think?”
“Right,” she huffs.
“Please don’t get into an argument right now,” Haru cuts in. She’s been rushing around for
the past thirty minutes, fretting about every corner of the living room. Despite this, she still
manages to look otherwise quite calm.
“No arguments here,” Akechi says drily. “Is something happening?”
“Those bodyguards you hired are showing up,” Ann says from the couch. “Apparently.”
“Yes, we’ve reached an accord,” Haru confirms. “I’ve signed the required contract.”
Also from the couch, Makoto swears she hears Sae audibly frown.
“And you’re certain you trust these people?” she says.

Sae looks at him with vague disgust. Makoto herself can’t settle on mirroring her expression,
or snorting very loudly. She barely manages to do nothing.
Haru sighs, moving to adjust a pot plant for the fifth time. She nearly shatters it as she startles
violently at the sound of the apartment’s buzzer.
Makoto tenses. Ann splutters as her hair flies into her mouth with the speed of her head
whipping around. Sae closes her eyes. Akechi seems nonplussed.
No one moves, and as the seconds tick on Makoto feels herself tense further. Haru wrings her
hands and rapidly fixes her already perfect hair, and strides down the hall towards the door.
“Should we hide?!” Ann hisses.

“Well, they’re going to see us eventually,” Akechi says. “So it seems like wasted effort.”
“Shouldn’t you hide?” Sae folds her arms, hands tensing and flexing. “You’re the supposedly

“With any luck, they’ll be endeared,” Akechi says, but his lip curls. “Unless you suggest I
keep up the disguise permanently? I’m sure a face mask will work for long stretches of time”
“Alright fine, you’ve made your point,” Makoto snaps. “Then what—?”
The sound of three sets of shoes click down the hall.
Akechi eyes dart in the direction of the noise, and he lowers his voice to a hiss. “Consider

“And if they don’t?” Makoto hisses back.
“You won’t like my suggestion.”
Makoto manages to truncate the myriad curses that threaten to burst from her lips as the

“Thank you for your punctuality, Micheal-san,” Haru is saying.
“Not at all,” Micheal says, dressed what Makoto can only assume is an exact copy of the suit

“No,” Haru agrees. “It wouldn’t.”
Micheal hums, his gaze dragging over the living room. He gives a polite bow to the small

“Likewise!” Ann says, a bit too cheerful and a bit too loud. Makoto can see her actively

“Thank you,” Haru says, even as Makoto really isn’t sure what such a concession will

Futaba isn’t unfamiliar with crunch.
She’s worked overtime to get things done before. In fact, she’s worked herself into several
stupors, that her mom and then Sojiro mildly panicked about until they realised she was just
exhausted. However, the key distinction between then and now is that her self-imposed
fervour was just that: self imposed. There was no outside force dictating that she mash at her
keyboard until her fingers hurt, she simply felt like doing so.
She doesn’t particularly feel like doing so right now. She’d rather be asleep, honestly. She’d
rather be doing a great many things other than preemptively figuring out all the backdoors to
hijack the Shibuya Scramble television screens, and mashing her face against her PC tower
trying to edit a suitably cool calling card that past-timeline-her already did.
She kinda wishes Ren brought a USB with him back in time. Woulda been helpful. And she
could have spent the day doing something that didn’t make her feel sick.
She ought to feel vindicated. Ready. Excited. Itching to fight, itching to stick it to Shido after
he killed her mom and then had his palace rub it in her face. Futaba is too drained to feel
anything other than mild dread.
Maybe it’ll be easy, she thinks, and then immediately backpedals lest her internal monologue
invite destruction from universal forces.
She, thankfully, didn’t have to write the calling card. Ren sent a summary of what the calling
card consisted of last time via the group chat, and everyone collectively agreed that pasttimeline-them did a pretty good job. (Barring Akechi and Sumire, naturally, the latter of
whom had to be bullied into adding a line or two of her own after saying she ‘didn’t really
mind if she wasn’t there!’ and the former, who wrote a spiteful and cutting paragraph that had

to be both trimmed and thoroughly toned down. Strangely, Futaba got the sense his heart
wasn’t really in it.)
The calling card script is kinda cheesy. Their various line deliveries, sent hastily via phone
recordings and with awful quality quickly masked by voice modifiers, equally so. Which of
course means it’s cool as hell. Futaba wishes she could appreciate it more.
She wishes she could focus,
This thing needs to be done today. No pushing it back, no breaks, no messing around because
they technically still have time, their time is up. Futaba has been running off of the
procrastinator’s gambit for so long that the realisation that the election is in two days has
thrown her for something of a panic-induced loop.
Focus.
She’s trying.
Where did her energy from when she took out Medjed go? She could use some of that right
about now. She thinks it died when time travel started getting involved. Could she get it back
if she asks nicely?
Focus. Necronomicon repeats, her voice beginning to sound exasperated.
Yes, yes, she’s making progress. Inchworm level progress, but still progress.
She’s actually quite close to being done. The various television networks and Scramble
screens proved to be not much of a challenge. She hasn’t hacked them yet, of course, just
done some reconnaissance, but when the time comes she suspects it’ll be easy pickings.
It’s late afternoon.
Work quick, work quicker.
Are you really satisfied with an anticlimax?
…Futaba does just kind of want this to be over.
But, no. No, Necronomicon is right, and Necronomicon is her, so it basically means that she’s
right: Shido is the chickenshit before the real final boss, but he still killed her mom. Laced
landmines into the ground to try and tear her family apart again and again, and it doesn’t
really matter what the calling card is, but by the gods that keep trying to screw them over is it
gonna be cool.
Futaba looks at her editing software, calling card near-finished in the timeline. It’s already
pretty cool. It could be cooler though. What’s the point of having another version of yourself
to compete with if you aren’t trying to one-up them constantly?
“Ren!” Futaba shouts without bothering to unshrimp herself from where she’s hunched over
her computer.

Ren scrambles into their shared room, looking frazzled. “What?!”
Futaba snickers, a grin splitting her face. There’s the energy she was looking for. Hey, maybe
she should get back into the hacktivist business while she’s at it. She feels great. “You’re
gonna need to rerecord some lines. We’re making this the shit.”

Well.

And, still, there is something to be said about transparency.

“Of course,” Makoto echoes dourly.

Makoto is getting the feeling that it’s his.

Chapter Summary

The lion, the pyramid, and the politician.

The Shibuya Scramble is never a place of peace. Only in the earliest hours of the morning
could it feasibly stake a claim, and even then it’s liable to come dead last against whatever
opponent one chooses to pit it against.
There is no peace, but it is largely consistent. Bright lights flash from cars and from the vivid
advertisements plastered over the 109. The evening sun manages to force its rays past the
horizon and through the jungle of concrete. People, a thousand and more, flow in erratic
waves. Uncaring of each other and uncaring to—
All the billboards that adorn the Scramble as wreaths go dark.
There is a collective gasp, the occasional shriek, as a heavily digitised voice clears their
throat over every loudspeaker in the Scramble, and further— every television station in
Japan.
“Goooood Evening, Japan!”
“Missed us, huh?”
(It is barely five seconds into the broadcast, that Masayoshi Shido already has various
assistants and lackeys banging on his door in a frenzied panic. His lips peel into a snarl.)
“Where was it we last left you again…?”
“Our apparent leader’s daring escape.”
“A veritable garbage tip of lies.”
“Our supposed involvement in the missing case of the Detective Prince. The suspicion of the
Mental Shutdowns and Psychotic Breakdowns.”
“Well, like we said: total lies, of course!”
(Akechi and Makoto are once again left to stare Micheal down as he shamelessly watches the
broadcast on his phone. At the mention of the Detective Prince, he raises an eyebrow at the

man in question.
Just as shamelessly, Haru announces, “We’ll be heading out. If anything happens, please
speak to Niijima-san in the living room.”
Micheal salutes, “Aye, aye, boss. Shall I wish you good luck?”
“Whatever for?” Haru asks innocently.
Ann chokes on her water.)
“Bet you’re wondering what we’re here for?”
“What tyrant will we topple next!”
“We’re glad you asked. The man behind it all, the one at the head of the Psychotic
Breakdowns and Mental Shutdowns, the spider at the centre of a conspiracy’s web rotting our
country from the inside out.”
“Your favourite for the vote.”
“Masayoshi Shido!”
(Sumire watches as both her parents gasp, eyes fixed to the TV. She continues to, very
silently, pack all her necessary thieving gear into a duffel bag.)
“A scumbag who chews people up and spits them out.”
“A bastard who’s ready to do the same to the rest of Japan.”
“Hear us, now.”
“But you don’t really need to listen!”
“Soon, you’ll be hearin’ all this asshole’s crimes from his own mouth.”
(Ryuji’s mom still gasps and claps at all the right moments when she sees the calling card on
TV, even though she already knows the whole deal by now.
“Futaba did an excellent job putting this all together,” Yusuke comments. Ryuji still doesn’t
really know why he’s here, actually.
He still claps him over the shoulder, and grins, “Our turn, yeah? Let’s kick some ass!”)
“You’d better watch it, Shido.”
(“Don’t die,” Sojiro says gruffly. Ren didn’t miss the smirk that flashed across his face when
the calling card played.
Ren salutes, as Futaba still wages war against her keyboard. “You got it, boss.”

“Don’t worry, chief,” Morgana snickers. “Shido’s got nothing on us!”
Sojiro snorts, waving a hand. Ren, again, can’t miss the twitch of his lips. He feels Joker’s
smirk crawl up his face in turn.)
“Tonight, the Phantom Thieves take your heart!”

To say that Sumire is prepared would be a blatant falsehood.
With the calling card delivered, the seas parted by Shido's cruise liner bleed even more red
than usual. The fringes of her vision pulse, and even without any notable navigational
abilities, she can feel the shadow's ire as strongly as if he were glaring at her face to face.
She can hear the creak of Crow's gauntlets as he squeezes his hands into painful fists. The
strain of Joker's gloves is just as telling.
"Are we ready?" Joker asks. The smirk on his face when they entered the palace has since
faded into tight concentration.
“Five extra minutes milling about won’t change whatever the answer to that question is,”
Crow snaps. “Let’s go already.”
“…I’m ready,” Oracle says, pointedly.
Joker tugs sharply on his gloves. “Good.” He spins on his heel, cloak whirling in a flashy
spin. “Let’s move.”
They waste no time in doing so. They don’t even have to warp to a saferoom, with the
treasure so close. They don’t bother with the preceding shadows, nor do they pay any mind
when they’re spotted anyway. Quickly, they approach the central chamber built in perfect
reflection of the Diet Building itself. The only place on the ship to do so, aside from the
facade on the deck.
“Where is he?” Skull hisses, a moment too soon.
It is only by coming face to face with his shadow that Sumire wonders if she has ever seen
Masayoshi Shido in person before.
His shadow looks almost insultingly normal. The only otherworldly feature: his golden eyes
shielded by rectangular orange sunglasses that perch on his nose. Otherwise: his suit is crisp,
tie straight, hands calmly folded behind his back as he stands at the peak of the
representative’s chamber.
“You all look very confident for a band of insolent children who haven’t won yet,” Shido
comments.
“Confidence earned,” Crow says, flicking his gun’s safety on and off in what Sumire assumes
must be a nervous tick. “Your ship is a joke.”

“Must we have this back and forth?” Haru interjects. “We’re all aware there’s no negotiation
to be had here.”
“Is that so?” The shadow does not step forward, yet Sumire still feels the urge to step back.
She manages to hold her ground. “My fool of a son seems to rather enjoy an open rapport.”

“How do we leave!?” Futaba shrieks.
Ren’s mind begins to tick into panic-stricken overdrive.
Exiting the Metaverse can be achieved via two methods. The first, the far more reliable, is via
the Nav. Clearly a certain god isn’t too keen on them using such a method. Opportunistic
bastard.
The second, far less reliable, the loophole employed in their scatter-shot mess of an
Interrogation room plan the first-year-over, is simply passing by the place you entered.
Ren stares out at the shattered ship. There is only water where the deck once was.
“We swim,” he says.
“I cant!” Futaba tugs violently on his hand.
“Nor can I,” Yusuke admits.
“Then grab onto someone,” Ren says, preparing to step off of the ledge as the water’s surface
gets rapidly closer.
Goro snatches him by the arm. “Are you a fucking fool.”
“We’ll drown in that, able to swim or no,” Haru says coolly.
There is another, much louder, much closer, scream of metal beneath their feet. “Then how,”
Ren grits, and echoes: “do we leave.”
As Goro seethes and Haru closes her eyes to breathe, Makoto kicks the leg off a side table.
“Driftwood,” she announces.
“That’s definitely not going to—”
Ann doesn’t get the chance to finish before the part of the ship that lies across the expanse of
water stretching in front of them explodes in fire. Ren grinds his teeth as the others shout in
shock, knowing that if that life boat had been dangling somewhere still, it’s drenched in
flames now.
Sumire takes out her phone again, furiously tapping at the Nav.

Access Denied.
Access Denied.
Access Denied.
Access—
“The palace is going to tear itself apart before we get anywhere, at this rate,” Goro says.
“What the eff happens then?!” Ryuji shouts.
“We die, right?” Futaba is mumbling, “We get crushed, turned to paste,”
“We get spit back out to reality, which ultimately fixes the problem,” Goro interrupts.
“But?” Ren pushes.
Ren is sure Goro has an anecdote or two. Perhaps even three or four, of daring non-escapes
from palaces that crashed down around his ears, that spat him back out onto the pavement
and scraped his knees. Ren is sure that there is some knowledge, some wisdom, like stick to
the left, or pull your ears twice and hold your breath that saves any poor fool in this
circumstance from certain death.
Ren does not hear it, because—
There is a tear, a seam, a fraying winding unravelling thread
Ren, for all that he suddenly feels barely lucid, has the distinct thought that this is not how
un-reality is supposed to function.
There is a miasma,
This is bad, that metal angel says.
There is salt, and there is blood,
There is steel, and velvet.
Quite bad! The grinning phantom agrees.
There is no longer a hand, he thinks, gripping his own.
Hold tight.
Hold as many as you can!
There is one, and another, and another,
And not nearly enough!

Reach for—
What?
There is concrete.
And there is red.
Ren reaches for the red—
***
On one half of a veil, five are spit across the paved ground with scraped knees and shouts of
protest.

On the other half, another five tumble beneath a reddened sky.
“Hey!” Morgana shouts, “We made it to Mementos!”

“We’re back in the real world?” Haru asks, dizzy as she stumbles to her feet.
“The eff?!” Ryuji groans, splayed out over some grass.

“I thought Goro said we’d be back in reality?” Sumire says, dusting off her knees. She
worriedly stares at the sky, at her phone, at the still-unresponsive Nav.
“Better here than right in front of the Diet, right?” Ann mumbles, still face down. “Better
here than drowning.”

“We need to go,” Akechi says, “Quickly. Where are the others?”

“Where is everyone else…?” Yusuke asks, head on a swivel.
“Futaba?” Ren shouts, “Goro?”
“I can’t see Haru, Ryuji, and Makoto, either!” Morgana bounds up and down in a panic.

Makoto’s eyes are wide, stricken, “I can’t see them. I can’t see them— where did they—?”

“They didn’t get caught, did they?!” Ryuji blurts.
“How?!” Futaba says, shrill, “It’s not like we were unconscious!”

“They’re not here,” Ren determines, “Are they back in the real world?”
“What, did we trip and miss?” Ann says incredulously.
Sumire holds out her phone,

Haru holds out her phone,
Access Denied.

Ren swears, colourfully.

Akechi swears, creatively.
“We have to go,” Makoto echoes dully, “We can’t just stand here. We’re right in front of the
National Diet,”
“We’re going,” Haru says, swiping away from the Nav to Micheal’s contact.

“We’re stuck in Mementos!?” Morgana shrieks.
“What do we do?!” Ann cries in similar hysterics.
“What will we eat?” Yusuke demands.
“What about our plan?” Ren blurts in a panic before he can remember his veil of leader calm.
Sumire yanks painfully on her own ponytail.

Futaba sniffles, as the five of them wait with hoods up on a nondescript street corner.

Ann drops into a crouch and buries her face in her knees.

“It’s, uh,” Ryuji tries very hard to smile. “We’ll fix this, yeah? S’not the end of the world.”
“It’s the seventeenth,” Akechi says flatly, as the clock has ticked past midnight, “Give it a
few days.”
(Even severed in twain, the Judgement grows to its final rank)
